## Stakeholders

- **CLI users** reading error messages — currently see inconsistent capitalization depending on which code path produced the error.
- **MCP clients** parsing or summarizing error messages — capitalization difference is one more thing they must handle.
- **Future maintainers** adding new `NotFound`-style errors — currently must pick which casing without obvious guidance.

## Where

- `crates/kanban-domain/src/error.rs:86-87` — `NotFound { entity: &'static str, id: Uuid }` Display: `"{entity} {id} not found"`.
- `crates/kanban-domain/src/error.rs:91-96` — `NotFoundByName { entity: &'static str, name: String, available: Vec<String> }` Display: `"{entity} '{name}' not found..."`.
- All `KanbanError::not_found("...", id)` call sites — lowercase entity tags (e.g. `"sprint"`, `"card"`, `"column"`).
- All `KanbanError::not_found_by_name("...", name, available)` call sites — capitalized entity tags (e.g. `"Sprint"`, `"Card"`, `"Column"`).
- Pinned by KAN-655's new CLI tests at `crates/kanban-cli/tests/cli_integration.rs:1859-1916` — one test asserts `"Sprint"`, the other asserts `"sprint"`, deliberately matching the asymmetric paths.

## Why

A user sees `"sprint <uuid> not found"` when they pass an unknown UUID and `"Sprint 'foo' not found"` when they pass an unknown name. Same fundamental error class, two different shapes for the entity tag. It looks like a bug to anyone reading two consecutive errors from different paths. It also makes downstream tooling (LLM agents, log aggregators) treat the same error as two slightly different things.

The asymmetry is pre-existing — KAN-655 didn't introduce it but is now the first place tests explicitly pin the two casings to prevent regressions until a deliberate normalization happens.

## How

Pick one canonical convention and apply it everywhere.

**Option A — lowercase everywhere.** Match current `NotFound`. `"sprint 'foo' not found"`. Reads like sentence-mid-clause.

**Option B — capitalized everywhere.** Match current `NotFoundByName`. `"Sprint <uuid> not found"`. Reads like a complete sentence.

**Recommend B**: capitalized. Error messages typically render at the start of an error line (whether from `eprintln!`, MCP client display, or TUI banner) where sentence-leading capitalization is more readable. Also matches `kanban_domain::pluralize` and existing `Validation`/`UnsupportedFutureVersion` Display lines which start with capitalized words.

### Mechanical change

1. Update all `KanbanError::not_found("foo", id)` call sites: `"foo"` → `"Foo"`.
2. Update `is_not_found()` and `not_found_by_name` docs/tests if they assert lowercase.
3. Update the KAN-655 CLI test `test_card_create_with_assign_unknown_uuid_fails_with_useful_error` from `"sprint"` → `"Sprint"`. (The name test already uses `"Sprint"`.)
4. Update any TUI banner / CLI stderr golden tests that assert lowercase entity tags.
5. Update any other crate tests across `kanban-service`, `kanban-mcp`, `kanban-tui`, `kanban-cli` that match on lowercase tags.

`grep -rn 'KanbanError::not_found("' crates/` and `grep -rn '"sprint not found\|"card not found\|"column not found' crates/` give a complete call-site inventory.

## Offender example

```
$ kanban card create --board B --column TODO --title X --assign nonexistent
Error: Sprint 'nonexistent' not found

$ kanban card create --board B --column TODO --title X --assign 11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555
Error: sprint 11111111-... not found
```

Same logical error, two visible shapes.

## Solution example

```
$ kanban card create --board B --column TODO --title X --assign nonexistent
Error: Sprint 'nonexistent' not found

$ kanban card create --board B --column TODO --title X --assign 11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555
Error: Sprint 11111111-... not found
```

Both lead with `Sprint` regardless of the lookup-key shape.

## Acceptance criteria

- One canonical entity-tag convention (recommended: capitalized) applied across every `KanbanError::not_found*` call site.
- KAN-655's two CLI tests use the same casing for both name-path and UUID-path assertions.
- Workspace tests pass after the rename; no regressions in TUI / CLI / MCP error-message contents observed by users.
- Doc comment on `DomainError::NotFound` and `NotFoundByName` documents the convention so future variants pick the right casing without guessing.
- Changeset is `bump: patch` (user-visible message change is cosmetic, no API shape change).
card.title: Normalize entity-tag casing across NotFound and NotFoundByName variants

card.description:
## Stakeholders

- **Users upgrading a V1 or V2 JSON file to 0.7.x** — anyone whose `kanban.json` predates KAN-415-ish (V2) or KAN-256-ish (V1), opened by a 0.7.0+ binary. Files are unrecoverable if the destructive V→V7 chain fails partway through.
- **Both async (`Migrator::migrate`) and sync (`migrate_to_v7_sync`) load paths** — they share the gap; the fix needs to land in both, or in the shared policy helper plus a coordinated orchestrator reorder.

## Where

- `crates/kanban-persistence-json/src/migration/backup.rs:15-22` — `pre_v7_backup_path_for` returns `None` for both `FormatVersion::V1` and `FormatVersion::V2`.
- `crates/kanban-persistence-json/src/migration/migrator.rs:71-76` (async) and `crates/kanban-persistence-json/src/json_file_store.rs:94-101` (sync, post-KAN-650) — both orchestrators run `migrate_v1_to_v2*` then `migrate_v2_to_v3*` **before** checking the backup policy, so V1 and V2 sources are overwritten before the policy gets to fire.
- `crates/kanban-persistence-json/src/json_file_store.rs:154` — `migrate_v1_to_v2_sync` writes `.v1.backup` then **removes it on V1→V2 success** (`let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&backup_path)`). The V1 backup only protects the V1→V2 transition itself, not the subsequent destructive chain.
- `crates/kanban-persistence-json/src/migration/migrator.rs:142-188` — `Migrator::migrate_v1_to_v2` (async) does the same: backup created, then removed on success.
- Misleading comment in `pre_v7_backup_path_for` that V2 "is shape-stable through V2→V3 and needs no backup" — true for the V2→V3 step alone, **not** true for the V→V7 chain that runs after.

## Why

### The V2 gap (originally documented)

`pre_v7_backup_path_for(V2, path)` returns `None`, so the destructive `split_graph` + `v6_to_v7_rename` chain runs against the now-V3 file on disk with no backup. If either step fails:

1. The original V2 content is gone (overwritten in place by `migrate_v2_to_v3_sync` / `migrate_v2_to_v3`).
2. No `.v2.backup` was ever written.
3. The user has a partially-transformed V3 (or V6) file on disk and nothing to roll back to.

### The V1 gap (caught in PR #321 final review)

The V1 case looks safer because `migrate_v1_to_v2_sync` writes its own `.v1.backup`. But that backup is **removed on V1→V2 success**. The full trace:

1. V1 source → `migrate_v1_to_v2_sync` writes `.v1.backup`, transforms file, removes `.v1.backup` on V1→V2 success.
2. `migrate_v2_to_v3_sync` runs against the now-V2 file. No backup.
3. `pre_v7_backup_path_for(V1, path)` returns `None` (V1 is excluded).
4. Destructive chain runs against the now-V3 file with **no backup**.
5. If split_graph or v6_to_v7_rename fails, the user has a partially-transformed file on disk and **no V1 original to recover from** — the `.v1.backup` was already cleaned up two steps ago.

The V1 case is structurally identical to the V2 case: in both, the per-step backup (or absence thereof) covers only one transition and is gone by the time the destructive chain runs.

### Why this matters

This is a pre-existing gap that both async and sync share. KAN-650 brought the sync path to parity with async, which means the gap is now consistently present in both rather than only in sync. The fix needs to live in the shared backup policy plus a coordinated change in both orchestrators.

Real-world likelihood: low. V1 and V2 files are old vintage. Most users have long since migrated. But a fresh checkout of an old branch, a backup tape restore, an old fork — these can all surface V1/V2 files in a 0.7.x environment.

## How

Two approaches:

### Option A (recommended): extend the backup policy to cover V1 AND V2

Change `pre_v7_backup_path_for`:

```rust
pub(crate) fn pre_v7_backup_path_for(from: FormatVersion, path: &Path) -> Option<PathBuf> {
    match from {
        FormatVersion::V1 => Some(path.with_extension("v1.backup")),
        FormatVersion::V2 => Some(path.with_extension("v2.backup")),
        FormatVersion::V3 => Some(path.with_extension("v3.backup")),
        FormatVersion::V4 => Some(path.with_extension("v4.backup")),
        FormatVersion::V5 => Some(path.with_extension("v5.backup")),
        FormatVersion::V6 => Some(path.with_extension("v6.backup")),
        _ => None,
    }
}
```

Then **move the backup creation in both orchestrators to fire BEFORE `migrate_v1_to_v2*` runs**, not after the per-step migrations. The full chain becomes:

```rust
// Sync orchestrator (post-fix)
let backup_path = crate::migration::pre_v7_backup_path_for(from, path);
if let Some(backup) = &backup_path {
    std::fs::copy(path, backup)?;  // captures original (V1, V2, V3, V4, V5, V6) state
}

let result = (|| -> PersistenceResult<Vec<u8>> {
    if from == FormatVersion::V1 { migrate_v1_to_v2_sync(path)?; }
    if from <= FormatVersion::V2 { migrate_v2_to_v3_sync(path)?; }
    run_split_and_rename_chain_sync(from, path)
})();

// ...cleanup logic unchanged
```

This creates one outer backup that covers the entire chain. The existing per-step `.v1.backup` mechanism inside `migrate_v1_to_v2_sync` becomes redundant for the chained-through case and should be removed to avoid double-backups. Two options:

- **(A1)** Remove the per-step backup from `migrate_v1_to_v2*` entirely. Cleaner. Breaks any caller that invokes `migrate_v1_to_v2` directly (if any exist; check the call graph).
- **(A2)** Keep the per-step backup but suppress it when called from the orchestrator (e.g., add a `skip_backup: bool` parameter). Less invasive but adds a parameter to a per-step function.

Recommend **(A1)** if `migrate_v1_to_v2*` has no direct callers outside the orchestrator (grep to verify before deciding).

### Option B: per-step backups for V2 too

Don't change the outer policy. Instead, give `migrate_v2_to_v3*` its own `.v2.backup` similar to V1→V2. Each per-step migration manages its own backup, with the same "remove on success" semantics.

This makes both V1 and V2 gaps disappear from the orchestrator's perspective. But it still leaves the asymmetric "remove on success" behavior: a V1→V7 chain still loses the V1 backup once V1→V2 succeeds. Each per-step protects only itself.

To make Option B truly equivalent in protection, you'd also need to NOT remove the per-step backup until the entire orchestrator returns Ok. That's effectively the outer wrap from Option A wearing per-step clothing.

### Recommendation

**Option A with A1.** Single outer backup covering the entire chain, with the per-step `.v1.backup` mechanism removed (assuming no external callers). Clean, one mental model, matches what the user expects.

## Offender examples

```
# V2 source — today
$ ls /tmp/board.*
/tmp/board.json    # was V2, now a partially-transformed V3 or V6 file
# No .v2.backup. No way back to the V2 original.

# V1 source — today
$ # Mid-chain failure scenario:
$ # 1. .v1.backup written by migrate_v1_to_v2
$ # 2. V1→V2 success, .v1.backup removed
$ # 3. V2→V3 success
$ # 4. split_graph fails
$ ls /tmp/board.*
/tmp/board.json    # now a partially-transformed V3 file
# Neither .v1.backup nor any other backup exists.
```

## Solution example

```
# After fix: V1 or V2 source with mid-chain failure
$ ls /tmp/board.*
/tmp/board.json        # broken partial migration
/tmp/board.v1.backup   # OR /tmp/board.v2.backup — original content, preserved
```

## Acceptance criteria

- `pre_v7_backup_path_for` returns `Some(path.v1.backup)` for V1 and `Some(path.v2.backup)` for V2 (in addition to existing V3/V4/V5/V6).
- Both orchestrators write the outer backup **before** any per-step migration runs (V1→V2, V2→V3, split_graph, v6_to_v7_rename).
- The per-step backup inside `migrate_v1_to_v2_sync` and `Migrator::migrate_v1_to_v2` is removed (assuming no external direct callers; verify by grep first).
- A test pins V1 → V7 success: backup is cleaned up after the full chain succeeds.
- A test pins V1 → V7 mid-chain failure (artificial poison after V2→V3 or during split_graph): `.v1.backup` is preserved.
- A test pins V2 → V7 success: backup is cleaned up.
- A test pins V2 → V7 failure: `.v2.backup` is preserved.
- The existing V3/V4/V5/V6 tests from KAN-650 continue to pass unchanged.
- Doc-comment on `pre_v7_backup_path_for` no longer claims "V1/V2 manage their own backups" or "V2 is shape-stable" — that reasoning was only ever true for the per-step transitions in isolation.

## Out of scope

- Adding fsync to the backup `copy` (covered by KAN-658).
- Restructuring the migration logging / report shape (covered by KAN-661).
card.title: V1/V2 → V7 migration runs destructive chain without backup (pre-existing async + sync gap)
Mirror .v{N}.backup writes in sync JSON migration path

# STATUS: in progress on branch KAN-655/add-negative-path-tests-for-card-create-assign

## Stakeholders

- **Future maintainers** of `card create --assign` and the equivalent MCP path — without negative tests, regressions in the error path land silently.
- **CLI users** who mistype a sprint name and need a meaningful error rather than a panic or successful-looking no-op.
- **MCP clients** — agents trying to learn the schema by trial-and-error need clean, descriptive errors that pattern-match cleanly.

## Where (current state, verified)

- `crates/kanban-service/tests/create_card_with_sprint.rs` — three happy-path tests (UUID-assigns, no-sprint-default, undo). No negative paths.
- `crates/kanban-domain/src/commands/card_commands.rs:258` — `context.get_sprint(sprint_id)?` returns `KanbanError::not_found("sprint", id)` for unknown UUID.
- `crates/kanban-domain/src/commands/card_commands.rs:259-264` — cross-board validation branch currently returns `KanbanError::validation(...)` with the message `"sprint {id} belongs to board {b} but card is being created on board {a}"`. **No structured variant** — message-only.
- `crates/kanban-cli/src/handlers/card.rs:23,315` — `--assign` wiring via `resolve_assign_sprint`, returns `Result<Option<Uuid>, String>` where the String is `KanbanError.to_string()`.
- `crates/kanban-mcp/src/lib.rs:1014-1040` — `tool_create_card` calls `mcp_resolve_sprint_in_board` then `create_card`. Errors flow through `kanban_err_to_mcp` to `McpError::invalid_params(d.to_string(), None)`.
- `crates/kanban-cli/tests/cli_integration.rs:1684-1713` (positive `--assign` test), `:1778-1800` (negative `--assign` with no value).
- `crates/kanban-mcp/tests/integration.rs` — no card-create-with-sprint tests; pattern is direct `McpContext` method calls (no tool-router invocation).

## Why

KAN-556 is a release-headline minor feature crossing TUI/CLI/MCP. Happy paths covered; every error branch untested. Specifically the cross-board validation at `card_commands.rs:259-264` has zero coverage and any refactor could silently break it.

## Scope

Two production changes plus six tests.

### Production change (small, in-scope)

**Promote the cross-board case to a typed error variant.** Today the branch returns `KanbanError::validation(format!(...))`, which can only be asserted on by message substring — brittle to wording. Add a new `DomainError::SprintBoardMismatch { sprint_id, sprint_board, card_board }` variant, return it from the cross-board branch, and assert structurally in the new tests.

This also fixes a latent inconsistency: every other not-found-style error in the domain is a typed variant; the cross-board check is the odd one out.

CLI/MCP error rendering is unaffected — both call `.to_string()` on the error, and the new variant's `Display` impl produces the same human-readable message as the current `format!`.

### Tests added

**Domain/service (extend `crates/kanban-service/tests/create_card_with_sprint.rs`):**

1. `test_create_card_with_unknown_sprint_uuid_returns_not_found`
   - Pass `CreateCardOptions { sprint_id: Some(Uuid::new_v4()), .. }` against a board with no such sprint.
   - Assert `matches!(err, KanbanError::Domain(DomainError::NotFound { entity: "sprint", .. }))` and `err.is_not_found()`.

2. `test_create_card_with_cross_board_sprint_returns_typed_error`
   - Two boards A and B, column on A, sprint on B.
   - Assert `matches!(err, KanbanError::Domain(DomainError::SprintBoardMismatch { .. }))`.
   - Also assert message contains "board" as a sanity check, but the variant is the load-bearing assertion.
   - Pins the production-code change above as well as the validation branch.

**CLI (extend `crates/kanban-cli/tests/cli_integration.rs` near existing `--assign` tests at line 1700):**

3. `test_card_create_with_assign_unknown_name_fails_with_useful_error`
   - `kanban card create --assign nonexistent ...`
   - `.failure()`, `.stderr(predicate::str::contains("sprint"))`, `.stderr(predicate::str::contains("nonexistent"))`.

4. `test_card_create_with_assign_unknown_uuid_fails_with_useful_error`
   - Same with a random UUID.
   - Same predicates on the UUID string.

**MCP (extend `crates/kanban-mcp/tests/integration.rs` following the existing direct-method-call pattern):**

5. `test_mcp_create_card_with_unknown_sprint_name_returns_error`
   - Direct call to `mcp_ctx.mcp_resolve_sprint_in_board("nonexistent", board.id)`.
   - Assert error message contains "sprint" and "nonexistent".

6. `test_mcp_create_card_with_cross_board_sprint_returns_typed_error`
   - Two boards, sprint on B, call create_card on A with sprint B's UUID.
   - Assert the surfaced error matches the `SprintBoardMismatch` variant via the structured error path.

## Out of scope (per discovery)

The card's original draft listed "ambiguous sprint name" and "sprint number lookup without board context" as missing coverage. Per `crates/kanban-domain/src/operations.rs:235-315`, those scenarios live in the **resolver** (`resolve_sprint_id_global`), not in the create-card command. `CreateCard::execute` only ever receives a UUID; name/number resolution happens upstream. Resolver-level negative coverage is a separate ticket if needed.

## How

Order of operations:

1. Add `DomainError::SprintBoardMismatch { sprint_id, sprint_board, card_board }` variant in `crates/kanban-domain/src/error.rs`. `Display` impl reproduces the existing message format.
2. Change `card_commands.rs:259-264` to return the new variant instead of `KanbanError::validation(...)`.
3. Write the six tests above. Per TDD note: these document existing behavior plus the new variant; tests should pass on first run.
4. Run focused test suites then full workspace.

## Testing / validation

- `cargo test -p kanban-domain` (new error variant)
- `cargo test -p kanban-service --test create_card_with_sprint`
- `cargo test -p kanban-cli --test cli_integration -- card_create_with_assign`
- `cargo test -p kanban-mcp --test integration -- create_card`
- `cargo test --workspace`
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` + `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `DomainError::SprintBoardMismatch` variant added with fields `{ sprint_id, sprint_board, card_board }`.
- [ ] `card_commands.rs` cross-board branch returns the new variant; message text preserved.
- [ ] `cargo tarpaulin -p kanban-domain --include-files 'src/commands/card_commands.rs'` shows the cross-board branch covered.
- [ ] All six tests added and passing.
- [ ] CLI tests invoke the real binary via `assert_cmd` and assert stderr contains both "sprint" and the offending name (UUID or string).
- [ ] MCP tests exercise the same code via the direct-method-call pattern used in `integration.rs`.
- [ ] No regressions in workspace test suite; fmt + clippy clean.
- [ ] Changeset added at `.changeset/kan-655-card-create-assign-negative-tests.md` with `bump: patch`. Description notes both the new error variant and the test additions.

# STATUS: implemented in PR #318 (in review)

Branch: `KAN-657/document-chocolatey-re-push-recovery-release-recovery-md`
PR: https://github.com/fulsomenko/kanban/pull/318
Commit: `5af99676`

Decision against earlier card draft: runbook lives at
`packaging/chocolatey/RECOVERY.md`, NOT `docs/release-recovery.md`. The
constraint being documented (no re-push of same id+version) is
chocolatey-specific. Top-level `docs/` does not exist in this repo;
creating it for a single chocolatey-specific runbook would be an odd
new pattern. Reconsider only if more publishers (e.g. winget) gain
similar quirks.

---

## What shipped

1. **`packaging/chocolatey/RECOVERY.md`** — 130-line runbook with:
   - Diagnosis flowchart keyed on what `community.chocolatey.org/packages/kanban/<VERSION>` shows
   - Four scenarios fully covered:
     - Push succeeded but workflow reported failure → do nothing, wait
     - Malformed nupkg → cut X.Y.Z+1
     - API key rejected → rotate, re-run
     - Moderation backlog → wait
   - Anti-patterns section (do not re-run after confirmed push; do not edit X.Y.Z in place; do not let runbook drift from workflow error message)
   - "Reading this in a hurry" quick-reference table

2. **`.github/workflows/release.yml`** — `choco push` step now:
   - Pre-checks `community.chocolatey.org/api/v2/Packages(Id='kanban',Version='X')` and exits 0 if 200 returned (already-published case → job safe to re-run)
   - Wraps the actual push in try/catch that on failure prints the runbook pointer + "do not simply re-run this job" warning

3. **`packaging/chocolatey/README.md`** — paragraph cross-linking RECOVERY.md.

## Pre-check honest limitation (documented in runbook)

Packages in `Submitted` or `Waiting for Reviewer` status are NOT
visible via the public v2 OData API. So the pre-check returning 404
does not prove the package is unpublished — it might be in the
moderation queue. The runbook tells operators to verify on
community.chocolatey.org/packages/kanban/<VERSION> before deciding to
"safely re-run".

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Recovery runbook exists, covers all four scenarios with actionable steps
- [x] Workflow `choco push` step prints recovery pointer on failure

card.description:
# STATUS: implemented in PR #317 (in review, branch in DOING)

Branch: `KAN-656/fix-chocolatey-artifact-poll-head-redirect-to-s3-returns-403`
PR: https://github.com/fulsomenko/kanban/pull/317
Commits:
- `90e9644c` — primary fix: collapse HEAD poll + download/hash into one `gh release view --json assets` call
- `c12b2fab` — review follow-ups: explicit `permissions: contents: read` + `2>$null` on `gh` stderr
- `97f90a57` — expand changeset to mention the follow-up changes

---

## Stakeholders

- **Release manager (Max)** — if the poll flakes, the Chocolatey job spuriously fails post-release.
- **Windows users** — slower or failed Chocolatey publish means the new version is unavailable on Windows for hours/days.

## Where

- `.github/workflows/release.yml:309-332` — (old) `publish-chocolatey` job's `Wait for release asset to be fetchable` step.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml:334-346` — (old) subsequent `Compute Windows ZIP SHA256` step that downloaded and hashed the asset.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml:309-340` — (new) single `Read Windows ZIP digest from GitHub Release` step.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml:304-305` — (new) `permissions: contents: read` on the `publish-chocolatey` job.

## Why (root cause)

The previous poll used `Invoke-WebRequest -Method Head` against the GitHub release-download URL. GitHub release-download URLs **302-redirect to S3-style presigned URLs** on `release-assets.githubusercontent.com`. PowerShell's `Invoke-WebRequest` auto-follows the redirect. The signed redirect target is **cryptographically signed for a specific HTTP method** — a URL signed for GET returns 403 on HEAD.

Well-documented S3 / presigned-URL behavior:

- AWS re:Post — [403 when accessing S3 signed HTTPS URL with Postman or Python](https://repost.aws/questions/QUXlm00GaUSd2GAWQfkVf47w/403-when-accessing-s3-signed-https-url-with-postman-or-python).
- Gitea #35086 — [HEAD requests to attachments always result in 403 Forbidden if using minio](https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/issues/35086).
- grab #43 — [Response from github is 403 when downloading a release file](https://github.com/cavaliergopher/grab/issues/43).

Result: the poll's HEAD would have chased the 302, hit 403, treated the asset as not-ready, and exhausted the 150s budget. Latent — this code path has not fired yet; 0.7.0 will be the first release that produces a Windows artifact.

## How (the 2026 approach)

`gh release view --json assets` returns a structured `state` field per asset, and since the [2025-06-03 changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2025-06-03-releases-now-expose-digests-for-release-assets/) it also exposes the SHA256 digest in the `digest` field. So both the readiness signal AND the checksum we needed to compute locally are right there in the API response.

Verified live against `cli/cli` v2.93.0:

```json
{
  "name": "gh_2.93.0_checksums.txt",
  "state": "uploaded",
  "digest": "sha256:f62a3bc9dedc88262c9c2b56eb653cb3ded6bde8076bdbb151f4cce9c8729da5",
  "size": 1950,
  ...
}
```

### Replacement step (shipped)

```yaml
- name: Read Windows ZIP digest from GitHub Release
  id: sha
  shell: pwsh
  env:
    VERSION: ${{ needs.release.outputs.new }}
    GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
  run: |
    $asset = "kanban-v$env:VERSION-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip"
    $ok = $false
    for ($i = 1; $i -le 30; $i++) {
      $json = gh release view "v$env:VERSION" --repo $env:REPO `
        --json assets --jq ".assets[] | select(.name == `"$asset`")" 2>$null
      if ($json) {
        $obj = $json | ConvertFrom-Json
        if ($obj.state -eq 'uploaded' -and $obj.digest) {
          $sha = $obj.digest -replace '^sha256:', ''
          Write-Output "Found $asset: sha=$sha"
          "sha=$sha" | Out-File -FilePath $env:GITHUB_OUTPUT -Append
          $ok = $true
          break
        }
        Write-Output ("Attempt {0}: state='{1}' digest='{2}'" -f $i, $obj.state, $obj.digest)
      } else {
        Write-Output ("Attempt {0}: asset not yet listed" -f $i)
      }
      Start-Sleep -Seconds 5
    }
    if (-not $ok) {
      Write-Error "Release asset never became ready after 30 attempts (~150s)"
      exit 1
    }
```

And on the job header:

```yaml
publish-chocolatey:
  name: Publish to Chocolatey
  needs: [release, build-windows]
  if: needs.release.outputs.has_changesets == 'true'
  runs-on: windows-latest
  permissions:
    contents: read    # explicit — protects against future org-default tightening
  steps:
    ...
```

### Why this is the *proper* 2026 way

- **Authoritative source for the digest**: GitHub generates and stores it server-side at upload time.
- **Method-agnostic**: GitHub REST API via `gh`, no signed-URL HEAD/GET asymmetry.
- **Single round-trip per poll** instead of HEAD → 302 → S3 403 → retry.
- **Pre-existing `gh` auth**: uses `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` already in scope on the runner; no separate credential.
- **`state == "uploaded"` AND non-empty `digest`** are both required — handles the brief window where an asset is committed to the Release but the digest hasn't been populated yet.
- **Explicit permissions scope**: `contents: read` on the job protects against future org-level token-default tightening silently breaking the lookup.
- **Suppressed stderr (`2>$null`) on the per-iteration call**: keeps the action log clean while the release tag is still being created upstream (no scary red error text on iterations 1-2 before the tag exists).
- **Single source of truth**: the digest the chocolatey package verifies against is the same digest GitHub serves to other clients.

## Offender example (real-world reproduction)

```
$ curl -I "https://github.com/.../releases/download/v0.7.0/kanban-v0.7.0-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip"
HTTP/2 302
location: https://release-assets.githubusercontent.com/...?X-Amz-Signature=...

$ curl -I "https://release-assets.githubusercontent.com/...?X-Amz-Signature=..."
HTTP/2 403   # signed for GET, not HEAD

$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" "https://release-assets..."
200          # GET works fine on the same URL
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The `publish-chocolatey` job no longer issues HEAD requests against `releases/download/...`.
- [x] The asset readiness check uses `gh release view --json assets` and reads `state`.
- [x] The SHA256 used to template `$checksum64$` in the chocolatey nuspec is read from the `digest` field, not computed locally.
- [x] The `Compute Windows ZIP SHA256` step is removed (merged into the readiness step).
- [x] Explicit `permissions: contents: read` on the job.
- [x] `2>$null` suppression on the per-iteration `gh` call to keep logs clean.
- [x] `yamllint` clean.
- [x] Downstream step (`Stage Chocolatey package with substitutions`) reads `${{ steps.sha.outputs.sha }}` unchanged.
- [ ] Real-run validation deferred to the first 0.7.x release with Windows artifacts.

## References

- GitHub Changelog: [Releases now expose digests for release assets (2025-06-03)](https://github.blog/changelog/2025-06-03-releases-now-expose-digests-for-release-assets/)
- [gh release view manual](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_release_view)
- [REST API endpoints for release assets](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/releases/assets)
- [Gitea #35086](https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/issues/35086), [grab #43](https://github.com/cavaliergopher/grab/issues/43), [AWS re:Post on signed-URL HEAD/GET asymmetry](https://repost.aws/questions/QUXlm00GaUSd2GAWQfkVf47w/403-when-accessing-s3-signed-https-url-with-postman-or-python).
card.title: Fix Chocolatey artifact poll: HEAD redirect to S3 returns 403

# SUPERSEDED (2026-06-30) — see KAN-803 finding. NOT building.
Old Phase A (whole-snapshot SQLite parity). Premise disproven: SQLite write-through merges per-row; no whole-snapshot clobber on the live path.

---
Phase A of KAN-803. Bring SQLite to parity with JSONs existing optimistic-concurrency apparatus so concurrent TUI/CLI/MCP writes never silently lose data. REUSE the existing ConflictResolver + the two TUI dialogs; do NOT build new UX. Mechanism: saved_at compare-and-swap in SqliteStore::save (atomic in the write tx) -> ConflictDetected; poll-based ChangeDetector for SQLite emitting the same ChangeEvent the FileWatcher does. Children are PR-sized, TDD. This sub-epic is THIS sprint. See KAN-803 for the full grounded design + decisions.
card.title: feat(persistence): Phase A — SQLite optimistic-detection parity

card.description:
# SUPERSEDED (2026-06-30) — see KAN-803 finding. NOT building.
saved_at/version whole-snapshot CAS. Guarded PersistenceStore::save, which the SQLite app NEVER calls (it persists via flush=stamp_writer). Wrong mechanism + wrong method. Built green on branch KAN-806/sqlite-save-cas; superseded. Real gap is per-row OCC (new card).

---
Context: Phase A of KAN-803 / KAN-804. The core fix for SQLite silent data loss.

Current state:
- `SqliteStore::save` (crates/kanban-persistence-sqlite/src/sqlite_store/persistence_store.rs:12-40) applies the full snapshot then `stamp_writer()` updates `saved_at` (metadata.rs:43-55) with NO pre-check → last-writer-wins.
- `apply_snapshot_async` (snapshot.rs:24-96) already wraps the write in one tx (begin/commit). Metadata row has `saved_at TEXT` (schema.sql:9).
- Contrast JSON: `JsonFileStore::save` (json_file_store.rs:285-301) returns `PersistenceError::ConflictDetected { path, source }` (error.rs:20) when its last-known metadata != on-disk.

Target:
- The store tracks the last-known `saved_at` it observed (open + each successful load/save) e.g. `Mutex<Option<DateTime<Utc>>>` on `SqliteStore`.
- In `save`, INSIDE the existing tx, do an atomic CAS: `UPDATE metadata SET saved_at=?, ... WHERE id=1 AND saved_at=<expected>`. If `rows_affected()==0` → roll back the tx and return `ConflictDetected { path, source: None }`. On success, advance the tracked last-known to the new `saved_at`.
- First-write / fresh-open case: expected = the value read at open (or a sentinel) so a legitimate first save passes.

Step-by-step (TDD):
1. Red: `test_save_with_stale_saved_at_returns_conflict` — handle A saves; handle B (same path) loads+saves; A saves again → `ConflictDetected`, and A's data is NOT applied (B's snapshot still on disk).
2. Red: `test_save_advances_last_known_so_consecutive_saves_succeed` — same handle saves twice in a row → both Ok (own writes never self-conflict).
3. Green: add last-known tracking + CAS in the tx.
4. Refactor.

Tests (name → asserts): the two above + `test_first_save_on_fresh_db_succeeds`.
Acceptance: stale concurrent save → ConflictDetected (no clobber); consecutive own saves succeed; tx rolls back on conflict; clippy -D warnings + fmt green.
Dependencies: none (foundation for A2–A5). After this lands, the KAN-769 stale→conflict contract case (omitted in PR #353) passes → finished in A5.

## Phase 3/4 verified enrichment (2026-06-27)
All refs verified ACCURATE. Key implementation detail surfaced by the gauntlet:
- ATOMICITY: today `stamp_writer()` (metadata.rs:43-55) runs AFTER `apply_snapshot_async` COMMITS — two separate txs. The CAS must be in the SAME tx as the snapshot apply. Fold the metadata UPDATE into the snapshot tx (e.g. a new `apply_snapshot_and_stamp_async(snapshot, expected_saved_at)`), do the CAS there, roll back the whole tx on conflict.
- Field: add `last_known_saved_at: std::sync::Mutex<Option<DateTime<Utc>>>` to `SqliteStore` (alongside `instance_id`); init at `open()` by reading the metadata `saved_at`; advance it on every successful save AND load.
- CAS: `UPDATE metadata SET saved_at=?, writer_version=?, writer_commit=? WHERE id=1 AND saved_at=<expected>`; `rows_affected()==0` (with Some(expected)) → `tx.rollback()` + return `PersistenceError::ConflictDetected { path, source: None }`. First-write / fresh-open (expected=None) → unconditional UPDATE branch (no WHERE saved_at).
- Tests feasible: existing tests open multiple `SqliteStore::open(&path)` handles on one TempDir path (each gets its own pool + last-known). RED until this lands.

## Execution learnings (VALIDATED — spike 2026-06-28)
- DISCRIMINATOR CHANGE (critical): do NOT CAS on `saved_at`. Wall-clock is not guaranteed monotonic or high-resolution; the spike demonstrated a real lost-update hole (`probe_equal_saved_at_lets_stale_save_clobber`): two saves sharing a `saved_at` string (coarse clock / NTP step) let a later stale save clobber silently with no error. Use a monotonic `version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` on the metadata row as the discriminator (validated collision-proof by `probe_version_integer_cas_is_collision_proof`).
  - Migration: bump SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION 2→3; additive `ALTER TABLE metadata ADD COLUMN version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` in migrate() (mirror the existing writer_version/writer_commit ALTER block in init.rs).
  - CAS becomes: `UPDATE metadata SET version = version + 1, saved_at = ?, writer_version = ?, writer_commit = ? WHERE id = 1 AND version = ?`. rows_affected()==0 (with Some(expected_version)) → rollback tx + ConflictDetected. Fresh open (expected=None) → unconditional branch.
  - Track `last_known_version: Arc<Mutex<Option<i64>>>` (NOT saved_at). Keep `saved_at` purely as a human-facing "last saved" timestamp.
- FIELD TYPE: must be `Arc<Mutex<...>>`, not bare `Mutex` — KAN-807's poller shares the same baseline. Expose a `pub(crate)` accessor returning the Arc.
- ATOMICITY/WAL: validated. CAS rides inside the snapshot tx; on conflict the whole tx (data + version stamp) rolls back, B's data survives, WAL stays clean, a fresh handle works after (`probe_db_usable_after_conflict_rollback`). `checkpoint()` correctly stays AFTER commit (a conflict returns before checkpoint).
- SCOPE GAP (decide): the conflict guard only covers the async `PersistenceStore::save`. The SYNC `DataStore` save path (data_store.rs:484 → apply_snapshot_async) has NO guard. Decide whether it needs one or whether all writes funnel through `PersistenceStore::save`.
- make_rt() provides a multi-threaded runtime — no current_thread friction (probe #3).
card.title: feat(persistence-sqlite): saved_at compare-and-swap in save → ConflictDetected

card.description:
# SUPERSEDED (2026-06-30) — see KAN-803 finding. NOT building.
poll-based ChangeDetector for whole-snapshot conflicts — moot; SQLite has no whole-snapshot conflict.

---
Context: Phase A of KAN-803 / KAN-804. SQLite has no external-change detection; a long-lived TUI never learns CLI/MCP wrote.

Current state:
- `ChangeDetector` trait + `FileWatcher` (notify) (kanban-persistence/src/watch/file_watcher.rs) broadcast `ChangeEvent`; own-write suppressed via a counter set before atomic rename.
- This watches the JSON FILE only. notify on a SQLite `.db`/WAL is unreliable (WAL writes don't map cleanly to file-content events).

Target:
- A `SqlitePoller` (impl `ChangeDetector`) that, on the TUI tick interval, reads `saved_at` from the metadata row and emits the SAME `ChangeEvent` the FileWatcher does when it advances past the last value THIS handle wrote.
- Own-write suppression: compare against the store's tracked last-known `saved_at` (from A1) so your own save never fires the event.
- Same broadcast/subscribe shape as FileWatcher so the TUI consumes it unchanged.

Step-by-step (TDD):
1. Red: `test_poller_emits_change_event_when_external_writer_advances_saved_at`.
2. Red: `test_poller_suppresses_own_write` (advance via this handle → no event).
3. Green: implement poll + compare + emit.
4. Refactor.

Tests: the two above + `test_poller_no_event_when_saved_at_unchanged`.
Acceptance: external write → exactly one ChangeEvent; own write → none; clippy/fmt green.
Dependencies: A1 (uses the tracked last-known saved_at).

## Phase 3/4 verified enrichment (2026-06-27)
Refs ACCURATE (ChangeDetector trait + `ChangeEvent { path, detected_at }` at kanban-persistence/src/traits.rs:125-147; FileWatcher broadcast::channel(10)).
- New file crates/kanban-persistence/src/watch/sqlite_poller.rs: `SqlitePoller` impl `ChangeDetector`, reusing the SAME `broadcast::channel(10)` + `ChangeEvent` so the TUI consumes it unchanged.
- DRIVE: poll on the TUI tick (16ms, kanban-tui/src/events.rs:33) — do NOT self-spawn a tokio task like FileWatcher. `poll()` reads `saved_at`; if it advanced past the handle's last-known (KAN-806), broadcast a `ChangeEvent`.
- OWN-WRITE suppression is implicit: SqliteStore advances last-known on its own save, so the next poll sees `current == last_known` → no event (no separate counter needed, unlike FileWatcher).
- PERF refinement: reuse the store's existing pool for the `SELECT saved_at` rather than opening a fresh read-only connection every tick.
- Tests: test_poller_emits_change_event_when_external_writer_advances_saved_at / _suppresses_own_write / _no_event_when_unchanged.

## Execution learnings (VALIDATED — spike 2026-06-28)
- PLACEMENT CORRECTION: the poller CANNOT live in `crates/kanban-persistence/src/watch/` — `kanban-persistence` has no sqlx/sqlite dep and `kanban-persistence-sqlite` depends ON it (one-directional). It lives at `crates/kanban-persistence-sqlite/src/sqlite_poller.rs`, implementing the `ChangeDetector` trait imported from `kanban-persistence`. Forced by the dependency graph, not a choice.
- TWO CURSORS (card implied one): the poller needs BOTH (a) the shared store baseline `last_known_version` (own-write suppression — never mutated by the poller) AND (b) a poller-local `last_emitted` cursor to de-dupe a static external value (else a single external write re-fires a ChangeEvent every 16ms tick).
- DISCRIMINATOR: with KAN-806 now using a monotonic `version` integer, the poller compares `version > last_emitted` (monotonic, NTP-step-proof) instead of comparing timestamps. This fixes a poller bug too: a backwards NTP step on a wall-clock would have made a real external write look "earlier" and be missed.
- POOL REUSE: build via `SqlitePoller::from_store(&store)` sharing `store.pool().clone()`; do NOT open a new connection per tick (probe #5 — clean, needs only a pub(crate) accessor for the shared Arc).
- `store.path()` is a `PersistenceStore` TRAIT method, not inherent — use the `pub(crate) path` field directly or add an inherent accessor.
card.title: feat(persistence-sqlite): poll-based ChangeDetector emitting ChangeEvent

card.description:
# SUPERSEDED (2026-06-30) — see KAN-803 finding. NOT building.
SQLite backend whole-snapshot conflict wiring — moot (see KAN-803 finding).

---
Context: Phase A of KAN-803 / KAN-804. Wire A1/A2 through the service backend.

Current state:
- `backend.reload()` (kanban-service/src/backend.rs:34) default no-op; JSON overrides to discard cache (json_backend.rs:335). SQLite backend (sqlite_backend.rs) has NO reload override — it is write-through (live queries, no cache), so reload is presently meaningless.
- SqliteBackend save path must propagate the new `ConflictDetected` from A1 up to the service/TUI unchanged (same KanbanError mapping JSON uses; error_mapping.rs).

Target:
- SqliteBackend save returns the propagated `ConflictDetected` so callers get the same error type as JSON.
- Provide/own the `SqlitePoller` (A2) lifecycle on the SQLite backend and expose its subscription like JSON exposes the FileWatcher, so the TUI can subscribe uniformly.
- `reload()` for SQLite: re-read authoritative `saved_at` + drop any cached derived state; align semantics with JSON so the TUI's reload path is backend-agnostic.

Step-by-step (TDD): red tests for (a) SqliteBackend save propagates ConflictDetected, (b) reload refreshes last-known saved_at → a subsequent save succeeds; green; refactor.
Tests: `test_sqlite_backend_save_propagates_conflict`, `test_sqlite_backend_reload_refreshes_then_save_succeeds`.
Acceptance: parity with JSON backend at the service boundary (same error, subscribe, reload contract); clippy/fmt green.
Dependencies: A1, A2.

## Phase 3/4 verified enrichment (2026-06-27)
Refs ACCURATE. `ConflictDetected` ALREADY propagates typed across the boundary (json_backend maps via `KanbanError::from`, error_mapping.rs maps to ErrorCode::ConflictDetected) — SQLite inherits this once KAN-806 raises it; no stringification.
- KEY unifying design (shared with KAN-809): add to the `KanbanBackend` trait a `fn change_subscription(&self) -> Option<broadcast::Receiver<kanban_persistence::ChangeEvent>>` defaulting to `None`. JSON returns its FileWatcher `subscribe()`; SQLite returns its `SqlitePoller` `subscribe()`. This is what makes the TUI backend-agnostic.
- SqliteBackend owns the `Arc<SqlitePoller>` (KAN-807) lifecycle (create + start_watching in `open()`), and exposes `change_subscription()`.
- `reload()` for write-through SQLite: re-read authoritative `saved_at` into the store's last-known (and `last_metadata`); no cache to clear. Mirrors JSON's reload contract so the TUI reload path is backend-agnostic.
- Tests: test_sqlite_backend_save_propagates_conflict, test_sqlite_backend_reload_refreshes_then_save_succeeds.
card.title: feat(service): SQLite backend surfaces ConflictDetected and reload re-reads

card.description:
# SUPERSEDED (2026-06-30) — see KAN-803 finding. NOT building.
TUI wiring for SQLite whole-snapshot conflict dialog — moot; SQLite conflict is per-row, JSON owns the whole-snapshot dialog (KAN-812).

---
Context: Phase A of KAN-803 / KAN-804. The TUI resolution UX already exists; just feed SQLite into it.

Current state:
- TUI subscribes to the FileWatcher and on a change opens `render_external_change_detected_popup` (Reload/Keep, conflict_popup.rs:67) or, on a save conflict, `render_conflict_resolution_popup` (Overwrite/Take-theirs/Retry, conflict_popup.rs:12). Wiring at main_loop.rs:44-88,282-321; handlers dialog_handlers.rs:458-499.
- These fire only for JSON file-change events today.

Target:
- Subscribe to the SQLite backend's `SqlitePoller` (A3) the same way the JSON FileWatcher is subscribed, so the SAME two dialogs fire when another process writes the `.db`.
- No new dialog/UX; reuse ConflictResolver. Make the main-loop change/conflict branch backend-agnostic.

Step-by-step (TDD): red characterization tests simulating an external SQLite write → ExternalChangeDetected dialog opens; a stale save → ConflictResolution dialog opens; green wiring; refactor.
Tests: `test_external_sqlite_write_opens_external_change_dialog`, `test_sqlite_stale_save_opens_conflict_resolution_dialog`, `test_take_theirs_reloads_sqlite`.
Acceptance: identical conflict/reload UX on SQLite and JSON; clippy/fmt green.
Dependencies: A3.

## Phase 3/4 verified enrichment (2026-06-27)
Refs ACCURATE and GOOD NEWS: the main-loop SELECT branch (main_loop.rs:282-321) is ALREADY backend-agnostic — it polls a generic `broadcast::Receiver<ChangeEvent>` and routes to the ExternalChangeDetected / ConflictResolution dialogs with no mention of FileWatcher/JSON. The save-worker conflict path (lifecycle.rs:186-191) already opens the dialog on `KanbanError::ConflictDetected`.
- ONLY change point: the INIT wiring (main_loop.rs:44-88) hardcodes `FileWatcher::new()`. Replace with `self.ctx.backend().change_subscription()` (the trait method from KAN-808) → store the returned `rx` in `self.persistence.file_change_rx`. JSON-specific `start_watching` stays guarded behind `if let Some(watcher)`.
- NO new dialog/UX; reuse the two existing popups + handlers (dialog_handlers.rs:458-499) + ConflictResolver.
- Tests: new crates/kanban-tui/tests/sqlite_change_detection_tests.rs modeled on existing conflict_detection_tests.rs / conflict_popup_tests.rs: test_external_sqlite_write_opens_external_change_dialog, test_sqlite_stale_save_opens_conflict_resolution_dialog, test_take_theirs_reloads_sqlite.

card.description:
# SUPERSEDED (2026-06-30) — see KAN-803 finding. NOT building.
contract-parity test for the whole-snapshot SQLite save CAS — moot.

---
Context: Phase A of KAN-803 / KAN-804. Closes the KAN-769/PR #353 finding.

Current state:
- PR #353 added portable contract-parity cases to crates/kanban-persistence-sqlite/src/sqlite_store/tests/persistence_store.rs but DELIBERATELY omitted `save_with_stale_metadata_returns_conflict` because SQLite had no conflict detection. A1 adds it.
- JSON runs the shared `kanban_persistence::store_contract_tests!` macro (tests/contract.rs); SQLite can't (async sqlx vs sync StoreFactory) so cases are bespoke in the rt.block_on style.

Target:
- Add `test_sqlitestore_save_with_stale_metadata_returns_conflict` mirroring the shared helper (kanban-persistence/src/test_helpers/contract.rs:98): handle A saves; handle B loads+saves; A saves → assert `PersistenceError::ConflictDetected`.

Investigation for GitHub issue #358 "Projects random order".

## Symptom
The projects/boards list reshuffles on every launch.

## Root cause
`snapshot_impl` in crates/kanban-domain/src/in_memory_store/snapshot.rs ordered boards with `sort_by_key(|b| b.position)`. Legacy boards default to `position = 0`, so all ties collapsed to a single sort key and fell back to non-deterministic `HashMap` iteration order.

## Affected code
- File: crates/kanban-domain/src/in_memory_store/snapshot.rs
- Function: `snapshot_impl` (board sort)

## Fix direction
Sort by the composite key `(position, created_at, id)` so ties resolve deterministically. Fixed in PR #371.

cards.description:
## Problem

TUI can update all fields on BoardUpdate (10), CardUpdate (11), and SprintUpdate (7), but CLI and MCP can only update a subset:

- **BoardUpdate**: 4/10 fields exposed (missing: task_sort_field, task_sort_order, sprint_duration_days, task_list_view, active_sprint_id, completion_column_id)
- **CardUpdate**: 6/11 fields exposed (missing: position, column_id, sprint_id, assigned_prefix, card_prefix)
- **SprintUpdate**: 5/7 fields exposed (missing: name_index, status)

Some missing fields have dedicated methods (move_card, assign_card_to_sprint, activate/complete/cancel_sprint), so those are intentional. But `assigned_prefix`, `card_prefix` on cards and all the board settings have NO way to be set outside TUI.

## Root Cause

Architectural asymmetry:

1. **TUI** (`tui_context.rs`) operates directly on in-memory Rust structs. It constructs full `CardUpdate`/`BoardUpdate`/`SprintUpdate` structs and passes them to the command executor. No serialization boundary.

2. **CLI** (`cli.rs` + handlers) parses command-line arguments via clap, then constructs the update structs from those args. If no clap flag exists for a field, it's unreachable.

3. **MCP** (`context.rs`) builds CLI argument vectors and shells out to the kanban binary, parsing JSON responses. It inherits all CLI limitations.

The domain layer supports all fields. The bottleneck is entirely in CLI argument definitions.

## Why This Happened

The KanbanOperations trait enforces method parity (all 37 operations exist everywhere), but it doesn't enforce field-level completeness within those methods. The trait signature is:

```rust
fn update_card(&mut self, id: Uuid, updates: CardUpdate) -> Result<Card>;
```

Both TUI and CLI implement this, but TUI populates all CardUpdate fields while CLI only populates fields that have corresponding clap arguments.

## Solution Options

### Option A: Add missing CLI flags
Add clap arguments for all missing fields in the update commands. Straightforward but expands CLI surface area significantly.

Files to modify:
- `crates/kanban-cli/src/cli.rs` - Add clap args
- `crates/kanban-cli/src/handlers/card.rs` - Wire args to CardUpdate
- `crates/kanban-cli/src/handlers/board.rs` - Wire args to BoardUpdate
- MCP would automatically get parity since it delegates to CLI

### Option B: Direct domain access for MCP
Have MCP implement KanbanOperations by directly manipulating the data file (like TUI does) instead of shelling out to CLI. This would give MCP full field access without CLI changes.

Downside: Duplicates file I/O logic that currently lives in CLI.

### Option C: Extract shared library
Factor out the file I/O and state management into a shared library that both TUI and a new "direct" MCP implementation can use. CLI remains a thin wrapper.

This is the cleanest long-term but highest effort.

## Recommendation

Option A is pragmatic for now. The missing fields are:
- Card: `assigned_prefix`, `card_prefix` (2 fields)
- Board: `task_sort_field`, `task_sort_order`, `sprint_duration_days`, `task_list_view`, `active_sprint_id`, `completion_column_id` (6 fields)

Card prefixes are useful for CLI users. Board settings are more TUI-specific but could still be exposed.

## Files Reference

- Trait: `crates/kanban-domain/src/operations.rs:19-89`
- TUI impl: `crates/kanban-tui/src/tui_context.rs:92-571`
- CLI impl: `crates/kanban-cli/src/context.rs:172-685`
- MCP impl: `crates/kanban-mcp/src/context.rs:121-554`
- CLI args: `crates/kanban-cli/src/cli.rs`

Investigation for GitHub issue #360 "Tasks priority change from list".

## Symptom
Pressing `p` in the card list does nothing, even though the list advertises `p: priority`.

## Root cause
The `card_list` `p` binding pointed at `KeybindingAction::EditCard`, and the Normal-mode input router had no lowercase `p` arm, so the keypress was routed to nothing actionable for setting priority.

## Affected code
- kanban-tui keybinding table: `card_list` `p` binding
- kanban-tui Normal-mode input router (no lowercase `p` arm)

## Fix direction
Add a dedicated `SetCardPriority` action + `handle_set_card_priority_key` handler + router arm gated to the cards panel, and repoint the `card_list` `p` binding at it. Fixed in PR #372.

Deep-dive audit across architecture, code reuse, abstractions, test structure, file sizes, functional composition, and overall quality. Prioritized by velocity impact (what unlocks faster development first).

## Priority 1 — App God Object
**File**: `crates/kanban-tui/src/app.rs` (2,060 lines)
**Velocity Impact**: Critical — every feature touches this file, causing constant merge conflicts

The `App` struct has 58 public fields and 37+ methods spanning: UI state, dialog modes, selection tracking, animation, search, filters, sorting, relationships, sprint assignment, file watching, and save workers. All handler files are just `impl App` extensions.

`DialogMode` has 20+ variants. Each requires: an enum entry, a match arm in `handle_key_event()`, a render function in `ui.rs`, and a handler somewhere across 3 handler files.

**Fix**: Create a `DialogState` trait. Each dialog becomes a self-contained struct. Adding a dialog = creating one file.

## Priority 3 — Keybinding System
**Files**: `app.rs:336–730`, `keybindings/registry.rs`, `keybindings/*.rs`

`KeybindingRegistry` exists and generates help text but is NOT used for event routing. Actual dispatch happens in a giant raw match in `handle_key_event()` (lines 536–730).

**Fix**: Make the registry the single source of truth. Route events through it. Makes keybindings user-configurable.

**Effort**: 2–3 days

[x] 2026-04-06 22:53:34

Contains all render functions for every view, every dialog, panels, footer, help overlay. 20+ dialog render functions all live here.

**Velocity Impact**: High — same `KanbanOperations` impl copy-pasted 3 times; every domain change requires 3 edits

All three contexts implement `KanbanOperations` with nearly identical logic. `JsonFileStore` used directly in all three.

**Fix**: Extract shared `BaseContext` into `kanban-domain` or a new `kanban-context` crate.

## Priority 6 — Test Structure (Shadow `tests/` Directories)
**Velocity Impact**: Medium — hard to find, run, or scope tests; no isolated domain command tests

`kanban-core`, `kanban-domain`, `kanban-persistence` all use inline `#[cfg(test)]`. `mockall` is in workspace but not used with `#[automock]`. Domain command files (`board_commands.rs`, `card_commands.rs`, etc.) have zero isolated unit tests.

**Fix**: Move inline tests to `tests/` directories mirroring `src/`. Add `#[automock]` to persistence traits.

## Priority 7 — Handler Reorganization
**Files**: `crates/kanban-tui/src/handlers/` (4,979 lines across 6 files)
**Velocity Impact**: Medium — unclear where to add new behavior; handlers too long to scan

- `detail_view_handlers.rs`: 3 functions, 1,056 lines (one fn is 280+ lines)
- `count_headers_in_viewport()` duplicated between `navigation_handlers.rs:24` and `render_strategy.rs:17`
- Column move-up/move-down are 90% identical (~90 lines duplicate logic)
- Dialog match arm pattern repeated 8 times across handler files

**Fix**: Reorganize by domain concern. Extract HOF for repeated dialog pattern. Deduplicate viewport helper.

## Priority 8 — Domain Model Sizes
**Files**: `board.rs` (918L), `card.rs` (728L), `card_lifecycle.rs` (600L), `card_graph.rs` (636L)
**Velocity Impact**: Medium — violates 300-line guideline 2–3x; slow to navigate

**Effort**: 1–2 days

---

## Priority 9 — Type Safety via Newtypes
**Files**: All `type XxxId = Uuid` declarations in domain models
**Velocity Impact**: Medium — current aliases allow silently swapping IDs; bugs are slow to find

`type BoardId = Uuid`, `type CardId = Uuid` etc. mean a fn taking `(card_id: Uuid, column_id: Uuid)` will compile fine if you swap the args.

**Fix**: Convert to newtypes: `pub struct CardId(Uuid)`. Zero runtime cost.

**Effort**: 1–2 days

**File**: `kanban-core/src/traits.rs` lines 5–20
**Velocity Impact**: Low — but causes confusion

`Repository<T, Id>` and `Service<T, Id>` traits are defined but never implemented anywhere. CLAUDE.md references a `kanban-db` crate that doesn't exist.

**Fix**: Delete unused traits, update CLAUDE.md to reflect actual architecture.

**Effort**: 0.5 days

Codebase Quality Audit — Prioritized Findings

Scoring Key

- Velocity Impact: How much faster will the team move after this refactor?
- Effort: Low / Medium / High (in dev-days)

---
Priority 1 — App God Object

Files: crates/kanban-tui/src/app.rs (2,060 lines)
Velocity Impact: 🔴 Critical — every feature touches this file, causing constant merge conflicts and context overload

The App struct has 58 public fields and 37+ methods spanning: UI state, dialog modes, selection tracking, animation, search, filters,
sorting, relationships, sprint assignment, file watching, and save workers. All handler files (card_handlers.rs, navigation_handlers.rs,
etc.) are just impl App extensions that mutate any of these fields freely.

What to do: Split into focused sub-structs:
```sh
ModalState        { mode, mode_stack }
SelectionState    { board_selection, card_focus, board_focus, focus }
FilterState       { active_sprint_filters, hide_assigned, sort_field, sort_order }
MultiSelectState  { selected_cards, selection_mode_active, sprint_assign_selection }
AnimationState    { animating_cards }
RelationshipState { relationship_card_ids, parents_list, children_list }
DialogState       { input, priority_selection, column_selection, import_files }
```

Effort: 4–6 days | Payoff: Every handler/render file becomes independently navigable. New contributors can own one sub-struct without
reading all 2,060 lines.

---
Priority 2 — Dialog System Consolidation

Files: handlers/dialog_handlers.rs, handlers/popup_handlers.rs, app.rs, ui.rs, DialogMode enum
Velocity Impact: 🔴 Critical — adding one new dialog currently requires touching 4+ files in 4 different places

DialogMode has 20+ variants. Each one requires: an enum entry, a match arm in handle_key_event(), a render function in ui.rs, and a
handler somewhere across 3 handler files. There is no single place to add a dialog.

What to do: Create a DialogState trait:

```rust
pub trait DialogState: Send {
    fn handle_key(&mut self, key: KeyEvent) -> DialogResult;
    fn render(&self, frame: &mut Frame, area: Rect);
}
```

Each dialog becomes a self-contained struct. Adding a dialog = creating one file.

Effort: 3–4 days | Payoff: Dialogs become plug-and-play. Directly reduces the cost of new features.

---
Priority 3 — Keybinding System

Files: `app.rs:336–730`, `keybindings/registry.rs`, `keybindings/*.rs`
Velocity Impact: 🟠 High — keybindings are hardcoded in two places; adding/changing a binding is risky

The `KeybindingRegistry` exists and generates help text — but is not used for event routing. Actual dispatch happens in a giant raw match in
 `handle_key_event()` (lines 536–730). Key detection uses a fragile string-parsing approach (`keycode_matches_binding_key()`, lines 336–391).

What to do: Make the registry the single source of truth. Route events through it. This also makes keybindings configurable by users.

Effort: 2–3 days | Payoff: Changing or adding keybindings goes from risky multi-file surgery to a one-liner data change.

---
Priority 4 — `ui.rs` Rendering Monolith Split

Files: `crates/kanban-tui/src/ui.rs` (1,792 lines)
Velocity Impact: 🟠 High — all render work lands in one file; unrelated UI changes conflict constantly

Contains all render functions for every view, every dialog, panels, footer, help overlay. 20+ dialog render functions all live here.

What to do:

```sh
ui/
├── mod.rs          (entry point only)
├── views/
│   ├── main.rs
│   ├── card_detail.rs
│   ├── board_detail.rs
│   └── sprint_detail.rs
├── dialogs/        (one file per DialogMode)
├── footer.rs
├── help.rs
└── banner.rs
```

Effort: 2–3 days (mostly mechanical file splitting) | Payoff: Parallel UI work without conflicts. Each dialog/view is independently
editable.

---
Priority 5 — Context Triplication

Files: kanban-tui/src/tui_context.rs (583 lines), kanban-cli/src/context.rs (697 lines), kanban-mcp/src/context.rs (688 lines)
Velocity Impact: 🟠 High — same KanbanOperations impl copy-pasted 3 times; every domain operation change requires 3 edits

All three contexts implement KanbanOperations with nearly identical logic but divergent concrete types (JsonFileStore used directly in all
 three).

What to do: Extract a shared BaseContext (or KanbanContextImpl) into kanban-domain or a new kanban-context crate. Let each consumer
specialize only what differs (persistence transport, output format).

Effort: 3–4 days | Payoff: Domain-level operation changes propagate automatically to CLI, TUI, and MCP.

---
Priority 6 — Test Structure (Shadow tests/ Directories)

Velocity Impact: 🟡 Medium — currently hard to find, run, or scope tests

What exists:
- `kanban-tui/tests/` — 6 integration test files (good)
- `kanban-cli/tests/` — 1 large integration test file (good)
- `kanban-mcp/tests/` — 1 integration test file (good)
- `kanban-core`, `kanban-domain`, `kanban-persistence` — all tests are inline (`#[cfg(test)]` at bottom of each .rs file)

What's missing: Unit tests for kanban-domain commands (board_commands.rs, card_commands.rs, column_commands.rs, sprint_commands.rs — zero
isolated tests). mockall is in the workspace but not used with #[automock].

What to do: Move domain + persistence inline tests to tests/ directories mirroring src/. Add #[automock] to persistence traits so TUI/CLI
can be tested with in-memory stores.

Effort: 2–3 days | Payoff: Faster test discovery, ability to run domain tests in isolation, unblocks testing handlers without full
persistence setup.

---
Priority 7 — Handler Reorganization

Files: `crates/kanban-tui/src/handlers/` (4,979 lines total across 6 files)
Velocity Impact: 🟡 Medium — unclear where to add new behavior; handlers too long to scan

Problems:
- `detail_view_handlers.rs` has 3 functions totaling 1,056 lines (one function is 280+ lines)
- `handle_card_detail_key()` and `handle_board_detail_key()` are 230–280 line match blocks
- `count_headers_in_viewport()` is duplicated between `navigation_handlers.rs:24` and `render_strategy.rs:17`
- Column move-up/move-down are 90% identical (~90 lines of duplicate logic)

What to do: Reorganize by domain concern (handlers/card/, handlers/board/, handlers/navigation/). Extract the 8-repeated dialog match
pattern into a single HOF. Deduplicate count_headers_in_viewport.

Effort: 2–3 days | Payoff: Clear home for new handlers, ~150 lines of duplicate code eliminated.

---
Priority 8 — Domain Model Sizes

Files: `kanban-domain/src/board.rs` (918 lines), `card.rs` (728 lines), `card_lifecycle.rs` (600 lines), `dependencies/card_graph.rs` (636 lines)
Velocity Impact: 🟡 Medium — violates the 300-line guideline 2–3x over; slow to navigate

What to do: Split `board.rs` into `board/mod.rs` + `board/operations.rs` + `board/serialization.rs`. Split `card.rs` into `card/mod.rs` +
`card/update.rs` + `card/lifecycle.rs`.

Effort: 1–2 days | Payoff: Navigation speed, reduced cognitive load when editing one concern.

---
Priority 9 — Type Safety via Newtypes

Files: `kanban-domain/src/board.rs:9`, `card.rs:9`, `column.rs`, etc.
Velocity Impact: 🟡 Medium — current type BoardId = Uuid allows swapping IDs silently; bugs are slow to find

// Current: compile-time silent bug possible
`fn move_card(card_id: Uuid, column_id: Uuid)`

// With newtypes: compile error if swapped
`fn move_card(card_id: CardId, column_id: ColumnId)`

Effort: 1–2 days | Payoff: Eliminates a whole class of runtime bugs. Zero cost at runtime.

---
Priority 10 — Remove Dead Abstractions

Files: `kanban-core/src/traits.rs` (lines 5–20)
Velocity Impact: 🟢 Low — but causes confusion for new contributors

`Repository<T, Id>` and `Service<T, Id>` traits are defined but never implemented. The `CLAUDE.md` documentation still references a kanban-db
crate that doesn't exist.

What to do: Either delete these traits and update `CLAUDE.md`, or implement them (the persistence trait pattern exists in
`kanban-persistence/src/traits.rs` and is real).

Effort: 0.5 days | Payoff: Reduces architectural confusion.

---

cards.description:
Follow-up items from code review of PR #189 (KAN-224/decompose-app-rs-into-focused-modules). Zero blockers — PR was merged as-is.

---

## 1. Rename `SelectionHub` to something clearer

**File:** `crates/kanban-tui/src/app/selection.rs:4`
**Type:** Naming / readability

```rust
pub struct SelectionHub {
    pub board: SelectionState,
    pub active_board_index: Option<usize>,
    pub active_card_index: Option<usize>,
    pub sprint: SelectionState,
    pub active_sprint_index: Option<usize>,
    pub card_navigation_history: Vec<usize>,
}
```

`Hub` implies it coordinates or dispatches between things (like an event hub or message hub). This struct is just a plain data grouping of selection indices and cursor state. A reader seeing `self.selection.board` would not immediately know what "hub" means here.

**Suggested names:** `AppSelection`, `CursorState`, or simply `SelectionState` (if the `kanban_core::SelectionState` name collision can be resolved via aliasing or renaming the core type).

**Action:** Rename the struct and the `App` field from `selection: SelectionHub` to `selection: AppSelection` (or chosen name). Search all handler files for `self.selection.` — they all need updating but it is a trivial find-replace.

---

## 2. `FocusState` mixes two different lifecycle concerns

**File:** `crates/kanban-tui/src/app/focus.rs:91-95`
**Type:** Design / cohesion

```rust
pub struct FocusState {
    pub active: Focus,        // toggled on every Tab/hjkl press
    pub card_focus: CardFocus,   // only meaningful inside CardDetail mode
    pub board_focus: BoardFocus, // only meaningful inside BoardDetail mode
}
```

`active` is the global panel focus (Boards vs Cards) and changes constantly during normal navigation. `card_focus` and `board_focus` are sub-panel cursors that are only semantically relevant when the app is in `AppMode::CardDetail` or `AppMode::BoardDetail` respectively — outside those modes their values are stale/irrelevant.

Grouping them together in `FocusState` means a reader of `FocusState` has to mentally track when each field is valid. It also means detail-mode logic and navigation logic both mutate the same struct.

**Option A (preferred):** Move `card_focus: CardFocus` into a `CardDetailState` struct (does not exist yet, could live in a new `card_detail.rs`), and `board_focus: BoardFocus` into a `BoardDetailState`. These would be separate `App` fields only consulted in their respective modes.

**Option B (minimal):** Keep them in `FocusState` but rename to `FocusState.panel` (instead of `active`) to signal it is the panel-level concern, and add comments on `card_focus`/`board_focus` that they are detail-mode sub-cursors.

---

## 3. Drop redundant `#[derive(Default)]` on `PersistenceState`

**File:** `crates/kanban-tui/src/app/persistence.rs:3,16`
**Type:** Cleanup / consistency

```rust
#[derive(Default)]   // <-- never actually called
pub struct PersistenceState {
    pub save_file: Option<String>,
    pub file_change_rx: Option<...>,
    pub file_watcher: Option<...>,
    pub save_worker_handle: Option<...>,
    pub save_completion_rx: Option<...>,
}

impl PersistenceState {
    pub fn new(save_file: Option<String>, save_completion_rx: ...) -> Self { ... }
}
```

`App::new` always constructs `PersistenceState` via `PersistenceState::new(save_file, save_completion_rx)`. The `Default` impl (which would give all-`None`) is never invoked anywhere in the codebase. Having both is misleading — it suggests `Default` is a valid construction path when in practice `save_completion_rx` needs to come from the state manager and should never silently default to `None`.

**Action:** Remove `#[derive(Default)]`. If `App` ever needs a fully-defaulted construction path (e.g. for tests), the `new(None, None)` call is explicit and clear enough. Alternatively, drop `new()` and use a struct literal in `App::new` — matching how every other sub-struct (`AnimationState::default()`, `FilterState::default()`, etc.) is constructed — but that requires callers to know all field names, so the `new()` constructor is probably worth keeping.

---

## 4. `viewport_height` and `last_frame_area` are redundant in `ViewState`

**File:** `crates/kanban-tui/src/app/view.rs:11`
**Type:** Cleanup / derived state

```rust
pub struct ViewState {
    pub strategy: Box<dyn ViewStrategy>,
    pub card_list_component: CardListComponent,
    pub viewport_height: usize,   // <-- redundant?
    pub last_frame_area: Rect,    // <-- source of truth
}
```

`last_frame_area` is a `ratatui::layout::Rect` that contains the full terminal dimensions from the most recent render frame. `viewport_height` is a `usize` that is a subset of that information (the height of the card list viewport area, which is derived from the frame area minus borders/padding).

Storing both means there are two sources of truth that can drift: if `last_frame_area` is updated but `viewport_height` is not recomputed, scroll calculations could use a stale height.

**Action:** Audit all reads of `self.view.viewport_height`. If it is always set immediately after a frame render using `last_frame_area`-derived math, consider computing it on-demand via a `ViewState::viewport_height()` method rather than storing it. If it is genuinely updated at a different cadence, document why.

---

## 5. `ANIMATION_DURATION_MS` bypasses the re-export pattern

**File:** `crates/kanban-tui/src/app/animation.rs:6`, `crates/kanban-tui/src/app/mod.rs` (animation tick handler)
**Type:** Consistency / style

Every other symbol from the 12 sub-modules is re-exported at the `app/mod.rs` level:
```rust
pub mod animation;
pub use animation::{AnimationState, CardAnimation};  // types re-exported
// ANIMATION_DURATION_MS is NOT re-exported
```

But the const is accessed internally via its module path:
```rust
if elapsed >= animation::ANIMATION_DURATION_MS {
```

This is the only place in `mod.rs` that reaches back into a sub-module via its path rather than using a re-exported name. It works, but it is inconsistent and slightly surprising — a reader skimming `mod.rs` would not see `ANIMATION_DURATION_MS` in the re-export list and might not realise it is defined in `animation.rs`.

**Option A:** Add `pub use animation::ANIMATION_DURATION_MS;` to the re-export block (makes it consistent, but exports an internal implementation detail at crate level).

**Option B (preferred):** Since this const is only used in one place inside `mod.rs`, make it `pub(super)` in `animation.rs` (currently `pub(crate)`) and access it as `animation::ANIMATION_DURATION_MS` — but add a comment in the re-export block: `// ANIMATION_DURATION_MS intentionally not re-exported (internal use only)`.

**Option C:** Inline the value (`150u128`) directly at the use site and delete the named const — it is only used once.

cards.description:
## Problem

There is no first-class CLI command to complete a card. The current workarounds are both bad:

- `card update KAN-X --status done` — sets a metadata field that is redundant with column position (see KAN-324)
- `card move KAN-X --column-id <uuid>` — requires the user to know the UUID of the completion column

Neither is discoverable or ergonomic. Completing a card is one of the most common operations and should be a single, obvious command.

## Proposed Commands

```
kanban <file> card complete <ID>   # move to completion column, set completed_at
kanban <file> card reopen <ID>     # move back to first column, clear completed_at
```

## Behaviour

**`card complete`**:
1. Look up the card by identifier (e.g. `KAN-12`)
2. Resolve the completion column: use `board.completion_column_id` if set; otherwise fall back to the column with the highest `position` value on the card's board
3. Move the card to that column (reuse the `MoveCard` command internally)
4. `completed_at` is set as a side effect of the move (see KAN-324 — this should be driven by column, not `CardStatus`)

**`card reopen`**:
1. Look up the card
2. Resolve the first column: column with `position == 0` on the card's board
3. Move the card there
4. `completed_at` is cleared as a side effect

## Offending Gap

`kanban-cli/src/cli.rs` — `CardAction` enum has no `Complete` or `Reopen` variant:
```rust
// currently
pub enum CardAction {
    Create(CardCreateArgs),
    List(CardListArgs),
    Get { id: String },
    Update(CardUpdateArgs),
    Move(CardMoveArgs),
    Archive { id: String },
    ...
}
```

`kanban-mcp/src/lib.rs` — no `complete_card` or `reopen_card` tool registered.

The completion column resolution logic does not exist as a reusable function anywhere in `kanban-domain` — it is implied but never extracted.

## Steps to Resolution

1. **Domain** — add `fn resolve_completion_column(board: &Board, columns: &[Column]) -> Option<&Column>` and `fn resolve_first_column(columns: &[Column]) -> Option<&Column>` in `kanban-domain`
2. **Red** — write tests for both resolution functions covering: `completion_column_id` set, `completion_column_id` null (falls back to max position), empty columns list
3. **Service** — add `complete_card(card_id: Uuid)` and `reopen_card(card_id: Uuid)` to `KanbanOperations` trait and implement in `KanbanContext`
4. **CLI** — add `Complete { id: String }` and `Reopen { id: String }` to `CardAction` in `cli.rs`; add handlers in `handlers/card.rs`
5. **MCP** — register `complete_card` and `reopen_card` tools in `kanban-mcp/src/lib.rs`
6. **Green + refactor** — run full test suite

## Files Affected

- `crates/kanban-domain/src/` — new column resolution helpers
- `crates/kanban-service/src/context.rs` — `complete_card`, `reopen_card` impl
- `crates/kanban-domain/src/operations.rs` (or wherever `KanbanOperations` is defined) — trait methods
- `crates/kanban-cli/src/cli.rs` — new `CardAction` variants
- `crates/kanban-cli/src/handlers/card.rs` — handler arms
- `crates/kanban-mcp/src/lib.rs` — new tool registrations

## Related

- KAN-323 — fix misleading 'Card not found' on missing file
- KAN-324 — remove `CardStatus`; `completed_at` should be driven by column move, not status field
