cards.description:
Follow-up to KAN-226 (PR #190): extract kanban-service crate.

## Items

### 1. Make KanbanContext fields private (+ pub(crate) accessors if needed)

Fields currently pub in crates/kanban-service/src/context.rs:
  pub boards: Vec<Board>
  pub columns: Vec<Column>
  pub cards: Vec<Card>
  pub sprints: Vec<Sprint>
  pub archived_cards: Vec<ArchivedCard>
  pub graph: DependencyGraph

External callers confirmed by grep — none access fields directly:
- crates/kanban-cli/src/context.rs: imports KanbanContext, delegates via KanbanOperations methods
- crates/kanban-mcp/src/context.rs: same pattern
- crates/kanban-mcp/tests/integration.rs: uses KanbanContext::load_json() + trait methods only
- crates/kanban-service/tests/persistence.rs: same

The 490 field accesses in kanban-tui are against TuiContext (crates/kanban-tui/src/tui_context.rs), not KanbanContext. No conflict.

KanbanOperations already covers all read paths. Making fields private is a zero-impact change. No new accessors should be needed unless something is missed.

### 2. Make execute() pub(crate)

crates/kanban-service/src/context.rs:
  pub fn execute(&mut self, command: Box<dyn Command>) -> KanbanResult<()>

Only called internally within the same file by KanbanOperations impl methods. No external callers (confirmed by grep across all crates). Exposes the command pattern internals unnecessarily.

Fix: change to pub(crate).

### 3. Make DataSnapshot pub(crate)

crates/kanban-service/src/context.rs:
  pub struct DataSnapshot { ... }

Serialisation detail used only within the crate for save()/load()/import_board()/export_board(). Not part of the public API contract.

Fix: change to pub(crate).

## Non-issue: Uuid::new_v4() in save()

The review flagged PersistenceMetadata::new(Uuid::new_v4()) in KanbanContext::save() as a possible regression vs. the old self.store.instance_id() call. It is not.

JsonFileStore::save() (crates/kanban-persistence/src/store/json_file_store.rs:112) unconditionally overwrites the passed instance_id with its own stable instance_id:
  snapshot.metadata.instance_id = self.instance_id;

Conflict detection uses FileMetadata (file mtime + size on disk), not instance_id. The old call was equally irrelevant. No action needed.
cards.title: KAN-227: Tighten visibility in kanban-service crate

cards.description:
## Context

KAN-216 added per-card ### grouping to CHANGELOG.md. Each bullet point is a commit subject line, but there is no link back to the actual commit on GitHub.

## Current output

### KAN-193 Bring MCP to full feature parity (2026-03-17)
- feat: update MCP server tools for full CLI parity
- feat: bring MCP context to full parity with CLI

## Expected output

### KAN-193 Bring MCP to full feature parity (2026-03-17)
- feat: update MCP server tools for full CLI parity ([abc1234](https://github.com/owner/repo/commit/abc1234))
- feat: bring MCP context to full parity with CLI ([def5678](https://github.com/owner/repo/commit/def5678))

## Approach

Modify create-changeset.sh to capture commit hashes alongside subjects. Instead of:
  git log ... --pretty=format:"- %s"
Use:
  git log ... --pretty=format:"- %s (%H)"

Then in aggregate-changelog.sh, after deriving the repo URL (already done for PR links), replace bare hashes at end of bullet lines with Markdown links. Short hash (7 chars) shown in label.

## Acceptance criteria

- create-changeset.sh stores full commit hash alongside each subject line
- aggregate-changelog.sh converts hashes to GitHub commit links using remote URL
- Legacy changeset files without hashes are handled gracefully (lines left unchanged)
- Short hash (7 chars) is shown in the link label

cards.description:
## Context

`CardQueryBuilder::search(query)` (query/mod.rs:81) always calls `CompositeSearcher::all(query)`, hardwiring all three search methods (title, branch name, card identifier) with no way to narrow them. The builder accepts only a plain string — no field selection.

## Current behaviour

```
CompositeSearcher::all(query)
  → TitleSearcher
  → BranchNameSearcher
  → CardIdentifierSearcher   ← always on, cannot be excluded
```

`CompositeSearcher` already has a builder-style API (`new() + with_search()`) that supports selective composition, but it is never surfaced past the domain layer.

## Proposed change

### Domain layer

Change `CardQueryBuilder` to accept a pre-built searcher instead of (or alongside) a plain string:

```rust
pub fn search_with(mut self, searcher: CompositeSearcher) -> Self { ... }
```

### Interface layer

Each interface builds the searcher from user-supplied flags:

- **CLI**: `kanban card list --search "foo" --search-by title,identifier`
  Maps flag values to `SearchBy` variants, builds `CompositeSearcher::new().with_search(...)`
- **MCP**: `tool_list_cards` accepts an optional `search_fields` array param; handler builds the searcher before passing to `CardQueryBuilder`
- **TUI**: current all-fields behaviour is fine as default; could add a mode toggle

## Notes

- `CompositeSearcher::all(query)` remains valid for the default/unspecified case
- No changes needed to the searcher structs themselves — the primitive is already correct
cards.title: Expose selective search fields via CardQueryBuilder and interface flags

cards.description:
## Context

Search exists only in the TUI (via `CardQueryBuilder` + `CompositeSearcher`). The CLI and MCP have no search capability — `card list` and `tool_list_cards` only filter by board/column/sprint/status. The `CompositeSearcher` itself only covers title, branch name, and identifier; it does not search description or any other field.

## What we want

A search command/parameter that searches **all meaningful text fields** on a card, **across all boards**, with results ranked or at least consistently ordered.

### Fields to search (case-insensitive substring match)

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| `title` | already in TitleSearcher |
| `description` | not currently searched anywhere |
| `identifier` | e.g. KAN-5 — already in CardIdentifierSearcher |
| `branch_name` | derived field — already in BranchNameSearcher |
| `priority` | e.g. "critical", "high" |
| `status` | e.g. "blocked", "in_progress" |

Fields **not** worth searching: `id`, `column_id`, `sprint_id`, `position`, `points`, `due_date`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `completed_at`, `sprint_logs`.

## Required changes

### 1. Domain — extend `CompositeSearcher`

Add `DescriptionSearcher`, `PrioritySearcher`, `StatusSearcher` to `kanban-domain/src/search/mod.rs` and include them in `CompositeSearcher::all`.

### 2. Domain — `CardQueryBuilder` cross-board variant

`CardQueryBuilder` is scoped to a single board today (takes `&Board`). A cross-board search needs a variant that iterates all boards, or a new free function that runs the search across the full cards/columns/boards/sprints slices.

### 3. CLI — `card list --search <query>`

Add `--search` flag to `CardListArgs`. Wire it through `build_filter` → `CardQueryBuilder` (or the cross-board variant). Results should include the board name alongside each card for context.

### 4. CLI — dedicated `card search <query>` command (optional alternative)

If a dedicated subcommand is preferred over a flag on `list`, add `CardAction::Search { query: String }` to the CLI. Always searches across all boards.

### 5. MCP — `tool_list_cards` search param

Add optional `search: Option<String>` to `ListCardsRequest`. When present, pass it through `CardQueryBuilder::search()`. Also works cross-board when no `board_id` filter is given.

## Acceptance criteria

- `kanban <file> card list --search "auth"` returns all cards whose title, description, identifier, branch name, priority, or status contain "auth", across all boards
- `tool_list_cards` with `search: "blocked database"` returns matching cards
- Empty or missing `search` behaves identically to today (no regression)
- TUI search behaviour unchanged (already uses `CompositeSearcher::all`)
cards.title: Add full-text card search to CLI and MCP

cards.description: In kanban-persistence-sqlite, edge weights are stored as f32 (REAL) and cast back to f64 on load. This causes precision loss for dependency graph edge weights. Currently documented in code comments as acceptable since weights are relative ordering hints, but should be tracked for potential future fix (store as f64 / DOUBLE).

cards.description:
When migrating kanban data from JSON to SQLite, the migration fails with FOREIGN KEY constraint failed because the JSON store has no FK enforcement — orphaned references accumulate over time (e.g., cards pointing to deleted columns/sprints). Currently this requires manual data cleaning. We need a built-in utility to detect and repair these violations.

## Approach

Add a `validate` function to `kanban-domain` (pure logic, no I/O) and a `Validate` CLI subcommand. Also integrate validation into `migrate` so it auto-repairs before saving.

## FK Relationships to Validate

- `column.board_id` → boards (CASCADE → Remove column)
- `sprint.board_id` → boards (CASCADE → Remove sprint)
- `card.column_id` → columns (CASCADE → Remove card)
- `card.sprint_id` → sprints (SET NULL → Set to None)
- `board.active_sprint_id` → sprints (SET NULL → Set to None)
- `board.completion_column_id` → columns (SET NULL → Set to None)
- `archived_card.card.column_id` → columns (CASCADE → Remove archived card)
- `archived_card.original_column_id` → columns (Not blocking, no FK in schema)
- `graph edges` source/target → cards (Remove edge)

## Implementation

### Step 1: crates/kanban-domain/src/integrity.rs (new file)

Types: IntegrityReport, Violation, ViolationKind enum covering all FK relationships.

Two public functions:
- `validate(snapshot: &Snapshot) -> IntegrityReport` — builds HashSet<Uuid> per entity type, checks all references
- `repair(snapshot: &mut Snapshot) -> RepairSummary` — validates, then applies fixes in cascade order (parents first): remove orphaned columns/sprints → recompute valid sets → remove orphaned cards → null dangling refs → remove orphaned archived cards → remove dangling edges

### Step 2: Register module in crates/kanban-domain/src/lib.rs

Add `pub mod integrity;` and re-export public types.

### Step 3: Validate CLI subcommand in crates/kanban-cli/src/cli.rs

Add Validate(ValidateArgs) with --fix flag. Uses existing file argument from Cli.

### Step 4: crates/kanban-cli/src/handlers/validate.rs (new file)

1. Load store via make_store(file)
2. Deserialize StoreSnapshot.data → Snapshot
3. Call validate(&snapshot), print report
4. If --fix and violations exist: call repair(&mut snapshot), re-serialize, save back

### Step 5: Wire into crates/kanban-cli/src/main.rs

### Step 6: Auto-repair in crates/kanban-cli/src/handlers/migrate.rs

After loading snapshot, before saving to target: deserialize, validate, repair if needed, re-serialize, save.

### Tests (TDD)

Unit tests in integrity.rs:
- test_validate_clean_snapshot_returns_no_violations
- test_validate_card_with_missing_column_returns_orphaned_card
- test_validate_card_with_missing_sprint_returns_dangling_ref
- test_validate_column_with_missing_board_returns_orphaned_column
- test_validate_board_with_missing_active_sprint_returns_dangling_ref
- test_validate_edge_with_missing_card_returns_dangling_edge
- test_validate_archived_card_with_missing_column_returns_violation
- test_repair_removes_orphaned_cards
- test_repair_nulls_dangling_sprint_refs
- test_repair_cascades_column_removal_to_cards
- test_repair_on_clean_snapshot_is_noop

Integration tests in validate.rs:
- test_validate_reports_violations
- test_validate_fix_repairs_and_saves
- test_migrate_auto_repairs_violations

## Key Files

- crates/kanban-domain/src/integrity.rs (Create)
- crates/kanban-domain/src/lib.rs (Edit)
- crates/kanban-cli/src/cli.rs (Edit)
- crates/kanban-cli/src/handlers/validate.rs (Create)
- crates/kanban-cli/src/handlers/mod.rs (Edit)
- crates/kanban-cli/src/handlers/migrate.rs (Edit)
- crates/kanban-cli/src/main.rs (Edit)

## Verification

1. cargo test -p kanban-domain — unit tests pass
2. cargo test -p kanban-cli — integration tests pass
3. Manual: kanban kanban.json validate — reports violations
4. Manual: kanban kanban.json validate --fix — repairs and saves
5. Manual: kanban migrate --from kanban.json --to kanban.db — succeeds without manual cleanup
cards.title: Add referential integrity validation and repair utility

## Summary

CHANGELOG.md entries should link to individual commits on GitHub. Each changelog line item gets a clickable short-hash link when aggregated.

## Current State (Paused)

Initial implementation landed but needs simplification before merging. The current approach embeds hashes in changeset files, which go stale on rebase and require a manual `--refresh` step. See "Next Steps" below for the better approach.

### Commits on `develop` (to be reverted/reworked)

- `0da3460` feat: append commit hashes to changeset entries and add --refresh flag
- `3d7dd35` feat: convert commit hashes to clickable links in aggregate-changelog
- `e8d2064` feat: convert commit hashes to clickable links in update-changelog
- `7aa8e77` feat: validate commit hash format in CI changeset job
- `b422699` docs: document commit hash format and --refresh flag in changeset README

## Next Steps — Simplified Approach

**Don't store hashes in changeset files.** Instead, derive them at merge time from `git log`.

### What to revert
- `create-changeset.sh`: remove `(%H)` from git log format, remove `--refresh` flag entirely
- `ci.yml`: remove commit hash validation block and `fetch-depth: 0` on changeset job
- `.changeset/README.md`: revert to original example without hashes

### What to keep (with modification)
- `aggregate-changelog.sh` and `update-changelog.sh`: keep `REPO_URL` derivation and link generation, but change hash source from parsing the changeset file to looking up commits by subject:

```bash
subject="${line#- }"
hash=$(git log --all --format="%H" --fixed-strings --grep="$subject" -1)
if [ -n "$hash" ]; then
  short="${hash:0:7}"
  echo "$line ([\`$short\`]($REPO_URL/commit/$hash))"
else
  echo "$line"
fi
```

### Why this is better
- Changeset files stay clean (just `- feat: description`)
- No staleness after rebase — hashes derived at merge time are always correct
- No `--refresh` flag needed
- No CI validation needed
- Manual entries without matching commits pass through unchanged

# Steps to Add Your Project to Nixpkgs

## 1. Add Yourself as a Maintainer

First, you'll need to add yourself to the maintainer list in maintainers/maintainer-list.nix with a separate commit titled "maintainers: add <your-handle>".

## 2. Create the Package Expression

Since your Kanban is a Rust project, you'll use buildRustPackage from rustPlatform nixpkgs/doc/languages-frameworks/rust.section.md at master · NixOS/nixpkgs

[default.nix](./default.nix) 

## 3. Determine Package Location

Decide which pkgs/ subfolder your expression should live in, then add your expression under a directory like pkgs/applications/misc/kanban/default.nix or similar

## 4. Add to Package Index

Add an entry in pkgs/top-level/all-packages.nix so nixpkgs can find your package 

## 5. Fork and Test

Fork the nixpkgs repository, make your changes in a local branch, then build from the root of nixpkgs with nix-build -A kanban Nixpkgs/Contributing - NixOS Wiki

## 6. Handle the Hash Values

For the cargoHash, you can initially use an empty string or fake hash, and Nix will tell you the correct hash when you try to build nixpkgs/doc/languages-frameworks/rust.section.md at master · NixOS/nixpkgs

## 7. Submit a Pull Request

Once your package builds successfully, format your code with a Nix formatter like alejandra, then open a PR on GitHub with the title format "kanban: init at <version>" 

## 8. Wait for Review

Be patient - it's normal for PRs to sit for weeks. If you need help, you can reach out on NixOS Discourse or the Matrix channels

## Important Considerations

Read the commit conventions specific to pkgs and include relevant information in your commit messages so others can understand why changes were made 

The maintainers field is for you as the Nix expression maintainer, not the project maintainer. By submitting this package, you're taking responsibility for ongoing maintenance like version bumps

cards.description:
## Problem

The current workflow bumps the version on every merge to develop. This causes:

1. One version bump per feature/fix/refactor instead of one per release
2. Risk of mismatch between the bumped version in Cargo.toml and the published version on crates.io
3. Bump and publish can get out of sync, delaying the actual publish by one push to master

## Current Flow

1. PR merges to develop → aggregate-changesets.yml bumps version immediately
2. PR from develop to master → release.yml publishes and tags

The gap between steps 1 and 2 is where things go wrong. The version is already bumped but not yet published, so any failure or extra commit can desync the two.

## Desired Flow

1. PRs merge to develop — changesets accumulate, NO version bump
2. When ready to release, create PR from develop to master
3. On merge to master: evaluate all accumulated changesets, determine aggregate bump type, bump version, update changelog, publish to crates.io, create tag — all atomically
4. If any step fails, the whole thing rolls back (no partial state)

## Research Needed

- How to make bump + changelog + publish + tag atomic in a single workflow
- What happens if crates.io publish fails mid-way (some crates published, some not)
- Whether to keep the CI changeset validation on develop PRs (probably yes)
- How to handle the develop → master sync after a release without conflicts
- Review scripts/bump-version.sh, scripts/publish-crates.sh, and both workflows for the refactor

## Risk

The previous workflow was designed to avoid exactly the sync issues we're now hitting. Need to be careful not to introduce new failure modes while fixing the current ones.
cards.title: Redesign release workflow: defer version bump to master merge

cards.description:
## Bug

When assigning a card to a sprint via the TUI ('a' key), the wrong sprint gets assigned. Cards end up on old Completed sprints instead of the intended one.

## Root Cause

Index mismatch between the sprint selection dialog and the selection handler:

**Dialog rendering** (`selection_dialog.rs:194-202`) filters OUT Completed/Cancelled sprints:
```rust
.filter(|s| s.status != SprintStatus::Completed && s.status != SprintStatus::Cancelled)
```
Shows: `[(None), Sprint #11 "a-new-year" (Planning)]`

**Selection handler** (`popup_handlers.rs:209-215`) uses UNFILTERED list:
```rust
let board_sprints: Vec<_> = self.ctx.sprints.iter()
    .filter(|s| s.board_id == board_id)
    .collect();
if let Some(sprint) = board_sprints.get(selection_idx - 1) { ... }
```
Unfiltered: `[Sprint #1 (Completed), Sprint #6 (Completed), ..., Sprint #11 (Planning)]`

User selects index 1 (Sprint #11 in filtered list) -> handler does `get(0)` on unfiltered list -> gets Sprint #1 "an-eventful-october".

## Affected Code

- `crates/kanban-tui/src/handlers/popup_handlers.rs:209-215` -- single card assignment
- `crates/kanban-tui/src/handlers/popup_handlers.rs:337-343` -- multi-card assignment (same bug)

## Fix

Apply the same Completed/Cancelled filter in the handler that the dialog uses:
```rust
let board_sprints: Vec<_> = self.ctx.sprints.iter()
    .filter(|s| s.board_id == board_id)
    .filter(|s| s.status != SprintStatus::Completed && s.status != SprintStatus::Cancelled)
    .collect();
```

Both single-card and multi-card paths need the fix.

## Notes

- CLI is not affected (uses UUID directly, no index-based selection)
- MCP is not affected (no sprint assignment tool yet)
cards.title: Fix TUI sprint assignment selecting wrong sprint (index mismatch)

cards.description:
## Problem

The three interfaces (TUI, CLI, MCP) are not at feature parity. `KanbanOperations` trait in `kanban-domain` enforces compile-time parity between TUI (`TuiContext`) and CLI (`CliContext`) — 36 methods. But the MCP server has a separate `McpTools` trait with only 14 methods, delegates to CLI subprocesses, and has no compile-time enforcement.

## Current State

- `KanbanOperations` (36 methods) in `crates/kanban-domain/src/operations.rs:19-84`
- `CliContext` implements it at `crates/kanban-cli/src/context.rs:172`
- `TuiContext` implements it at `crates/kanban-tui/src/tui_context.rs:92`
- MCP has separate `McpTools` trait (14 methods) at `crates/kanban-mcp/src/tools_trait.rs`
- MCP spawns CLI subprocesses via `CliExecutor` at `crates/kanban-mcp/src/executor.rs`
- MCP crate has **zero dependency** on `kanban-domain`, `kanban-core`, or `kanban-persistence`

## Desired End State

- MCP implements all 36 `KanbanOperations` methods as MCP tools
- MCP depends on `kanban-domain`, `kanban-core`, `kanban-persistence` directly
- `McpTools` trait and `CliExecutor` are deleted
- `McpContext` struct implements `KanbanOperations` (same pattern as `CliContext`)
- Adding a method to `KanbanOperations` causes a compile error in MCP until wired up
- No subprocess spawning, no CLI arg building, no retry logic

## Missing from MCP (22 operations)

**Board**: update_board
**Column**: get_column, update_column, reorder_column
**Card**: restore_card, list_archived_cards, assign_card_to_sprint, unassign_card_from_sprint, get_card_branch_name, get_card_git_checkout, bulk_archive_cards, bulk_move_cards, bulk_assign_sprint
**Sprint** (all 8): create, list, get, update, activate, complete, cancel, delete
**Import/Export**: export_board, import_board

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1: Add Dependencies and Create McpContext

1. **Update `crates/kanban-mcp/Cargo.toml`** — add `kanban-core`, `kanban-domain`, `kanban-persistence`, `uuid` as dependencies

2. **Create `crates/kanban-mcp/src/context.rs`** — `McpContext` struct following `CliContext` pattern:
   - Same fields: `boards`, `columns`, `cards`, `sprints`, `archived_cards`, `graph`, `store`
   - Same `load()` async constructor via `JsonFileStore`
   - Same `execute()` method using `CommandContext`
   - Same `save()` async method
   - `impl KanbanOperations for McpContext` (copy from `CliContext`)
   - Local `DataSnapshot` struct (same as CLI's — simple 6-field serialize/deserialize)

**Key design**: `KanbanOperations` uses `&mut self`, MCP tools receive `&self`. Solution: `Arc<tokio::sync::Mutex<McpContext>>`

**Verify**: `cargo build --package kanban-mcp`

### Phase 2: Replace Subprocess Delegation

1. **Update `KanbanMcpServer`** — replace `executor: Arc<CliExecutor>` with `ctx: Arc<tokio::sync::Mutex<McpContext>>`

2. **Update `main.rs`** — `KanbanMcpServer::new()` becomes async (loads data at startup)

3. **Add helpers**:
   - `parse_uuid(s: &str) -> Result<Uuid, McpError>` for String→Uuid conversion
   - `to_mcp_error(e: impl Display) -> McpError` to reduce boilerplate
   - `list_result<T: Serialize>(items: Vec<T>) -> CallToolResult` for consistent list responses

4. **Rewrite existing 14 tool implementations** — each tool: lock mutex → call trait method → save on writes → serialize result

   Read pattern:
   ```rust
   async fn tool_list_boards(&self) -> Result<CallToolResult, McpError> {
       let ctx = self.ctx.lock().await;
       let boards = ctx.list_boards().map_err(to_mcp_error)?;
       Ok(list_result(boards))
   }
   ```
   Write pattern:
   ```rust
   async fn tool_create_board(&self, Parameters(req): Parameters<CreateBoardRequest>) -> Result<CallToolResult, McpError> {
       let mut ctx = self.ctx.lock().await;
       let board = ctx.create_board(req.name, req.card_prefix).map_err(to_mcp_error)?;
       ctx.save().await.map_err(to_mcp_error)?;
       Ok(json_result(serde_json::to_value(&board).unwrap()))
   }
   ```

5. **Delete dead code**:
   - Delete `crates/kanban-mcp/src/executor.rs`
   - Delete `crates/kanban-mcp/src/tools_trait.rs`
   - Remove `mod executor`, `mod tools_trait`, all `use` of deleted types from `lib.rs`

**Verify**: `cargo build --package kanban-mcp`, existing 14 tools still work

### Phase 3: Add Missing 22 MCP Tools

Add request types + `#[tool]` wrappers for all missing operations:

**Board** (1 tool):
- `tool_update_board` — "Update a board's properties (name, description, prefixes)"

**Column** (3 tools):
- `tool_get_column` — "Get a specific column by ID"
- `tool_update_column` — "Update a column's properties (name, position, WIP limit)"
- `tool_reorder_column` — "Move a column to a new position"

**Card** (10 tools):
- `tool_restore_card` — "Restore an archived card"
- `tool_list_archived_cards` — "List all archived cards"
- `tool_assign_card_to_sprint` — "Assign a card to a sprint"
- `tool_unassign_card_from_sprint` — "Remove a card's sprint assignment"
- `tool_get_card_branch_name` — "Get git branch name for a card"
- `tool_get_card_git_checkout` — "Get git checkout command for a card"
- `tool_bulk_archive_cards` — "Archive multiple cards"
- `tool_bulk_move_cards` — "Move multiple cards to a column"
- `tool_bulk_assign_sprint` — "Assign multiple cards to a sprint"

**Sprint** (8 tools):
- `tool_create_sprint` — "Create a new sprint"
- `tool_list_sprints` — "List all sprints for a board"
- `tool_get_sprint` — "Get a specific sprint by ID"
- `tool_update_sprint` — "Update sprint properties"
- `tool_activate_sprint` — "Activate a sprint"
- `tool_complete_sprint` — "Complete an active sprint"
- `tool_cancel_sprint` — "Cancel an active sprint"
- `tool_delete_sprint` — "Delete a sprint"

**Import/Export** (2 tools):
- `tool_export_board` — "Export board data as JSON"
- `tool_import_board` — "Import board data from JSON"

Also update `ListCardsRequest` to add `status` filter parameter.

**Verify**: `cargo build`, `cargo clippy`, all 36 tools listed when connecting

### Phase 4: Verification

- `cargo build` (full workspace)
- `cargo clippy --package kanban-mcp`
- `cargo test`
- Connect via `.mcp.json`, verify all 36 tools appear
- Test sprint CRUD, card archive/restore, bulk ops, export/import through MCP

## What We're NOT Doing

- NOT extracting shared base context crate (MCP context will duplicate CliContext pattern — acceptable)
- NOT changing `KanbanOperations` trait itself
- NOT adding undo/redo to MCP (TUI-specific)
- NOT changing `.mcp.json` config or CLI binary interface
- NOT adding new operations beyond existing 36

## References

- `crates/kanban-domain/src/operations.rs:19-84` — KanbanOperations trait
- `crates/kanban-cli/src/context.rs:39-683` — CliContext (model for McpContext)
- `crates/kanban-tui/src/tui_context.rs:17-569` — TuiContext (reference)
- `crates/kanban-mcp/src/lib.rs` — current MCP server
- `crates/kanban-mcp/src/executor.rs` — CliExecutor (to delete)
- `crates/kanban-mcp/src/tools_trait.rs` — McpTools (to delete)

cards.description:
## Problem

Every new keybinding must be added in two places:
1. `keybindings/` registry (for footer display and help popup)
2. `handle_key_event()` hardcoded match in `app/mod.rs` (for actual dispatch)

These can silently drift apart — a key can appear in help but do nothing, or work but not show in help.

## Complications

- **Context-dependent keys**: `n` creates board or card depending on focus; `e` edits board or card
- **Multi-key sequences**: `gg` needs pending-key state
- **Terminal access**: some handlers (`e`, card detail editing) need `terminal` + `event_handler` params that `execute_action()` doesn't receive
- **Return value**: some branches set `should_restart_events = true`

## Proposed Approach

1. Extend `KeybindingAction` to carry context (e.g. `CreateItem` instead of separate `CreateBoard`/`CreateCard`, resolved at dispatch time by focus)
2. Pass `terminal` and `event_handler` into `execute_action()` so all handlers can be dispatched uniformly
3. Add a `needs_restart` return value from `execute_action()`
4. Handle multi-key sequences (`gg`) as a pre-processing step before dispatch
5. Make the registry the single source of truth — remove the hardcoded match in `handle_key_event` for Normal mode
6. All other modes (CardDetail, BoardDetail, etc.) could follow the same pattern incrementally
cards.title: Unify keybinding dispatch with registry

The TUI crate contained business logic (filtering, sorting, searching, export/import) that should be reusable by:
- Future API server

- `crates/kanban-tui/src/clipboard.rs`: Use `SetExtLinux::wait_until()` to give clipboard managers time to take ownership

cards.description:
---
  Investigation: -V flag shows commit: unknown in release builds

  Root Cause

  The version string is constructed at compile time in crates/kanban-cli/src/cli.rs:4-8:

  const VERSION: &str = concat!(
      env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"),
      "\ncommit: ",
      env!("GIT_COMMIT_HASH")
  );

  The commit hash is resolved in crates/kanban-cli/build.rs:8-27 with this priority:

  1. GIT_COMMIT_HASH env var (if set and not empty / not "unknown")
  2. git rev-parse HEAD — works when .git is present
  3. Falls back to "unknown"

  Why It Fails in Release / Nix Builds

  default.nix:14 uses lib.cleanSource ./. which strips the .git directory before building — standard Nix practice for reproducible builds. Without .git, step 2 fails and the fallback fires.

  Neither the Nix derivation (default.nix, flake.nix), the dev shell (shell.nix), nor the CI workflows (ci.yml, release.yml) set GIT_COMMIT_HASH as an env var at build time.

  Why cargo run -- -V Works

  Running directly from the repo means .git exists on disk, so git rev-parse HEAD succeeds in the build script.

  Proposed Fix

  Two separate concerns:

  1. Drop commit line when unknown — Change the version string construction so commit: unknown is never shown. This requires either:
  - A build-time cfg flag (not possible with env! alone)
  - Splitting the version into base + optional suffix evaluated at runtime via clap's .version() method with a String rather than a compile-time &str

  2. Inject hash during Nix/release builds — In default.nix, pass the commit rev as an env var before the build:
  preBuild = ''
    export GIT_COMMIT_HASH="${self.rev or "unknown"}"
  '';
  self.rev is available in flake context when the working tree is clean and committed. The or "unknown" handles dirty trees gracefully.

  Files Involved

  ┌───────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │               File                │                 Relevance                  │
  ├───────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ crates/kanban-cli/src/cli.rs:4-13 │ Version string constant + clap wiring      │
  ├───────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ crates/kanban-cli/build.rs:1-28   │ Build script that resolves GIT_COMMIT_HASH │
  ├───────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ default.nix:14                    │ lib.cleanSource strips .git                │
  ├───────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ flake.nix                         │ Has access to self.rev for injecting hash  │
  ├───────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ .github/workflows/release.yml     │ Does not set GIT_COMMIT_HASH               │
  └───────────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  Acceptance Criteria

  - kanban -V on a release/Nix build shows only the semver (e.g. 0.2.0), no commit: line
  - kanban -V on a dev build (cargo run) still shows the commit hash
  - kanban -V on a Nix build from a clean committed tree shows the correct short commit hash
  - No commit: unknown output in any scenario

cards.description:
## Bug

`tool_list_cards` in the MCP server always returns at most 50 cards regardless of the actual total, and `total_pages` is always 1.

## Root Cause

The MCP context's `list_cards` delegates to the CLI `card list` command via `execute_list`. The CLI command is called without `--page` or `--page-size` args, so it defaults to page 1 with page_size 50. Only those 50 items are returned to the MCP layer, which then paginates them — meaning `total` is always capped at 50 (the page size), not the actual number of cards.

**Location**: `crates/kanban-mcp/src/context.rs` — `execute_list` (line 115) and `list_cards` (line 255)

```rust
// execute_list only captures items, ignores pagination metadata
fn execute_list<T: serde::de::DeserializeOwned>(&self, args: &[&str]) -> KanbanResult<Vec<T>> {
    let response: ListResponse<T> = self.executor.execute(args)?;
    Ok(response.items)  // only 50 items from page 1
}
```

## Fix

Update `ListResponse` to include `total_pages`, then loop through all pages in `execute_list` to collect the full result set before returning to the MCP layer for client-side pagination.

cards.description:
## Challenge
When the terminal window was too small to show all keybindings in the help popup, entries were silently cut off with no scroll support.

## Solution
Implemented scrollable help menu by reusing the existing `ListComponent` infrastructure from the card lists, following the same patterns used throughout the rest of the TUI.

## Changes

### `crates/kanban-core/src/pagination.rs`
- Added `Page::get_adjusted_viewport_height(raw)` — computes content rows after reserving lines for scroll indicators (above=1 if scrolled, below=1 if items extend past viewport).

### `crates/kanban-tui/src/components/generic_list.rs`
- `ListComponent::get_adjusted_viewport_height` now delegates to `Page::get_adjusted_viewport_height` (deduplication).

### `crates/kanban-tui/src/app.rs`
- Replaced `help_selection: SelectionState` + `help_page: Page` with `help_list: ListComponent`.
- On help open: `help_list.update_item_count(bindings.len())` + `set_scroll_offset(0)`.
- On help close (3 locations): `help_list.update_item_count(0)`.
- Navigation (j/k): uses two-step `ensure_selected_visible` pattern matching `navigation_handlers.rs`.
- Key-shortcut jump: uses `help_list.jump_to(index)` + `ensure_selected_visible`.

### `crates/kanban-tui/src/ui.rs` — `render_help_popup`
- Layout changed to `[Length(2), Min(0), Length(2)]`: fixed header, scrollable bindings body, fixed footer.
- `all_lines` now contains only the N binding lines (no header/footer offset arithmetic needed).
- Uses `help_list.get_adjusted_viewport_height` + `help_list.get_render_info` for correct scroll state.
- Scroll indicators rendered via shared `render_scroll_indicators` helper with label `"item"` (fixes "entrys" pluralisation bug from `"entry"`).
- Fixed footer (hint line) always visible regardless of scroll position.

## Commits
- `feat(pagination): add get_adjusted_viewport_height to Page`
- `refactor(generic_list): delegate get_adjusted_viewport_height to Page`
- `feat(help): replace help_selection+help_page with help_list ListComponent`
- `feat(help): fixed header/footer layout with ListComponent scroll in render_help_popup`

2026-03-21 00:20:17
---

PR #185 — KAN-221: Scrollable Help Menu

Overview

Replaces the static Paragraph-based help popup with a ListComponent-backed scrollable list. Fixes
clipping on small terminals, pins the header/footer, and fixes a pluralisation bug ("entrys" →
"items"). Also generalises render_scroll_indicators and extracts get_adjusted_viewport_height up to
 kanban-core.

---
Code Quality

Positives:
- The get_adjusted_viewport_height extraction to Page is a clean improvement — ListComponent now
just delegates, eliminating duplication
- render_scroll_indicators generalisation is well done; the split-call pattern (above and below
separately) is a bit awkward but avoids a larger API change
- render_help_popup signature change to &mut App is appropriate given it now writes
help_viewport_height
- The two-step ensure_selected_visible pattern for navigation is consistent with the existing
navigation_handlers.rs approach

Issues:

1. help_viewport_height as mutable state on App is a design smell. Viewport height is a render-time
 concern, not application state. It's written during render_help_popup and read during event
handling (handle_help_keys). This creates a frame-lag: on the very first keypress after opening
help, help_viewport_height is 0 (initialised in open_help via set_scroll_offset(0) but never set).
The adjusted height will be wrong until the first render frame completes.

// app.rs:513
self.help_list.update_item_count(context.bindings.len());
self.help_list.set_scroll_offset(0);
// help_viewport_height is still 0 here
2. render_scroll_indicators called twice per render site for above/below. The split above/below
calls work but produce a confusing API — a caller passing show_above=false, items_above=0 just to
get the below indicator feels wrong. A struct or two-field tuple would be cleaner, or the function
could take an Option for each side. Minor, but it was touched in this PR so it's worth noting.
3. update_item_count(0) used for "reset" (lines 870, 884, 1707). The intent is clearing the list,
but zeroing total_items is semantically different from "close/reset". If ListComponent ever gains
invariants around total_items, this could silently break. A reset() method would be clearer.
4. render_help_popup signature is now &mut App but it's called from the render path. Render
functions mutating application state is an architectural concern — it makes render_* functions
harder to reason about and test. The help_viewport_height field is the only reason for this; see
point 1.
5. all_lines is built eagerly (iterating all bindings), then only page_info.visible_indices are
rendered. For typical keybinding counts this is fine, but it's unnecessary work — the visible lines
 could be built directly from visible_indices.

---
Potential Issues / Risks

- Frame-lag on first navigation: If the user opens help and immediately presses j before the first
render, help_viewport_height == 0 means get_adjusted_viewport_height(0) == 0, so
ensure_selected_visible(0) is a no-op. The selection will scroll correctly after the next render.
Low severity but worth a comment.
- render_help_popup not called if help mode is never rendered (unlikely in practice, but
theoretically help_viewport_height stays 0 if render is skipped for any reason).
- No test coverage added for the new scroll logic in the help context — the existing pattern in the
 codebase seems to rely on manual testing, which is noted in the PR description.

---
Suggestions

1. Pass viewport_height into handle_help_keys from the call site, or compute it from a
terminal-size accessor, rather than caching it on App.
2. Consider a ListComponent::reset() method instead of update_item_count(0).
3. Add a render_scroll_indicators_pair variant or use a small struct to avoid the split above/below
 calls.
4. Build rendered_lines directly from page_info.visible_indices to avoid the intermediate all_lines
 allocation.

---
Verdict

The core fix is correct and the approach is sound. The main concern is help_viewport_height on App
creating a render/event coupling — it works in practice due to the TUI render loop but is fragile.
All other issues are minor. Approve with nits — the frame-lag concern is worth addressing before
merge if there's appetite, otherwise it should at minimum be documented.

cards.description:
Plan: Decompose app.rs into Focused Modules

Context

crates/kanban-tui/src/app.rs is a 2,060-line god object with 58 public fields spanning unrelated concerns: mode navigation, focus tracking, entity selection, filtering, multi-select, dialog state, sprint views, relationships, animations, persistence, and UI state. All 9 handler files (impl App) freely mutate any field. This makes it impossible to discover where to add/change something without reading the entire file, and causes constant merge conflicts.

The goal is purely structural: split fields and their co-located logic into focused sub-structs in named modules with zero behavioral change. After this refactor, adding a new sprint feature means editing sprint_view.rs. Adding a filter means editing filter.rs. The App struct becomes a thin orchestrator.

Target Structure

crates/kanban-tui/src/app/
├── mod.rs          ← Thin App struct + new() + run() + handle_key_event() + execute_action()
├── mode.rs         ← AppMode, DialogMode, ModeManager (push/pop/open_dialog/is_dialog/get_base_mode)
├── focus.rs        ← Focus, CardFocus, BoardFocus, FocusState
├── selection.rs    ← SelectionHub (board/card/sprint selection + active indices)
├── filter.rs       ← FilterState (sprint filters, hide_assigned, sort field/order, search, filter_dialog)
├── multi_select.rs ← MultiSelectState (selected_cards, selection_mode_active)
├── dialog_input.rs ← DialogInputState (import, priority, column, sprint_assign, task_list_view selections)
├── sprint_view.rs  ← SprintTaskPanel enum, SprintViewState (panel + card lists + components)
├── relationship.rs ← RelationshipState (card_ids, selected, selection, search, parents/children lists)
├── view.rs         ← ViewState (strategy, card_list_component, viewport_height, last_frame_area)
├── animation.rs    ← CardAnimation, ANIMATION_DURATION_MS, AnimationState
├── persistence.rs  ← PersistenceState (save_file, app_config, file_watcher, channels)
└── ui_state.rs     ← UiState (banner, help_list, help_pending_action, card_navigation_history)

Migration Steps (each must compile before proceeding)

Step 1: app.rs → app/mod.rs (mkdir + mv). Files Touched: 0. Effort: 5 min
Step 2: Extract enums to mode.rs, re-export. Files Touched: mod.rs. Effort: 20 min
Step 3: Extract Focus/CardFocus/BoardFocus/SprintTaskPanel to focus.rs, sprint_view.rs. Files Touched: mod.rs. Effort: 15 min
Step 4: Extract CardAnimation + constant to animation.rs. Files Touched: mod.rs. Effort: 10 min
Step 5: Introduce ModeManager with Deref; mode+mode_stack → mode: ModeManager. Files Touched: mod.rs + ~20 write sites in handlers/ui.rs. Effort: 75 min
Step 6: Introduce FocusState; 3 fields → focus: FocusState. Files Touched: 9 handler files, ui.rs, render_strategy.rs, keybindings/registry.rs. Effort: 45 min
Step 7: Introduce SelectionHub; 5 fields → selection: SelectionHub. Files Touched: all 9 handlers, app.rs, ui.rs, state/snapshot.rs. Effort: 75 min
Step 8: Introduce FilterState; 7 fields → filter: FilterState. Files Touched: app.rs, navigation/sprint/card/filter_handlers, state/snapshot.rs. Effort: 40 min
Step 9: Introduce MultiSelectState; 2 fields → multi_select: MultiSelectState. Files Touched: navigation/popup/card_handlers, app.rs. Effort: 20 min
Step 10: Introduce DialogInputState; 6 fields → dialog_input: DialogInputState. Files Touched: popup/card/column/detail_view/board_handlers. Effort: 25 min
Step 11: Introduce SprintViewState; 5 fields → sprint_view: SprintViewState. Files Touched: app.rs, popup/card/detail_view_handlers, ui.rs. Effort: 35 min
Step 12: Introduce RelationshipState; 7 fields → relationship: RelationshipState. Files Touched: navigation/popup/card/detail_view_handlers. Effort: 30 min
Step 13: Introduce ViewState; 4 fields → view: ViewState. Files Touched: app.rs, navigation/card_handlers, ui.rs. Effort: 20 min
Step 14: Introduce AnimationState; 1 field → animation: AnimationState. Files Touched: app.rs, card_handlers. Effort: 20 min
Step 15: Introduce PersistenceState; 6 fields → persistence: PersistenceState. Files Touched: app.rs, state/mod.rs only. Effort: 20 min
Step 16: Introduce UiState; 4 fields → ui: UiState; keep App shims. Files Touched: app.rs, detail_view_handlers. Effort: 20 min
Step 17: Move method bodies into sub-struct impls (populate, apply_sort, sync, switch_strategy, animation tick). Files Touched: app.rs + sprint_view/view/animation modules. Effort: 45 min

Total: ~8 hours

Critical Files

- crates/kanban-tui/src/app.rs → becomes app/mod.rs
- crates/kanban-tui/src/ui.rs — updated in steps 6, 11, 13, 16
- crates/kanban-tui/src/state/snapshot.rs — apply_to_app accesses active_board_index + current_sort_field; updated in steps 7 and 8
- crates/kanban-tui/src/keybindings/registry.rs — reads app.mode, app.focus, app.card_focus, app.board_focus; updated in steps 5 and 6
- crates/kanban-tui/src/handlers/detail_view_handlers.rs — touches the most sub-struct categories; use as integration canary

Verification

After each step: cargo check --package kanban-tui
After all steps: cargo build && cargo test --package kanban-tui && cargo clippy -- -D warnings

cards.description:
## Context

`kanban-mcp` currently shells out to the `kanban` CLI binary for all operations (board/column/card/sprint CRUD). This creates two problems:

1. **Build cost**: Nix builds of `kanban-mcp` must also build the full `kanban-cli` binary as a runtime dep.
2. **Storage backend isolation**: When KAN-159 lands, the MCP server cannot participate in pluggable storage — it is locked into whatever store the CLI subprocess uses, with no injection point.

## Relationship to KAN-159

KAN-159 establishes `DynStore = Arc<dyn PersistenceStore + Send + Sync>` as the abstraction seam in the TUI. The same pattern needs to apply to `kanban-mcp`. Without this card, MCP is stranded on JSON forever even after SQLite ships.

## Goal

Extract `crates/kanban-cli/src/handlers/` into a new `kanban-service` crate whose functions accept `Arc<dyn PersistenceStore + Send + Sync>`. Both `kanban-cli` and `kanban-mcp` depend on `kanban-service` and wire up their own store instance.

## Target Dependency Graph

```
kanban-cli --+
             +--> kanban-service --> kanban-persistence (PersistenceStore trait)
kanban-mcp --+                            ^              ^
                                   JsonFileStore     SqliteStore
```

## Work Items

- [ ] Create crates/kanban-service/ with handlers migrated from kanban-cli/src/handlers/
- [ ] Handlers accept Arc<dyn PersistenceStore + Send + Sync> instead of reading disk directly
- [ ] Update kanban-cli to depend on kanban-service (no behavioral change)
- [ ] Rewrite kanban-mcp/src/context.rs to call kanban-service directly (replace executor.rs subprocess model)
- [ ] Remove kanban from crates/kanban-mcp/default.nix nativeBuildInputs and postInstall wrap
- [ ] Update kanban-mcp integration tests to not require KANBAN_BIN

## Acceptance Criteria

- kanban-mcp Nix derivation has no dependency on the kanban or kanban-cli binary
- MCP server works with both JSON and SQLite stores (after KAN-159 merges)
- No behavioral regression in CLI or MCP
cards.title: Extract kanban-service crate from kanban-cli handlers

cards.title: Add disabled option support to list components to avoid hardcoded skip logic

cards.description:
Submit the kanban CLI to the Arch User Repository so Arch users can install via `yay -S kanban`.

No approval needed — push and it goes live immediately.

## Prerequisites

- AUR account at https://aur.archlinux.org
- SSH key registered in AUR profile:
  ```
  ssh-keygen -f ~/.ssh/aur
  # add contents of ~/.ssh/aur.pub to AUR account > My Account > SSH keys
  ```
- Add to ~/.ssh/config:
  ```
  Host aur.archlinux.org
    IdentityFile ~/.ssh/aur
    User aur
  ```

## Package Name

Use `kanban` — not taken in official repos, `kanban-bin` is taken but for a different project (GitLab kanban). Plain source build gets the plain name.

## PKGBUILD

Create a `PKGBUILD` file:

```bash
# Maintainer: Your Name <email>
pkgname=kanban
pkgver=0.3.5
pkgrel=1
pkgdesc="Terminal-based kanban board with MCP server integration"
arch=("x86_64")
url="https://github.com/youruser/kanban"
license=("MIT")
makedepends=("rust" "cargo")
source=("$pkgname-$pkgver.tar.gz::https://github.com/youruser/kanban/archive/v$pkgver.tar.gz")
sha256sums=("SKIP")

build() {
    cd "$pkgname-$pkgver"
    cargo build --release --locked --bin kanban
}

package() {
    cd "$pkgname-$pkgver"
    install -Dm755 "target/release/kanban" "$pkgdir/usr/bin/kanban"
    install -Dm644 LICENSE "$pkgdir/usr/share/licenses/$pkgname/LICENSE"
}
```

Replace sha256sums SKIP with the real hash once the release tarball exists:
```
curl -L <tarball-url> | sha256sum
```

## Submission

```bash
git clone ssh://aur@aur.archlinux.org/kanban.git
cd kanban
cp /path/to/PKGBUILD .
makepkg --printsrcinfo > .SRCINFO
git add PKGBUILD .SRCINFO
git commit -m "Initial import"
git push
```

## Ongoing Maintenance

- Update pkgver + sha256sums on each release, regenerate .SRCINFO, push
- Watch AUR comments for bug reports
- If you stop maintaining, disown via the AUR web UI


AUR auto-publish workflow
---

 After each GitHub release of kanban, the AUR package at aur.archlinux.org/kanban needs to be updated with the new version and sha256. This should be fully automated via a separate GitHub Actions workflow — decoupled from the release job so a failure doesn't block a
 release.

 No shared scripts, no flake inputs between repos. Just a standalone workflow with ~20 lines of shell.

 Files to create

 .github/workflows/aur-publish.yml (new, in main kanban repo)

 Triggered by release: published. Clones the AUR repo, updates PKGBUILD and .SRCINFO, commits and pushes.

```yaml
 name: Publish to AUR

 on:
   release:
     types: [published]

 jobs:
   aur-publish:
     name: Update AUR package
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     steps:
       - uses: cachix/install-nix-action@v27
         with:
           github_access_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
           extra_nix_config: |
             experimental-features = nix-command flakes

       - name: Setup AUR SSH key
         run: |
           mkdir -p ~/.ssh
           echo "${{ secrets.AUR_SSH_KEY }}" > ~/.ssh/aur_key
           chmod 600 ~/.ssh/aur_key
           ssh-keyscan aur.archlinux.org >> ~/.ssh/known_hosts

       - name: Clone AUR repo
         env:
           GIT_SSH_COMMAND: "ssh -i ~/.ssh/aur_key -o IdentitiesOnly=yes"
         run: |
           git clone ssh://aur@aur.archlinux.org/kanban.git /tmp/aur-kanban

       - name: Update PKGBUILD and .SRCINFO
         run: |
           VERSION="${{ github.event.release.tag_name }}"
           VERSION="${VERSION#v}"
           TARBALL_URL="https://github.com/fulsomenko/kanban/archive/v${VERSION}.tar.gz"
           SHA256=$(curl -sL "$TARBALL_URL" | sha256sum | awk '{print $1}')

           cd /tmp/aur-kanban
           sed -i "s/^pkgver=.*/pkgver=${VERSION}/" PKGBUILD
           sed -i "s/^pkgrel=.*/pkgrel=1/" PKGBUILD
           sed -i "s/sha256sums=.*/sha256sums=(\"${SHA256}\")/" PKGBUILD

           MAKEPKG_CONF=$(find /nix/store -name "makepkg.conf" -path "*/pacman-*/etc/*" 2>/dev/null | head -1)
           nix-shell -p pacman libarchive --run \
             "makepkg --printsrcinfo --config ${MAKEPKG_CONF}" 2>/dev/null \
             | grep -v "^Kanban\|^📦\|^🦀" > .SRCINFO

       - name: Commit and push
         env:
           GIT_SSH_COMMAND: "ssh -i ~/.ssh/aur_key -o IdentitiesOnly=yes"
         run: |
           cd /tmp/aur-kanban
           git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
           git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
           git add PKGBUILD .SRCINFO
           git commit -m "Update to ${{ github.event.release.tag_name }}"
           git push
```

 Secret setup

 1. Generate key

 ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f /path/to/key -C "github-actions kanban AUR" -N ""

 2. Store in sops-nix

 Add the private key to your sops secrets and activate it via NixOS. Path managed by sops.

 3. Register public key on AUR

 1. cat /path/to/key.pub
 2. https://aur.archlinux.org → My Account → SSH Public Key → paste and save

 4. Add to GitHub Actions secrets

 gh secret set AUR_SSH_KEY --repo fulsomenko/kanban < <(sops -d path/to/encrypted/aur-key)

 Required secret name: AUR_SSH_KEY

 Verification

 After merging and setting the secret:
 1. Publish a release (or re-publish an existing one) to trigger the workflow
 2. Pull ~/fulsomenko/aur/kanban and check for a new commit
 3. Verify AUR page reflects the version

cards.description:
`aggregate-changelog.sh` produces a flat list of every commit message, losing the
per-feature grouping that older entries (≤ 0.1.10) had. The 0.3.0 entry has 60+
raw commit lines instead of sections grouped by ticket/changeset.

**Current output (0.3.0):**
```
- feat: update MCP server tools for full CLI parity
- feat: bring MCP context to full parity with CLI
- fix: error handling in MCP executor
...
```

**Expected output (matching 0.1.10 style):**
```
### KAN-193 Bring MCP to full feature parity (2026-03-17)
- feat: update MCP server tools for full CLI parity
- feat: bring MCP context to full parity with CLI
...

### KAN-212 Paginated list responses (2026-03-17)
- feat(core): add PaginatedList<T> ...
```

## Cause

`aggregate-changelog.sh` reads changeset files (one per ticket) but concatenates
their descriptions into a single flat section rather than emitting a heading per
changeset.

## Acceptance criteria

- Each changeset file produces its own `###` heading in the CHANGELOG, using the
ticket ID and description from the changeset frontmatter
- Commit-level bullet points appear under their respective heading
- The 0.3.0 entry is retroactively corrected to match the grouped format
- Future releases produce grouped output automatically

find_card_by_identifier uses .find() and returns the first match, which is ambiguous when two cards on different boards share the same card number and prefix (e.g. two boards both using KAN prefix both having card #210).

## Problem

CardIdentifierSearcher::matches() checks prefix+number but has no board scope. If the caller does not filter by board first, the wrong card can be returned — as demonstrated when 'KAN-210' resolved to an older card instead of the newly created one.

## Options

- Add an optional board_id scope to find_card_by_identifier so callers can narrow the search
- In CLI/MCP contexts where a single board is in use, auto-scope to that board
- Return all matches and error if ambiguous (forcing the caller to use a UUID)
- Document the limitation and require UUID when identifier is ambiguous
cards.title: Disambiguate card identifier lookup across boards

cards.description:
Currently undo/redo stores full Snapshot clones (all boards, columns, cards, sprints, graph) for every operation. This is wasteful — editing a single card title clones the entire board state.

Design and implement a command-based undo mechanism where each command produces an inverse operation (e.g., UpdateCard stores the old field values, CreateCard produces DeleteCard). This enables:
- Per-field undo granularity for external editor edits
- Significantly reduced memory usage for undo history
- Composable batch undo (a bulk operation stores N inverse commands as one entry)

Scope:
- Define an InverseCommand trait or extend Command with fn inverse() -> Box<dyn Command>
- Migrate existing commands to produce inverses
- Update HistoryManager to store inverse commands instead of Snapshots
- Update KanbanContext.undo()/redo() to execute inverses
- Ensure external editor mutations (board name, card title, card metadata JSON) use per-field inverses
- Maintain backward compatibility: snapshot-based undo can coexist during migration

Depends on: KAN-264/KAN-265 (history-aware execute in KanbanContext)
cards.title: Command-based undo: per-field inverse operations instead of full snapshots

cards.description: Currently search is limited (KAN-236, KAN-237 cover partial groundwork). Need a first-class search experience: full-text search across card titles, descriptions, and tags; filtering by multiple fields simultaneously (priority, status, assignee, points range, due date); search in both TUI (fuzzy, incremental) and CLI/MCP (structured query). Should replace the scattered filter/search workarounds currently spread across the codebase.

cards.description:
## Goal

Replace the single flat `KanbanError` enum (in `kanban-core`) with per-layer error types that have precise, minimal responsibility. This is the foundation for all future error handling across the codebase.

## Current Problem

`KanbanError` in `kanban-core` is used by every crate, meaning:
- Persistence concepts (`ConflictDetected`, `Io`) sit next to domain concepts (`CycleDetected`, `NotFound`)
- The core crate couples upward to higher-layer concerns
- Callers cannot match precisely — `NotFound(String)` loses type information
- Graph errors (`CycleDetected`, `SelfReference`, `EdgeNotFound`) are domain-specific but in core

## Target Architecture

```
kanban-core        → KanbanError (thin top-level wrapper, used by service + CLI + TUI + MCP)
kanban-domain      → DomainError (NotFound, Validation, DependencyError)
kanban-persistence → PersistenceError (Io, Serialization, ConflictDetected)
```

Each layer only knows its own error type. Boundaries convert via `#[from]`.

## Layer Design

### kanban-domain: DomainError

```rust
#[derive(Error, Debug)]
pub enum DomainError {
    #[error("{entity} {id} not found")]
    NotFound { entity: &'static str, id: Uuid },

    #[error("validation error: {0}")]
    Validation(String),

    #[error(transparent)]
    Dependency(#[from] DependencyError),
}

#[derive(Error, Debug)]
pub enum DependencyError {
    #[error("cycle detected: adding this edge would create a circular dependency")]
    CycleDetected,

    #[error("self-reference not allowed")]
    SelfReference,

    #[error("edge not found")]
    EdgeNotFound,
}
```

`NotFound { entity: &'static str, id: Uuid }` — typed id, readable message, no enum bloat as domain grows.

Helper constructors on `DomainError` keep call sites clean:
```rust
impl DomainError {
    pub fn board_not_found(id: Uuid) -> Self { Self::NotFound { entity: "board", id } }
    pub fn card_not_found(id: Uuid)  -> Self { Self::NotFound { entity: "card",  id } }
    pub fn column_not_found(id: Uuid)-> Self { Self::NotFound { entity: "column",id } }
    pub fn sprint_not_found(id: Uuid)-> Self { Self::NotFound { entity: "sprint",id } }
    pub fn archived_card_not_found(id: Uuid) -> Self { Self::NotFound { entity: "archived card", id } }
}
```

### kanban-persistence: PersistenceError

```rust
#[derive(Error, Debug)]
pub enum PersistenceError {
    #[error("IO error: {0}")]
    Io(#[from] std::io::Error),

    #[error("serialization error: {0}")]
    Serialization(String),

    #[error("file conflict: {path} was modified by another instance")]
    ConflictDetected {
        path: String,
        #[source]
        source: Option<Box<dyn std::error::Error + Send + Sync>>,
    },
}
```

### kanban-core: KanbanError (top-level wrapper)

```rust
#[derive(Error, Debug)]
pub enum KanbanError {
    #[error(transparent)]
    Domain(#[from] DomainError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    Persistence(#[from] PersistenceError),

    #[error("internal error: {0}")]
    Internal(String),
}
```

TUI, CLI, and MCP work with `KanbanError`. They can match on `KanbanError::Domain(DomainError::NotFound { entity, id })` when they need precision, or treat all errors uniformly for display.

## Migration Steps

1. **Add `DomainError` + `DependencyError` to `kanban-domain`**
   - New file: `crates/kanban-domain/src/error.rs`
   - Export from `crates/kanban-domain/src/lib.rs`

2. **Add `PersistenceError` to `kanban-persistence`**
   - New file: `crates/kanban-persistence/src/error.rs`
   - Export from `crates/kanban-persistence/src/lib.rs`

3. **Update `kanban-core` KanbanError**
   - Depends on `kanban-domain` and `kanban-persistence` (check if circular — may need to move KanbanError out of core entirely, or keep core as the aggregator crate)
   - Remove `NotFound`, `Validation`, `Io`, `Serialization`, `ConflictDetected`, `CycleDetected`, `SelfReference`, `EdgeNotFound`, `Connection`

4. **Update `kanban-domain` command and graph code**
   - All commands return `DomainResult<()>` (type alias for `Result<T, DomainError>`)
   - Graph errors return `DependencyError`

5. **Update `kanban-persistence`**
   - All persistence code returns `PersistenceResult<T>`

6. **Update `kanban-service`**
   - Service methods return `KanbanResult<T>` as today
   - `?` operator handles conversion via `#[from]`

7. **Update TUI, CLI, MCP**
   - Match arms updated where needed
   - `cargo check` drives this mechanically

## Watch Out For

- `kanban-core` currently has no dependencies on other workspace crates — if `KanbanError` wraps `DomainError`, core would need to depend on domain, inverting the dependency flow. Consider making `kanban-service` own the top-level error instead, with `kanban-core` remaining a pure abstractions crate (traits + result type only).
- `KanbanResult<T>` type alias must be updated at its definition site

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `DomainError` defined in `kanban-domain` with `NotFound { entity, id }`, `Validation`, `Dependency` variants
- [ ] `DependencyError` sub-enum with `CycleDetected`, `SelfReference`, `EdgeNotFound`
- [ ] `PersistenceError` defined in `kanban-persistence`
- [ ] `KanbanError` in core (or service) wraps both via `#[from]`
- [ ] No stringly-typed `NotFound(String)` anywhere in the codebase
- [ ] `cargo test --workspace` passes
- [ ] `cargo clippy --workspace` passes clean
- [ ] KAN-171 can use `DomainError::card_not_found(id)` directly in CommandContext helpers

## Problem

The `sqlite` feature in `kanban-cli` is opt-in, meaning neither `default.nix` nor `nixpkgs/package.nix` ship with SQLite storage support. Users who open a `.db`/`.sqlite`/`.sqlite3` file get no backend match.

## Changes Required

### 1. `crates/kanban-cli/Cargo.toml`
Add `sqlite` to the default features:
```toml
default = ["tui", "sqlite"]
```

### 2. `crates/kanban-service/Cargo.toml`
Add `sqlite-storage` to the default features:
```toml
default = ["json-storage", "sqlite-storage"]
```

### 3. `default.nix`
No changes needed — it already builds with default features (unless `withTui` is false, in which case `--no-default-features` is passed and SQLite would also be excluded, which is fine for the MCP-only use case).

### 4. `nixpkgs package.nix`
No changes needed — plain `buildRustPackage` picks up defaults. The sqlx sqlite feature bundles its own SQLite (no extra `nativeBuildInputs` required).

## Build Implications

| Concern | Impact |
|---|---|
| Compile time | sqlx + bundled SQLite C compilation adds time to clean builds (~30-60s). Incremental builds unaffected. |
| Binary size | ~1-2 MB increase from statically linked SQLite engine. |
| System deps | None — sqlx 0.8 bundles SQLite by default, no system library needed. |
| Cross-platform | SQLite C code compiles everywhere Rust does, `platforms = all` stays valid. |
| Runtime | Zero cost if user never opens a SQLite file — factory just registers in StoreRegistry. |

## Affected Crates
- `kanban-cli` (feature gate)
- `kanban-service` (feature gate)
- `kanban-tui` (already has `sqlite` feature, will be activated transitively via `kanban-cli`)
cards.title: Make SQLite a default feature in kanban-cli

## Context

KAN-256 fixed SQLite `.db` loading by adding a second async load path in `run()`, but introduced some issues worth cleaning up.

## Issues to Address

1. **Extension allowlist duplicates `SqliteStoreFactory::matches`** — hardcoded `"db" | "sqlite" | "sqlite3"` in `App::new()` must stay in sync with the factory. Unify by always deferring to `store.load()` when `state_manager.store().is_some()`, removing the extension check entirely.

2. **JSON files get loaded twice** — once via `import_board_from_file` in `new()`, then again via `store.load()` in `run()` (since `JsonStoreFactory` also creates a store). The store load wins but the first is wasted work with double migration.

3. **Restore removed comment** — `// Clear undo/redo history after initial file load (not an undoable action)` was removed without reason.

4. **No test for async store load path** — add an integration test that creates a SQLite store, saves data, and verifies it loads correctly on startup.

## Proposed Fix

Make `store.load()` in `run()` the **only** initial load path when a store exists. Remove `import_board_from_file` from `new()` entirely. Adjust `test_failed_import_clears_save_file` to test through the async path.

## Context
Current `JsonFileStore` loads entire state into memory and serializes full JSON on every save. This is O(n) for both read and write, blocking scalability past ~1000 cards.

## Architecture: Implement Behind PersistenceStore Trait
The `PersistenceStore` trait in `kanban-persistence/src/traits.rs` is the seam for adding new storage backends.

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1: Schema Design
Create `schema.sql` with tables for: metadata, boards, columns, cards, sprints, archived_cards. Add indexes for common queries (cards by column, cards by sprint).

### Phase 2: SqliteStore Implementation
New file: `kanban-persistence/src/store/sqlite_store.rs`
- Use `sqlx` with SQLite driver (async-compatible)
- Implement `PersistenceStore` trait
- Transaction wrapping for atomic operations
- Connection pooling for concurrent access

### Phase 3: Incremental Saves (Key Optimization)
Instead of full-state snapshots:
- Track dirty entities in `DirtyTracker` struct
- Only INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE changed rows
- Use `updated_at` timestamps for conflict detection

### Phase 4: Migration from JSON
- Detect `.json` vs `.db` file extension
- Auto-migrate: load JSON -> create SQLite -> write all entities
- Keep JSON as backup until verified

## SOLID Considerations
- **Single Responsibility**: SqliteStore only handles persistence, not domain logic
- **Open/Closed**: Add new store without modifying existing code
- **Liskov**: SqliteStore substitutable for JsonFileStore via trait
- **Dependency Inversion**: TUI/CLI depend on PersistenceStore trait, not concrete impl

## Abstraction for JSON vs SQL
Create shared `StoreOperations` trait for common patterns that both JsonFileStore and SqliteStore implement.

## Files to Create/Modify
- `crates/kanban-persistence/Cargo.toml` - add sqlx, feature flag
- `crates/kanban-persistence/src/store/sqlite_store.rs` - new
- `crates/kanban-persistence/src/store/mod.rs` - export SqliteStore
- `crates/kanban-persistence/src/schema.sql` - DDL
- `crates/kanban-persistence/src/migration/json_to_sqlite.rs` - new
- `crates/kanban-cli/src/main.rs` - store selection logic

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] SqliteStore implements PersistenceStore trait
- [ ] Feature flag: `--features sqlite` to enable
- [ ] JSON->SQLite migration preserves all data
- [ ] Incremental saves (not full snapshots)
- [ ] Concurrent read safety via connection pool
- [ ] Benchmarks showing improvement over JSON

## Context
Domain layer uses command pattern (`kanban-domain/src/commands/`), but commands are not persisted. Need to evaluate if this adds value or just complexity.

## Current Implementation Analysis

### What Exists
- `Command` trait with `execute()` and `description()`
- Commands for all CRUD operations
- `CommandContext` with mutable refs to all state
- Command descriptions logged to `VecDeque<String>` (audit only)

### What's Missing for Event Sourcing
- Commands not persisted to storage
- No replay mechanism
- No event versioning
- No projection rebuilding
- No undo/redo

### Questions to Answer
1. Are commands persisted? -> No, only snapshots
2. Is this event-sourcing? -> No, just structural pattern
3. Can we implement undo/redo? -> Not without persisting commands
4. Does the abstraction help? -> Provides uniform API, but adds indirection

## Evaluation Criteria
- Keep if: Command pattern enables future undo/redo, improves testability
- Simplify if: Just adding boilerplate without benefit

## Recommendation
Keep command pattern BUT document its purpose:
- Enables uniform operation interface for TUI/CLI
- Provides audit log via descriptions
- Future-proofs for undo/redo if commands are persisted
- Add `Undoable` trait for commands that support reversal

## Files to Analyze
- `crates/kanban-domain/src/commands/mod.rs`
- `crates/kanban-domain/src/commands/*.rs` - all command impls
- `crates/kanban-tui/src/state/mod.rs` - command execution

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Document command pattern purpose in code comments
- [ ] Add `Undoable` trait (empty for now, marks intent)
- [ ] Create `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` explaining design decisions
- [ ] Decision: keep, simplify, or extend for undo/redo
cards.title: Evaluate command pattern implementation

## Problem

`next_sprint_number` on `Board` is stored state that has drifted out of use:
- `allocate_sprint_number()` (the only method that reads/writes it) is **never called** anywhere in the codebase
- Sprint numbers are actually assigned via `sprint_counters: HashMap<String, u32>` (keyed by prefix) through `get_next_sprint_number(prefix: &str)` in `board.rs`

`sprint_counters` has the same fundamental problem — it is stored state that can diverge from reality when the file is hand-edited or migrated. `ensure_sprint_counter_initialized()` already derives the correct starting value from existing sprints (max sprint_number for the prefix + 1), proving the information is fully derivable.

This caused a concrete bug: `demo/fixtures/demo.json` ended up with two sprints both labelled KAN 1 because `sprint_counters` fell out of sync during manual editing.

## Options

1. **Remove `next_sprint_number` only** — dead field cleanup. Low risk, small change.
2. **Remove both `next_sprint_number` and `sprint_counters`** — replace with a computed function `next_sprint_number_for(prefix, sprints) -> u32` that returns `max(sprint.sprint_number where sprint.prefix == prefix) + 1`, defaulting to 1. Eliminates the entire class of drift bugs.

Option 2 is preferred. The max-scan cost is negligible at this scale.

## Affected files

- `crates/kanban-domain/src/board.rs` — remove field + `allocate_sprint_number()`, replace `get_next_sprint_number()` with pure function
- `crates/kanban-domain/src/commands/sprint_commands.rs` — pass sprints slice to the new function instead of mutating board counter
- `crates/kanban-persistence-sqlite/src/upserts.rs` — drop `next_sprint_number` column writes
- `crates/kanban-persistence-sqlite/src/builders.rs` — drop `next_sprint_number` field read
- `crates/kanban-persistence-json/` — field will naturally stop being serialized once removed from struct
- Tests in `kanban-service`, `kanban-persistence-sqlite` that reference `next_sprint_number`
- `demo/fixtures/demo.json` — fix the duplicate KAN 1 sprint_number while touching this

cards.description:
## Context

Discussed in CAT-260 session. Two related but distinct capabilities worth designing before adding more backends.

---

## Use Case 1: Board routing (per-board store selection)

Different boards live in different backends:

```
work_board    → work.sqlite
personal      → ~/notes/personal.json
archive_2024  → archive://2024.tar.gz
```

Requires a routing layer: board_id → store locator. Currently absent from the architecture. The StoreRegistry can hold many factories but each invocation resolves to exactly one store instance.

---

## Use Case 2: Entity federation (intra-board splitting)

Within a single board, different entity types live in different stores:

```
board metadata  → config.json
cards           → cards.sqlite        (queryable, indexed)
attachments     → ~/docs/             (markdown files, one per card)
activity log    → append-only.log
```

---

## Key design insight

A FederatedStore could itself implement PersistenceStore. It assembles a Snapshot by reading from multiple sub-stores and writes back to the right one per entity type. From KanbanContext perspective it is still one store — federation is opaque to the rest of the system. This fits the existing plugin pattern: FederatedStoreFactory is just another factory that instantiates multiple sub-stores internally.

```
KanbanContext
  └── FederatedStore  (implements PersistenceStore)
        ├── SqliteStore     ← cards, columns
        ├── JsonStore       ← board metadata, config
        └── MarkdownStore   ← card descriptions as .md files
```

---

## Open design questions

- **Consistency**: if writing cards to sqlite succeeds but writing markdown fails, what is the state? Need a compensation or rollback strategy.
- **Assembly**: what is the merge key when loading? board ID? card ID?
- **Config shape**: how does a user express 'cards for board X go to Y, attachments go to Z'? Needs a BoardLocator or routing config format.
- **Migration**: how do you move an entity from one sub-store to another without data loss?
- **Cross-store operations**: moving a card between boards in different stores requires coordinating two stores with no transaction guarantee between them.

---

## Relationship to backend consolidation (CAT-260)

The current one-to-one (app → store) architecture is fine for now. This is a future direction. Decide the shape of BoardLocator and FederatedStore before adding more backends so the config format does not need to change later.
cards.title: Multi-store architecture: board routing and entity federation

cards.description: Currently KanbanContext loads the entire dataset into Vec<T> fields on startup. PersistenceStore is a snapshot interface (load/save blobs). This makes storage backends interchangeable serialization formats only — SQLite's query engine goes unused. Goal: PersistenceStore becomes a query interface (list_boards, list_cards(filter), get_card, upsert_card, delete_card, etc.). KanbanContext becomes a thin coordinator that delegates reads/writes to the store. SQLite then runs real WHERE clauses. JSON backend becomes honest: loads everything, queries in memory. Undo/redo needs rethinking without full-world clones.
cards.title: Refactor storage to on-demand querying instead of full snapshot in memory

## Documentation Revamp — Root README + 9 Crate READMEs

Complete rewrite of all project documentation to be accurate, dense, and compelling.

### Files Modified

| File | Lines | Notes |
|------|-------|-------|
| `README.md` | 373 | Full rewrite: hero tagline, feature grid, installation, quick start, full keybinding tables for all 5 contexts, architecture diagram + crate table, persistence details, roadmap |
| `crates/kanban-mcp/README.md` | 182 | All 40 tools documented (was 14); organized by section with parameter types |
| `crates/kanban-domain/README.md` | 307 | All models fully documented: Board, Column, Card (every field), Sprint, SprintLog, ArchivedCard, FieldUpdate, DependencyGraph, HistoryManager, error hierarchy, business rules |
| `crates/kanban-tui/README.md` | 321 | New: module structure, AppMode/DialogMode enums (all 26 dialogs), focus system, view strategies, event loop, full keybinding tables, editor integration, clipboard, components |
| `crates/kanban-service/README.md` | 236 | Expanded: all KanbanContext fields, complete method tables for all operation groups, undo/redo API, state accessors, utility functions, command execution flow |
| `crates/kanban-cli/README.md` | 180 | New: full command reference for board/column/card/sprint/top-level, card identifier resolution, JSON output format, BatchOperationResult, shell completions, env vars |
| `crates/kanban-core/README.md` | 174 | Fixed phantom traits (removed Repository/Service/Loggable that don't exist); documented AppConfig, PaginatedList, Page/PageInfo, InputState, SelectionState, Editable, Graph |
| `crates/kanban-persistence/README.md` | 159 | New: PersistenceStore, StoreFactory, StoreRegistry, ChangeDetector, Serializer, MigrationStrategy, all shared types |
| `crates/kanban-persistence-json/README.md` | 101 | New: V2 envelope format, save/load flows, atomic writes, conflict detection, debounced saving, JsonStoreFactory match logic |
| `crates/kanban-persistence-sqlite/README.md` | 112 | New: SqliteStore, connection pool config, all 14 tables, transactional save/load, schema versioning, SqliteStoreFactory magic-byte detection |

### Key Fixes
- MCP README previously listed 14 tools; now documents all 40
- kanban-core previously referenced phantom `Repository`, `Service`, `Loggable` traits not present in source
- kanban-tui and kanban-cli had no READMEs
- Card model was missing `sprint_logs`, `completed_at`, `assigned_prefix`, `card_prefix` field docs
- Status transition semantics (Done <-> completed_at) were undocumented
- All keybinding tables verified against `crates/kanban-tui/src/keybindings/` source
cards.title: Revamp all documentation — root README + 9 crate READMEs

cards.description:
## Problem

The carry-over dialog exists but is not reachable from the natural sprint completion flow. Three separate gaps:

---

### Gap 1: Auto-trigger silently skipped when no Planning sprint exists

**File:** `crates/kanban-tui/src/handlers/sprint_handlers.rs` lines 135-150

When completing a sprint, the dialog only appears if a Planning sprint already exists. If there is none, the dialog is skipped entirely with no feedback. The user has no idea carry-over was even possible.

**Fix:** After sprint completion, if there are uncompleted cards but no Planning sprint, show a message:
```
"Sprint completed. X cards not carried over (no planning sprint available)."
```
Or offer to create a new Planning sprint inline.

---

### Gap 2: 'c' key silently does nothing on a completed sprint

**File:** `crates/kanban-tui/src/handlers/sprint_handlers.rs` lines 88-106

`handle_complete_sprint_key()` returns `None` silently when the sprint is already Completed or Cancelled. The 'c' keybinding description still says "Complete this sprint" regardless of sprint status.

**Fix options:**
- Change keybinding hint text to "Carry over cards" when viewing a completed sprint
- Or show an error/info message: "Sprint already completed. Use M to carry over cards."

---

### Gap 3: 'M' key for carry-over is undiscoverable

**File:** `crates/kanban-tui/src/keybindings/sprint_detail.rs` lines 109-114
**File:** `crates/kanban-tui/src/handlers/detail_view_handlers.rs` lines 705-714

'M' is the only way to trigger carry-over from a completed sprint view, but it is not shown in the context help bar when the sprint is completed. Users have no way to know it exists.

**Fix:** Ensure 'M' ("Carry over cards") appears in the bottom help bar when viewing a Completed or Cancelled sprint.

---

### Summary of expected UX

| User action | Current behaviour | Expected behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| Press 'c' to complete sprint with uncompleted cards + Planning sprint exists | Dialog shown | (correct) |
| Press 'c' to complete sprint with uncompleted cards + no Planning sprint | Silent skip | Show message / offer to create Planning sprint |
| View completed sprint, press 'c' | Silent no-op | Show hint to use 'M' or rebind |
| View completed sprint, press 'M' | Works but undiscoverable | Show in help bar |
cards.title: KAN-210 follow-up: carry-over dialog disconnect from sprint completion flow

cards.description:
The release workflow continued to the tag/GitHub release steps even after publish-crates.sh exited with code 1. Add safeguards so a partial publish causes the entire job to abort and surface a clear failure, preventing tag/version mismatches and orphaned crates on crates.io.

## Resolution

Already implemented. publish-crates.sh has `set -uo pipefail` and the publish loop explicitly calls `exit 1` on failure (lines 43-45). The CI job will abort on any crate publish failure.

No code change needed.
cards.title: Fail release job immediately if any crate publish fails
