cards.description:
## Stakeholder summary — Where, Why, How

**Where.** New top-level `docs/MIGRATIONS.md` (or expanded section in `crates/kanban-persistence/README.md`) plus a CI check that pins the doc against the source of truth (`FormatVersion` enum and the registered migration steps). Touches no production code paths — pure documentation infrastructure.

**Why.** Today the migration story is reconstructable but only by reading across six places: the `FormatVersion` enum (`crates/kanban-persistence/src/traits.rs`), the migrator's dispatch table (`crates/kanban-persistence-json/src/migration/migrator.rs`), per-version transform modules (`v1_to_v2.rs`, `v2_to_v3.rs`, `split_graph.rs`), the three persistence READMEs, the changesets, and `CLAUDE.md` / `CONTRIBUTING.md`. An operator asking "I have a file at V4 — what does the upgrade do, and can I roll back?" has to grep four crates and read three READMEs to find the answer. Worse, the docs drift (CLAUDE.md and CONTRIBUTING.md were stale for several releases and only refreshed in PR #287). We hit a real data-loss bug during PR #287's smoke testing because the cross-backend / cross-binary compatibility story wasn't written down — an older binary downgraded `version: 6` to `version: 3` and the next V6-aware load silently destroyed every edge.

The deeper concern: the kanban app supports two persistence backends (JSON, SQLite), three apps (CLI, MCP, TUI), and a growing format history. Without a central matrix, any new migration risks repeating "implicit knowledge" mistakes — backups in the wrong places, support promises the binaries don't honour, migration paths that silently lose data when versions and binaries don't line up. We need one document that any operator or contributor can read in 5 minutes to understand the full story.

**How.** One markdown doc with five sections: (1) per-version envelope shape + transform table, (2) backend support matrix (which binaries handle which format, where the boundaries are), (3) backup file behaviour, (4) operator FAQ (forward-compat, backward-compat, rollback, cross-backend migration via `kanban migrate`), (5) extension guide for new format versions. Pinned by a CI check that asserts `FormatVersion` enum length matches the matrix row count and the legacy-table drop list in the SQLite store is referenced by name.

---

## Engineering spec

### Doc structure

**Proposed file:** `docs/MIGRATIONS.md` (new top-level docs directory) — easier to deep-link from issues and CI than nested under a crate README.

```markdown
# Kanban file-format migration matrix

This document is the single source of truth for how kanban data files
evolve. Cross-reference against `FormatVersion` (in
`crates/kanban-persistence/src/traits.rs`) — these two must agree.

## 1. JSON envelope versions

| Version | First shipped | Envelope shape changes | Transform module | Backup written on upgrade |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| V1 | (genesis) | Root-level `{boards, ...}` with no version field | — | `.v1.backup` |
| V2 | (envelope) | Wraps payload in `{version, metadata, data}` | `v1_to_v2.rs` | — |
| V3 | KAN-… | Drops board `prefix_counters`, card `assigned_prefix` and `card_prefix`; renumbers colliding cards | `v2_to_v3.rs` | — |
| V4 | KAN-… | Adds `command_log` array (later removed in KAN-405) | (no transform — shape stable from V3) | `.v3.backup` |
| V5 | KAN-… | Refines `command_log` (later removed in KAN-405) | (no transform) | `.v4.backup` |
| V6 | KAN-504 | Splits `graph.cards.edges` into three sub-graphs `parent_child` / `blocks` / `relates` keyed by relation kind; per-kind metadata (severity, kind) populated with defaults for migrated edges | `split_graph.rs` | `.v5.backup` |

V4 and V5 are version bumps with shape-stable envelopes (the
command_log addition/refinement). KAN-405 removed the command_log
field from persistence; the field is ignored by current readers.
Files at V3/V4/V5 are structurally equivalent to the split-graph
transform, which is why all three feed the same migration step.

## 2. SQLite schema

| Component | Source of truth | Current value |
|---|---|---|
| Envelope schema version | `metadata.schema_version` column | `1` (never bumped) |
| Edge tables | per-kind: `spawns_edges`, `blocks_edges`, `relates_edges` | KAN-504 |
| Retired tables (auto-dropped on open) | `command_log` (pre-KAN-405 schema), `undo_state`, `card_edges` (single-table pre-KAN-504) | dropped by `drop_legacy_*_if_present` helpers in `sqlite_store.rs` |

SQLite has no migration framework — schema evolution happens
through one-shot legacy-table drops on `SqliteStore::open`. New
tables are added by editing `schema.sql`; obsolete tables are
dropped at open time. If a future change requires breaking schema
evolution (e.g. adding a NOT NULL column with a backfill), a real
migration framework will be needed; see the extension guide below.

## 3. Backup files

| Backup | Created by | Cleaned by |
|---|---|---|
| `<path>.v1.backup` | V1→V2 step in `v1_to_v2.rs` | not auto-cleaned (kept indefinitely; user removes manually) |
| `<path>.v3.backup` | V3→V6 step in `migrator.rs` before the split-graph transform | removed on successful migration; preserved on failure |
| `<path>.v4.backup` | V4→V6 step | same |
| `<path>.v5.backup` | V5→V6 step | same |

The `.v{N}.backup` files are the operator's escape hatch: if a
post-V6 binary opens an older file and the migration succeeds, the
backup is removed. If migration fails, the backup is left in place
and a `tracing::error!` records the path.

## 4. Backend support matrix

| Format | JSON backend | SQLite backend | Pre-KAN-504 binaries | KAN-504+ binaries |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| V1 | reads & migrates | — | reads & migrates to V2 | reads & migrates to V6 |
| V2 | reads & migrates | — | reads natively | reads & migrates to V6 |
| V3 | reads & migrates | — | reads natively | reads & migrates to V6 |
| V4 | reads & migrates | — | reads natively (with command_log) | reads & migrates to V6 (command_log ignored) |
| V5 | reads & migrates | — | reads natively | reads & migrates to V6 |
| V6 | **writes** | (graph-aware tables) | **CANNOT READ** (rejects unknown version OR silently downgrades the version field, leading to data loss on next V6-aware load) | reads natively |

**Critical:** running a pre-KAN-504 binary against a V6 JSON file is
unsafe. Some pre-V6 binaries downgrade the version field on save
while preserving the V6-shape data; without the idempotency guard
landed in PR #287 commit `0c2316d`, the next V6-aware load would
silently wipe every edge. Treat older binaries as read-only against
V6 files; do not let them save.

## 5. Operator FAQ

**Q: Which version is my file?** — `head -c 200 kanban.json | jq .version` for JSON; `sqlite3 kanban.sqlite "SELECT schema_version FROM metadata"` for SQLite.

**Q: Can I roll back to an older version?** — If you still have the `.v{N}.backup`, yes — `cp kanban.json.v5.backup kanban.json`. Otherwise: no in-tree downgrade path; restore from your own backups.

**Q: What does `kanban migrate <source> <backend>` do?** — Opens `source` (any supported format), writes to the target backend (JSON ↔ SQLite). Not coupled to the format-version chain — it just snapshots-and-saves. Does NOT create a backup of the source; preserve the source yourself if needed.

**Q: What if a future format bump arrives while a user is on V6?** — Same chain extends: a new `v6_to_v7.rs` (or `v6_to_v7` block in `migrator.rs`) registers the transform, `FormatVersion::V7` joins the enum, and this matrix gets a new row. The version detector caps at V6 today; bump there too.

**Q: Are formats backwards-compatible?** — On a single binary: yes (reads any older format). Across binaries: no, you cannot load a V6 file with a pre-V6 binary. The factory will downgrade or refuse depending on the binary's age.

## 6. Adding a new format version

When a domain change requires a new format version:

1. **Add the variant to `FormatVersion`** in `crates/kanban-persistence/src/traits.rs`. Bump the integer in `from_u32` / `to_u32`.
2. **Write the transform** in `crates/kanban-persistence-json/src/migration/v{N-1}_to_v{N}.rs`. Mirror the `v2_to_v3.rs` or `split_graph.rs` shape: pure function on `serde_json::Value`, atomic write at the file level.
3. **Add the migration arm to `migrator.rs::migrate`**. Pick a `.v{N-1}.backup` strategy.
4. **Update the JSON reader's accepted-version range** in `json_file_store.rs` (`2..=N`).
5. **If SQLite schema also changes**, edit `schema.sql` and add a `drop_legacy_*_if_present` helper if older shapes need removal.
6. **Add this matrix's row, then the test** at the bottom of this card (see §7).
7. **Write the changeset** describing the change and what binaries must be on for forward-compat.

## 7. CI pin

A small test in `crates/kanban-persistence/tests/migration_matrix_doc.rs` (or similar) reads `docs/MIGRATIONS.md` and asserts:
- The row count in §1 equals `FormatVersion` enum length
- Every legacy-table drop helper named in `sqlite_store.rs` appears in §2
- The current `FormatVersion::V6` matches the last row of §1
- The doc was edited in the same commit as any `FormatVersion` enum change (via a CI grep, not test)

If the doc drifts, the test fails loudly, forcing the next format change to update the matrix in the same PR.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `docs/MIGRATIONS.md` exists with the six sections above, populated with the current state (V1..V6 JSON, SQLite schema_version=1, the three legacy-table drops)
- [ ] All cross-references (file paths, function names, commit hashes for the data-loss bug) resolve in the current tree
- [ ] CI test pins the row count = enum length invariant
- [ ] `kanban-persistence/README.md`, `kanban-persistence-json/README.md`, `kanban-persistence-sqlite/README.md` each link to `docs/MIGRATIONS.md` as the canonical reference
- [ ] `CLAUDE.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` reference `docs/MIGRATIONS.md` instead of restating the chain inline
- [ ] Workspace gate clean (fmt / clippy / test)

### Out of scope

- Implementing forward-compat (older binaries reading V6) — that's a separate architectural decision; this card just documents the lack of it
- A SQLite migration framework — separate card if needed
- Auto-detecting "binary downgraded my file" on load — partially addressed by the PR #287 idempotency guard; this card documents the protection
- `kanban migrate` backup behaviour — documented here, not changed

### Risks

- **Documentation drift**: the CI pin mitigates structural drift but can't catch every prose inconsistency. Reviewers must read the doc when bumping versions.
- **Operator surprise**: this doc will be the first time many users learn that pre-V6 binaries are unsafe against V6 files. A clear warning in the FAQ + a release-notes mention covers it.
- **Cross-backend gaps**: SQLite's `schema_version=1` mechanism is largely unused; if a future SQLite migration is needed, the matrix expands and this card's structure may need to split per-backend.
cards.title: Centralise migration history into docs/MIGRATIONS.md with CI pin

## Stakeholder summary — Where, Why, How

**Where.** New parameterised test module under `crates/kanban-persistence-json/tests/` (or extends the existing `migrator.rs` inline tests). No production code changes.

**Why.** The migration coverage today exercises the chain in fragments but never end-to-end:

| Test | Path covered |
|---|---|
| `test_migrate_v1_to_v2` | V1 → V2 only |
| `test_migrate_v2_to_v3_*` (5 tests on different shape concerns) | V2 → V3 only |
| `test_migrate_v1_to_v3_via_chain` | V1 → V2 → V3 (good — first chain test) |
| `test_split_graph_*` (split-graph step in isolation) | V3/V4/V5 → V6 transform only, no chain |
| `test_migrate_v4_to_v6_skips_legacy_steps` | V4 → V6 (skips V1 / V2 steps) |
| `test_migrate_v5_to_v6_skips_legacy_steps` | V5 → V6 (skips V1 / V2 steps) |
| `test_migrate_v6_to_v6_is_a_noop_byte_for_byte` | V6 idempotency |

What we don't have:
- **V1 → V6 end-to-end** (the full real-world upgrade path: V1 → V2 → V3 → split_graph)
- **V2 → V6**
- **V3 → V6 with real data** (only structural step tests exist — no "loaded a real V3 fixture with cards, columns, sprints, and edges; ran the chain; loaded the resulting V6 envelope into `KanbanContext`; asserted every field round-trips")

Why it matters: each step's test runs against a minimal fixture tailored to that step. A user's actual file usually has cards, columns, sprints, edges, archived cards, sprint logs — combinations that the per-step tests don't exercise. A V1 user upgrading to V6 in one shot crosses three transforms; a regression in any one (or in their composition) could pass per-step tests and silently lose data on the chain. The data-loss bug found during PR #287's smoke test (commit `0c2316d`) was caught only because real-world data was used; a chain test against fixtures would have surfaced similar issues earlier.

**How.** A parameterised test that, for every starting version V1..V5, writes a realistic fixture, runs `Migrator::migrate(Vn, V6, path)`, then loads the resulting file through `JsonFileStore` into a full `KanbanContext` and asserts the rehydrated state matches expected baseline (boards / columns / cards / archived / sprints / graph — including per-kind edge metadata). One small fixture suite shared across all starting versions, with per-version-specific shape adjustments.

---

## Engineering spec

### Coverage matrix to deliver

For each starting `Vn` where `n ∈ {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}`, a test verifying:

1. Fixture round-trips to a valid V6 envelope on disk
2. Resulting V6 envelope deserialises into a `KanbanContext` without error
3. Per-domain assertions:
   - Boards preserved (count, names, card_prefix, card_counter)
   - Columns preserved (count, names, board_id, position, wip_limit)
   - Cards preserved (count, title, status, priority, column assignment, sprint binding)
   - Archived cards preserved
   - Sprints preserved (count, status, prefix, name_index)
   - Graph edges: per-kind counts match expected (parent_child / blocks / relates), metadata survives where applicable (severity, kind, archived_at)
4. Backup files written for V3/V4/V5 starting points (`.v3.backup` / `.v4.backup` / `.v5.backup`); cleaned up on success
5. Resulting file is byte-shape compatible with a freshly-saved V6 file (no leftover legacy fields like `direction` / `weight`)

### Proposed test layout

```
crates/kanban-persistence-json/tests/migration_chain.rs
├── fn make_v1_fixture(path: &Path)   // root-level shape
├── fn make_v2_fixture(path: &Path)   // envelope, no version-3 changes yet
├── fn make_v3_fixture(path: &Path)   // post-prefix-cleanup, pre-split graph
├── fn make_v4_fixture(path: &Path)   // V3 shape + command_log (ignored)
├── fn make_v5_fixture(path: &Path)   // V4 shape + refined command_log (ignored)
├── async fn assert_v6_round_trips(path: &Path, expected: &Baseline)
└── #[tokio::test] per starting version:
    - test_full_chain_v1_to_v6_preserves_all_domain_data
    - test_full_chain_v2_to_v6_preserves_all_domain_data
    - test_full_chain_v3_to_v6_preserves_all_domain_data
    - test_full_chain_v4_to_v6_preserves_all_domain_data
    - test_full_chain_v5_to_v6_preserves_all_domain_data
```

Each fixture seeds a non-trivial graph (2 boards, 3 columns per board, 5 cards per column, 2 sprints, 2 archived cards, 4 parent_child edges, 2 blocks edges with Severity::High, 1 relates edge with RelatesKind::Duplicates). The V1/V2/V3 fixtures use the pre-split-graph schema (`graph.cards.edges`), the V4/V5 fixtures add a phantom `command_log` field that should be ignored, and the post-migration V6 envelope is asserted edge-for-edge against a hand-built baseline.

### Specific assertions per chain

**V1 → V6 chain:**
- V1 → V2 step adds the envelope (verified by intermediate state? — probably not; only end state matters here)
- V2 → V3 step strips `prefix_counters`, `assigned_prefix`, `card_prefix`; renumbers any collisions
- V3 → V6 step (split_graph) routes `ParentOf` to `parent_child`, `Blocks` to `blocks` with `severity: "Medium"`, `RelatesTo` to `relates` with `kind: "General"`
- `.v3.backup` is written before the split and removed on success
- The final envelope loads via `JsonFileStore::open` and the resulting `KanbanContext` contains the right boards, cards, edges

**V3 → V6 chain:**
- Already-V3 envelope skips V1→V2 and V2→V3 steps
- Goes directly to split_graph
- `.v3.backup` written + removed
- Same final assertions

**V4 / V5 → V6:**
- `command_log` field is ignored (no error, no preservation — the field is dead since KAN-405)
- `.v4.backup` / `.v5.backup` written + removed

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Five parameterised tests (one per starting version V1..V5) pass
- [ ] Each test exercises real `Migrator::migrate(Vn, V6, path)` (not just the split_graph step in isolation)
- [ ] Each test loads the resulting file through `JsonFileStore::open` and into `KanbanContext`, asserting domain data round-trips
- [ ] Per-kind edge metadata (severity / kind / archived_at) is preserved for V3/V4/V5 starting points
- [ ] Backup files are written and cleaned up correctly for V3/V4/V5 starting points
- [ ] V1 and V2 starting points do NOT write a backup before split_graph (current behaviour — flag if this is a gap worth fixing as a separate card)
- [ ] `cargo test --workspace` green
- [ ] Tests run in under 5 seconds total (parameterised over 5 starting versions; each does a real tempfile I/O cycle)

### Out of scope

- Adding backup safety for V1 and V2 starting points (the current chain has no rollback for V1/V2 starts; if this is wrong, a separate card)
- Migrating SQLite legacy shapes — that has its own helpers; not part of the JSON chain
- Round-tripping through SQLite as well — would be a separate cross-backend test

### Notes / why the bug discovered in PR #287 wouldn't have been caught

The data-loss bug fixed in commit `0c2316d` (idempotency guard when version claims pre-V6 but data is already V6-shape) is a different scenario from the clean V1→V6 chain. The chain tests proposed here would exercise the "honest" upgrade path; the bug we hit needed a fixture with a deliberate version/shape mismatch (which is now pinned by `test_transform_preserves_v6_shape_data_when_version_claims_pre_v6`). Both kinds of test are valuable and complementary.

### Suggested priority

Medium. The lack of an end-to-end test isn't a known-bug-waiting-to-happen, but it's a real coverage gap that would surface composition issues. Worth scheduling alongside the migration-matrix doc (card #518) — the matrix and the chain test together establish "this is what we support and this is how we prove it."
cards.title: End-to-end V1..V5 → V6 migration-chain test with real domain data

cards.description:
## Goal
Establish ONE well-tested construction boundary for every domain entity (Board, Column, Card, Sprint) so that every way an entity comes into existence -- wire DTO, CLI args, MCP request, and persistence rehydration -- funnels through explicit, type-checked factory entry points. Cement the DTO->domain and persistence->domain relations with tests so neither can drift silently.

## Why now
- The HTTP server transition needs a clean, deterministic create path. Today `Board::new(name, card_prefix)` accepts only 2 of ~6 create fields, forcing the API handler into a "create-then-update" dance (`CreateBoardRequest::into_parts` returns a follow-up `BoardUpdate`).
- `new()` calls `Uuid::new_v4()` + `Utc::now()` internally -> non-deterministic, untestable, blocks client-supplied IDs.
- Construction logic is scattered: domain `new()`, serde `Deserialize`, and per-backend row->domain mappers (sqlite `conversions.rs`) each rebuild entities independently with no shared contract or drift guard.

## Core model: two construction INTENTS, several ARMS
Construction is not one operation. Split by intent:

A. CREATION -- births a NEW entity; server MINTS identity/time/counters; input is partial + untrusted.
   Arms: `CreateXRequest` DTO (HTTP), CLI create args, MCP create request.
   Consumes a neutral domain spec `NewX`.

B. RECONSTITUTION (rehydration) -- restores an EXISTING entity; all fields (incl. id, created_at, counters) come back verbatim; input is complete + trusted (we wrote it).
   Arms: JSON snapshot deserialize, SQLite row mapping.
   Consumes a complete domain record `XRecord` (full field set).

The "factory" = these two domain primitives + the per-source adapter arms feeding them. Note creation and reconstitution have OPPOSITE trust + completeness models; conflating them is the current mistake.

## Domain-layer primitives (lowest layer; owns invariants)
Per entity:
- `struct NewX { /* only client-supplyable create fields */ }` -- the creation spec.
- `fn X::create(spec: NewX, id: Id, now: DateTime) -> KanbanResult<X>` -- injects identity + clock (DIP), seeds counters, applies defaults, enforces invariants. ATOMIC: one call -> valid entity, no follow-up patch.
- `fn X::reconstitute(record: XRecord) -> X` (or `TryFrom<XRecord>`) -- accepts the full field set verbatim; used ONLY by persistence + tests. Cheap structural validation; assumes invariants already held.

Identity/clock injected via params (or small `IdSource`/`Clock` traits) so creation is deterministic + testable. This alone is a SOLID win independent of the DTO work.

## The arms (where each LIVES -- respects dependency inversion)
- domain (kanban-domain): owns `NewX`, `XRecord`, `create`, `reconstitute`. Zero knowledge of DTOs or storage.
- Wire arm (kanban-service::api::v1): `impl TryFrom<CreateXRequest> for NewX`. Untrusted -> may fail (validation, enum decode).
- CLI arm (kanban-cli) + MCP arm (kanban-mcp): build the SAME `NewX` from their inputs -> same `create`.
- Persistence arms:
  - JSON (kanban-persistence-json): serde -> `XRecord` -> `reconstitute`.
  - SQLite (kanban-persistence-sqlite): row -> `XRecord` -> `reconstitute`. Replaces ad-hoc per-table mapping with a funnel through the one primitive.

Every DTO/CLI/MCP/persistence crate depends on domain (never the reverse), so each arm sits in its own crate and calls DOWN into the domain factory. The DTO is "one arm"; persistence is another; neither lives in domain.

## Field-acceptance policy (the through-line)
A matrix per entity field x arm: which arms may set it.
- Server-managed (id, created_at, updated_at, card_counter, next_sprint_number, position): MINTED by `create`, RESTORED by `reconstitute`, NEVER accepted from a create DTO.
- Client create fields (name, description, prefixes, sort prefs...): accepted by create arms.
- Response DTO exposes id but HIDES internal counters.
This matrix is the contract the tests assert against; it extends the policy already started in the API DTO layer (e.g. `active_sprint_id`/`position` excluded from PATCH).

## Trust + validation model
- Wire/CLI/MCP create: untrusted + partial -> full invariant enforcement + FK checks.
- Persistence reconstitute: trusted + complete -> structural validation + migration only; do NOT re-run business rules that may legitimately differ across format versions.
- FK/uniqueness validation that needs the repository stays in the SERVICE create-handler (async, has the store) -- NOT in pure domain `create` (keep that I/O-free). Two tiers: pure construction (domain) + relational validation (service). Honors the D7 decision: replace any entity but respect foreign keys.

## Test strategy -- cement the relations
- Boundary table tests per entity per arm: input -> spec/record -> entity, asserting every field lands, defaults/invariants for omitted fields, server-managed fields minted-not-accepted.
- DTO<->domain: `CreateXRequest -> NewX -> X` (deterministic with injected id/clock -> EXACT assertions, not "some uuid").
- persistence<->domain round-trip: `X -> snapshot -> XRecord -> reconstitute -> X'` with `X == X'`, for BOTH JSON and SQLite. This is the persistence arm's drift guard.
- Keep the existing exhaustive-destructuring (`no ..`) compile guard so a new field fails to build until every arm + test handles it. Compiler guards STRUCTURE; tests guard SEMANTICS.

## Rollout (TDD, one entity at a time)
1. Board as the template: boundary + round-trip tests (red) -> add `NewBoard`/`BoardRecord` + `create`/`reconstitute` with injected id/clock (green) -> migrate API create handler off `into_parts`/create-then-update -> migrate JSON + SQLite arms onto `reconstitute` -> refactor.
2. Replicate for Column, Card, Sprint as `spawns` children of this epic.
3. Remove the create-then-update kludge once all create arms produce `NewX`.

## Decisions
DECIDED:
- DTO home: keep DTOs as a clean `api` module INSIDE `kanban-service` (no separate `kanban-api` crate now). A well-bounded module extracts to a crate trivially if a standalone consumer (e.g. a Rust client SDK) ever appears -- YAGNI. Option A reduces the pressure for a shared contract crate anyway. MCP drops its bespoke `requests/` and points at the shared `service::api` DTOs.
- id/clock injection: `create` RECEIVES `id` + `now` as plain params; the service/server layer generates them (`Uuid::new_v4()` / `Utc::now()`) and passes them in. Domain `create` calls NEITHER -- keeps it pure + deterministic so the cement tests can assert exact output. Symmetric with `reconstitute`, which already receives id/created_at from the record. Plain params now; a `Clock`/`IdSource` trait only if a future case needs to mint several ids/timestamps mid-construction (extract-when-needed, same as the crate call).

MORE DECIDED:
- `reconstitute` is an INHERENT fn (`Board::reconstitute(rec) -> KanbanResult<Board>`), matching `create` (which must be inherent -- it takes 3 args, can't be From/TryFrom). Both factory doors are named + discoverable. TryFrom would only pay off for generic `T: TryFrom<R>` code, which the per-entity (no-generic-repository) design does not use.
- `XRecord` is a DISTINCT domain record, NOT the entity's own serde. Only `BoardRecord` derives Serialize/Deserialize; the entity itself need not. Two reasons this matters: (1) reusing serde-into-entity is an UN-FUNNELLED construction path -- serde would mint a Board field-by-field with no invariants and no factory call, violating "every entity born through the factory"; (2) serde derives silently default/skip an added field, breaking the compile-lock, whereas a Default-free `BoardRecord` destructured exhaustively in `reconstitute` makes a new field a compile error. Bonus: persistence format evolves independently of the entity's in-memory shape. Cost: one mirror record + mapping per entity (modest; covered by the lock).
- Client-supplied IDs: IN SCOPE for v1. `id` stays a `create` PARAMETER (identity), not a field of `NewX` (content). Service decides the value: `let id = request.id.unwrap_or_else(Uuid::new_v4)` then `create(spec, id, now)`. Domain is indifferent to the source. Pulls in: (a) uniqueness check at the service FK/uniqueness tier -> 409 on collision; (b) enables idempotent PUT-create (`PUT /boards/{id}` create-or-replace), aligning with the RFC PUT semantics in the API spec. The create request DTO carries an optional `id` the service reads.

ALL MAJOR DECISIONS NOW RESOLVED -- spec ready to build Board-first.

## Out of scope / deferred
- Generic `Factory<T>` trait -- entities are heterogeneous; a generic factory is the wrong abstraction (same conclusion reached for the per-entity layout in KAN-762).
- Builder ergonomics beyond what create needs.

## Related
- Companion to the v1 API DTO surface (KAN-713) and the API CRUD spec epic (KAN-757); prerequisite for the HTTP backend (kanban-server / service `http` module).

## Hard requirement (primary acceptance criterion) -- refined
Manufacture every domain entity from ANY source -- TUI, CLI, MCP, API/server, and the persistence backends -- through one factory, with the DTO <-> persistence <-> domain relationship LOCKED AT COMPILE TIME.

Mechanism (canonical, Default-free boundary types = the lock):
- Two boundary types per entity, neither with a `Default` impl and never constructed with a `..` rest pattern:
  - `NewX` -- client-settable create fields. Fed by TUI / CLI / MCP / API create DTO.
  - `XRecord` -- complete field set (id, timestamps, counters). Fed by persistence-json (serde) + persistence-sqlite (rows).
- Because they are Default-free and `..`-free, you cannot build one without naming every field. Add a field to `XRecord` and every persistence arm + `reconstitute` fails to compile; add a field to `NewX` and every create arm fails to compile. This is automatic in the SOURCE->domain direction -- no convention required.

What the compiler does vs does not guarantee (be honest in the design):
- Compiler -> COVERAGE: no field is silently forgotten by any arm. Forgetting an arm is a build error.
- Tests -> CORRECTNESS: per-arm round-trip tests assert each field maps to the RIGHT place (`X -> record -> reconstitute -> X'`, `X == X'`). The compiler cannot verify `dto.name` went to `domain.name` rather than `domain.description`.
- The DECOMPOSE direction (Board -> row / Response) only breaks on a new field if destructured exhaustively -- enforce the existing "no `..`" rule with a CI grep over the conversion modules so it is not purely convention.

Net guarantee: compiler locks that every field is accounted for in every arm; tests lock that every field lands correctly. Together that is the DTO-to-persistence-to-domain compile-time lock.

See target topology diagram (hub-and-spoke: sources -> NewX/XRecord boundary types -> create/reconstitute -> Board -> decompose).

## Composition model -- granular per-entity, NOT top-down from Board
Verified the domain model is flat + relational, not a nested aggregate:
- `Board` has no `columns`/`cards` field (flat scalars + counters only).
- `Column` holds `board_id`; `Card` holds `column_id` (+ `sprint_id`). Children point UP by FK.
- No entity owns a `Vec` of children -- the only `Vec<Column>`/`Vec<Card>` are repository `list_*` query results, never owned fields. Separate tables/collections, assembled at query time.

Consequences for the factory:
- FOUR independent sibling factories (Board, Column, Card, Sprint), each with its own `NewX`/`XRecord`/`create`/`reconstitute`. NO god-factory on Board; constructing a Board does not construct its columns/cards.
- No construction-ordering dependency between factories -- `Card::create` never calls `Board::create`. A relationship is DATA: `Card::create` takes a `column_id: Uuid` field, not a `Column` object.
- FK existence validation lives at the SERVICE tier (has the repository), not in the pure domain `create`. Keeps each factory leaf-level + I/O-free, which is what makes the granular/bottom-up approach work.

Composition is a separate concern from construction:
- Composite CREATE (import a whole board; "new board with default columns") = service-layer orchestrator calling the granular factories in FK order (board -> columns -> cards). The import path is already this shape.
- Read-side composition (a "board detail" view) = assembled at query time from the flat entities into an aggregate response DTO; the factories are not involved.

Rationale: bottom-up granular is the only shape consistent with the existing flat/relational storage (separate SQLite tables, flat snapshot collections, per-entity in-memory stores). A top-down Board-owns-everything factory would fight the schema. The per-entity Board diagram is the TEMPLATE for one of four siblings, not a root that builds the others.

## Consumption model + crate placement
DECIDED (Option A, entity-centric): in-process apps consume the DOMAIN ENTITY; the DTO is the wire projection at the API edge ONLY; `XRecord` is internal persistence<->domain plumbing, NEVER app-facing. No double-consumption path. (This SUPERSEDES the earlier framing of apps consuming persistence records directly.) Shared boundary types still must live at/below the lowest level every consumer reaches.

Current state (verified):
- No `kanban-api` crate exists yet; v1 DTOs live in `kanban-service::api::v1`.
- MCP DUPLICATES the DTOs: both `kanban-mcp/src/requests/board.rs` and `kanban-service/.../boards/requests.rs` define their own `pub struct CreateBoardRequest`. The requirement is meant to end this.
- Dep reality: cli/tui/mcp depend on domain+persistence+service; `kanban-server` depends on core+domain+service but NOT persistence.

Why `XRecord` lives in `kanban-domain` (not persistence): `reconstitute(XRecord)` lives in domain, so the record type must be in domain (or core) -- otherwise domain would depend on persistence, inverting the layering. This holds independent of Option A; it is NOT about apps consuming records (under Option A they do not).

Target placement:
- kanban-domain: entities + `NewX` + `XRecord` + `XUpdate` + `create`/`reconstitute`. Lowest layer. Apps consume the ENTITY from here (Option A); `XRecord` is consumed only by persistence + `reconstitute`, not by apps.
- kanban-api (NEW, lean; depends only on kanban-domain): wire DTOs (`CreateXRequest`, `XResponse`, `Update/ReplaceXRequest`) + DTO<->domain conversions. Every app + server (+ future client SDK) depends on it -> one shared contract, no per-app duplication. Carries no service/persistence weight.
- kanban-persistence(+json+sqlite): consumes `XRecord` from domain (rows/serde <-> record).
- kanban-service: depends on api+domain+persistence; orchestration, FK validation, backends-as-modules.
- apps (cli/tui/mcp/server): depend on kanban-api for the contract + kanban-service for behavior. MCP drops its bespoke `requests/` and uses the shared DTOs.

Compile-lock survives the split: kanban-api conversions exhaustively destructure the domain boundary types, so a new domain field breaks every DTO arm at build time -- now across a crate boundary (stronger isolation).

DECIDED: keep DTOs as a clean `api` module in `kanban-service` (NOT a separate `kanban-api` crate) -- see Decisions section. The placement below describes the LOGICAL homes; the api module + domain types live in their current crates, extractable later if a standalone consumer appears.

See crate-layering diagram (core -> domain -> {api, persistence} -> service -> apps; apps reach api for DTOs and domain for records; server->domain records edge has no persistence dep).

## Read side (consumption) -- symmetric to the write-side factory  (DECIDED: Option A)
Consumption mirrors construction. Where construction is sources -> NewX/XRecord -> entity, consumption is entity -> projection:
- In-process (TUI / CLI / MCP / service logic): consume the rich domain ENTITY. ONE in-process surface; full fidelity + behavior; internal fields (counters) available when needed.
- Wire edge (HTTP API; CLI/MCP JSON output): project entity -> response DTO via `From<&X> for XResponse` (the read counterpart of `create`/`reconstitute`). External clients consume the DTO: stable, versioned, field-controlled (hides counters).
- `XRecord`: internal persistence<->domain plumbing only; never surfaces to apps.

Anti-patterns explicitly rejected:
- DTO as the universal in-process type (anemic; loses domain behavior + hidden fields). Rejected because this TUI is rich, not thin/presentational. Would only fit a thin HTTP client (Option B).
- Persisting DTOs / DTO-as-storage-format -- couples the storage schema to API versioning. This is WHY `XRecord` is a separate record from the DTO; do not re-couple them.

Net: ONE in-process type (entity) + ONE wire projection (DTO) at DIFFERENT boundaries (in-process vs over-the-wire) -- not two redundant app-facing consumption sites. The double-consumption path is explicitly NOT taken.

## Execution learnings — Board A+B spike (VALIDATED against real code)
Slices A (KAN-772) + B (KAN-773) were executed to green in a worktree (domain 505 tests, json 84, sqlite 52 — all green; clippy -D warnings + fmt clean; commits 815b85f4, 89ae26f5). Learnings below; most apply to ALL FOUR entities — fold into each A/B card before executing.

1. **`!Deserialize` removal has MORE forcing functions than `Snapshot`.** Removing `<E>: Deserialize` (slice B) breaks EVERY in-domain `#[derive(Deserialize)]` type holding the entity. For Board that was FOUR: `Snapshot.boards`, `ImportEntities.boards` (commands/board_commands.rs), `BoardExport.board` + `AllBoardsExport` (export/models.rs). Each B-slice MUST `grep -rn "derive(Deserialize)"` + the entity and funnel ALL sites, not just Snapshot. Expect ~3-4 per entity (import + export DTOs).
2. **Snapshot-serde mechanism DECIDED (resolves the open question):** per-field `#[serde(with = "...")]` adapters living in each `<E>_factory.rs`, providing BOTH a vec adapter (`<e>_vec_serde` for `Vec<E>`) AND a single adapter (`<e>_serde` for one `E`) — NOT a `SnapshotRecord` mirror, NOT a private mod inside snapshot.rs (the sites span modules, so the adapter must be public). In-crate import path is `crate::error::KanbanResult` (NOT `kanban_domain::...` from inside the crate).
3. **serde-default helper fns must be `pub(crate)`** for the verbatim `Deserialize`-migration move (slice A) to compile — the `#[serde(default="fn")]` attrs reference currently-private fns. Recurs in any entity with such helpers (Card, Sprint likely have them).
4. **`From<&E> for <E>Record` must deref `Copy` fields** (e.g. `TaskListView`), not `.clone()` them — clippy `clone_on_copy` fails under `-D warnings`. Audit each record's `Copy` fields.
5. **Import path:** `KanbanResult`/`KanbanError` come from `kanban_domain::error` (re-exported at crate root), NOT `kanban-core`.
6. **SQLite round-trip fixtures must null FK columns** (Board: `active_sprint_id`/`completion_column_id`) or the standalone insert hits `FOREIGN KEY constraint failed`. Recurs for Column.board_id, Card.column_id/sprint_id, Sprint.board_id.
7. **Compile-lock empirically VERIFIED:** adding a dummy field to `BoardRecord` broke all three doors — `Deserialize` init (E0063), `reconstitute` destructure (E0027), `From<&Board>` init (E0063). The lock works as designed.
8. **Corrected A->B sequencing HOLDS:** A additive (keeps Deserialize) + B funnels all sites then removes the derive = workspace green at the boundary. Confirmed by compiling all downstream crates.

## Execution learnings — Card A+B spike (refinements to the above)
Card slices A (KAN-782) + B (KAN-783) executed to green (domain 519, json 84, sqlite 52/38/21; commits 4cdc5c10, 728d49aa). Refines the Board learnings:

- AMEND #1: the `grep derive(Deserialize) + entity` sweep must ALSO catch direct `serde_json::from_str::<E>` in TESTS, not just `#[derive(Deserialize)]` structs. Card had 4 struct sites + 1 test site (editable.rs). Count the test sites.
- AMEND #3: the `pub(crate)` serde-default-helper gotcha applies ONLY to entities with NAMED default fns (`#[serde(default = "fn")]`) — Board (and likely Sprint). Card uses plain attr-level `#[serde(default)]` (zero values), so `CardRecord` is a PLAIN DERIVE with no hand-written Deserialize and no pub(crate) promotion. Check each entity.
- #9 (embedding wrappers + card-owned side tables): a wrapper type that embeds the entity (e.g. `ArchivedCard { card: Card }`) takes a SINGLE `#[serde(with = "<e>_serde")]` on the embedded field and KEEPS its own derive — do NOT build a parallel `<Wrapper>Record`. A card-owned side table (e.g. `sprint_logs`) reassembles into `XRecord` INSIDE the `row -> record -> reconstitute` funnel with no call-site change (the existing positional `row_to_x(row, side_rows)` design absorbs it).
- #10 (Snapshot stays Vec<E>): `Snapshot.<e>` fields stay `Vec<E>` with `#[serde(with = "<e>_vec_serde")]`; the in_memory_store layer is UNTOUCHED (no apply_snapshot/snapshot_impl edits, no KanbanResult propagation). Do NOT migrate `Snapshot` to hold `Vec<XRecord>` — an earlier per-entity card sketch suggested this; it is unnecessary churn. The Sprint B card (KAN-788) likely carries the same over-engineered sketch — apply the lean Board pattern there too.


## Execution learnings — Foundation spike (KAN-770)
- The compile-lock has TWO independent halves: (a) TYPE-level (NewX/XRecord Default-free + no `..`, enforced by the grep CI guard) and (b) ERROR-layer (exhaustive match arms, enforced by the compiler). The Foundation spike validated (b) end-to-end + the guard mechanics of (a); the A/B/C/D slices exercise (a)'s type side.
- CONVENTION (pin it): per-entity records live in `crates/kanban-domain/src/<e>_factory.rs` (NewX + XRecord + create/reconstitute/From + the <e>_vec_serde/<e>_serde adapters). The CI guard glob and the record-file naming must agree.
- Any embedded shell/CI script in a card MUST be executed before shipping — the Foundation card shipped a no-op guard that passed its probe. Treat scripts in cards as untested until run.

## Execution learnings — Board service vertical spike (C + D-core)
Board slices C (KAN-774) + D-core (KAN-791) executed to green (kanban-service + kanban-domain; commits ca6de0ec, 82f4e34b). Validated: killing create-then-update (atomic create, no follow-up patch), client-id + AlreadyExists/409 end-to-end, the thin-shim strategy avoiding all caller churn. Two new learnings, the first is SAFETY-CRITICAL and applies to ALL FOUR D-core cards (791/793/795/797):

- #11 (FREEZE THE CREATE-COMMAND STRUCT SHAPE): `CreateX` domain commands are (a) serialized into the persisted `command_log` table (`commands_json`) and deserialized on REPLAY, and (b) built as struct literals at dozens of sites across domain/service/TUI (CreateBoard: 47 sites / 18 files incl. kanban-tui). The per-entity D cards' sketch of "rework `CreateX` to carry `{id, spec: NewX, now}`" is UNSAFE — it breaks reading existing command logs AND mass-churns literals (and pulls in a tui rebuild). CORRECT PATTERN: keep the `CreateX` struct shape unchanged; change ONLY `execute`'s BODY to funnel through `X::create(...)`. Put full create-field fidelity + id-uniqueness conflict + FK validation in a SERVICE-tier `create_X_from_spec(id: Option<Uuid>, spec: NewX)` that is an INHERENT method on `KanbanContext` (NOT on the `KanbanOperations` trait — that trait is dual-implemented by TUI+CLI, so adding to it churns tui). The spike routed the rich spec path via `ImportEntities { boards: vec![board], .. }` (single entity, correct inverse); the alternative is a new `CreateXFromSpec` command carrying a serde-capable `NewX`. The wire card should pick; `ImportEntities` is the lower-risk default. NOTE: at the frozen-command tier `now` stays internal (`Utc::now()` in execute, same determinism as today); only the service spec path is deterministic/injected.
- #12 (`From<X>` -> `From<&X>` is safe): the response projection (`BoardResponse::from`) had one (test) caller; the by-ref switch needed only `.clone()` on owned fields + Copy reads. Expect the trivial swap for the other entities.
- `into_parts` (the create-then-update kludge) had ZERO production callers — dead code with only a unit test. Deletion is risk-free; the cards' "an HTTP handler runs create-then-update" framing is wrong (no handler exists yet). A sibling `columns/conversions.rs::into_parts` still exists (Column D-core handles it).

## Execution learnings — Card D-core dual-FK spike (KAN-795)
Executed green (domain 523, +11 service integration tests; commit ac21b407). Validated dual-FK service-tier validation.

- #13 (SPRINT-LOG SEEDING TRAP — silent data loss): do NOT funnel `NewCard.sprint_id` into `Card::create` inside `CreateCard::execute`. `Card::create` sets `sprint_id` WITHOUT seeding a `SprintLog`, and the post-create `assign_to_sprint` SHORT-CIRCUITS when `card.sprint_id` already equals the target (card.rs:256) — so the log silently vanishes. Pass `sprint_id: None` into the create spec and let `assign_to_sprint` set the id + log together atomically. Pinned by `test_card_create_does_not_seed_sprint_log_for_present_sprint_id`. (This supports the deferred design question on KAN-781: the sprint association is best treated as an INSERTED assignment, not a direct create-time FK.)
- Dual-FK fit: required column FK -> `KanbanError::not_found("Column", id)`; optional sprint FK -> `not_found("Sprint", id)`; cross-board sprint -> the EXISTING `DomainError::SprintBoardMismatch` (no new variant needed). Client-id collision (live OR archived) -> `already_exists`/409.
- DERIVE the owning board from `column.board_id` (single source of truth). `create_card_from_spec(client_id: Option<Uuid>, spec: NewCard)` takes NO `board_id` param — a caller-supplied one could disagree with the column's board and mis-route minting/the sprint-match. Card-specific (Board/Sprint own board_id directly; Column takes it as create input).
- Ordering: validate ALL FKs + uniqueness BEFORE reading/bumping `card_counter`, so a rejected create never advances the counter (pinned by two counter-unchanged tests).
- #11 confirmed for Card: the frozen `CreateCard` command already carries the full field set, so NO `ImportEntities` reroute and NO new command were needed — just build the frozen command from the spec, change only execute's body.

## Quality gate — SOLID / complexity / performance / modularity (spec + 8-commit spike)
Four-lens principal review of the design AND the executed spike. VERDICT: SOUND and ready to scale; bounded refinements only, no blocking issues.
- SOLID: SOUND. DIP fully respected (domain depends on nothing; id/clock/FK injected at the service edge). SRP/ISP clean (NewX/XRecord/create/reconstitute each one reason to change; boundary types minimal + focused). LSP n/a (heterogeneous entities, no hierarchy = correct). OCP's forced-edits-at-every-arm is the INTENTIONAL drift-guard, not a violation.
- Complexity: PROPORTIONATE. ~16 compiler symbols/entity is isolation (event-sourcing + versioned wire DTOs + two construction intents), not bloat; the create path is 7 hops of BREADTH, each hop <50 lines of DEPTH. No must-simplify. Distinct XRecord earns its keep: forbids the `serde_json::from_str::<Entity>` construction backdoor and powers the compile-lock.
- Performance: PASS at realistic scale (hundreds-to-thousands of entities; factory overhead <5% of load/save, dominated by DB I/O + JSON). ONE real code-quality nit (logged on KAN-783).
- Modularity/coupling/cohesion: HIGH cohesion (each *_factory.rs is exactly one entity's construction concern incl. its serde adapters); HEALTHY coupling — the compile-lock fails LOUD; a field empirically touches ~8 (Board)/10 (Card) LOAD-BEARING files, all necessary (no redundant coupling).

ACTIONS before replicating to Column/Sprint (bounded):
1. PERF: `From<&Card>` clones `sprint_logs` Vec on every write -> borrow instead (KAN-783).
2. CONSIDER a BOUNDED `serde_adapter!(entity, Entity, EntityRecord)` macro to collapse the per-entity vec/single serde-adapter pair (~100 LOC across 4 entities) WITHOUT the wrong abstraction. NOT a generic `Factory<T>` (stays rejected; create/reconstitute arms are entity-specific and must not be unified). Evaluate before the Sprint factory.
3. DOCUMENT THE CONSTRUCTION SEAM (coherence): the FROZEN `CreateX` command (a backward-compat boundary for `command_log` replay) and the service `create_X_from_spec` (the new API entry) BOTH funnel through the SINGLE `X::create`. They are ONE construction mechanism with a persistence-compat boundary, NOT two. A Column/Sprint implementer must change only `execute`'s BODY, never the `CreateX` struct shape (root learning #11). This framing belongs on each D-core card.
4. Confirm the CI-guard fix (foundation, the rg no-op) is scheduled (KAN-770).


## Rerun finding — PUT-create scoping (all entities)
Idempotent PUT-create (create-or-replace at `PUT /v1/<e>/{id}`) is an HTTP-method/handler concern -> it belongs in each entity's D-WIRE card, NOT D-core. D-core = create funnel + client-id uniqueness conflict only. The service-tier `create_or_replace` method + the handler binding live with the consumer wiring. Apply to 792/794/796/798 (wire) and strike the PUT-create step from 791/793/795/797 (core).


## Rerun findings — Board D-wire (consumer wiring, executed first time; commit 5ff33b3d)
Board is now FULLY factory-ized end-to-end: CLI/TUI/MCP/server all create Boards through `create_board_from_spec`; MCP bespoke DTO removed. New cross-entity findings for the D-WIRE cards (792/794/796/798):
- MCP SCHEMARS FEATURE-GATE (real, the cards understated this): rmcp `Parameters<P>` requires `P: schemars::JsonSchema`. The shared service DTO cannot derive it without a layering violation. FIX: add an OPTIONAL `schemars` feature to kanban-service (`#[cfg_attr(feature = "schemars", derive(JsonSchema))]` on each wire request DTO + the enum DTOs; schemars with `uuid1`), enabled ONLY by kanban-mcp. Non-MCP consumers do not pull schemars. Every entity's MCP wiring needs this.
- EDGE WIRE-CASING is a USER-VISIBLE change: projecting CLI/MCP JSON via XResponse flips domain PascalCase enums -> wire snake_case AND drops internal counters. Intended (Option A) but a behavioral change for anyone parsing CLI/MCP JSON -> note it in the changeset. The CLI paginated `list` edge may stay on domain projection (small inconsistency; full edge-projection consistency is a follow-up).
- SERVER was a bare stub -> promote to lib+bin for a typed create seam (handler binds CreateXRequest -> into_new_X -> create_X_from_spec/create_or_replace -> XResponse); transport/router stays in the server epic (KAN-708).
- TUI create was already factory-correct transitively (D-core funneled the CreateX command through X::create); wire step adds characterization tests, not a rewrite.

## Goal-alignment review (2026-06-27) — DECIDED notes from PR #353 final pass

A full goal-alignment review (7 dedicated agents, one per goal cluster) found the goals delivered. Two items recorded as deliberate decisions / tracked findings:

DECIDED — blank-name coercion is a MIGRATION, not a business-rule re-run. `Board::reconstitute` and `Column::reconstitute` coerce a blank/whitespace name to "Untitled" on load (create stays strict). This is permitted by the trust model ("structural validation + MIGRATION only") — it is a forward migration of legacy data that predates the blank-name invariant, not re-running a create-time rule. Rejecting instead would brick a board that legitimately carried a blank name before the factory existed. The asymmetry (Board/Column coerce; Sprint/Card restore verbatim) is principled: only Board/Column ever had the blank-name rule. The migrated value self-heals (persisted on next save). Supersedes any reading of "restore verbatim" as forbidding this coercion.

FINDING (tracked, pre-existing, OUT of factory scope) — SQLite does NOT satisfy the full PersistenceStore contract that JSON does. JSON runs the shared `store_contract_tests!` / `context_contract_tests!` macros (tests/contract.rs); SQLite cannot use them directly because its store construction is async (sqlx needs a Tokio context) while the macro's `StoreFactory` is sync. The portable contract cases were reproduced as bespoke SQLite tests (empty-snapshot roundtrip, metadata increment, instance_id idempotency — commit on PR #353). Two cases are genuine BACKEND DIVERGENCES, deliberately not ported:
  - `exists()` is true right after `open()` (SQLite creates the db file on open; JSON creates on first save). Benign.
  - `save()` has NO optimistic-concurrency / stale-metadata conflict detection — JSON returns `ConflictDetected`, SQLite is last-writer-wins (persistence_store.rs save() just applies + stamps + checkpoints). For two app instances on the same .db this is a silent lost-update where JSON would error. Defensible (a real DB serializes writes at the connection/transaction level) but it is a real cross-backend contract inconsistency. Decide later: (1) accept + document the divergence in the PersistenceStore trait contract, or (2) add an optimistic-metadata guard to SqliteStore::save for parity. Full shared-harness parity additionally needs an async-factory refactor of the contract macros. Candidate for its own card if (2) is chosen.

cards.description:
## 1. Context / why

Root spec: **KAN-769** (`refactor(domain): entity construction factory`). Decided design brief: `/tmp/fc/DESIGN-BRIEF.md`.

This card is the **cross-cutting foundation** for the four per-entity factory subtrees (Board, Column, Card, Sprint). It **precedes ALL entity factory cards** — it establishes the conventions, the compile-lock CI guard, the id/clock seam, and the error mapping that every entity's A/B/C/D slices then follow uniformly. It introduces no entity-specific types itself; it ships the guard + docs + (one) error variant + (one) error-mapping arm that the entity cards depend on.

Depends on nothing. Everything in KAN-769's `spawns` subtree depends on this.

## 2. The `Default`-free + no-`..` rule (the compile-time coverage lock)

The lock works because boundary types are **`Default`-free and never constructed with a `..` rest pattern**. You cannot build one without naming every field, so adding a field is a build error in every arm until each is updated. This is the SOURCE→domain coverage guarantee the compiler gives for free (KAN-769 "Compile-time lock"). Tests still guard CORRECTNESS (right field → right place); the compiler only guards COVERAGE.

The rule applies to **these type families** (per entity X ∈ {Board, Column, Card, Sprint}):

- **`NewX`** — the create spec (client-settable create fields only). Must NOT derive `Default`. Every arm that builds a `NewX` (`From`/`TryFrom<CreateXRequest>`, CLI arg builder, MCP arg builder) destructures its source exhaustively and constructs `NewX` field-by-field with no `..`.
- **`XRecord`** — the complete persisted field set (id, timestamps, counters). The ONLY type deriving `Serialize`/`Deserialize` for persistence; distinct from the entity. Must NOT derive `Default`. `X::reconstitute` destructures it exhaustively; `From<&X> for XRecord` constructs it exhaustively; the SQLite `row_to_x()` and `upsert_x()` and the JSON envelope mapping go through it.
- **Every DTO ⇄ domain conversion module** under `crates/kanban-service/src/api/v1/<entity>/conversions.rs` and `.../response.rs`: each `From`/`TryFrom`/`into_parts` already destructures and constructs exhaustively (see the doc comment at `crates/kanban-service/src/api/v1/boards/conversions.rs:1-5` — *"Each conversion destructures and constructs exhaustively (no `..`) so a new field is a compile error."*). This card promotes that file-local convention to a workspace-enforced rule over the whole conversion + factory surface.

Why this exact set: these are precisely the types on the construct/decompose seam where a forgotten field would silently round-trip wrong (DTO field dropped, persisted column lost). The entity struct itself is exempt — it stops deriving `Deserialize` (per KAN-769), so the only way to mint one is the factory, and the factory's inputs are the locked types above.

`Default::default()` is banned in the same module globs because a `Default` impl re-opens the hole: `XRecord { name, ..Default::default() }` would compile with a missing field. Banning the *call* (the grep below) plus not deriving `Default` on the boundary types is belt-and-braces.

## 3. The CI guard (concrete grep + probe)

### 3a. The guard

A **workspace integration test** in the lowest crate that can see the offending paths is awkward (the conversion modules live in `kanban-service`, the records in `kanban-domain`), and the patterns are pure text. So implement the guard as a **shell script invoked from a new CI job**, mirroring the existing `scripts/*.sh` + `check-crate-list-sync` job pattern already wired into `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (see the `release-validation` job, ci.yml:209-211, which runs `nix develop --command check-crate-list-sync`).

Add `scripts/check-factory-compile-lock.sh`:

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Fails the build if a `..` rest pattern or `Default::default()` appears in the
# factory boundary + DTO conversion modules. These types are Default-free and
# must be destructured/constructed exhaustively so a new field is a compile error
# (the DTO<->persistence<->domain compile-time coverage lock). See KAN-769.
set -euo pipefail

# Path globs the lock covers. Extend as entity factories land.
GLOBS=(
  'crates/kanban-domain/src/**/record.rs'      # XRecord defs + reconstitute + From<&X>
  'crates/kanban-service/src/api/v1/**/conversions.rs'
  'crates/kanban-service/src/api/v1/**/response.rs'
)

# Match either a `..` rest pattern or a Default::default() call.
#   - `\.\.`  inside a struct literal/pattern: the rest pattern.
#   - Default::default()  the banned call.
# We grep with ripgrep (available in the dev shell) over the globs, excluding
# lines that opt out with the audited marker `// lock-exempt:`.
PATTERN='(\.\.[[:space:]]*[},])|Default::default\(\)'

violations=0
for g in "${GLOBS[@]}"; do
  while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
    if matches=$(grep -nE "$PATTERN" "$f" | grep -v '// lock-exempt:'); then
      echo "FACTORY LOCK VIOLATION in $f:"
      echo "$matches"
      violations=1
    fi
  done < <(find . -path "./${g//\*\*/*}" -name '*.rs' -print0 2>/dev/null)
done

# Glob expansion above is approximate; prefer ripgrep when present for true ** support:
if command -v rg >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  violations=0
  for g in "${GLOBS[@]}"; do
    if matches=$(rg -nE "$PATTERN" -g "$g" . 2>/dev/null | grep -v '// lock-exempt:'); then
      echo "FACTORY LOCK VIOLATION:"; echo "$matches"; violations=1
    fi
  done
fi

if [ "$violations" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo ""
  echo "❌ Factory boundary modules must be Default-free and use no \`..\` rest pattern."
  echo "   Destructure/construct every field explicitly so a new field is a compile error."
  echo "   If a \`..\` is genuinely required, annotate the line with \`// lock-exempt: <reason>\`."
  exit 1
fi
echo "✅ Factory compile-lock guard clean"
```

Notes on the regex:
- `(\.\.[[:space:]]*[},])` matches a `..` immediately followed (ignoring whitespace) by `}` or `,` — i.e. a struct rest pattern `Foo { a, .. }` or `..Default::default()` / `..base`. It deliberately does NOT match range expressions like `0..10` (followed by a digit) or `..=`. Tune to `\.\.[A-Za-z_]*[[:space:]]*}` if range false-positives appear in these specific modules (they should not — these files are pure mapping code).
- `Default::default()` catches the explicit call even when the `..` heuristic would miss it.
- The `// lock-exempt: <reason>` escape hatch keeps the guard from being a straitjacket; any exemption is greppable and reviewable.

Make it executable and expose it in the dev shell the same way the other scripts are (they are on `PATH` inside `nix develop`; confirm via `flake.nix`/`scripts/` wiring used by `check-crate-list-sync`). Then add a CI step. Plug it into **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`** as a step on the existing `clippy` (Lint) job, or as its own job mirroring the changeset job:

```yaml
  factory-lock:
    name: Factory Compile Lock
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: cachix/install-nix-action@v27
        with:
          github_access_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          extra_nix_config: |
            experimental-features = nix-command flakes
      - name: Check factory compile lock
        run: nix develop --command check-factory-compile-lock
```

(If wiring a bare-name dev-shell command is more than this card wants, the step can instead run `bash scripts/check-factory-compile-lock.sh` directly without the dev shell, since the script only needs `grep`/`rg`/`find`.)

### 3b. Deliberately-failing probe (PROVE the guard works, then revert)

As part of this card, demonstrate the guard fires:

1. Temporarily edit one covered file (e.g. add a throwaway line to `crates/kanban-service/src/api/v1/boards/conversions.rs`):
   ```rust
   let _probe = BoardUpdate { name: None, ..Default::default() }; // intentional probe
   ```
2. Run `bash scripts/check-factory-compile-lock.sh` locally — it MUST print `FACTORY LOCK VIOLATION` and exit non-zero.
3. **Revert** the probe line.
4. Run the script again — it MUST print `✅ Factory compile-lock guard clean` and exit 0.

Capture both outputs in the PR description as evidence. The probe is never committed; only the passing guard ships.

## 4. The id/clock seam (shared by all entities)

The domain `create` is pure: it **never** calls `Uuid::new_v4()` or `Utc::now()`. The service generates identity + clock and passes them in (KAN-769 Decisions; brief §17):

- Domain signature template (each entity card implements its own): `X::create(spec: NewX, id: Uuid, now: DateTime<Utc>) -> KanbanResult<X>`.
- The create request DTO (`CreateXRequest`) carries an **optional** `pub id: Option<Uuid>` (identity is a `create` parameter, not a content field of `NewX`).
- Service create handler:
  ```rust
  let id = req.id.unwrap_or_else(Uuid::new_v4);
  let now = Utc::now();
  // uniqueness check BEFORE construction (see below)
  let entity = X::create(spec, id, now)?;
  ```
- **Uniqueness check location:** the **service create handler** (it owns the repository / store; the pure domain `create` stays I/O-free — KAN-769 "Trust + validation model" / "FK existence validation lives at the SERVICE tier"). Check `store.get_x(id)` (or the in-memory equivalent) before constructing; if present → collision.
- This is what enables **idempotent PUT-create** (`PUT /x/{id}` create-or-replace): a client-supplied id that already exists either replaces (PUT semantics) or 409s (POST semantics), decided per route by the entity's service card.

## 5. The error model

`create` and `reconstitute` both return `KanbanResult<X>` (alias `Result<T, KanbanError>`, defined at `crates/kanban-domain/src/error.rs:232`). Map failures to these **real** variants (verified in `crates/kanban-domain/src/error.rs`):

| Failure | Variant | Constructor / form | Wire code (api/v1/error_mapping.rs) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Invariant violation in `create` (e.g. empty required field, bad enum combo) | `DomainError::Validation(String)` | `KanbanError::validation("…")` (`error.rs:270`) | `ErrorCode::ValidationFailed` → HTTP 422 |
| Structural-validation failure in `reconstitute` (malformed record, impossible counter) | `DomainError::Validation(String)` | `KanbanError::validation("…")` | `ErrorCode::ValidationFailed` → 422 |
| WIP-limit on a Card create | `DomainError::WipLimitExceeded { column_id, limit }` | `DomainError::wip_limit_exceeded(..)` (`error.rs:186`) | `ErrorCode::WipLimitExceeded` → 409 |
| Card sprint/board mismatch | `DomainError::SprintBoardMismatch { .. }` | direct | `ErrorCode::SprintBoardMismatch` → 422 |
| **FK target missing** (service tier: `Column.board_id`, `Card.column_id`/`sprint_id` point to nothing) | `DomainError::NotFound { entity, id }` | `KanbanError::not_found("Board", id)` (`error.rs:235`) | `ErrorCode::NotFound` → 404 |
| **Client-supplied id collision** (idempotent PUT-create POST path) | **NEW: `DomainError::AlreadyExists { entity, id }`** (see below) | new constructor `KanbanError::already_exists(entity, id)` | **NEW: `ErrorCode::AlreadyExists` → 409** |

**Gap found — no id-collision variant exists today.** `KanbanError::ConflictDetected` (`error.rs:202`) is specifically file-level optimistic-concurrency ("was modified by another instance"); its api message is deliberately scrubbed to *"resource was modified by another writer; reload and retry"* (`error_mapping.rs:60-62`) — wrong semantics for "an entity with this id already exists." This card adds the missing variant so the entity service cards have a target:

- In `crates/kanban-domain/src/error.rs`, add to `DomainError`:
  ```rust
  #[error("{entity} {id} already exists")]
  AlreadyExists { entity: &'static str, id: Uuid },
  ```
  plus `KanbanError::already_exists(entity, id)` and `is_already_exists()` predicate mirroring the existing `not_found` helpers (`error.rs:235`, `error.rs:275`).
- In `crates/kanban-service/src/api/v1/error.rs`, add `ErrorCode::AlreadyExists` (the `#[non_exhaustive]` enum at `error.rs:11`), its `Display` arm `"ALREADY_EXISTS"` (`error.rs:34`), and map it to **409** in `http_status()` (`error.rs:64`, alongside the other 409s).
- In `crates/kanban-service/src/api/v1/error_mapping.rs`, add the `DomainError::AlreadyExists { .. } => ErrorCode::AlreadyExists` arm (the exhaustive match at `error_mapping.rs:19-33`) and include `ErrorCode::AlreadyExists` in the **client-safe / user-facing message** group (`error_mapping.rs:45-57`) so it returns `err.to_string()` (the id is safe to echo, unlike the file-path conflict).

Both exhaustive matches (`error_mapping.rs` code-match and message-match, and `error.rs::http_status`) will fail to compile until the new arm is added — the existing no-`_` discipline does the enforcement.

## 6. Per-entity A/B/C/D card template (uniform across all four subtrees)

Every entity (Board first as the TEMPLATE, then Column, Card, Sprint as `spawns` children) gets one epic + four atomic cards:

- **A — `feat(domain): <Entity> factory core`** (`01-domain-core.md`): add `New<E>` + `<E>Record` (both `Default`-free, distinct from the entity) + `<E>::create(spec, id, now) -> KanbanResult<E>` (inject id/clock, remove internal `Uuid::new_v4`/`Utc::now`) + `<E>::reconstitute(record) -> KanbanResult<E>` + `From<&<E>> for <E>Record`. Stop the entity deriving `Deserialize`. Pure domain unit tests only.
- **B — `refactor(persistence): route <Entity> json+sqlite through <E>Record/reconstitute`** (`02-persistence.md`): JSON serde and SQLite `row_to_*`/`upsert_*` go through `<E>Record` + `reconstitute`/decompose; remove un-funnelled direct construction. Full `X → store → load → X'` round-trip tests on BOTH json and sqlite.
- **C — `feat(service): <Entity> v1 wire DTOs + conversions`** (`03-dto.md`): `Create/Update/Replace<E>Request` + `<E>Response` DTOs in `kanban-service::api::v1`; conversions (`Create<E>Request → New<E>` carrying optional client `id`; `Update/Replace → <E>Update`; `From<&<E>> for <E>Response` hiding internal counters). Exhaustive destructuring (the compile-lock this card guards). Per-arm boundary tests.
- **D — `feat(service): wire all consumers to the <Entity> factory + FK/client-id`** (`04-service.md`): create handler funnels through `<E>::create` (kill any create-then-update kludge, e.g. `CreateBoardRequest::into_parts` at `boards/conversions.rs:46`); FK + uniqueness validation tier including client-id collision → `AlreadyExists` (this card's new variant); idempotent PUT-create; wire CLI/TUI/MCP/server to the factory + DTO edge; MCP drops its bespoke `requests/` DTOs. Integration tests per consumer.

Sequencing within an entity: A → B → C → D. Across entities: Board is the reference; the other three mirror it.

## 7. Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `scripts/check-factory-compile-lock.sh` added, executable, greps the factory `record.rs` + `api/v1/**/{conversions,response}.rs` globs for `..` rest patterns and `Default::default()`, honoring `// lock-exempt:`.
- [ ] Guard wired into `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (own `factory-lock` job or a step on the `clippy` job), mirroring the `check-crate-list-sync` wiring (ci.yml:209-211).
- [ ] Guard **proven**: deliberately-failing probe makes it exit non-zero; reverting makes it pass — both outputs captured in the PR.
- [ ] `DomainError::AlreadyExists { entity, id }` + `KanbanError::already_exists` + `is_already_exists()` added with unit tests (display includes entity + id; predicate true/false).
- [ ] `ErrorCode::AlreadyExists` added with `Display` = `"ALREADY_EXISTS"`, `http_status()` = 409, exhaustive-match arm in `error_mapping.rs`, classified as client-safe message; mapping test extended.
- [ ] Conventions documented: extend **CONTRIBUTING.md** ("Adding a Field to a Domain Model", line 145) with the `NewX`/`XRecord` `Default`-free + no-`..` rule and the id/clock seam; the per-arm coverage note matches the existing exhaustive-struct guidance at CONTRIBUTING.md:151. Cross-reference KAN-769.
- [ ] `cargo test --workspace` green; `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean.
- [ ] A `.changeset/kan-XXX-*.md` added (the changeset job at ci.yml:98 requires it for PRs to `develop`).

## 8. Dependencies / sequencing

- **Depends on:** nothing.
- **Precedes:** ALL entity factory cards (every A/B/C/D slice for Board, Column, Card, Sprint). The CI guard, the `AlreadyExists` error variant/code, and the documented conventions must exist before the first entity slice lands so each slice is validated by the lock from day one.

## Tests (TDD red → green → refactor) — explicit
Both deliverables are testable; write tests FIRST (red), present for review, implement (green), refactor.

**Error variant** (`DomainError::AlreadyExists` + `ErrorCode::AlreadyExists` + `http_status`):
- `test_already_exists_maps_to_error_code_already_exists` — `ApiError::from(&KanbanError::already_exists(..))` yields `ErrorCode::AlreadyExists`. (Red: won't compile until the variant + the `error_mapping.rs` arm exist.)
- `test_already_exists_error_code_http_status_is_409` — `ErrorCode::AlreadyExists.http_status() == 409`.
- `test_already_exists_message_names_entity_not_scrubbed` — unlike `ConflictDetected` (file-level optimistic concurrency, message scrubbed), the already-exists message is client-actionable (names entity/id) and must be preserved. Adding the variant forces both exhaustive matches (`error_mapping.rs:19-33,45-57` and `error.rs::http_status:64-81`) to gain an arm — a compile error until handled (the compile-lock in action).

**CI compile-lock guard** (the deliberately-failing probe IS the red→green):
- Red: insert a `..` rest pattern (or `Default::default()`) into a watched conversion module (e.g. `api/v1/boards/conversions.rs`) and run the guard script — it MUST fail the build.
- Green: revert the probe — guard passes on the clean tree.
- Wire as a CI job mirroring `check-crate-list-sync` (ci.yml:209-211); if feasible also a workspace `#[test]` that shells the grep so it runs under `cargo test`.
- Refactor: tighten the regex/path globs; document the no-`..`/`Default`-free rule in CONTRIBUTING.md.

**Acceptance additions:**
- [ ] AlreadyExists tests written first (red), present for review, then variant + mapping (green); `cargo test --workspace` green.
- [ ] Guard proven via the failing probe, then reverted; guard wired into CI.

## Execution learnings (spike, applied) — CORRECTIONS
- CRITICAL: the embedded guard script was BROKEN — `rg -nE` is invalid (ripgrep has no -E flag; it took the pattern positionally), and `2>/dev/null` swallowed the error so the guard was a SILENT NO-OP that PASSED its own probe. Fix: pass the regex positionally, drop `-E` and the error redirect, and use `m=$(rg ... || true); if [ -n "$m" ]` (not `if matches=$(...)` under set -e). A guard that does not guard is worse than none — the corrected reference is spike commit 7dd3ace2.
- The `record.rs` glob matches NOTHING: records live in `<e>_factory.rs` (board_factory.rs, card_factory.rs). Point the glob at `crates/kanban-domain/src/*_factory.rs` and PIN that naming convention so future ColumnRecord/SprintRecord land where the guard looks.
- Line refs (error_mapping.rs:19-33, http_status:64-81, ci.yml:209-211) are approximate/stale — verify before citing.
- The error-layer compile-lock VALIDATED: adding AlreadyExists forced the code-match, message-match, and http_status match to update. Executed green: commit 7dd3ace2.

## Rerun finding (guard comment-awareness)
The compile-lock guard greps RAW TEXT, so a prose comment in a *_factory.rs module using `Foo { .. }` shorthand trips it (a doc comment containing `.. }` failed the guard). FIX (recommended): make the guard skip the comment portion of each line (strip from `//` before matching), OR document that factory-module prose must avoid the literal `.. }` / `.. ,` token. Found during the from-0 rerun (KAN-772 rerun).
