## Stakeholder summary — Where, Why, How

**Where.** TUI render path for the card detail view. `crates/kanban-tui/src/app/mod.rs::get_card_for_detail_view` (the lookup at the renderer boundary), `crates/kanban-tui/src/ui/card_detail.rs::render_card_detail` (the consumer that goes blank on miss), `crates/kanban-tui/src/handlers/detail_view_handlers.rs` (sidebar relationship accessors), plus every mutation handler that gates on `self.model.card(active_card_id).is_some()` (priority popup, sprint assign, points dialog, manage parents/children, edit metadata, edit description) — those gates already short-circuit correctly for archived cards but need an audit.

**Why.** Observed during KAN-534 smoke-testing: while the TUI views card A in the detail view, an external writer (CLI / MCP / another TUI session) archives A. The detail panel goes blank. The user is stranded with no card and no signal that A moved to the archive — the only recourse is to back out and re-navigate via the archived-cards view.

Root cause: `get_card_for_detail_view` resolves via `model.card(active_card_id)` which consults only the live-card map. After archive, A lives in `model.archived_card(id)` instead. The lookup never falls back. The renderer at `ui/card_detail.rs:66` then takes the implicit `else` branch (no content), producing the blank panel.

**How.** A one-line substitution at the lookup boundary, plus an audit of downstream consumers to confirm they fail safely (no-op) rather than silently mutating archived cards.

---

## Engineering spec

### Current state

`crates/kanban-tui/src/app/mod.rs:1462-1466`:

```rust
pub fn get_card_for_detail_view(&self) -> Option<Card> {
    self.selection
        .active_card_id
        .and_then(|id| self.model.card(id).cloned())  // live-only
}
```

`Model::card(id)` (`app/model.rs:31-34`) consults only the live cards HashMap. After archive the card lives in `model.archived_card(id)` (parallel map at `app/model.rs:48-51`), but the lookup never falls back.

Renderer at `crates/kanban-tui/src/ui/card_detail.rs:66`:

```rust
if let Some(card) = app.get_card_for_detail_view() {
    // render the card
}
// implicit empty path on None — panel goes blank
```

### Proposed solution

Substitute `get_card_for_detail_view` to use the existing fallback helper at `app/mod.rs:1455-1460`:

```diff
 pub fn get_card_for_detail_view(&self) -> Option<Card> {
     self.selection
         .active_card_id
-        .and_then(|id| self.model.card(id).cloned())
+        .and_then(|id| self.get_card_by_id(id))
 }
```

`get_card_by_id` already does the fallback:

```rust
pub fn get_card_by_id(&self, card_id: uuid::Uuid) -> Option<Card> {
    self.model
        .card(card_id)
        .or_else(|| self.model.archived_card(card_id))
        .cloned()
}
```

For downstream surfaces that need to branch on archive state (the visual cues in KAN-536), expose:

```rust
pub fn active_card_is_archived(&self) -> bool {
    self.selection
        .active_card_id
        .map(|id| self.model.archived_card(id).is_some())
        .unwrap_or(false)
}
```

### Offender table

| File:line | Symbol | Today | Required change |
|---|---|---|---|
| `app/mod.rs:1462-1466` | `get_card_for_detail_view` | `model.card(id).cloned()` — live-only | `get_card_by_id(id)` — falls back to archived |
| `ui/card_detail.rs:66` | `render_card_detail` | Takes implicit `else` branch on `None`, renders nothing | Same code path; lookup fix above means we no longer hit `else` for archived cards |
| `handlers/detail_view_handlers.rs::get_current_card_parents` | Sidebar parent list | `self.model.graph().parents(id)` — live edges only | Route through `parents_including_archived` (introduced by KAN-516; introduce locally if KAN-516 not landed) when active card is archived |
| `handlers/detail_view_handlers.rs::get_current_card_children` | Sidebar child list | Same | Same |
| `handlers/detail_view_handlers.rs:961` `handle_manage_parents` | Manage Parents dialog | Gated on `self.model.card(id).is_some()` | Stays strict — confirm clean short-circuit for archived active card (do not open dialog) |
| `handlers/detail_view_handlers.rs:1014` `handle_manage_children` | Manage Children dialog | Same | Same |
| `handlers/popup_handlers.rs:54` | Priority popup Enter branch | Gated | Stays strict |
| `handlers/popup_handlers.rs:257` | Sprint-assign popup Enter branch | Gated | Stays strict |
| `handlers/popup_handlers.rs:593` | Manage-relationship toggle | Gated | Stays strict |
| `handlers/dialog_handlers.rs:138` | Points dialog | Gated | Stays strict |
| `app/mod.rs:1789` `edit_card_field` | Title / description editor | Gated | Stays strict |
| `app/mod.rs:2349` `get_current_priority_selection_index` | Priority dialog seed value | Returns 0 on miss | Confirm acceptable for archived cards |
| `app/mod.rs:2370` `get_current_sprint_selection_index` | Sprint dialog seed value | Same | Same |

### Alternatives considered

**1. `get_card_for_detail_view → get_card_by_id` substitution (proposed).**

- *Pros*: one-line change at the lookup boundary; reuses an existing helper; no new types; downstream consumers see no API change; ships in a single commit.
- *Cons*: archived-vs-live distinction must be re-derived at any consumer that needs to branch (currently just the visual cues in KAN-536, served by a single boolean getter); no compile-time enforcement that consumers know they might see an archived card.

**2. Introduce a `RenderableCard` enum.**

```rust
pub enum RenderableCard {
    Live(Card),
    Archived { card: Card, archived_at: DateTime<Utc> },
}
```

Change `get_card_for_detail_view` to return `Option<RenderableCard>`.

- *Pros*: the type system enforces archived-handling at every consumer; mutation paths can refuse to compile against the archived variant; clean and explicit.
- *Cons*: large API surface change; every consumer (detail renderer, sidebar accessors, manage-parents/children, popups, dialogs) must pattern-match; ripples into theme + accessor APIs; significantly bigger PR.

**3. Extend `Model` with a unified `card_view(id) -> CardView` returning a rich struct.**

```rust
pub struct CardView<'a> {
    pub card: &'a Card,
    pub archived_at: Option<DateTime<Utc>>,
}
```

- *Pros*: single lookup primitive; renderers depend on a stable abstraction that carries archive metadata for free; less churn than #2 because consumers can still treat the inner `Card` normally.
- *Cons*: introduces a new type; needs construction at every consumer; doesn't enforce archive-handling at the type level the way #2 does.

**Recommendation**: ship #1 first as the user-visible fix. Promote to #2 or #3 only if KAN-536's visual cues end up needing more than a single boolean from this card.

### Tests

- Inline TUI unit test in the existing `setup_reload_resort_fixture` style: seed A live, set `active_card_id = Some(A.id)`, externally archive A via `app.ctx.archive_card(A.id)`, reload model, assert `get_card_for_detail_view()` returns `Some(card)` with `card.id == A.id`.
- Assert `get_current_card_parents()` and `get_current_card_children()` return A's archive-time relationships, not empty.
- Inline test that each mutation gate (priority popup, sprint assign, manage parents/children, points dialog, edit description) is a no-op for an archived active card — neither mutates state nor panics.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] After an external `card archive` against the active card, the detail panel continues to render the card's title and description.
- [ ] The sidebar Parents and Children lists show the card's archive-time relationships.
- [ ] All mutation surfaces (priority popup, sprint-assign popup, points dialog, manage parents / children, edit title / description, `e` Metadata) are no-ops when the active card is archived — no state mutation, no panic, no silent-wrong-card edit.
- [ ] Restoring the card externally and reloading returns the detail view to its live appearance with no manual re-navigation.

### Risks

- **Mutation creep.** A consumer that today returns early on `model.card(id) = None` could be edited later to skip the strict guard. New tests pin the no-op behaviour at each surface.
- **Performance.** `get_card_by_id` performs two HashMap lookups per render frame instead of one. Negligible at TUI render rates with O(1) lookups, but worth noting under heavy archive populations.
- **Stale archive metadata.** If the in-memory model briefly disagrees with on-disk state during the file-watcher debounce window, the detail view may render the live card for ~500ms after an external archive. Acceptable transient.

### Out of scope

- Visual cues to communicate archived state (KAN-536).
- Editing or mutating archived cards from the detail view (rejected — strict mutation guard remains).
- CLI / MCP archived-card read paths (KAN-516).
- Edge-collection refactor (KAN-517).
- Restoring archived cards from the detail panel — separate UX question; for now restore stays in the archived-cards view.

### Key file references

- `crates/kanban-tui/src/app/mod.rs:1455-1466` — `get_card_by_id`, `get_card_for_detail_view`
- `crates/kanban-tui/src/app/model.rs:31-51` — `Model::card`, `Model::archived_card`
- `crates/kanban-tui/src/ui/card_detail.rs:65-167` — `render_card_detail`
- `crates/kanban-tui/src/handlers/detail_view_handlers.rs:961-1135` — manage parents/children, sidebar accessors, navigation
- `crates/kanban-tui/src/handlers/popup_handlers.rs:41-595` — priority, sprint-assign, manage-relationship popups
- `crates/kanban-tui/src/handlers/dialog_handlers.rs:115-167` — points dialog
- `crates/kanban-tui/src/app/mod.rs:1788-2380` — `edit_card_field`, priority/sprint selection index helpers
cards.title: TUI: detail view stays usable when the active card is externally archived

> ⚠ SEQUENCING CORRECTION (read first):
> As the **final step of this slice** — after `Snapshot` + sqlite read/write route through `ColumnRecord` — **remove `Column`'s `Deserialize` derive** (moved here from slice A). It lands green because nothing deserializes `Column` directly anymore; this is what enforces "the only way to make a `Column` is the factory." Slice A left the derive in place so it could ship green independently.

## Context / why

Slice B of the Column entity factory (epic: Column entity factory; root spec `KAN-769`). Both persistence backends currently build `Column` directly, bypassing the factory. Route JSON (serde) and SQLite (rows) through `ColumnRecord` + `Column::reconstitute` (read) and `From<&Column> for ColumnRecord` (write), so persistence is a funnelled construction arm. Depends on slice A.

## Current state (researched)

- **SQLite read**: `row_to_column` at `crates/kanban-persistence-sqlite/src/sqlite_store/conversions.rs:56` constructs `Column { id, board_id, name, position, wip_limit, created_at, updated_at }` directly from a `SqliteRow` (un-funnelled).
- **SQLite write**: `SqliteStore::write_column_with_conn` at `crates/kanban-persistence-sqlite/src/sqlite_store/entities/column.rs:11` binds `column.id`, `column.board_id`, `column.name`, `column.position`, `column.wip_limit`, timestamps. Schema `columns` table at `crates/kanban-persistence-sqlite/src/schema.sql:57` (id, board_id, name, position, wip_limit, created_at, updated_at; FK board_id → boards ON DELETE CASCADE).
- **JSON**: columns serialize/deserialize via the domain `Snapshot.columns: Vec<Column>` (`crates/kanban-domain/src/snapshot.rs:28`) through `Column`'s derived serde; the JSON store persists raw `data` bytes (`crates/kanban-persistence-json/src/json_file_store.rs`). After slice A removed `Column: Deserialize`, the snapshot must carry `Vec<ColumnRecord>` (or map through it) — this slice fixes that.
- **In-memory store**: `crates/kanban-domain/src/in_memory_store/columns.rs` (HashMap of `Column`); snapshot apply maps `snapshot.columns` at `crates/kanban-domain/src/in_memory_store/snapshot.rs:35`. The in-memory store is the live state, not a serialized backend; it holds `Column`, not `ColumnRecord`.

## Target

- **SQLite read**: `row_to_column` builds a `ColumnRecord` from the row, then returns `Column::reconstitute(record)`. Net signature stays `fn row_to_column(row) -> KanbanResult<Column>`.
- **SQLite write**: in `write_column_with_conn`, decompose via `let rec = ColumnRecord::from(column);` and bind from `rec.*` (or keep binding from `column.*` — equivalent; prefer routing through `ColumnRecord` for symmetry and to make a new field break the bind list). Keep the `ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE` upsert.
- **JSON / snapshot**: the serialized snapshot's column collection deserializes into `ColumnRecord` and is rehydrated via `Column::reconstitute`. Decide the seam:
  - Preferred: the domain `Snapshot` keeps `columns: Vec<Column>` for in-process use, but its `Serialize`/`Deserialize` routes each `Column` through `ColumnRecord` (e.g. a `#[serde(with)]` adapter or a `SnapshotWire` mirror that holds `Vec<ColumnRecord>` and maps on load/save). Pick the same mechanism the Board template uses to stay consistent across the four siblings.
- Remove any remaining direct `Column { .. }` construction in the persistence crates.

## Step-by-step (TDD red → green → refactor)

1. **Red (sqlite)**: add a round-trip test (below) to `crates/kanban-persistence-sqlite/src/sqlite_store/tests/entities.rs` asserting `write → load → equal`, including a `Some(wip_limit)` and a `None` case. (Likely already partially covered — extend to assert the funnel and exact equality.)
2. **Green (sqlite)**: rewrite `row_to_column` (`conversions.rs:56`) to build `ColumnRecord` then `Column::reconstitute`. Route `write_column_with_conn` through `ColumnRecord::from(column)`.
3. **Red (json/snapshot)**: add a round-trip test that serializes a snapshot containing columns and deserializes it back, asserting columns survive verbatim (and that deserialization goes through `ColumnRecord`/`reconstitute`, not `Column: Deserialize` which no longer exists).
4. **Green (json)**: implement the snapshot serde seam through `ColumnRecord`. Ensure `crates/kanban-persistence-json/src/json_file_store.rs` load path still produces `Vec<Column>` for the domain.
5. **Refactor**: delete dead direct-construction code; confirm no `Column { .. }` literal remains in persistence crates (`rg 'Column \{' crates/kanban-persistence*`). Confirm `..`-free decompose.

## Tests

- `test_sqlite_column_round_trip_preserves_all_fields` (sqlite `tests/entities.rs`) — write a `Column` with `wip_limit: Some(7)`, distinct created/updated timestamps; load by id; assert field-for-field equal.
- `test_sqlite_column_round_trip_none_wip_limit` — same with `wip_limit: None`; assert it loads back `None`.
- `test_row_to_column_funnels_through_reconstitute` — assert the loaded column equals `Column::reconstitute(expected_record)` (the funnel is observable: a column built any other way would still equal, so make this assert exact fields incl. position).
- `test_json_snapshot_column_round_trip` (json crate) — snapshot with N columns → serialize → deserialize → `Vec<Column>` equal to the originals (order by position preserved).
- `test_json_snapshot_column_deserialize_uses_record` — a snapshot JSON missing a future-required field fails to deserialize at the `ColumnRecord` boundary (compile-lock guard at the serde edge; assert the record, not `Column`, owns serde).
- Full backend round-trip on BOTH: `test_column_create_store_load_equal_json` / `_sqlite` — `Column::create(spec,id,pos,now)` → upsert → load → `Column'`, assert `Column == Column'`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `row_to_column` returns `Column::reconstitute(ColumnRecord { .. })`; no direct `Column { .. }` in sqlite conversions.
- [ ] SQLite write routes through `ColumnRecord::from(&column)` (or equivalent funnel) with an exhaustive bind list.
- [ ] JSON snapshot serde for columns routes through `ColumnRecord`; `Column` no longer needs `Deserialize`.
- [ ] Round-trip tests on BOTH backends green (`X → store → load → X'`, `X == X'`).
- [ ] `cargo test -p kanban-persistence-sqlite -p kanban-persistence-json -p kanban-domain` green; `clippy -D warnings` clean; `fmt` clean.

## Dependencies / sequencing

Depends on slice A (`ColumnRecord`/`reconstitute` must exist). Precedes C and D. Follows the Board template slice B.

## Entity-specific quirks

- Column has no migration chain of its own (no legacy fields like Board's `prefix_counters`/`next_card_number`) — the record is a straight mirror, simpler than Board.
- The sqlite `columns` table FK `board_id → boards ON DELETE CASCADE` is unchanged; reconstitute does NOT re-validate FK existence (trusted/complete input per the spec).
- `position` ordering in `list_columns_by_board` (sort by position) is unaffected; reconstitute restores `position` verbatim.

## Implementation sketch (before -> after)

All snippets are faithful to the current tree; `ColumnRecord` / `Column::reconstitute` / `From<&Column> for ColumnRecord` land in **slice A** (`crates/kanban-domain/src/column.rs`), mirroring the Board template. This slice routes the two persistence backends through that funnel.

### Assumed slice-A shape (domain, for reference)

```rust
// crates/kanban-domain/src/column.rs
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ColumnRecord {
    pub id: ColumnId,
    pub board_id: BoardId,
    pub name: String,
    pub position: i32,
    pub wip_limit: Option<i32>,
    pub created_at: DateTime<Utc>,
    pub updated_at: DateTime<Utc>,
}

impl Column {
    pub fn reconstitute(record: ColumnRecord) -> KanbanResult<Self> { /* trusted input -> Column */ }
}

impl From<&Column> for ColumnRecord { /* straight mirror */ }
```

After slice A, `Column` keeps `Serialize` but **drops `Deserialize`** (line `column.rs:10`), so every read path must go through `ColumnRecord`.

### 1. SQLite read — `crates/kanban-persistence-sqlite/src/sqlite_store/conversions.rs:56`

**Before** (direct `Column { .. }` literal):

```rust
pub(crate) fn row_to_column(row: &SqliteRow) -> KanbanResult<Column> {
    let id_str: String = row.try_get("id").map_err(db_err)?;
    let board_id_str: String = row.try_get("board_id").map_err(db_err)?;
    let created_at_str: String = row.try_get("created_at").map_err(db_err)?;
    let updated_at_str: String = row.try_get("updated_at").map_err(db_err)?;

    Ok(Column {
        id: p_uuid(&id_str)?,
        board_id: p_uuid(&board_id_str)?,
        name: row.try_get("name").map_err(db_err)?,
        position: row.try_get("position").map_err(db_err)?,
        wip_limit: row.try_get("wip_limit").map_err(db_err)?,
        created_at: p_dt(&created_at_str)?,
        updated_at: p_dt(&updated_at_str)?,
    })
}
```

**After** (build `ColumnRecord`, then funnel through `reconstitute`):

```rust
use kanban_domain::ColumnRecord;

pub(crate) fn row_to_column(row: &SqliteRow) -> KanbanResult<Column> {
    let id_str: String = row.try_get("id").map_err(db_err)?;
    let board_id_str: String = row.try_get("board_id").map_err(db_err)?;
    let created_at_str: String = row.try_get("created_at").map_err(db_err)?;
    let updated_at_str: String = row.try_get("updated_at").map_err(db_err)?;

    let record = ColumnRecord {
        id: p_uuid(&id_str)?,
        board_id: p_uuid(&board_id_str)?,
        name: row.try_get("name").map_err(db_err)?,
        position: row.try_get("position").map_err(db_err)?,
        wip_limit: row.try_get("wip_limit").map_err(db_err)?,
        created_at: p_dt(&created_at_str)?,
        updated_at: p_dt(&updated_at_str)?,
    };
    Column::reconstitute(record)
}
```

Signature is unchanged (`fn(row) -> KanbanResult<Column>`), so `list_columns_by_board` and its position sort are untouched.

### 3. SQLite write — `crates/kanban-persistence-sqlite/src/sqlite_store/entities/column.rs:7`

**Before** binds straight off `column.*`:

```rust
.bind(column.id.to_string())
.bind(column.board_id.to_string())
.bind(required_str(&column.name, "column.name")?)
.bind(column.position)
.bind(column.wip_limit)
.bind(fmt_dt(&column.created_at))
.bind(fmt_dt(&column.updated_at))
```

**After** decomposes via `ColumnRecord::from(column)` and binds off `rec.*` (the upsert SQL with `ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE` is unchanged; a future field added to the record breaks this bind list, which is the point):

```rust
use kanban_domain::ColumnRecord;

pub(crate) async fn write_column_with_conn(
    conn: &mut sqlx::SqliteConnection,
    column: &Column,
) -> KanbanResult<()> {
    let rec = ColumnRecord::from(column);
    sqlx::query(
        "INSERT INTO columns (id, board_id, name, position, wip_limit, created_at, updated_at)
         VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
         ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET
            board_id=excluded.board_id, name=excluded.name,
            position=excluded.position, wip_limit=excluded.wip_limit,
            updated_at=excluded.updated_at",
    )
    .bind(rec.id.to_string())
    .bind(rec.board_id.to_string())
    .bind(required_str(&rec.name, "column.name")?)
    .bind(rec.position)
    .bind(rec.wip_limit)
    .bind(fmt_dt(&rec.created_at))
    .bind(fmt_dt(&rec.updated_at))
    .execute(&mut *conn)
    .await
    .map_err(db_err)?;
    Ok(())
}
```

### 4. JSON snapshot serde — `crates/kanban-domain/src/snapshot.rs:28`

`Snapshot.columns` stays `Vec<Column>` for in-process use, but since `Column: Deserialize` is gone, the field deserializes **through `ColumnRecord`** via a `#[serde(with)]` module adapter (same mechanism the Board sibling uses). `Column` still serializes natively (it keeps `Serialize`), and the wire shape is byte-identical because `ColumnRecord` is a straight field mirror.

**Before:**

```rust
/// All columns across all boards.
#[serde(default)]
pub columns: Vec<Column>,
```

**After:**

```rust
/// All columns across all boards.
#[serde(default, with = "column_record_serde")]
pub columns: Vec<Column>,
```

```rust
// crates/kanban-domain/src/snapshot.rs  (or a shared persistence_serde module)
mod column_record_serde {
    use super::*;
    use crate::ColumnRecord;
    use serde::{Deserializer, Serializer, Deserialize, Serialize};

    pub fn serialize<S: Serializer>(cols: &[Column], s: S) -> Result<S::Ok, S::Error> {
        // Column keeps Serialize; ColumnRecord mirror is wire-identical.
        cols.serialize(s)
    }

    pub fn deserialize<'de, D: Deserializer<'de>>(d: D) -> Result<Vec<Column>, D::Error> {
        let records = Vec::<ColumnRecord>::deserialize(d)?;
        records
            .into_iter()
            .map(Column::reconstitute)
            .collect::<KanbanResult<Vec<_>>>()
            .map_err(serde::de::Error::custom)
    }
}
```

The JSON store (`crates/kanban-persistence-json/src/json_file_store.rs`) persists the raw `data` bytes unchanged; the only seam is at the `Snapshot` serde edge, so the load path still yields `Vec<Column>` for the domain and the in-memory store apply at `crates/kanban-domain/src/in_memory_store/snapshot.rs:35` is unaffected.

## Pre-flight note (spike): pin the serde-adapter seam against the EXECUTED Board B (commit 89ae26f5) — PUBLIC `column_vec_serde` (+`column_serde` if a wrapper embeds Column) in column_factory.rs, `crate::error::KanbanResult` import, `Snapshot.columns` stays Vec<Column> + #[serde(with)]. Grep all in-domain Deserialize+Column sites + test from_str before dropping the derive. SQLite round-trip fixture: column_id FK needs a real board.

## Context / why

Slice C of the Column entity factory (epic: Column entity factory; root spec `KAN-769`). The Column DTOs already exist (KAN-713) but `CreateColumnRequest` feeds a create-then-update kludge (`into_parts`) instead of the factory. Align the create DTO onto `NewColumn` + an optional client `id`, keep the update/replace/reorder conversions, and keep `ColumnResponse` hiding nothing internal (Column has no counters, but the response stays the controlled wire projection). Depends on slice A.

## Current state (researched)

- `crates/kanban-service/src/api/v1/columns/requests.rs`:
  - `CreateColumnRequest { name: String, wip_limit: Option<i32> }` (`requests.rs:6`) — NO `id`, NO `board_id` (board comes from the `POST /v1/boards/:id/columns` path).
  - `UpdateColumnRequest { name: Option<String>, position: Option<i32>, wip_limit: Patch<i32> }` (`requests.rs:15`) — merge-patch (RFC 7386), `wip_limit` carries `skip_serializing_if`.
  - `ReplaceColumnRequest { name, position, wip_limit: Option<i32> }` (`requests.rs:27`) — full replace.
  - `ReorderColumnRequest { position: i32 }` (`requests.rs:36`).
- `crates/kanban-service/src/api/v1/columns/conversions.rs`:
  - `TryFrom<UpdateColumnRequest> for ColumnUpdate` (`conversions.rs:11`) — validates position, destructures exhaustively.
  - `TryFrom<ReplaceColumnRequest> for ColumnUpdate` (`conversions.rs:32`).
  - `CreateColumnRequest::into_parts() -> KanbanResult<(String, ColumnUpdate)>` (`conversions.rs:58`) — the create-then-update kludge to KILL.
  - `validate_position` (`conversions.rs:74`), `validate_wip_limit` (`conversions.rs:83`) — non-negativity, no upper bound.
- `crates/kanban-service/src/api/v1/columns/response.rs`: `ColumnResponse { id, board_id, name, position, wip_limit, created_at, updated_at }` (`response.rs:10`); `From<Column> for ColumnResponse` (`response.rs:20`).

## Target

In `crates/kanban-service/src/api/v1/columns/`:

- Extend `CreateColumnRequest` with an optional client id and a destination board:
  ```rust
  pub struct CreateColumnRequest {
      #[serde(default)]
      pub id: Option<Uuid>,        // client-supplied id (idempotent PUT-create); minted if absent
      pub name: String,
      #[serde(default)]
      pub wip_limit: Option<i32>,
  }
  ```
  `board_id` stays out of the body for the nested `POST /boards/:id/columns` route (path-supplied). Add a conversion that builds `NewColumn` given the path `board_id`:
  ```rust
  impl CreateColumnRequest {
      /// Validate + split into the optional client id and the domain create spec.
      /// position is server-assigned (append) — NOT carried here.
      pub fn into_new_column(self, board_id: BoardId) -> KanbanResult<(Option<Uuid>, NewColumn)>;
  }
  ```
  Validate `wip_limit >= 0`; destructure `CreateColumnRequest` exhaustively (no `..`). Build `NewColumn { board_id, name, wip_limit }` exhaustively.
- DELETE `CreateColumnRequest::into_parts` (`conversions.rs:58`) and its tests once slice D's handler consumes `into_new_column`.
- Keep `TryFrom<UpdateColumnRequest>`/`TryFrom<ReplaceColumnRequest> for ColumnUpdate` and `ReorderColumnRequest` as-is (they already destructure exhaustively).
- `ColumnResponse` + `From<Column> for ColumnResponse` stay; keep the exhaustive field mapping (compile-lock on decompose). Column has no internal-only fields, so nothing is hidden — note that explicitly in the doc comment.

## Step-by-step (TDD red → green → refactor)

1. **Red**: add boundary tests (below) for `into_new_column`; they fail to compile until `id` + the method exist.
2. **Green**: add `id` to `CreateColumnRequest`; implement `into_new_column(board_id)` returning `(Option<Uuid>, NewColumn)`; reuse `validate_wip_limit`.
3. Remove `into_parts` + its three tests (`test_create_column_request_into_parts_*` at `conversions.rs:141`–`170`).
4. **Refactor**: ensure exhaustive destructuring everywhere; confirm the CI `no ..` / `no Default::default()` grep passes over `columns/`.

## Tests (in `columns/conversions.rs` / `requests.rs`)

- `test_create_column_request_into_new_column_maps_fields` — `{ id: None, name: "Doing", wip_limit: Some(3) }`.into_new_column(board_id) → `(None, NewColumn { board_id, name: "Doing", wip_limit: Some(3) })`.
- `test_create_column_request_carries_client_id` — `{ id: Some(uuid), .. }` → returned `Option<Uuid>` is `Some(uuid)`.
- `test_create_column_request_absent_id_is_none` — JSON `{"name":"Backlog"}` → `id == None` (minted by service later).
- `test_create_column_request_rejects_negative_wip_limit` — `wip_limit: Some(-5)` → `Err` (validation).
- `test_create_column_request_omits_position` — assert `NewColumn` has no position field (compile-level; the spec carries no position).
- `test_create_column_request_serde_round_trip_with_id` — serialize/deserialize incl. the new optional `id`.
- Keep existing: `test_update_column_request_into_column_update`, `test_update_column_request_rejects_negative_wip_limit`, `test_replace_column_request_clears_omitted_wip_limit`, `test_replace_column_request_rejects_negative_position` (already at `conversions.rs:98`+).
- `test_column_response_from_column` (keep, `response.rs:39`) — exhaustive field assertion + serde round-trip.
- `test_create_column_request_exhaustive_destructure_compiles` — note/test asserting `into_new_column` destructures every field (compile-lock; a new field breaks the build).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `CreateColumnRequest` carries optional `id`; `into_new_column(board_id) -> (Option<Uuid>, NewColumn)` exists and validates.
- [ ] `into_parts` and its tests removed.
- [ ] Update/Replace/Reorder conversions and `ColumnResponse` unchanged in behavior; all destructure exhaustively (no `..`, no `Default::default()`).
- [ ] Boundary tests per arm green; serde round-trips green.
- [ ] `cargo test -p kanban-service` green; `clippy -D warnings` clean; `fmt` clean; CI `no ..` grep passes over `api/v1/columns/`.

## Dependencies / sequencing

Depends on slice A (`NewColumn`). Precedes D (the handler consumes `into_new_column`). Follows the Board template slice C.

## Entity-specific quirks

- `board_id` is supplied by the route path (`POST /boards/:id/columns`), so it is a parameter to `into_new_column`, not a body field — distinct from Card where `column_id`/`sprint_id` may be body fields.
- `position` is server-assigned on create and therefore absent from `CreateColumnRequest`; it IS present in `UpdateColumnRequest`/`ReplaceColumnRequest`/`ReorderColumnRequest` (client may reposition after create).
- `ColumnResponse` hides nothing (no counters) — but remains the controlled wire type; do not collapse it into the entity.

## Stakeholder summary — Where, Why, How

**Where.** TUI render layer. `crates/kanban-tui/src/components/card_list_item.rs` (per-row rendering), `crates/kanban-tui/src/ui/card_detail.rs` (detail panel border and title block), `crates/kanban-tui/src/theme/colors.rs` and `crates/kanban-tui/src/theme/styles.rs` (accent colour and reusable border style), and every list consumer that constructs a `CardListItemConfig` (sprint task lists, card list view, archived-cards view).

**Why.** Once the detail view can render archived cards (sibling KAN-535), the user must be able to tell at a glance that the card on screen is archived. Without a visual signal, an externally archived card is indistinguishable from a live one — the user might attempt to edit, assign sprints, or manage relationships, all of which silently no-op against the strict mutation guard, producing a confusing dead-feeling UI.

The cue needs to surface on every list view (active board, sprint detail, archived-cards view itself) plus on the detail panel.

**How.** Add an `is_archived: bool` field to `CardListItemConfig` (driving an `[A] ` badge plus `Modifier::DIM` on rows). Extend the detail panel renderer to swap its border to the existing `deleted_view_focused_border` style and append `(ARCHIVED on YYYY-MM-DD)` to the title block when the active card is archived. Source the accent colour from the theme module so it tracks any user-configured palette.

---

## Engineering spec

### Current state

**Card list row** at `crates/kanban-tui/src/components/card_list_item.rs:9-122`:

```rust
pub struct CardListItemConfig<'a> {
    // ... no is_archived field
}

pub fn render_card_list_item(config: CardListItemConfig) -> Line<'static> {
    let is_done = config.card.status == CardStatus::Done;
    // ...
    if is_done {
        title_style = title_style.add_modifier(Modifier::CROSSED_OUT);
    }
    // ...
}
```

The only status-driven cue today is `CROSSED_OUT` for `Done`. Archive state is not communicated at all.

**Detail panel** at `crates/kanban-tui/src/ui/card_detail.rs:65-167`: builds a `Block` with the default theme border. Title block renders the card's title verbatim, no archive marker.

**Archived-cards view panel border** at `crates/kanban-tui/src/render_strategy.rs:326-330,490-493` already uses `deleted_view_focused_border()` (defined at `crates/kanban-tui/src/theme/styles.rs:13`). This is the existing convention; the work below extends it to the per-card detail panel.

**Theme module** at `crates/kanban-tui/src/theme/colors.rs:1-32` defines `Color` constants (`FOCUSED_BORDER`, `DONE_TEXT`, `PRIORITY_*`, etc.). No `ARCHIVE_ACCENT` constant exists yet; `deleted_view_focused_border()` inlines its colour.

### Proposed solution

#### 1. Theme

Add to `theme/colors.rs`:

```rust
pub const ARCHIVE_ACCENT: Color = Color::Yellow;
```

Refactor `deleted_view_focused_border()` at `theme/styles.rs:13` to consume `ARCHIVE_ACCENT` instead of inlining the colour. Single source of truth.

#### 2. Card list row

Extend `CardListItemConfig`:

```rust
pub struct CardListItemConfig<'a> {
    // ... existing fields
    pub is_archived: bool,
}
```

In `render_card_list_item`:

```rust
let mut spans = vec![];
if config.is_archived {
    spans.push(Span::styled(
        "[A] ",
        Style::default().fg(theme::colors::ARCHIVE_ACCENT),
    ));
    title_style = title_style.add_modifier(Modifier::DIM);
}
// ... existing rendering with title_style now possibly DIM'd
```

Update every `CardListItemConfig::new(...)` construction site (active card list, sprint task lists, archived-cards-view list) to pass the correct `is_archived` value. Archived-cards-view always passes `true`; live lists pass `false`; once KAN-535 surfaces archived cards in mixed contexts, compute via `model.archived_card(card.id).is_some()`.

#### 3. Detail panel border

In `ui/card_detail.rs::render_card_detail`, after fetching the card:

```rust
let archived = app.active_card_is_archived();  // new helper, see KAN-535
let mut panel_config = PanelConfig::new(&title).with_focus_indicator(&title);
if archived {
    panel_config = panel_config.with_custom_border_style(deleted_view_focused_border());
}
```

This mirrors the archived-cards-view panel border at `render_strategy.rs:326-330` exactly.

#### 4. Detail title block

When archived, append the formatted archive date to the title row. The timestamp lives on `ArchivedCard::archived_at`, not on `Card`, so surface it via a new App helper:

```rust
pub fn active_card_archived_at(&self) -> Option<chrono::DateTime<chrono::Utc>> {
    let id = self.selection.active_card_id?;
    self.model
        .archived_cards()
        .iter()
        .find(|ac| ac.card.id == id)
        .map(|ac| ac.archived_at)
}
```

Title block in `card_detail.rs`:

```rust
let mut title_spans = vec![Span::raw(&card.title)];
if let Some(archived_at) = app.active_card_archived_at() {
    title_spans.push(Span::styled(
        format!(" (ARCHIVED on {})", archived_at.format("%Y-%m-%d")),
        Style::default().fg(theme::colors::ARCHIVE_ACCENT),
    ));
}
```

### Offender / surface table

| File:line | Surface | Today | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| `theme/colors.rs:1-32` | Colour constants | No archive accent | Add `pub const ARCHIVE_ACCENT: Color = Color::Yellow;` |
| `theme/styles.rs:13` | `deleted_view_focused_border` | Inlines colour | Refactor to use `ARCHIVE_ACCENT` |
| `components/card_list_item.rs:9-21` | `CardListItemConfig` struct | No `is_archived` field | Add `pub is_archived: bool` |
| `components/card_list_item.rs:21-122` | `render_card_list_item` | No archive branch | Prepend `[A] ` span when `is_archived`; apply `Modifier::DIM` to title |
| `ui/card_detail.rs:65-95` | Detail panel `Block` + title | Default border; plain title | Swap to `deleted_view_focused_border()` when archived; append ` (ARCHIVED on YYYY-MM-DD)` to title in `ARCHIVE_ACCENT` |
| `app/mod.rs` (new helpers) | `App` API | None | Add `active_card_is_archived` and `active_card_archived_at` |
| `app/model.rs` | `Model::archived_card` returns `Option<&Card>` | Doesn't expose `archived_at` (lives on `ArchivedCard` wrapper) | Either add a sibling `archived_card_metadata(id) -> Option<&ArchivedCard>` or iterate `archived_cards()` from the App helper |
| `render_strategy.rs` + every `CardListItemConfig::new(...)` site | Construction sites | Don't pass `is_archived` | Pass `false` in live contexts; `true` in archived-view contexts; once KAN-535 mixes archived rows into live lists, compute via `model.archived_card(card.id).is_some()` |

### Alternatives considered

#### Badge style

| Option | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|
| `[A]` prefix + `Modifier::DIM` (proposed) | Compact; works in monochrome terminals; doesn't shift row layout | Cryptic to first-time users; competes visually with sprint markers |
| `Modifier::CROSSED_OUT` (strikethrough) | Conveys "removed" intuitively | Misleads — archived is not deleted; restore is normal. Already used for `Done` status, would collide for archived-Done cards |
| Unicode icon (📦 archive box) | Distinctive | Inconsistent font support; column alignment breakage in some terminals |
| Suffix ` (archived)` | Verbose but unambiguous | Eats horizontal real-estate; truncation hides the cue |

#### Border style

| Option | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|
| Solid orange via `deleted_view_focused_border()` (proposed) | Matches existing archived-list panel convention; one source of truth | Colour-only cue; no fallback for accessibility |
| Solid orange + dashed | Distinct from any current style | Ratatui has no `BorderType::Dashed` for box-drawing in all terminals; renders inconsistently |
| Solid orange + bold corners | Stronger visual weight | Ratatui has no per-corner styling; would need a custom block widget |

#### Title format

| Option | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|
| Suffix ` (ARCHIVED on YYYY-MM-DD)` (proposed) | Reads naturally; title stays prominent | Long suffix; can wrap on narrow terminals |
| Prefix `[ARCHIVED] ` | Banner-style; eye catches first | Title visually demoted behind the marker |
| Separate row above title | More space; bigger marker | Eats vertical space; complicates the existing layout in `card_detail.rs` |

### Tests

- `crates/kanban-tui/tests/card_detail_tests.rs`: render the detail panel for an archived card to a `TestBackend`; assert the border style equals `deleted_view_focused_border()` and the title row contains `"(ARCHIVED on "`.
- `crates/kanban-tui/tests/card_list_component.rs`: render `CardListItemConfig` with `is_archived = true`; assert the `[A] ` prefix is present and the title `Style` has `Modifier::DIM` set.
- Theme test: assert `deleted_view_focused_border()` derives its colour from `ARCHIVE_ACCENT` (single source of truth).

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every list row that represents an archived card shows the `[A] ` prefix in `ARCHIVE_ACCENT` and renders the title with `Modifier::DIM`.
- [ ] The card detail panel's border uses `deleted_view_focused_border()` when the active card is archived.
- [ ] The card detail title row ends with ` (ARCHIVED on YYYY-MM-DD)` in `ARCHIVE_ACCENT`; the date comes from `ArchivedCard::archived_at`.
- [ ] `deleted_view_focused_border()` and the row badge both source their colour from `theme::colors::ARCHIVE_ACCENT` (single source of truth).
- [ ] Snapshot / render-to-string tests cover the badge, border, and title suffix.

### Dependency

Depends on KAN-535 landing first — without the lookup fix, the detail panel can't open an archived card, so border / title cues have nowhere to render. The badge work on list rows is independent and can ship first.

### Risks

- **Theme conflicts.** Orange may clash with user-configured palettes. Mitigation: source the colour from `theme::colors::ARCHIVE_ACCENT` so any theme override takes effect.
- **Accessibility / colour-blindness.** Colour-only cues fail. The `[A]` badge is the non-colour fallback; document it as the primary signal and colour as secondary.
- **TTY without colour.** `Modifier::DIM` may not render in pure TTY; the `[A]` badge remains visible regardless.
- **Snapshot test brittleness.** Render-to-string tests over visual styles are fragile if `Color` rendering varies across ratatui versions. Assert on text content (`[A]`, `(ARCHIVED on `) and `Modifier` flags rather than raw style bytes.
- **Status marker collision.** `Done` already applies `CROSSED_OUT`. An archived `Done` card would have both — verify they compose correctly and aren't visually noisy.

### Out of scope

- CLI / MCP archived-card visual cues (KAN-516).
- Editing or mutating archived cards from any UI (rejected — strict mutation guard).
- Restoring archived cards from the detail panel — separate UX question.
- Richer theming infrastructure (existing colour-constant model is the in-scope shape).

### Key file references

- `crates/kanban-tui/src/theme/colors.rs:1-32` — existing colour constants
- `crates/kanban-tui/src/theme/styles.rs:13` — `deleted_view_focused_border()`
- `crates/kanban-tui/src/components/card_list_item.rs:9-122` — `CardListItemConfig`, `render_card_list_item`
- `crates/kanban-tui/src/ui/card_detail.rs:65-167` — detail panel renderer
- `crates/kanban-tui/src/render_strategy.rs:326-330,490-493` — existing archived-list border usage
- `crates/kanban-tui/src/app/model.rs:40-51` — `Model::archived_cards`, `Model::archived_card` (returns `Option<&Card>`; `archived_at` lives on the wrapping `ArchivedCard`)

cards.description:
## Background

Distribute `kanban` via Chocolatey, the de-facto package manager for Windows. Today Windows users have no first-class install path: they must download release binaries by hand from GitHub releases (and as of this writing, even that download isn't automated — see prereq subtask). Chocolatey covers the bulk of Windows package-manager users; winget complements it (separate future card, will be filed analogously to this one).

This card is the umbrella for all Chocolatey work, scoped narrowly to one registry. It supersedes the Chocolatey section of KAN-452 and is structurally analogous to KAN-465 (the Homebrew sibling).

## Deliverable shape

```powershell
choco install kanban
# or
choco install kanban --version=0.6.0
```

End state:

- A `kanban` package exists on community.chocolatey.org, owned by `fulsomenko` (or comparable username — see subtask on account/key).
- Each upstream release (driven by `release.yml`) auto-publishes the corresponding Chocolatey version. Moderation is asynchronous (1-7 days for the first version; usually well under 24h for subsequent versions).
- The Chocolatey package downloads the official Windows release archive from GitHub at install time and verifies it against an embedded SHA256.

## Approach summary

Chocolatey packages are NuGet packages wrapping PowerShell installer scripts. Unlike Homebrew (which builds from source), Chocolatey packages ship the precompiled binary URL + SHA, and the user's machine downloads and unpacks it at install time. This means we need:

1. A Windows release archive published to GitHub releases at a stable URL (prereq subtask).
2. A `.nuspec` metadata file plus PowerShell install/uninstall scripts (the package source).
3. CI that, on each upstream release, computes the SHA256 of the Windows archive, substitutes version + SHA into the package, runs `choco pack` and `choco push`.
4. A Chocolatey community account with an API key in a CI secret.
5. User-facing docs (README) and maintainer docs (CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Subtask breakdown

This card is the umbrella. Each piece below is its own child card:

1. **packaging/chocolatey/ skeleton** — author `kanban.nuspec` + `tools/*.ps1` + `LICENSE.txt` + `VERIFICATION.txt`.
2. **release.yml: Windows release archive** — build and upload `kanban-v$VERSION-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip` + `SHA256SUMS` on tag push. Also serves future winget work.
3. **Chocolatey community account + CHOCO_API_KEY secret** — register the account, reserve the package ID, generate the API key, add the repo secret.
4. **release.yml: Chocolatey publish step** — sed/replace substitution, `choco pack`, `choco push`, log post-publish verification URL.
5. **Docs: README + CONTRIBUTING** — Windows install path; maintainer playbook (file layout, release flow, secret rotation, local validation, troubleshooting).

Suggested execution order: (1) and (2) and (3) in parallel — they have no inter-dependencies. (4) depends on all three. (5) depends on (4) landing and producing a real, installable package.

## Maintenance burden expectations

- **Moderation lag**: first push typically reviewed within 1-7 days. Subsequent versions usually auto-pass once the maintainer relationship is established, but Chocolatey occasionally re-flags packages after policy changes.
- **Per-release work**: zero in the steady state. release.yml handles version+SHA substitution and push automatically; moderator approval is the only async piece, and that lands without intervention if the package is well-formed.
- **CVE / security**: if a CVE is filed against the published Windows binary or one of its dependencies, file a new release with the fix; Chocolatey moderation will typically expedite security-tagged updates.
- **Package ownership transfer**: out of scope for this card. If the package is ever to be transferred to another maintainer, that is a manual Chocolatey support ticket.
- **API key rotation**: out-of-band; track separately if/when the key is suspected of being leaked.

## Out of scope (separate cards if/when)

- **winget** — analogous registry, will be split out as a parallel sibling card filed separately. Reuses the Windows release archive from prereq subtask #2.
- **Self-publishing to a Chocolatey internal feed** — only relevant for enterprise distribution.
- **Bundling auxiliary tools** (e.g. shell completions, man pages) into the Chocolatey package — initial release ships only the `kanban.exe` binary + LICENSE.
- **Code signing the binary** — unsigned binaries trigger SmartScreen warnings on first launch but Chocolatey moderation does not require signing.
- **Polling for moderation approval** in CI — post-publish verification is intentionally manual; if friction grows, file a follow-up "verify chocolatey publish landed" card.

## Related

- **KAN-452** — superseded for the Chocolatey portion; this card is the new home for choco work.
- **KAN-465** — sibling, Homebrew equivalent. Mirror its CI patterns and structural style where applicable.
- **KAN-446** — AUR pipeline hardening; reference idioms (SHA256 computation, conditional gating on `has_changesets`) are reused.

cards.description:
> ⚠ SPLIT (read first): this card was too large (service logic + wiring 4 consumers). It is now a SUB-EPIC. The executable detail lives in its two children:
> - **KAN-793** — service create funnel (CreateX -> X::create, FK + client-id/conflict, idempotent PUT, service tests)
> - **KAN-794** — point CLI/TUI/MCP/server at the factory + DTO edge (depends on KAN-793)
> The sections below are retained as the combined overview.

## Context / why

Slice D of the Column entity factory (epic: Column entity factory; root spec `KAN-769`). Funnel the service create path through `Column::create`, kill the create-then-update kludge, validate the `board_id` FK and any client-supplied `id` at the service tier, support idempotent PUT-create, and point CLI/TUI/MCP at the shared factory + DTO edge (MCP drops its bespoke column request DTO). Depends on slices A, B, C.

## Current state (researched)

- **Service create**: `KanbanContext::create_column_impl(board_id, name, position: Option<i32>)` at `crates/kanban-service/src/context/columns.rs:7` — mints `id = Uuid::new_v4()` (line 18), computes append `position` from `list_columns_by_board(board_id).len()` (line 23), runs a `CreateColumn` command (line 19). NO FK existence check, NO client-id support, NO uniqueness check.
- **Command**: `CreateColumn { id, board_id, name, position }` at `crates/kanban-domain/src/commands/column_commands.rs:95`; `execute` (line 103) calls `Column::new(...)` then overwrites `column.id = self.id` — a second un-funnelled construction path to remove.
- **Reorder**: `reorder_column_impl(id, new_position)` at `columns.rs:60` builds a `ColumnUpdate` (position-only) and routes through `update_column_impl`.
- **Public API**: `create_column(board_id, name, position)` at `crates/kanban-service/src/context/mod.rs:86`.
- **MCP arm**: bespoke `CreateColumnRequest { board, name, position }` at `crates/kanban-mcp/src/requests/column.rs:5`; tool `tool_create_column` at `crates/kanban-mcp/src/tools/column.rs:20` calls `ctx.create_column(board_id, req.name, req.position)`.
- **CLI arm**: `crates/kanban-cli/src/handlers/column.rs` (calls `create_column`).
- **TUI arm**: `crates/kanban-tui/src/handlers/column_handlers.rs` + `tui_context.rs` (calls `create_column`).
- No FK-existence error mapping yet for "board not found on column create"; conflict mapping for duplicate id does not exist for columns.

## Target

- **Domain command**: change `CreateColumn::execute` (`column_commands.rs:103`) to build the column via `Column::create(NewColumn { board_id, name, wip_limit }, id, position, now)` instead of `Column::new(...)` + id overwrite. The command already carries `id`, `board_id`, `name`, `position`; add `wip_limit: Option<i32>` to `CreateColumn` so create is atomic (no follow-up update). Pass `now` (the command layer already has access to a clock at execute time — inject consistently with the Board template; if the command struct must stay clock-free, mint `now` in the service and pass it down, or have the command capture it at `execute`). Match whatever pattern Board's slice D establishes.
- **Service create**: rework `create_column_impl` to accept the create spec + optional client id:
  ```rust
  pub(super) fn create_column_impl(
      &mut self,
      spec: NewColumn,
      id: Option<Uuid>,
  ) -> KanbanResult<Column>
  ```
  Steps inside:
  1. FK check: `self.backend.get_board(spec.board_id)?` is `Some`, else `KanbanError::not_found("Board", board_id)` (or a validation/FK error consistent with Card's FK handling).
  2. Resolve id: `let id = id.unwrap_or_else(Uuid::new_v4);` then uniqueness check — `self.backend.get_column(id)?.is_none()`, else a conflict error (`KanbanError::conflict` / 409 mapping). Enables idempotent PUT-create.
  3. Compute append `position = self.backend.list_columns_by_board(spec.board_id)?.len() as i32`.
  4. `now = Utc::now()`; run the `CreateColumn` command carrying `{ id, board_id, name, position, wip_limit }`.
  - Keep a thin back-compat shim or update the public `create_column` signature on `KanbanContext` (`mod.rs:86`). Prefer updating callers to pass `NewColumn` (built from DTO via `into_new_column`).
- **Wire/server handler** (`POST /boards/:id/columns`, `PUT /columns/:id`): build `(id, NewColumn)` via `CreateColumnRequest::into_new_column(board_id)` (slice C) → `create_column_impl(spec, id)` → `ColumnResponse::from(column)`. `PUT /columns/:id` with a body id = create-or-replace (idempotent): if absent create with that id, if present replace.
- **MCP**: delete `crates/kanban-mcp/src/requests/column.rs` `CreateColumnRequest` (and the bespoke create path); have `tool_create_column` build `NewColumn` (resolving `board` name→id via the existing resolver at `crates/kanban-mcp/src/helpers/resolvers.rs`) and call the same service create. Reuse the shared `service::api` DTO where the tool surface allows.
- **CLI/TUI**: build `NewColumn` and call the updated create; behavior unchanged (append position, optional wip).
- **Error mapping**: add FK-not-found and id-conflict mappings in `crates/kanban-service/src/api/v1/error_mapping.rs` if not already covered.

## Step-by-step (TDD red → green → refactor)

1. **Red (domain command)**: test that `CreateColumn` with a `wip_limit` produces a column with that wip atomically (no follow-up). Fails until `CreateColumn` carries `wip_limit` and routes through `Column::create`.
2. **Green**: add `wip_limit` to `CreateColumn`; rewrite `execute` to call `Column::create`. Update `capture_inverse`/`DeleteColumn` inverse (`column_commands.rs:138`) to carry `wip_limit` so undo stays atomic (drop the create-then-update wip restore at `column_commands.rs:144`).
3. **Red (service)**: integration tests in `crates/kanban-service/tests/` for FK-missing, duplicate-id conflict, client-id honored, append position, idempotent PUT-create.
4. **Green (service)**: rework `create_column_impl`; add FK + uniqueness checks; thread `NewColumn`/`id`.
5. **Red/Green (consumers)**: update server handler, MCP tool (delete bespoke DTO), CLI, TUI; per-consumer tests.
6. **Refactor**: remove `Column::new` if now unused (or keep `#[cfg(test)]`); remove `into_parts` callers; confirm no create-then-update remains; run the CI `no ..` grep.

## Tests

- `test_create_column_routes_through_factory_sets_wip_atomically` (domain command) — create with `wip_limit: Some(2)`; resulting column has `wip_limit == Some(2)`, one command, no follow-up update.
- `test_create_column_missing_board_returns_not_found` (service integration) — `create_column_impl(NewColumn { board_id: random, .. }, None)` → `Err` not-found/FK.
- `test_create_column_with_client_id_uses_it` — pass `Some(id)`; created column has that id.
- `test_create_column_duplicate_id_returns_conflict` — create with an id, then create again with the same id → conflict error.
- `test_create_column_appends_position` — two creates on the same board → positions 0 then 1.
- `test_put_column_create_or_replace_is_idempotent` (server/service) — `PUT /columns/{id}` twice with the same id/body → 200 + identical state, no duplicate.
- `test_reorder_column_still_updates_position` — reorder unaffected by the refactor.
- `test_mcp_create_column_uses_shared_factory` (mcp integration) — `tool_create_column` resolves board by name and creates via the factory; bespoke `requests::column::CreateColumnRequest` no longer referenced.
- `test_cli_column_add_creates_via_factory` (cli integration, `assert_cmd`) — `kanban column add` creates a column with append position.
- Per the template: full `X → store → load → X'` already covered in slice B; here assert the create handler funnels through `Column::create`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `create_column_impl` consumes `NewColumn` + optional client `id`; mints `id`/`now`; validates FK `board_id` existence and id uniqueness (conflict on collision).
- [ ] Create funnels through `Column::create` (via `CreateColumn::execute`); the create-then-update kludge (`into_parts`, wip follow-up in inverses) is gone; `CreateColumn` carries `wip_limit`.
- [ ] Idempotent PUT-create works for columns.
- [ ] MCP drops bespoke column `CreateColumnRequest`; CLI/TUI/MCP/server all create through the one factory + DTO edge.
- [ ] `cargo test --workspace` green; `clippy -D warnings` clean; `fmt` clean; CI `no ..`/`no Default::default()` grep passes.

## Dependencies / sequencing

LAST Column slice; depends on A (`create`/`NewColumn`), B (persistence funnel), C (`into_new_column` + optional id DTO). Follows the Board template slice D.

## Entity-specific quirks

- FK is `board_id` only (single parent); FK check is one `get_board`. Card's slice D additionally validates `sprint_id`.
- `position` is server-assigned append; client cannot set it at create (only via update/reorder later).
- No counters to seed at create (simpler than Board/Card slice D).
- `DeleteColumn` keeps its guard (cannot delete a column containing cards / archived cards — `column_commands.rs:156`); unaffected, but its inverse should now re-create with `wip_limit` atomically via the enriched `CreateColumn`.
cards.title: feat(service): wire all consumers to the Column factory + FK/client-id

cards.description:
## Context / why

Epic: bring the **Card** entity under the one-factory construction boundary defined in the root spec **KAN-769** (`refactor(domain): entity construction factory`). Card is the most complex of the four sibling entities (Board, Column, Card, Sprint): two FKs (`column_id` required, `sprint_id` optional), a server-minted `card_number` sourced from the owning Board's `card_counter`, status-driven `completed_at`, and a `Vec<SprintLog>` history that persists to a **separate** table in SQLite. This epic delivers `NewCard` / `CardRecord` / `Card::create` / `Card::reconstitute` / `From<&Card> for CardRecord`, routes both persistence backends through the record, adds the v1 wire DTOs, and wires every consumer (CLI/TUI/MCP/server) to the factory — ending MCP's bespoke `requests/card.rs`.

This card is the parent of four atomic `spawns` children (A→B→C→D). The Board entity epic is the **template**; Card follows the same shape with the entity-specific quirks called out below.

## The four atomic slices

- **A — `01-domain-core.md`** `feat(domain): Card factory core — NewCard/CardRecord/create/reconstitute`
- **B — `02-persistence.md`** `refactor(persistence): route Card json+sqlite through CardRecord/reconstitute`
- **C — `03-dto.md`** `feat(service): Card v1 wire DTOs + conversions (create/update/replace/response)`
- **D — `04-service.md`** `feat(service): wire all consumers to the Card factory + FK/client-id`

## Card entity at a glance (researched)

- Struct: `crates/kanban-domain/src/card.rs:58-79`. Fields: `id: CardId(=Uuid)`, `column_id: ColumnId(=Uuid)` [FK, required], `title: String`, `description: Option<String>`, `priority: CardPriority`, `status: CardStatus`, `position: i32`, `due_date: Option<DateTime<Utc>>`, `points: Option<u8>`, `card_number: u32`, `sprint_id: Option<Uuid>` [FK, optional], `created_at`, `updated_at`, `completed_at: Option<DateTime<Utc>>`, `sprint_logs: Vec<SprintLog>`.
- Current constructor `Card::new(board: &mut Board, column_id, title, position)` at `card.rs:122-147` mints `id = Uuid::new_v4()`, `now = Utc::now()`, and `card_number = board.get_next_card_number()` (board.rs:277-282) — i.e. it both reads the clock/RNG **and mutates the Board counter**. This must be dismantled per the spec.
- The live create path does **not** go through `Card::new`: the service `create_card_impl` (`crates/kanban-service/src/context/cards.rs:10-39`) reads `board.card_counter` and passes a pre-minted `card_number` + `id` + `now` into the `CreateCard` command, whose `execute` (`crates/kanban-domain/src/commands/card/lifecycle.rs:97-171`) builds a `Card { .. }` literal directly and then applies a follow-up `CardUpdate` for the options — a **create-then-update kludge** the factory must replace.

## Field-acceptance matrix (the contract the tests assert)

| field | create arm (NewCard) | minted by `create` | restored by `reconstitute` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | no (it is a `create` **param**, optionally client-supplied) | yes (param) | yes |
| `column_id` | **yes** (FK, required) | — | yes |
| `title` | yes | — | yes |
| `description` | yes (optional) | — | yes |
| `priority` | yes (default `Medium`) | — | yes |
| `status` | no | `Todo` | yes |
| `position` | no | server-assigned (append index) | yes |
| `due_date` | yes (optional) | — | yes |
| `points` | yes (optional) | — | yes |
| `card_number` | no | **minted from Board.card_counter** (see quirk) | yes |
| `sprint_id` | yes (optional FK) | — | yes |
| `created_at` | no | `now` | yes |
| `updated_at` | no | `now` | yes |
| `completed_at` | no | `None` | yes |
| `sprint_logs` | no | `Vec::new()` | **yes, verbatim** |

## Entity-specific quirks (read before slicing)

1. **`card_number` minting and the inject-id pattern.** Today the service reads `board.card_counter` (cards.rs:19-23) and the command bumps it inside the domain `execute` (lifecycle.rs:121-123). The pure `Card::create` must NOT touch a Board. Decision for this epic: **`card_number` is a `create` parameter, exactly like `id`** — the service mints it (reads the Board counter, increments the Board, passes the number in), then calls `Card::create`. This keeps `create` Board-free and deterministic, symmetric with `id`/`now`. Bumping the Board's `card_counter` stays a **service-tier** responsibility (it is a sibling-entity write, not Card construction). See slice A and D.
2. **`sprint_id` is an optional FK** validated at the service tier; its presence in `NewCard` triggers an `assign_to_sprint` side-effect today (sprint log + name lookup). The factory's `create` takes only the `sprint_id` value; the sprint-log seeding on create stays orchestration in the service (it needs the Sprint + Board to resolve `sprint_number`/`sprint_name`). `NewCard` carries `sprint_id: Option<Uuid>`; `create` stores it but does NOT synthesize a SprintLog (no Sprint object in pure domain). `sprint_logs` always starts empty on create.
3. **`status` ↔ `completed_at` invariant**: `Done` ⇒ `completed_at = Some`, non-`Done` ⇒ `None` (card.rs:155-164). `create` always starts `Todo`/`None`; `reconstitute` restores both verbatim without re-deriving.
4. **`sprint_logs` separate SQLite table.** SQLite stores logs in a dedicated `sprint_logs` table (schema.sql:107-119), written/read separately (`entities/card.rs`, `row_to_sprint_log`). `reconstitute` must restore `sprint_logs` exactly; the round-trip test must include a card with ≥2 logs (one ended, one open).
5. **`ArchivedCard` wraps a full `Card`** (`archived_card.rs:11-12`) and `Snapshot.cards: Vec<Card>` (`snapshot.rs:21-32`) both rely on `Card: Deserialize`. Removing the entity's `Deserialize` (spec requirement) forces these to route through `CardRecord` too — slice B must handle the archived-card and snapshot paths, not just the live-card path.

## Dependencies / sequencing

- Precedes all: the **Foundation** card (shared `Patch`/`conv` helpers, the `api` module) already exists (`crates/kanban-service/src/api/v1/`).
- Within this epic: **A → B → C → D**, strictly. B depends on A's `CardRecord`/`reconstitute`; C depends on A's `NewCard`; D depends on A+C.
- The Board entity epic is the structural template; land Board first if both are in flight (it debugs the shared `conv`/`Patch` plumbing).

## Acceptance criteria (epic-level)

- [ ] All four child cards merged; `cargo test --workspace` green.
- [ ] `clippy -D warnings` clean, `cargo fmt --check` clean.
- [ ] No remaining `Card::new` callers outside tests; `CreateCard` command no longer builds a `Card { .. }` literal nor runs a follow-up `CardUpdate` for create options.
- [ ] `Card` no longer derives `Deserialize`; the only deserialization funnel is `CardRecord` → `Card::reconstitute`.
- [ ] MCP `requests/card.rs` `CreateCardRequest` removed in favour of the shared `service::api::v1` DTO.
- [ ] Compile-lock holds: adding a field to `CardRecord` breaks every persistence arm + `reconstitute`; adding a field to `NewCard` breaks every create arm; CI grep finds no `..` / `Default::default()` in the factory + conversion modules.

## TDD
This epic is an overview. Every child slice (A domain-core / B persistence / C dto / D service) follows Red → Green → Refactor: failing tests written and presented for review before implementation, then minimal implementation, then refactor. The executable TDD steps + named tests live on the child cards.

## Deferred design follow-up — sprint FK on create (discuss later)
Raised during the FK-validation spike, DEFERRED to its own card/discussion: should card creation accept `sprint_id` as a direct create-time FK (current design) OR should the card->sprint association be an INSERTED association via the explicit sprint-assignment step (assign_to_sprint + sprint_log) rather than a nullable FK set at create? Not blocking the factory. The Card D-core (KAN-795) spike validates the CURRENT direct-FK approach; revisit the model separately.
cards.title: Card entity factory (create + reconstitute + DTO wire edge)

cards.description:
## Background

Pushing to community.chocolatey.org requires (a) a community.chocolatey.org account, (b) an API key tied to that account, and (c) the API key configured as a CI secret in this GitHub repo. None of those exist today. This card stands up the credentials side so the release.yml Chocolatey publish step (separate subtask) can `choco push` without further setup.

This card is operational, not code. There is no PR; the deliverables are an account, a decided package ID, a key in a password manager, and a GitHub Actions secret. Acceptance is verified manually.

## Steps

### 1. Create the community.chocolatey.org account

- Sign up at `https://community.chocolatey.org/account/Register` with the project email (`max.blomstervall@gmail.com`).
- Choose username `fulsomenko` (matches GitHub org). If taken, fall back to `fulsomenko-kanban`. Username appears on the published package page as the maintainer.
- Confirm the email.

### 2. Reserve the package ID

Chocolatey IDs are global across the registry. Before doing CI work, sanity-check availability:

```
# from any machine with `choco` installed:
choco search kanban --by-id-only --exact
```

If `kanban` is taken by an unrelated project, fall back (in priority order):

1. `kanban-cli` — matches the workspace crate name and the install command.
2. `fulsomenko-kanban` — namespaced.

Pick once and update `<id>...</id>` in `packaging/chocolatey/kanban.nuspec` (the packaging-skeleton subtask) accordingly. README and CONTRIBUTING.md install instructions (the docs subtask) must use the chosen ID.

As of 2026-05-25, the availability of `kanban` on community.chocolatey.org is unverified. **Confirm and decide** at the time this card is executed. Document the decision in this card before closing — that decision propagates to every other Chocolatey-related card.

### 3. Generate the API key

- Sign in, go to account settings, find the "API Key" section.
- Generate a fresh key. **Copy immediately** — it cannot be re-read once you navigate away.
- Stash in a password manager (1Password, Bitwarden) under an entry named "Chocolatey community API key — kanban".

### 4. Add as repo secret

GitHub Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret:

- Name: `CHOCO_API_KEY`
- Value: the generated key

Or via the `gh` CLI (preferred for reproducibility and audit trail):

```
gh secret set CHOCO_API_KEY --repo fulsomenko/kanban --body "$YOUR_KEY"
```

### 5. Smoke-test the key locally (optional, only if a Windows machine is handy)

```
choco apikey --api-key="$YOUR_KEY" --source="https://push.chocolatey.org/"
# Stores the key locally for `choco push`. Does NOT push anything.
```

If this errors, the key is wrong; regenerate. If it succeeds, no further action — the same key value is what release.yml will use.

## Security notes

- The API key has full publish authority for any package owned by the account. Treat it like a deploy token.
- Rotate the key after any suspected leak. Chocolatey supports key regeneration via the same UI; the old key revokes immediately on regeneration.
- The key is NOT scoped per-package on community.chocolatey.org (Chocolatey-for-Business has scoped tokens; community does not). Implication: do not share this account with Chocolatey package work outside this project — one leaked key would compromise every package the account owns.
- Add `CHOCO_API_KEY` to the repo's documented secrets list (CONTRIBUTING.md, secrets section). If no such section exists, defer the doc update to the docs subtask.

## Why this isn't bundled into the CI subtask

Two reasons:

1. **Sequencing**: the package ID decision in step 2 propagates to the nuspec, install scripts, and README. Locking the ID in early — before the CI work — prevents rework if `kanban` turns out to be taken.
2. **Operational vs code**: account registration / key handling sits outside the PR review cycle. Splitting it out keeps the CI subtask focused on diffable code and avoids "this PR is waiting on Max to click a button on a website."

## Acceptance

- [ ] community.chocolatey.org account exists for `fulsomenko` (or fallback username, documented here).
- [ ] Package ID decision logged in this card and reflected in `packaging/chocolatey/kanban.nuspec` (skeleton subtask).
- [ ] API key generated, stashed in password manager.
- [ ] Repo secret `CHOCO_API_KEY` configured under `fulsomenko/kanban` with the key value (verifiable via `gh secret list --repo fulsomenko/kanban | grep CHOCO_API_KEY`).
- [ ] Local `choco apikey --api-key ...` smoke test succeeds (or, if no Windows machine accessible, defer to the CI subtask as the first real test — note the deferral here).

## Out of scope

- Any release.yml changes (separate subtask).
- Any nuspec / packaging files (separate subtask).
- Verifying the key actually pushes a package successfully — that happens in the CI subtask as part of the first real release.

## Related

- **Parent**: chocolatey umbrella card.
- **KAN-465** — sibling Homebrew card; the parallel is the `HOMEBREW_TAP_DEPLOY_KEY` secret. Same lifecycle: provision once, rotate on suspected leak.

## Findings (2026-05-25)

### Local secret status

The API key already exists locally, sops-encrypted, at `~/secrets/chocolatey/api.yaml`:

- File present, contains a `sops:` metadata block with an age recipient and a PGP-fallback recipient (fingerprint `D14A78F2AAC59A1B3E1F0547044B046E5745CC2B`). Encrypted with sops 3.12.2.
- YAML shape (verified via the encrypted file's structure, not by decrypting): `chocolatey.api.key`.
- Companion NixOS module at `~/secrets/chocolatey/default.nix` declares `secrets.chocolatey.enable` and a `sops.secrets."chocolatey/api/key"` entry owned by `max`, sourced from `./api.yaml`.

**Deployment state: NOT DEPLOYED.** `/run/secrets/chocolatey/` does not exist on this host, and `/run/secrets/` itself is not user-readable (so no sibling secrets are visible either). The chocolatey nix module is not currently activated on this machine. Implication: there is no runtime plaintext path to copy from — decryption must be done explicitly via sops.

### Current GitHub secrets on fulsomenko/kanban

```
AUR_SSH_KEY                  2026-03-23
CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN         2025-10-12
DEPLOY_KEY                   2025-10-13
HOMEBREW_KANBAN_DEPLOY_KEY   2026-05-15
HOMEBREW_TAP_DEPLOY_KEY      2026-05-15
```

No `CHOCO_API_KEY` (or any chocolatey-related secret) is configured. This is the missing piece this card delivers.

### Package ID availability on community.chocolatey.org

Verified via the public OData feed (`/api/v2/Packages()?$filter=Id eq '<id>'`) and the package page HTML route (`/packages/<id>`):

- `kanban` — **AVAILABLE** (OData feed empty; package page 404). Sanity-checked against `git` (found) to confirm the query isn't broken.
- `kanban-cli` — available (also empty + 404), but not needed.
- `fulsomenko-kanban` — available (also empty + 404), but not needed.

**Decision: use `kanban`.** This propagates to `packaging/chocolatey/kanban.nuspec` `<id>kanban</id>` and to README / CONTRIBUTING.md install instructions (`choco install kanban`).

### Setting CHOCO_API_KEY (commands for the user)

The runtime sops-decrypted path is not available on this machine, so the recommended one-liner is the direct sops-decrypt route. Run from any machine that has the age key required for `~/secrets/chocolatey/api.yaml`:

**Recommended (sops-decrypt, run by the user):**

```
sops -d ~/secrets/chocolatey/api.yaml | yq -r '.chocolatey.api.key' | gh secret set CHOCO_API_KEY --repo fulsomenko/kanban
```

`gh secret set` reads the value from stdin when `--body` is omitted, so the key never lands on disk or in shell history as plaintext.

**Fallback (only if the nix module ever gets activated and `/run/secrets/chocolatey/api/key` is readable as user `max`):**

```
sudo cat /run/secrets/chocolatey/api/key | gh secret set CHOCO_API_KEY --repo fulsomenko/kanban
```

After running, verify with:

```
gh secret list --repo fulsomenko/kanban | grep CHOCO_API_KEY
```

### What's still left for the user

1. Create the community.chocolatey.org account (step 1 above) if not already done, and generate the API key tied to it. If the value already at `~/secrets/chocolatey/api.yaml` came from a previous account, confirm the account is still active before relying on it.
2. Run the one-liner above to push the secret into GitHub Actions.
3. Tick the acceptance checkboxes once both are done.
