cards.description:
> ⚠ SEQUENCING CORRECTION (read first, overrides any "stop deriving Deserialize" step below):
> This slice is **purely additive** — keep `Card`'s `Deserialize` derive here so the workspace stays **green on its own**. Do NOT remove the derive in this card. Removing it would break `Snapshot`'s derive (same crate, holds `Vec<Card>`) and leave the build red until slice B. The derive removal is the FINAL step of **slice B** (Card persistence), after `Snapshot` + sqlite route through `CardRecord`. Net: this card lands green; B lands green; "only the factory constructs" is fully true at end of B.

## Context / why

Slice A of the **Card entity factory** epic (root spec **KAN-769**). Add the two `Default`-free boundary types and the two factory doors so every Card is born through `Card::create` (untrusted create) or `Card::reconstitute` (trusted rehydration), with id/clock/`card_number` injected. Pure domain only — **no** persistence or DTO changes here.

## Current state (researched)

- `Card` struct + serde derive: `crates/kanban-domain/src/card.rs:58-79`. It currently `#[derive(... Serialize, Deserialize)]` with `#[serde(default)]` on `card_number`, `sprint_id`, `completed_at`, `sprint_logs`.
- `Card::new(board: &mut Board, column_id, title, position)`: `card.rs:122-147` — mints `id`/`now`, calls `board.get_next_card_number()` (mutates Board), seeds defaults.
- Behavioural methods that already take an injected `now` (good, leave alone): `update(updates, now)` (card.rs:278-299), `assign_to_sprint(.., now)` (card.rs:247-262). Methods that still call `Utc::now()` internally: `move_to_column`, `update_status`, `update_priority`, `set_due_date`, `update_title`, `update_description`, `set_points`, `end_current_sprint_log` (card.rs:149-189, 264-271) — **out of scope for this slice**, leave as-is.
- `CardUpdate` (partial update) already exists: `card.rs:306-317`. Keep it; the DTO slice maps onto it.
- `CreateCardOptions` exists: `card.rs:319-327` — used by the current `create_card`/`CreateCard` path. Leave it for now; slice D decides its fate (it overlaps `NewCard`).
- `SprintLog`: `crates/kanban-domain/src/sprint_log.rs:5-13` — `Serialize, Deserialize`, leave its serde (it is a sub-record persisted inside `CardRecord`).
- `CardPriority` / `CardStatus`: `card.rs:11-25`.
- Board counter source: `board.rs:277-282` (`get_next_card_number`).
- No `NewCard`/`CardRecord`/`Card::create`/`Card::reconstitute` exists yet (grep confirms only `create_*` trait methods).

## Target

In `crates/kanban-domain/src/card.rs` (or a new `card/` submodule if the file exceeds ~300 lines after the additions — prefer a `card_factory.rs` sibling re-exported from `card.rs`).

```rust
/// Client-settable create fields ONLY (content). No id/timestamps/counters.
/// Default-free; never built with `..`.
pub struct NewCard {
    pub column_id: ColumnId,          // required FK (value, not object)
    pub title: String,
    pub description: Option<String>,
    pub priority: CardPriority,       // caller supplies; service defaults to Medium
    pub due_date: Option<DateTime<Utc>>,
    pub points: Option<u8>,
    pub sprint_id: Option<Uuid>,      // optional FK (value)
}

/// COMPLETE field set — the ONLY type that derives Serialize/Deserialize for
/// Card persistence. Default-free; distinct from `Card`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct CardRecord {
    pub id: CardId,
    pub column_id: ColumnId,
    pub title: String,
    pub description: Option<String>,
    pub priority: CardPriority,
    pub status: CardStatus,
    pub position: i32,
    pub due_date: Option<DateTime<Utc>>,
    pub points: Option<u8>,
    pub card_number: u32,
    pub sprint_id: Option<Uuid>,
    pub created_at: DateTime<Utc>,
    pub updated_at: DateTime<Utc>,
    pub completed_at: Option<DateTime<Utc>>,
    pub sprint_logs: Vec<SprintLog>,
}

impl Card {
    /// CREATE: id + card_number + clock injected by the service. Board-free.
    /// Seeds status=Todo, completed_at=None, sprint_logs=empty; created_at=updated_at=now.
    pub fn create(
        spec: NewCard,
        id: CardId,
        card_number: u32,
        now: DateTime<Utc>,
    ) -> KanbanResult<Card>;

    /// RECONSTITUTE: restore verbatim. Structural validation only. The single
    /// rehydration funnel.
    pub fn reconstitute(record: CardRecord) -> KanbanResult<Card>;
}

impl From<&Card> for CardRecord { /* exhaustive decompose, no `..` */ }
```

Decisions baked in:
- `card_number` is a **`create` parameter** (like `id`), NOT a field of `NewCard`. Rationale in the epic quirk #1: keeps `create` Board-free; the service mints it.
- `create` does **not** synthesize a SprintLog even when `spec.sprint_id` is `Some` — it just stores the id. Sprint-log seeding needs a Sprint object and stays in the service (quirk #2). `sprint_logs` starts empty.
- `priority` is a required field of `NewCard` (caller decides); the **service/DTO** layer applies the `Medium` default when the wire omits it (mirrors how Board's create DTO defaults). This keeps the domain free of an implicit default while the entity's documented create default remains `Medium`.

Remove the `Deserialize` derive from `Card` (`card.rs:58`) — keep `Serialize` only if a non-persistence consumer needs it; grep first (see Tests). Persistence round-trips through `CardRecord` (slice B). NOTE: removing `Card: Deserialize` will break `Snapshot`, `ArchivedCard`, the SQLite mappers, and `CreateCard::execute` at compile time — those breaks are **fixed in slices B and D**; this slice may need a temporary `Serialize`-only state, so coordinate: land A and B together if the workspace must stay green between merges, or keep `Deserialize` until B is ready and remove it in B. **Preferred: remove `Deserialize` in this slice and land A+B as a stacked pair** so the compile-lock is real.

## Step-by-step (TDD red → green → refactor)

1. **Red** — in `card.rs` tests (or `card_factory.rs` tests), add the factory unit tests below; they fail to compile (types absent).
2. **Green** — add `NewCard`, `CardRecord`, `Card::create`, `Card::reconstitute`, `From<&Card> for CardRecord`. Implement `create` by constructing the `Card` literal with injected `id`/`card_number`/`now`, `status: Todo`, `completed_at: None`, `sprint_logs: vec![]`, applying `spec` fields exhaustively. Implement `reconstitute` by destructuring `CardRecord` exhaustively into `Card`. Implement `From<&Card>` by destructuring `Card` exhaustively (no `..`).
3. **Refactor** — if `card.rs` > 300 lines, split the factory types into `card_factory.rs` and re-export. Ensure `create`/`reconstitute`/`From` all destructure exhaustively (compile-lock). Run `cargo fmt`, `clippy -D warnings`.

## Tests (pattern `test_<scenario>_<expected_outcome>`)

- `test_card_create_seeds_server_managed_defaults` — `create` yields `status==Todo`, `completed_at==None`, `sprint_logs` empty, `created_at==updated_at==now`, `id`/`card_number` equal the injected params.
- `test_card_create_applies_client_fields_from_spec` — title/description/priority/due_date/points/column_id/sprint_id all land from `NewCard`.
- `test_card_create_does_not_seed_sprint_log_for_present_sprint_id` — `spec.sprint_id=Some` ⇒ `card.sprint_id==Some` but `sprint_logs.is_empty()` (log seeding is service-tier).
- `test_card_create_is_deterministic_for_fixed_id_number_and_clock` — two calls with the same params produce equal cards (no internal RNG/clock).
- `test_card_reconstitute_restores_all_fields_verbatim` — build a `CardRecord` with non-default values incl. `status=Done`+`completed_at=Some`, `card_number=42`, `position=7`, two `SprintLog`s (one ended, one open); assert every field round-trips identically.
- `test_card_decompose_round_trip_via_record` — `let r = CardRecord::from(&card); let c2 = Card::reconstitute(r)?; assert_eq!(card, c2)` for a fully-populated card (with sprint logs).
- `test_card_record_serde_round_trip` — `CardRecord` → JSON → `CardRecord` equal (the persistence wire shape).
- `test_new_card_has_no_default_impl` — compile-fence doc/test note (a `Default::default()` on `NewCard` must not compile); enforced by the CI grep, asserted here as a comment + the absence of a `Default` derive.
- **Removal guard**: grep `crates/` for `Card:` deserialization sites before deleting the derive — `serde_json::from_*::<Card>` / `: Card` deser. Expected hits to migrate in B/D: `Snapshot` (snapshot.rs:32), `ArchivedCard` (archived_card.rs:12), SQLite `row_to_card`, `CreateCard::execute`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `NewCard`, `CardRecord` added; both `Default`-free; neither constructed with `..`.
- [ ] `Card::create(spec, id, card_number, now)` and `Card::reconstitute(record)` are inherent fns; neither calls `Uuid::new_v4()` nor `Utc::now()` nor touches a `Board`.
- [ ] `From<&Card> for CardRecord` exhaustively destructures `Card`.
- [ ] `Card` no longer derives `Deserialize` (land stacked with slice B to keep the workspace compiling).
- [ ] New unit tests pass; `cargo test --package kanban-domain` green; clippy/fmt clean.
- [ ] Compile-lock: adding a field to `CardRecord` breaks `reconstitute` + `From<&Card>`; adding a field to `NewCard` breaks `create`.

## Dependencies / sequencing

- First slice of the Card epic. Follows the **Board** domain-core slice as its template.
- Land **stacked with slice B** (`02-persistence.md`) so removing `Card: Deserialize` does not leave the workspace red.

## Execution learnings (spike, applied) — CORRECTIONS
- SUPERSEDES the Target prose that says "remove the Deserialize derive from Card": that is WRONG for slice A. Per the sequencing banner, slice A KEEPS Card: Deserialize; removal is slice B (KAN-783). Strike that paragraph when executing.
- CardRecord is a PLAIN derived Deserialize (no hand-written impl; no migration chain) with `#[serde(default)]` on card_number/sprint_id/completed_at/sprint_logs. Unlike BoardRecord.
- From<&Card>: 12 of 15 fields are Copy -> deref them (highest Copy ratio of the 4 entities). Compile-lock verified (E0027/E0063). Executed green: commit 4cdc5c10.

cards.description:
> ⚠ SEQUENCING CORRECTION (read first):
> As the **final step of this slice** — after `Snapshot` + sqlite read/write route through `CardRecord` — **remove `Card`'s `Deserialize` derive** (moved here from slice A). It lands green because nothing deserializes `Card` directly anymore; this is what enforces "the only way to make a `Card` is the factory." Slice A left the derive in place so it could ship green independently.

## Context / why

Slice B of the **Card entity factory** epic (root spec **KAN-769**). Make both persistence backends rehydrate `Card` exclusively through `CardRecord` → `Card::reconstitute` (from slice A), and decompose through `From<&Card> for CardRecord`. This removes every un-funnelled Card construction in persistence and makes the persistence↔domain relation a tested, compile-locked contract. Round-trip tests on **both** JSON and SQLite are the drift guard. Depends on slice A.

## Current state (researched)

### JSON (kanban-persistence-json)
- The JSON store keeps `data` as raw `serde_json::Value`/bytes (`crates/kanban-persistence-json/src/json_file_store.rs:34-35, 309-377`); it never deserializes `Card` itself.
- Deserialization to `Card` happens via the **domain `Snapshot`** type: `crates/kanban-domain/src/snapshot.rs:20-32` derives `Serialize, Deserialize` and holds `pub cards: Vec<Card>`. The service loads bytes → `Snapshot` (Card's own serde) → in-memory store (`crates/kanban-domain/src/in_memory_store/snapshot.rs:33-47`, `state.cards = snapshot.cards...`). This is the un-funnelled JSON construction path that must reroute through `CardRecord`.
- `ArchivedCard` (`crates/kanban-domain/src/archived_card.rs:11-12`) wraps a full `Card` and is also in `Snapshot.archived_cards` — same serde dependency.

### SQLite (kanban-persistence-sqlite)
- Row → `Card`: `crates/kanban-persistence-sqlite/src/sqlite_store/conversions.rs:73-104` (`row_to_card(row, sprint_logs)`) builds a `Card { .. }` literal directly. Sprint logs come from a separate query (`fetch_sprint_logs_for_card` / `fetch_sprint_logs_batch`, `entities/card.rs:11-23, 95-120`) and `row_to_sprint_log` (`conversions.rs:146-159`).
- `Card` → rows: `entities/card.rs:26-86` (`write_card` upserts the `cards` row, then `DELETE FROM sprint_logs WHERE card_id=?` + re-inserts each log). Schema: `cards` table `schema.sql:85-103`, `sprint_logs` table `schema.sql:107-119` (no FK on `sprint_id`; logs survive sprint deletion).
- Card read entry points: `data_store.rs:123-166` (`get_card`, `list_cards_by_column(s)`, `list_cards_by_sprint`), all funnelling into `row_to_card`.

## Target

The domain `Snapshot` must serialize/deserialize `CardRecord`, not `Card`, since `Card: Deserialize` is removed in slice A. Two viable shapes — pick **(1)**:

1. **`Snapshot` holds `Vec<CardRecord>`** (and archived cards hold `CardRecord`). The in-memory `apply_snapshot` maps `record → Card::reconstitute(record)?`; `snapshot_impl` maps `&card → CardRecord::from(card)`. This keeps the on-disk JSON shape byte-identical (field names match) while funnelling construction.
   - `crates/kanban-domain/src/snapshot.rs`: change `pub cards: Vec<Card>` → `pub cards: Vec<CardRecord>`; `archived_cards` similarly carries `CardRecord` inside the archived wrapper (introduce `ArchivedCardRecord { card: CardRecord, .. }` mirroring `ArchivedCard`).
   - `crates/kanban-domain/src/in_memory_store/snapshot.rs:14-15, 37`: build records on snapshot, `reconstitute` on apply (propagate the `KanbanResult`).

SQLite:
- `row_to_card` (`conversions.rs:73-104`): build a `CardRecord { .. }` from the row + `sprint_logs`, then return `Card::reconstitute(record)`. No more direct `Card { .. }` literal.
- `write_card` (`entities/card.rs`): decompose via `CardRecord::from(card)` and bind from the record (or keep binding from `&Card` fields — but route the **read** side through `reconstitute`; the write side already only reads scalar fields, so the minimal change is the read path). The compile-lock comes from the read side using the exhaustive `CardRecord`.
- `sprint_logs` continue to load via the separate batch query and feed `CardRecord.sprint_logs`; `reconstitute` restores them verbatim.

## Step-by-step (TDD red → green → refactor)

1. **Red (JSON)** — add a json round-trip test: build a fully-populated `Card` (Done status + completed_at, card_number, 2 sprint logs), save via the store, load, assert `Card == Card'`. Fails to compile once `Card: Deserialize` is gone / `Snapshot` still holds `Vec<Card>`.
2. **Green (JSON)** — change `Snapshot.cards`/archived to `CardRecord`; update `snapshot_impl`/`apply_snapshot_impl` to decompose/`reconstitute`. Adjust any migration code that constructs `Snapshot` cards (check `crates/kanban-persistence-json/src/migration/` — the V6/V7 steps operate on `serde_json::Value`, not typed `Card`, so they are unaffected; confirm with a grep for `Card` in `migration/`).
3. **Red (SQLite)** — add a sqlite round-trip test mirroring the JSON one (use `TempDir`).
4. **Green (SQLite)** — rewrite `row_to_card` to build `CardRecord` then `Card::reconstitute`. Keep `write_card` + the `sprint_logs` upsert as-is or decompose via `CardRecord::from`.
5. **Refactor** — ensure both arms destructure `CardRecord` exhaustively; remove any now-dead direct constructors; `fmt` + `clippy -D warnings`.

## Tests (pattern `test_<scenario>_<expected_outcome>`)

JSON (`kanban-persistence-json` inline tests, real tempfile):
- `test_json_card_round_trip_preserves_all_fields` — `Card → save → load → Card'`, `Card == Card'`, including `card_number`, `position`, `Done`+`completed_at`, `sprint_id`.
- `test_json_card_round_trip_preserves_sprint_logs_verbatim` — card with 2 `SprintLog`s (one `ended_at=Some`, one `None`) survives byte-for-byte.
- `test_json_archived_card_round_trip_preserves_card` — an archived card (wrapping a full `Card`) round-trips.

SQLite (`kanban-persistence-sqlite` inline tests, `TempDir`):
- `test_sqlite_card_round_trip_preserves_all_fields` — same field coverage as JSON.
- `test_sqlite_card_round_trip_restores_sprint_logs_from_separate_table` — write a card with 2 logs, reload, assert the logs come back ordered + complete (guards the separate-table reassembly through `reconstitute`).
- `test_sqlite_card_reconstitute_rejects_malformed_row` (optional) — a row with an unparseable enum/uuid surfaces a `KanbanError`, not a panic.

Cross-backend:
- `test_card_record_is_the_only_card_deserialization_funnel` — a compile-level guard: `Card` does not implement `Deserialize` (assert via the absence of a `from_str::<Card>` path; the CI grep enforces it).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] JSON and SQLite both rehydrate `Card` only via `CardRecord` → `Card::reconstitute`; no `Card { .. }` literal remains in persistence (`row_to_card` rewritten; `Snapshot` holds `CardRecord`).
- [ ] `sprint_logs` round-trip verbatim on both backends (separate-table reassembly verified on SQLite).
- [ ] Archived-card path migrated (`ArchivedCardRecord` or equivalent) since it embeds a `Card`.
- [ ] `cargo test --package kanban-persistence-json` and `--package kanban-persistence-sqlite` green; clippy/fmt clean.
- [ ] Compile-lock: adding a `CardRecord` field breaks both backend arms until handled.

## Dependencies / sequencing

- Depends on slice A (`01-domain-core.md`). **Land stacked with A** (A removes `Card: Deserialize`, which only compiles once this slice reroutes the snapshot + sqlite arms).
- Mirrors the Board persistence slice.

## Implementation sketch (before -> after)

Slice A introduces `CardRecord` (the flat, serde-deriving transfer struct) plus `Card::reconstitute(record: CardRecord) -> KanbanResult<Card>` and `impl From<&Card> for CardRecord`. `CardRecord` owns `sprint_logs: Vec<SprintLog>` so the separate-table reassembly funnels through it. This slice reroutes every persistence-side `Card` construction through that funnel. Citations below are the current code as it exists before the change.

### 1. SQLite read — BEFORE

`crates/kanban-persistence-sqlite/src/sqlite_store/conversions.rs:73-104` builds a bare `Card { .. }` literal and just drops the separately-queried `sprint_logs` into the last field:

```rust
pub(crate) fn row_to_card(row: &SqliteRow, sprint_logs: Vec<SprintLog>) -> KanbanResult<Card> {
    let id_str: String = row.try_get("id").map_err(db_err)?;
    let column_id_str: String = row.try_get("column_id").map_err(db_err)?;
    let sprint_id_str: Option<String> = row.try_get("sprint_id").map_err(db_err)?;
    // ... created_at_str / updated_at_str / completed_at_str / due_date_str / priority_str / status_str / points_raw ...

    Ok(Card {
        id: p_uuid(&id_str)?,
        column_id: p_uuid(&column_id_str)?,
        title: row.try_get("title").map_err(db_err)?,
        description: row.try_get("description").map_err(db_err)?,
        priority: p_enum(&priority_str, "priority")?,
        status: p_enum(&status_str, "status")?,
        position: row.try_get("position").map_err(db_err)?,
        due_date: due_date_str.as_deref().map(p_dt).transpose()?,
        points: points_raw
            .map(|v| u8::try_from(v).map_err(|_| ser_err(format!("points {v} out of range"))))
            .transpose()?,
        card_number: row.try_get::<i32, _>("card_number").map_err(db_err)? as u32,
        sprint_id: sprint_id_str.as_deref().map(p_uuid).transpose()?,
        created_at: p_dt(&created_at_str)?,
        updated_at: p_dt(&updated_at_str)?,
        completed_at: completed_at_str.as_deref().map(p_dt).transpose()?,
        sprint_logs,                       // <- separate sprint_logs table, attached raw
    })
}
```

The `sprint_logs` arg is filled by the separate-table queries `fetch_sprint_logs_for_card` / `fetch_sprint_logs_batch` (`entities/card.rs:11-23, 95-119`, each `row_to_sprint_log` per `conversions.rs:146-159`), then handed in at the call sites in `fetch_cards_with_filter` (`entities/card.rs:143-150`):

```rust
let mut logs_map = self.fetch_sprint_logs_batch(&card_ids).await?;
for row in &rows {
    let id_str: String = row.try_get("id").map_err(db_err)?;
    let logs = logs_map.remove(&id_str).unwrap_or_default();
    cards.push(row_to_card(row, logs)?);
}
```

### 1. SQLite read — AFTER

Same scalar parsing, but assemble a `CardRecord { .. }` (which now carries `sprint_logs`) and hand it to `Card::reconstitute`. No `Card { .. }` literal survives in persistence; the exhaustive `CardRecord` destructure is the compile-lock.

```rust
use kanban_domain::{Card, CardRecord, KanbanResult, SprintLog};

pub(crate) fn row_to_card(row: &SqliteRow, sprint_logs: Vec<SprintLog>) -> KanbanResult<Card> {
    let id_str: String = row.try_get("id").map_err(db_err)?;
    let column_id_str: String = row.try_get("column_id").map_err(db_err)?;
    let sprint_id_str: Option<String> = row.try_get("sprint_id").map_err(db_err)?;
    // ... same created_at_str / updated_at_str / completed_at_str / due_date_str / priority_str / status_str / points_raw ...

    let record = CardRecord {
        id: p_uuid(&id_str)?,
        column_id: p_uuid(&column_id_str)?,
        title: row.try_get("title").map_err(db_err)?,
        description: row.try_get("description").map_err(db_err)?,
        priority: p_enum(&priority_str, "priority")?,
        status: p_enum(&status_str, "status")?,
        position: row.try_get("position").map_err(db_err)?,
        due_date: due_date_str.as_deref().map(p_dt).transpose()?,
        points: points_raw
            .map(|v| u8::try_from(v).map_err(|_| ser_err(format!("points {v} out of range"))))
            .transpose()?,
        card_number: row.try_get::<i32, _>("card_number").map_err(db_err)? as u32,
        sprint_id: sprint_id_str.as_deref().map(p_uuid).transpose()?,
        created_at: p_dt(&created_at_str)?,
        updated_at: p_dt(&updated_at_str)?,
        completed_at: completed_at_str.as_deref().map(p_dt).transpose()?,
        sprint_logs,                       // <- separate sprint_logs query feeds the record here
    };

    Card::reconstitute(record)
}
```

The call sites in `fetch_cards_with_filter` (and the `get_card` / `list_cards_by_*` paths in `data_store.rs:123-166`) are unchanged: they still resolve `logs` from `fetch_sprint_logs_batch` and pass them positionally; the funnel is entirely inside `row_to_card`.

### 3. SQLite write — `write_card_with_conn`

The write side already only reads scalar `&Card` fields (`entities/card.rs:26-86`). Decompose once via `CardRecord::from(card)` and bind from the record so the `cards`-row binding is exhaustive-destructure-locked; the `sprint_logs` rows are still written to their own table exactly as today.

BEFORE (binds directly off `&Card`):

```rust
.bind(&id)
.bind(card.column_id.to_string())
.bind(required_str(&card.title, "card.title")?)
.bind(&card.description)
.bind(format!("{:?}", card.priority))
.bind(format!("{:?}", card.status))
// ... position / due_date / points / card_number / sprint_id / created_at / updated_at / completed_at ...
```

AFTER (binds off the decomposed record; sprint_logs loop untouched):

```rust
pub(crate) async fn write_card_with_conn(
    conn: &mut sqlx::SqliteConnection,
    card: &Card,
) -> KanbanResult<()> {
    let record = CardRecord::from(card);
    let id = record.id.to_string();

    sqlx::query("INSERT INTO cards (...) VALUES (...) ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET ...")
        .bind(&id)
        .bind(record.column_id.to_string())
        .bind(required_str(&record.title, "card.title")?)
        .bind(&record.description)
        .bind(format!("{:?}", record.priority))
        .bind(format!("{:?}", record.status))
        .bind(record.position)
        .bind(opt_dt(&record.due_date))
        .bind(record.points.map(|v| v as i32))
        .bind(record.card_number as i32)
        .bind(record.sprint_id.map(|id| id.to_string()))
        .bind(fmt_dt(&record.created_at))
        .bind(fmt_dt(&record.updated_at))
        .bind(opt_dt(&record.completed_at))
        .execute(&mut *conn)
        .await
        .map_err(db_err)?;

    // sprint_logs still live in their own table — re-derive from record.sprint_logs:
    sqlx::query("DELETE FROM sprint_logs WHERE card_id = ?")
        .bind(&id)
        .execute(&mut *conn)
        .await
        .map_err(db_err)?;
    for log in &record.sprint_logs {
        sqlx::query(
            "INSERT INTO sprint_logs (card_id, sprint_id, sprint_number, sprint_name,
                started_at, ended_at, status) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
        )
        .bind(&id)
        .bind(log.sprint_id.to_string())
        .bind(log.sprint_number as i32)
        .bind(&log.sprint_name)
        .bind(fmt_dt(&log.started_at))
        .bind(opt_dt(&log.ended_at))
        .bind(required_str(&log.status, "sprint_log.status")?)
        .execute(&mut *conn)
        .await
        .map_err(db_err)?;
    }
    Ok(())
}
```

(The `sprint_logs` table — `schema.sql:107-119`, no FK on `sprint_id`, `ON DELETE CASCADE` from `card_id` — is unchanged. Reassembly back into `CardRecord.sprint_logs` happens on the read side above.)

### 4a. JSON snapshot — `Snapshot.cards`

Slice A removes `Card: Deserialize`, so the domain `Snapshot` (`snapshot.rs:20-32`) can no longer hold `Vec<Card>`. Route it through `CardRecord`, keeping field names identical so the on-disk JSON stays byte-compatible.

BEFORE (`crates/kanban-domain/src/snapshot.rs:30-36`):

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, Default)]
pub struct Snapshot {
    // ...
    #[serde(default)]
    pub cards: Vec<Card>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub archived_cards: Vec<ArchivedCard>,
    // ...
}
```

AFTER:

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, Default)]
pub struct Snapshot {
    // ...
    #[serde(default)]
    pub cards: Vec<CardRecord>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub archived_cards: Vec<ArchivedCardRecord>,   // see 4b
    // ...
}
```

The decompose/reconstitute happens in the in-memory adapters. BEFORE the cards move as `Card` (`in_memory_store/snapshot.rs:14-15, 37`):

```rust
// snapshot_impl (build)
let mut cards: Vec<_> = state.cards.values().cloned().collect();   // Vec<Card>
cards.sort_by_key(|c| c.position);
// apply_snapshot_impl
state.cards = snapshot.cards.into_iter().map(|c| (c.id, c)).collect();
```

AFTER — `snapshot_impl` decomposes each `&Card` into a `CardRecord`; `apply_snapshot_impl` reconstitutes (propagating `KanbanResult`):

```rust
// snapshot_impl (build) — decompose
let mut cards: Vec<CardRecord> = state.cards.values().map(CardRecord::from).collect();
cards.sort_by_key(|r| r.position);

// apply_snapshot_impl — reconstitute
state.cards = snapshot
    .cards
    .into_iter()
    .map(|record| {
        let card = Card::reconstitute(record)?;
        Ok((card.id, card))
    })
    .collect::<KanbanResult<_>>()?;
state.rebuild_card_column_index();
```

### 4b. JSON snapshot — `ArchivedCard`

`ArchivedCard` embeds a full `Card` (`archived_card.rs:11-16`), so it inherits the lost `Deserialize`. Mirror it with an `ArchivedCardRecord` that swaps the embedded `Card` for a `CardRecord`; the wrapper metadata fields are unchanged.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ArchivedCardRecord {
    pub card: CardRecord,
    pub archived_at: DateTime<Utc>,
    pub original_column_id: ColumnId,
    pub original_position: i32,
}

impl From<&ArchivedCard> for ArchivedCardRecord {
    fn from(a: &ArchivedCard) -> Self {
        Self {
            card: CardRecord::from(&a.card),
            archived_at: a.archived_at,
            original_column_id: a.original_column_id,
            original_position: a.original_position,
        }
    }
}

impl ArchivedCardRecord {
    fn reconstitute(self) -> KanbanResult<ArchivedCard> {
        Ok(ArchivedCard {
            card: Card::reconstitute(self.card)?,
            archived_at: self.archived_at,
            original_column_id: self.original_column_id,
            original_position: self.original_position,
        })
    }
}
```

The snapshot adapters mirror 4a. BEFORE (`in_memory_store/snapshot.rs:17-18, 39-43`):

```rust
let mut archived_cards: Vec<_> = state.archived_cards.values().cloned().collect();  // Vec<ArchivedCard>
// apply
state.archived_cards = snapshot
    .archived_cards
    .into_iter()
    .map(|ac| (ac.card.id, ac))
    .collect();
```

AFTER:

```rust
// build — decompose
let mut archived_cards: Vec<ArchivedCardRecord> =
    state.archived_cards.values().map(ArchivedCardRecord::from).collect();
archived_cards.sort_by(|a, b| a.archived_at.cmp(&b.archived_at));

// apply — reconstitute
state.archived_cards = snapshot
    .archived_cards
    .into_iter()
    .map(|record| {
        let ac = record.reconstitute()?;
        Ok((ac.card.id, ac))
    })
    .collect::<KanbanResult<_>>()?;
```

The JSON store itself (`json_file_store.rs:34-35, 309-377`) keeps `data` as raw `serde_json::Value`/bytes and never touches `Card` directly, and the V6/V7 migration steps operate on `serde_json::Value` (not typed `Card`), so both are unaffected — the only JSON funnel is the `Snapshot` (de)serialization above.

## Execution learnings (spike, applied) — CORRECTIONS
- SUPERSEDES §4a: do NOT change Snapshot.cards to Vec<CardRecord>. Keep `Vec<Card>` + `#[serde(with = "crate::card_factory::card_vec_serde")]` (Board pattern). The in_memory_store snapshot apply/impl edits + KanbanResult propagation the card describes are UNNECESSARY.
- SUPERSEDES §4b: do NOT build ArchivedCardRecord. Add `#[serde(with = "crate::card_factory::card_serde")]` to ArchivedCard.card and keep ArchivedCard's own derive; the three Vec<ArchivedCard> sites then need nothing, and sqlite archived reads route through the existing row_to_card.
- Missed site: editable.rs test `test_card_deserialization_from_old_format` deserializes Card directly -> repoint to CardRecord/reconstitute.
- sprint_logs separate-table reassembly is lossless via row_to_card(row, logs) -> CardRecord -> reconstitute. FK fixture: real board+column for column_id, sprint_id=None. Executed green: commit 728d49aa.

## Quality-gate finding (performance, code-quality)
`From<&Card> for CardRecord` clones `card.sprint_logs: Vec<SprintLog>` on every write/serialize. For write-only paths, borrow `&card.sprint_logs` (or add a borrow-based decompose) rather than cloning the Vec. Negligible per single card; ~32KB of avoidable allocation per 1000-card snapshot save. Not blocking; fix when implementing the real slice.
cards.title: refactor(persistence): route Card json+sqlite through CardRecord/reconstitute

cards.description:
## Context / why

Slice C of the **Card entity factory** epic (root spec **KAN-769**). Card DTOs **do not exist yet** in `kanban-service::api::v1` (only `boards/` and `columns/` modules are present). This slice creates the Card request/response DTOs and their domain conversions from scratch, following the `columns/` module as the canonical pattern, with exhaustive destructuring (the compile-lock) and per-arm boundary tests. No service wiring yet (that is slice D).

## Current state (researched)

- `api/v1` module layout: `crates/kanban-service/src/api/v1/mod.rs` exports `boards::{...}`, `columns::{...}`, `enums::{SortFieldDto, SortOrderDto, TaskListViewDto}`, `Patch`, `Page`, etc. (mod.rs:10-19). No `cards` submodule.
- Column DTO template (mirror this exactly): `columns/requests.rs` (`CreateColumnRequest`, `UpdateColumnRequest` with `Patch<T>`, `ReplaceColumnRequest`), `columns/conversions.rs` (`TryFrom<…Request> for ColumnUpdate`, `into_parts`, validators, exhaustive destructure no-`..`), `columns/response.rs` (`From<Column> for ColumnResponse`), `columns/mod.rs`.
- `Patch<T>` (absent=NoChange / null=Clear / value=Set) → `FieldUpdate<T>`: `api/v1/patch.rs:13-44`. Use it for `description`, `due_date`, `points`, `sprint_id` in the Card PATCH DTO (these are `FieldUpdate` in `CardUpdate`).
- Domain targets the DTOs convert into:
  - `NewCard` (slice A) — create.
  - `CardUpdate` (`card.rs:306-317`): `title: Option<String>`, `description: FieldUpdate<String>`, `priority: Option<CardPriority>`, `status: Option<CardStatus>`, `position: Option<i32>`, `column_id: Option<ColumnId>`, `due_date: FieldUpdate<DateTime<Utc>>`, `points: FieldUpdate<u8>`, `sprint_id: FieldUpdate<Uuid>` — update/replace.
  - `Card` (`card.rs:58-79`) — response source via `From<&Card>`.
- Enum wire mirrors: `api/v1/enums.rs` mirrors Sort/TaskListView with snake_case + exhaustive `From`. **`CardPriority`/`CardStatus` have NO wire mirror yet** — add `CardPriorityDto`/`CardStatusDto` here (snake_case, exhaustive `From` both directions), matching the existing enum-mirror pattern. Domain `Display` already emits `low`/`medium`/`high`/`critical` and `todo`/`in_progress`/`blocked`/`done` (card.rs:27-47) — match those tokens.
- MCP's bespoke `CreateCardRequest` (`crates/kanban-mcp/src/requests/card.rs:4-28`) parses `priority`/`due_date`/`sprint_id` as loose strings — the new DTO supersedes it in slice D; do not touch MCP here.

## Target

New module `crates/kanban-service/src/api/v1/cards/` with `requests.rs`, `response.rs`, `conversions.rs`, `mod.rs`; mirror enums added to `api/v1/enums.rs`. Register `pub mod cards;` + re-exports in `api/v1/mod.rs`.

```rust
// cards/requests.rs
/// POST /v1/columns/:column_id/cards  (column_id from the path, NOT the body)
pub struct CreateCardRequest {
    #[serde(default)] pub id: Option<Uuid>,        // optional client-supplied id (idempotent PUT-create)
    pub title: String,
    #[serde(default)] pub description: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)] pub priority: Option<CardPriorityDto>, // omitted -> Medium default at conversion
    #[serde(default)] pub due_date: Option<DateTime<Utc>>,
    #[serde(default)] pub points: Option<u8>,
    #[serde(default)] pub sprint_id: Option<Uuid>, // optional FK
}

/// PATCH /v1/cards/:id — JSON Merge Patch
pub struct UpdateCardRequest {
    #[serde(default)] pub title: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)] pub priority: Option<CardPriorityDto>,
    #[serde(default)] pub status: Option<CardStatusDto>,
    #[serde(default)] pub position: Option<i32>,
    #[serde(default)] pub column_id: Option<Uuid>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Patch::is_no_change")] pub description: Patch<String>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Patch::is_no_change")] pub due_date: Patch<DateTime<Utc>>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Patch::is_no_change")] pub points: Patch<u8>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Patch::is_no_change")] pub sprint_id: Patch<Uuid>,
}

/// PUT /v1/cards/:id — full replace of client-editable fields. Omitted optional fields are cleared.
pub struct ReplaceCardRequest {
    pub title: String,
    pub priority: CardPriorityDto,
    pub status: CardStatusDto,
    pub position: i32,
    pub column_id: Uuid,
    #[serde(default)] pub description: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)] pub due_date: Option<DateTime<Utc>>,
    #[serde(default)] pub points: Option<u8>,
    #[serde(default)] pub sprint_id: Option<Uuid>,
}
```

```rust
// cards/conversions.rs
impl CreateCardRequest {
    /// column_id comes from the route path (not the body). Returns the optional
    /// client id alongside the spec so the service can mint-or-use it.
    pub fn into_new_card(self, column_id: ColumnId) -> KanbanResult<(Option<Uuid>, NewCard)>;
}
impl TryFrom<UpdateCardRequest>  for CardUpdate { /* Patch -> FieldUpdate, exhaustive */ }
impl TryFrom<ReplaceCardRequest> for CardUpdate { /* omitted Option -> Clear, exhaustive */ }
```

```rust
// cards/response.rs
pub struct CardResponse {
    pub id: Uuid,
    pub column_id: Uuid,
    pub title: String,
    pub description: Option<String>,
    pub priority: CardPriorityDto,
    pub status: CardStatusDto,
    pub position: i32,
    pub due_date: Option<DateTime<Utc>>,
    pub points: Option<u8>,
    pub card_number: u32,        // EXPOSED (it is the human identifier, e.g. KAN-5), unlike Board counters
    pub sprint_id: Option<Uuid>,
    pub created_at: DateTime<Utc>,
    pub updated_at: DateTime<Utc>,
    pub completed_at: Option<DateTime<Utc>>,
    // sprint_logs INTENTIONALLY HIDDEN from the wire response (internal history).
}
impl From<&Card> for CardResponse { /* exhaustive destructure of Card, no `..` */ }
```

Field-policy notes:
- `card_number` **is exposed** in the response (it is the user-facing card identifier driving `KAN-5`/branch names), in contrast to Board's internal `card_counter` which is hidden. It is NOT accepted on create (server-minted).
- `sprint_logs` is **hidden** from `CardResponse` (internal history; if a history endpoint is needed later it gets its own DTO).
- `id` on create is the only place a client id is accepted; it is a `create` identity param, never content.
- Conversions destructure both the request and the domain target exhaustively so a new field on either side fails to compile (compile-lock); the `From<&Card>` must name every `Card` field.

## Step-by-step (TDD red → green → refactor)

1. **Red** — add the per-arm boundary + compile-lock tests (below); they fail to compile (types absent).
2. **Green** — add `CardPriorityDto`/`CardStatusDto` to `enums.rs` (snake_case, exhaustive `From` both ways). Create `cards/` module + the three request DTOs, `CardResponse`, and the conversions. Register in `mod.rs`.
3. **Refactor** — factor shared validation (e.g. `points`/`position` non-negativity is already type-guarded; `points: u8` needs none). Ensure every conversion + `From<&Card>` destructures exhaustively. `fmt` + `clippy -D warnings`.

## Tests (pattern `test_<scenario>_<expected_outcome>`)

Requests serde:
- `test_create_card_request_minimal_omits_optionals` — `{"title":"x"}` parses; `id`/`description`/`priority`/`due_date`/`points`/`sprint_id` all `None`.
- `test_create_card_request_accepts_client_id` — `{"title":"x","id":"<uuid>"}` parses with `id == Some(uuid)`.
- `test_update_card_request_absent_is_no_change_null_is_clear` — for `description`/`due_date`/`points`/`sprint_id`: absent→`NoChange`, `null`→`Clear`, value→`Set` (mirrors the column Patch test).
- `test_update_card_request_omits_no_change_patch_fields_on_serialize` — `UpdateCardRequest::default()` serializes without the Patch keys.

Enum mirrors:
- `test_card_priority_dto_serializes_snake_case_and_round_trips_through_domain` — `Medium`→`"medium"`, all four variants round-trip.
- `test_card_status_dto_serializes_snake_case_and_round_trips_through_domain` — `InProgress`→`"in_progress"`, all four variants.

Conversions (boundary — each field lands in the RIGHT place):
- `test_create_card_request_into_new_card_maps_every_field` — given a fully-populated request + path `column_id`, the resulting `NewCard` has each field where expected; returned `Option<Uuid>` id matches the request id.
- `test_create_card_request_defaults_priority_to_medium_when_omitted` — omitted `priority` ⇒ `NewCard.priority == Medium`.
- `test_update_card_request_into_card_update_maps_patch_to_field_update` — `description: Patch::Clear` ⇒ `CardUpdate.description == FieldUpdate::Clear`; `status`/`position`/`column_id` map straight through.
- `test_replace_card_request_clears_omitted_optionals` — omitted `description`/`due_date`/`points`/`sprint_id` ⇒ `FieldUpdate::Clear`; required fields ⇒ `Some`.
- `test_card_response_from_card_exposes_card_number_hides_sprint_logs` — `CardResponse::from(&card)` carries `card_number`, every scalar field, and has no `sprint_logs` field (compile-level) ; serde round-trip equal.

Compile-lock:
- `test_card_conversions_destructure_exhaustively` — doc/marker note that all arms use full destructuring; enforced by the CI grep for `..`/`Default::default()` over `cards/conversions.rs` + `response.rs`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `cards/` module added with `CreateCardRequest` (with optional `id`), `UpdateCardRequest` (Patch fields), `ReplaceCardRequest`, `CardResponse`; `CardPriorityDto`/`CardStatusDto` added to `enums.rs`; all re-exported from `api/v1/mod.rs`.
- [ ] `CreateCardRequest::into_new_card(column_id)`, `TryFrom<Update/ReplaceCardRequest> for CardUpdate`, `From<&Card> for CardResponse` implemented with exhaustive destructuring.
- [ ] `card_number` exposed in the response, NOT accepted on create; `sprint_logs` hidden; client `id` accepted only as a create identity param.
- [ ] `cargo test --package kanban-service` green; clippy/fmt clean.
- [ ] Compile-lock: adding a `NewCard`/`CardUpdate`/`Card` field breaks the corresponding conversion arm.

## Dependencies / sequencing

- Depends on slice A (`NewCard`). Independent of slice B at the type level but should land after A.
- Mirrors the Board/Column DTO slice; `columns/` is the closest structural template (FK + optional `Patch` field).

## Background

Once Chocolatey publish lands (the release.yml subtask), Windows users have a real install path: `choco install kanban`. This needs to surface in user-facing docs so Windows users actually find it, and the maintainer-facing CONTRIBUTING.md needs the operational details so future contributors can debug or take over the Chocolatey pipeline.

This card is pure docs. No code, no CI, no Chocolatey-side action. It depends on the release.yml publish subtask actually landing first — otherwise the install command in README would be a lie.

## Files to update

### `README.md`

Locate the installation section (currently has cargo, AUR, nixpkgs). Add a Windows subsection:

```markdown
### Windows (Chocolatey)

    choco install kanban

Requires [Chocolatey](https://chocolatey.org/install) on Windows 10/11
or Windows Server 2016+. The package wraps the official Windows release
binary from GitHub Releases; verify locally with:

    choco info kanban
```

Order in the install list: put Chocolatey above AUR (Arch is niche; Chocolatey is the broadest Windows path), but below cargo (the universal-truth install). Final ordering: cargo, Chocolatey, AUR, nixpkgs, Homebrew (when KAN-465 lands).

If a "All install paths at a glance" mini-table exists or is added by KAN-465, append the row:

```markdown
| Windows (Chocolatey) | `choco install kanban`                  |
```

Tone match: README sets a "short, scannable" tone that this section must respect — no marketing prose, no install-time troubleshooting (push those to CONTRIBUTING.md).

### `CONTRIBUTING.md`

Add a Chocolatey-specific subsection inside the Packaging section. If no "Packaging" section exists (i.e. KAN-465 hasn't added one yet), create it as a top-level section in CONTRIBUTING.md and add Chocolatey as its first subsection. The brew subsection will join it later.

Content:

```markdown
## Packaging — Chocolatey

The Chocolatey package source lives at `packaging/chocolatey/`.
The release pipeline publishes to community.chocolatey.org on every
release.

### File layout

- `packaging/chocolatey/kanban.nuspec` — package metadata (templated).
- `packaging/chocolatey/tools/chocolateyinstall.ps1` — downloads the
  Windows release ZIP from GitHub at install time, verifies SHA256.
- `packaging/chocolatey/tools/chocolateyuninstall.ps1` — reverses the
  install.
- `packaging/chocolatey/tools/LICENSE.txt` — placeholder; populated at
  pack time from `LICENSE.md` at repo root.
- `packaging/chocolatey/tools/VERIFICATION.txt` — required by
  Chocolatey moderation; explains how to verify the binary.

### Release flow

On each release (driven by changesets), `.github/workflows/release.yml`
runs the `publish-chocolatey` job:

1. Builds the Windows release ZIP (`build-windows` job).
2. Downloads the published ZIP from GitHub releases and computes its
   SHA256.
3. Stages a copy of `packaging/chocolatey/` under `build/chocolatey/`
   with `$version$` and `$checksum64$` substituted.
4. Runs `choco pack` then `choco push`, authenticated via the
   `CHOCO_API_KEY` repo secret.

Moderation is asynchronous (1-7 days for a first version, typically
under 24 hours subsequently). Status:

    https://community.chocolatey.org/packages/kanban/<VERSION>

### Required repo secret

| Secret           | Scope                                          | Where issued                                |
|------------------|------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------|
| `CHOCO_API_KEY`  | Push access to community.chocolatey.org/api/v2 | community.chocolatey.org account settings   |

To rotate: regenerate the key in the Chocolatey account UI; update the
repo secret. Old key revokes immediately on regeneration.

### Local validation

On a Windows machine:

    cd packaging/chocolatey
    # Manually substitute placeholders for a local pack:
    (Get-Content kanban.nuspec) -replace '\$version\$', '0.6.0' | Set-Content kanban.nuspec
    Copy-Item ..\..\LICENSE.md tools\LICENSE.txt
    choco pack
    choco install kanban -s . -y --force
    kanban --version

Revert the in-tree substitutions before committing.

### Troubleshooting

- `choco push` exits non-zero with "Package already exists": expected
  if re-running for the same version; bump the version in `Cargo.toml`.
- Moderator rejection arrives via the account email. Common causes:
  missing VERIFICATION.txt, missing LICENSE.txt at the *package* level
  (not just the project root), or `$ErrorActionPreference` not `Stop`
  in install scripts. All three are covered by the current packaging
  files; rejections most likely indicate a regression.
- Install fails on a fresh Windows machine with "Could not find
  kanban.exe": the archive layout changed between the published ZIP
  and what `chocolateyinstall.ps1` expects. Re-pack against the actual
  artifact layout.
```

If CONTRIBUTING.md already has a "Packaging" or "Distribution" top-level section (created earlier by KAN-446 or KAN-465), nest "Chocolatey" under it rather than creating a sibling top-level. Don't duplicate the "release flow" prose if it already covers AUR/brew — just add the Chocolatey-specific bits.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `README.md` has a "Windows (Chocolatey)" installation entry in the right position relative to other install paths.
- [ ] `CONTRIBUTING.md` has a Chocolatey packaging section covering file layout, release flow, secrets, local validation, and troubleshooting.
- [ ] Install command in README is verified live: `choco install kanban` on a Windows machine succeeds (or, if moderation has not yet approved, this card is marked as "pending moderation" and revisited).
- [ ] Cross-references: `README.md` Chocolatey section links to `https://chocolatey.org/install` for users new to Chocolatey itself.
- [ ] No prose conflicts: the new sections do not contradict adjacent sections (e.g. cargo install instructions still correct, no "coming soon" prose left over from when Chocolatey wasn't yet shipping).
- [ ] If KAN-465 lands before this card, the existing Homebrew docs structure is reused (no duplicated Packaging top-level section).

## Out of scope

- Marketing the Chocolatey package (announcements, blog posts).
- Adding a Chocolatey badge to README header.
- Translating docs.
- Updating any external (off-repo) documentation site.

## Related

- **Parent**: chocolatey umbrella card.
- **Depends on**: release.yml publish subtask landing so the install command is live.
- **KAN-465** — analogous docs work for Homebrew may have created the top-level packaging section in CONTRIBUTING.md; nest under it if present.

cards.description:
## Background

Architectural direction set 2026-05-25 during the chocolatey publish work: as additional package registries get added, **each registry gets its own dedicated GitHub repo**, triggered by `repository_dispatch` from this main repo's `release.yml`. This matches what Homebrew and Nix already do today by necessity or convention.

The decision is not blocking. The chocolatey work (KAN-537 and children) is being delivered in the main repo first under the current Pattern A, with the explicit understanding that it will be migrated out under this card when the dispatch infrastructure is set up.

## Precedent (current state of each registry)

| Registry | Current location | Pattern |
|---|---|---|
| Homebrew | `fulsomenko/homebrew-tap` (separate repo) | B (forced by `brew tap user/X` convention) |
| Nix flake | self-managed separately | B (forced by nixpkgs PR model) |
| AUR | inline in this repo's `aur/PKGBUILD` + `release.yml` steps | A (in-repo) |
| Chocolatey | being added in `packaging/chocolatey/` + `release.yml` jobs (KAN-537 chain) | A (in-repo, transitional) |
| winget (future) | not yet | B target — should be filed straight into a dedicated repo |
| Homebrew core (future) | not yet | special: PR to `Homebrew/homebrew-core`, not a fulsomenko repo |

## What "Pattern B" looks like

Per-registry repo, named `fulsomenko/<registry>-kanban` (matching the existing `homebrew-tap` precedent on convention).

Contents at repo root:
- The registry's packaging source files (nuspec, PKGBUILD, winget manifests, etc.).
- `.github/workflows/publish.yml`, triggered by:
  - `workflow_dispatch` (manual re-publish lever).
  - `repository_dispatch` with event type `kanban-release` (fired from main repo on release).

The main repo's `release.yml` ends with one dispatch step per registry. Each registry repo's workflow handles its own pack + push, downloading the binary artifact from the main repo's GitHub release.

```
fulsomenko/kanban (main)
  release.yml:
    - publish crates.io
    - tag, GH release
    - build-windows job (artifact upload — stays here, KAN-539)
    - dispatch → fulsomenko/chocolatey-kanban
    - dispatch → fulsomenko/aur-kanban
    - dispatch → fulsomenko/homebrew-tap (replaces inline brew bump)
    - dispatch → fulsomenko/winget-kanban (future)
```

## Migrations in scope under this card

| Registry | Source location to drain | New repo to create |
|---|---|---|
| Chocolatey | `packaging/chocolatey/` + `publish-chocolatey` job in `release.yml` | `fulsomenko/chocolatey-kanban` |
| AUR | `aur/PKGBUILD` + AUR-related steps in `release.yml` | `fulsomenko/aur-kanban` |
| Homebrew tap workflow | inline "Bump formula in homebrew-tap" step in `release.yml` | already `fulsomenko/homebrew-tap` — move the bump *logic* to a workflow in the tap repo, replace inline step with a dispatch |

The `build-windows` job (KAN-539) stays in the main repo. It produces the GitHub release artifact that all Pattern-B registry repos download. Building artifacts is "the project's release", not "a particular registry's package".

## Prerequisites

### Dispatch credentials

Need a way for the main repo's release.yml to trigger workflows in each registry repo. `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot trigger workflows in another repo by default. Two options:

1. **Fine-grained PAT** — simpler. One PAT per target repo (or one PAT scoped to all of them). Set as secrets like `CHOCOLATEY_KANBAN_DISPATCH_TOKEN`. Faster to set up, harder to audit and rotate at scale.

2. **GitHub App** — better long-term. One App installed on the main repo and each registry repo, with `actions:write` scope. Revocable, scoped per-repo, observable in the App's audit log. ~30 min setup once. **Recommended given that we'll have ≥3 registry repos.**

### Repo conventions (apply to each new registry repo)

- Apache-2.0 `LICENSE.md` (copied verbatim from main repo).
- `README.md` pointing at main repo (analogous to the existing `fulsomenko/homebrew-tap` README).
- `CODEOWNERS` (Max).
- Minimal CI on PRs: `actionlint` for any workflows + registry-specific syntax check for the package source file (e.g. `xmllint` for nuspec, `namcap` for PKGBUILD, `winget validate` for winget).
- Branch protection on default branch matching main repo's conventions (signed commits if applicable, PR review required for non-trivial changes).

## Trade-offs (explicit)

**Pro Pattern B:**

- SRP at the repo level. Each registry's quirks are isolated; one registry's moderation rejection doesn't stall another.
- Independent versioning of packaging logic. A typo fix in `chocolateyinstall.ps1` doesn't bloat the main repo's git history.
- Easier to deprecate or hand off a single registry without surgery on the main repo.
- Matches what brew and nix already require, so onboarding "how do we publish?" has a single mental model rather than two ("brew/nix in their own repos, others inline").

**Con Pattern B:**

- More repos to maintain. Each registry repo needs branch protection, secrets, CI hygiene of its own.
- Cross-repo orchestration via dispatch tokens. One more piece of infrastructure to babysit; a broken token silently breaks publishing.
- Discoverability cost: "where does the choco package live?" → "the `chocolatey-kanban` repo." Mitigation: link from main README and CONTRIBUTING.
- Per-release CI cost goes up slightly (more parallel jobs across more repos) — negligible in practice.

## Acceptance (when this card is executed)

- [ ] Decision made between PAT and GitHub App for dispatch credentials. (Recommend App.)
- [ ] Empty `fulsomenko/chocolatey-kanban` and `fulsomenko/aur-kanban` repos exist on GitHub.
- [ ] Each has: LICENSE, README, CODEOWNERS, branch protection, minimal PR CI.
- [ ] Main repo's `release.yml` no longer has the `publish-chocolatey` job — replaced by a `repository_dispatch` step at the end of the `release` job.
- [ ] Main repo's AUR-related steps similarly extracted; only the dispatch step remains.
- [ ] Main repo's inline "Bump formula in homebrew-tap" step extracted into a workflow inside `fulsomenko/homebrew-tap` (triggered by dispatch); main repo just dispatches.
- [ ] `CHOCO_API_KEY` and `AUR_SSH_KEY` secrets move from main repo to their respective registry repos.
- [ ] At least one end-to-end release tag validates the new pipeline (all three registries publish successfully from a single main-repo release).
- [ ] Main repo's `packaging/chocolatey/` and `aur/` directories deleted; README install instructions still accurate.

## Not in scope (file separately)

- **The chocolatey publish work itself** — that is KAN-537 and its children, executing under Pattern A. This card is about migrating that work *out* later.
- **Adding new registries (winget, etc.)** — those should follow Pattern B from day 1; file separately and don't wait on this card.
- **Splitting the main repo's `release.yml`** further (e.g. extracting `build-windows` to its own workflow file). Tangential cleanup.
- **Homebrew-core submission** (KAN-465 Phase 2) — unrelated; uses a different mechanism (PR to upstream Homebrew/homebrew-core).

## Open questions to resolve before starting

- Naming convention: `fulsomenko/chocolatey-kanban` or `fulsomenko/kanban-chocolatey`? (`homebrew-tap` precedent says `<registry>-kanban`-ish but isn't perfectly analogous.) Pick a convention up front and apply uniformly.
- Do we want a single dispatch token covering all registry repos (one secret, simpler) or one per repo (more secrets, narrower blast radius)?
- Should the per-registry workflows be allowed to run on `workflow_dispatch` independently (manual re-publish of a specific version) — yes, recommend; comes for free.

## Related

- **Parent: KAN-452** — the umbrella for packaging restructure.
- **KAN-465 (Homebrew Phase 1)** — already Pattern B (`fulsomenko/homebrew-tap`). Reference for the dispatch-from-main-repo idiom, and for the README/CODEOWNERS/CI shape of a registry repo.
- **KAN-537 (Chocolatey umbrella)** — being delivered under Pattern A; this card represents the eventual migration out.
- **KAN-538 / KAN-541** — Pattern A files and CI job that will be moved out under this card.
- **KAN-539 (build-windows job)** — stays in main repo even after this card lands; produces the artifact every registry repo consumes.
- **KAN-446 (AUR pipeline hardening)** — current Pattern A AUR pipeline; subject to migration under this card.
cards.title: Extract per-registry packaging to dedicated repos (Pattern B)

cards.description:
> ⚠ SPLIT (read first): this card was too large (service logic + wiring 4 consumers). It is now a SUB-EPIC. The executable detail lives in its two children:
> - **KAN-795** — service create funnel (CreateX -> X::create, FK + client-id/conflict, idempotent PUT, service tests)
> - **KAN-796** — point CLI/TUI/MCP/server at the factory + DTO edge (depends on KAN-795)
> The sections below are retained as the combined overview.

## Context / why

Slice D of the **Card entity factory** epic (root spec **KAN-769**). Funnel the create path through `Card::create` (killing the create-then-update kludge and the `Card { .. }` literal in the command), enforce FK + uniqueness validation at the service tier (including client-supplied `id` collision → conflict, enabling idempotent PUT-create), and point every consumer — CLI, TUI, MCP, server — at the shared factory + `service::api::v1` Card DTOs. MCP drops its bespoke `requests/card.rs` create type. Depends on A + C (and stacked B).

## Current state (researched)

- Service create: `crates/kanban-service/src/context/cards.rs:10-39` (`create_card_impl`) reads `board.card_counter` for the number, mints `id`, and dispatches a `CreateCard` command.
- The `CreateCard` command (`crates/kanban-domain/src/commands/card/lifecycle.rs:84-187`) holds `id`, `card_number`, `board_id`, `column_id`, `title`, `position`, `options: CreateCardOptions`, `timestamp`; its `execute` (lines 97-171):
  1. checks WIP limit, loads the Board,
  2. builds a `Card { .. }` literal directly (the un-funnelled create path),
  3. bumps `board.card_counter` if `<= card_number` (lines 121-123),
  4. applies a follow-up `CardUpdate` for description/priority/points/due_date (the create-then-update kludge, lines 125-151),
  5. seeds a SprintLog if `options.sprint_id` is set (resolves Sprint name/number, lines 153-166),
  6. upserts board + card.
- Operations trait signature: `crates/kanban-domain/src/operations.rs:34-40` (`create_card(board_id, column_id, title, options)`), implemented in `context/mod.rs:110` and re-exposed by CLI (`crates/kanban-cli/src/context.rs:107-115`).
- CLI create handler: `crates/kanban-cli/src/handlers/card.rs:32` + `build_create_options` (`:346-355`) builds `CreateCardOptions` from CLI args.
- MCP create: `crates/kanban-mcp/src/requests/card.rs:4-28` (`CreateCardRequest`) — bespoke, loose-string priority/due_date/sprint; the MCP tool handler builds `CreateCardOptions` from it.
- No FK existence check for `column_id`/`sprint_id` at create today beyond the sprint-board-match in the command (lifecycle.rs:153-161); `column_id` existence is effectively assumed. No client-id support (id always minted).
- Batch ops untouched by this slice but adjacent: `context/cards_batch.rs`, `cards_batch_detailed.rs` (archive/move/assign-sprint). They construct commands, not cards, so they need no factory change.

## Target

1. **Funnel create through `Card::create`.** Refactor `CreateCard::execute` (or replace it) so the new card is built by `Card::create(NewCard{..}, id, card_number, now)` rather than a `Card { .. }` literal + follow-up `CardUpdate`. The sprint-log seeding (needs the Sprint) stays in `execute` as a post-create step calling `card.assign_to_sprint(..)`. The Board `card_counter` bump stays here too (sibling-entity write).
   - `CreateCard` should carry the already-minted `card_number` (it does) and translate its `options`/`title`/`column_id`/`position` into a `NewCard`. Prefer: have the **service** build `NewCard` and pass it (replace `title` + `options` on the command with a `new_card: NewCard`), keeping the command a thin transport. Decide during green; the invariant is: exactly one `Card::create` call, no follow-up patch for create fields.
2. **Service create flow (`create_card_impl`)** mints in the service per the inject-id pattern:
   ```rust
   let id = req_id.unwrap_or_else(Uuid::new_v4);
   // uniqueness: reject if a live OR archived card already has `id`
   if self.backend.get_card(id)?.is_some() || self.backend.get_archived_card(id)?.is_some() {
       return Err(KanbanError::conflict("Card", id)); // 409 on the wire
   }
   // FK existence: column must exist; sprint (if any) must exist and belong to the board
   let column = self.backend.get_column(column_id)?.ok_or_else(|| KanbanError::not_found("Column", column_id))?;
   if let Some(sid) = spec.sprint_id { /* validate sprint exists + board match */ }
   let card_number = /* mint from board.card_counter, bump board */;
   let now = Utc::now();
   // -> Card::create(spec, id, card_number, now), via the command
   ```
   Keep the actual construction inside the command/`execute` (it already owns the WIP check + board bump + upsert) but pass `id`/`card_number`/`now`/`NewCard` in from the service.
3. **Idempotent PUT-create**: a `PUT /v1/cards/:id` with a body creates-or-replaces. On create, the client id is used; on existing id, it replaces via the `ReplaceCardRequest` → `CardUpdate` path (slice C). The conflict check above only fires for `POST` create (mint-or-supplied) where the id must be new.
4. **Consumers**:
   - **CLI** (`handlers/card.rs`): build `NewCard` (via the DTO or directly) instead of `CreateCardOptions`; same `create` entry point. The `CreateCardOptions` type may be retired if no caller remains (grep; it is also used by the operations trait signature — update the trait to take `NewCard` or keep `CreateCardOptions` as the CLI-facing shape that converts to `NewCard`). Prefer updating the operations trait `create_card` to accept `NewCard` (+ optional client id) so all callers share one spec.
   - **MCP** (`requests/card.rs`): delete the bespoke `CreateCardRequest`; the MCP card-create tool deserializes the shared `service::api::v1::CreateCardRequest` (resolving `board`/`column`/`sprint` name-or-id strings to UUIDs first, then `into_new_card(column_id)`). Keep MCP's other request types unless the epic later migrates them.
   - **TUI**: route its create action through the same `create_card`/`NewCard` entry point (it currently calls the operations trait; update the call site to the new signature).
   - **server** (kanban-server / service `http` module, when present): the create handler consumes `CreateCardRequest` → `into_new_card` → service create; the response is `CardResponse`. (If the http module is still a stub, leave a typed seam + a test asserting the conversion compiles.)

## Step-by-step (TDD red → green → refactor)

1. **Red** — integration tests (below) in `kanban-service/tests/` (`#[tokio::test]`, `KanbanContext` + real persistence via `TempDir`), plus CLI (`assert_cmd`) and MCP (end-to-end tool call) tests.
2. **Green** —
   - Update the operations-trait `create_card` to take `NewCard` (+ optional client id); thread it through `context/mod.rs`, `context/cards.rs`, CLI/TUI context wrappers.
   - Refactor `CreateCard::execute` to call `Card::create` once (no follow-up `CardUpdate`); keep board-bump + sprint-log seeding.
   - Add the FK + uniqueness checks in `create_card_impl`; add a `KanbanError::conflict` constructor if absent (check `kanban-core` errors).
   - Delete MCP `CreateCardRequest`; point the MCP tool at the shared DTO.
3. **Refactor** — remove `CreateCardOptions` if dead; ensure no `Card::new` call remains outside tests (grep); `fmt` + `clippy -D warnings`.

## Tests (pattern `test_<scenario>_<expected_outcome>`)

Service (integration, real persistence):
- `test_create_card_funnels_through_factory_seeds_defaults` — created card has `status==Todo`, `completed_at==None`, `position` appended, `card_number` minted from the board counter, board counter incremented by 1.
- `test_create_card_mints_id_when_not_supplied` — no client id ⇒ a fresh uuid; two creates differ.
- `test_create_card_uses_client_supplied_id` — passing an id ⇒ the card has exactly that id.
- `test_create_card_with_duplicate_client_id_returns_conflict` — supplying an existing card's id (live or archived) ⇒ `KanbanError` conflict, no card created.
- `test_create_card_with_missing_column_returns_not_found` — unknown `column_id` ⇒ not-found, no mutation, board counter unchanged.
- `test_create_card_with_sprint_from_other_board_returns_mismatch` — `sprint_id` belonging to a different board ⇒ error (preserves the existing `SprintBoardMismatch`).
- `test_create_card_with_sprint_seeds_sprint_log` — valid `sprint_id` ⇒ `sprint_id` set AND one `SprintLog` recorded (service-tier seeding still works post-factory).
- `test_create_card_applies_all_create_options_in_one_call` — description/priority/points/due_date all present on the returned card with a single create (no observable intermediate update; e.g. `updated_at == created_at`).
- `test_put_create_card_is_idempotent_create_or_replace` — `PUT` with a new id creates; a second `PUT` same id replaces (no duplicate, fields updated).

CLI (`assert_cmd`):
- `test_cli_card_create_produces_card_through_factory` — `kanban card create` yields a card with the expected number/defaults.

MCP (end-to-end tool call):
- `test_mcp_create_card_uses_shared_dto_and_factory` — the MCP create tool, fed the shared request shape, creates a card; assert the bespoke `requests::card::CreateCardRequest` no longer exists (compile-level / module removed).

Regression:
- `test_no_card_new_callers_outside_tests` — grep-guard (CI) that `Card::new(` appears only under `#[cfg(test)]` / `tests/`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Card create funnels through `Card::create`; `CreateCard::execute` no longer builds a `Card { .. }` literal nor runs a follow-up `CardUpdate` for create fields.
- [ ] Service create validates `column_id` (required FK) and `sprint_id` (optional FK + board match), mints/accepts `id` with a uniqueness check (conflict on collision), and supports idempotent PUT-create.
- [ ] CLI, TUI, MCP, and server all create cards via the shared `NewCard`/factory; MCP's bespoke `CreateCardRequest` is deleted in favour of `service::api::v1::CreateCardRequest`.
- [ ] `card_number` minting + board-counter bump remain a service-tier responsibility; the domain `create` stays Board-free.
- [ ] `CreateCardOptions` removed if unused; no non-test `Card::new` callers remain.
- [ ] `cargo test --workspace` green; clippy `-D warnings` clean; fmt clean.

## Dependencies / sequencing

- Last slice of the Card epic. Depends on **A** (`Card::create`/`NewCard`) and **C** (DTOs); the persistence reroute **B** should already be merged. Mirrors the Board service-integration slice.
cards.title: feat(service): wire all consumers to the Card factory + FK/client-id

cards.description:
## Context / why
Root spec: **KAN-769** (`refactor(domain): entity construction factory -- DTO, CLI/MCP, and persistence arms`). This epic is the **Sprint** sibling of the four flat, independent entity factories (Board, Column, Card, Sprint). The Board entity is the structural TEMPLATE; Sprint follows the same A->B->C->D slicing.

Today a Sprint is born three ways with no shared contract: `Sprint::new(board_id, sprint_number, name_index, prefix)` which internally calls `Uuid::new_v4()` + `Utc::now()` (`crates/kanban-domain/src/sprint.rs:36-56`), serde `Deserialize` on the struct itself (`sprint.rs:16`), and the SQLite row mapper `row_to_sprint` (`crates/kanban-persistence-sqlite/src/sqlite_store/conversions.rs:106-129`). Each rebuilds a `Sprint` independently. The goal is ONE construction boundary: `Sprint::create(spec, id, now)` + `Sprint::reconstitute(record)` funneling every arm.

## Goal
Establish the two construction intents for Sprint:
- **CREATE** (`NewSprint` -> `Sprint::create(spec, id, now)`): births a new sprint; the service MINTS id, clock, and the **sprint_number + name_index** (the latter two allocated from the owning Board's counters/name-pool). Input is partial + untrusted.
- **RECONSTITUTE** (`SprintRecord` -> `Sprint::reconstitute(record)`): restores an existing sprint verbatim including `status`, `start_date`, `end_date`, `created_at`, `updated_at`. Input is complete + trusted. The single rehydration funnel for JSON + SQLite.

## The 4 atomic slices (children of this epic, A->B->C->D)
- **A — 01-domain-core.md** `feat(domain): Sprint factory core — NewSprint/SprintRecord/create/reconstitute`. Add `NewSprint` + `SprintRecord` (both `Default`-free, distinct from `Sprint`), `Sprint::create(spec, id, now)`, `Sprint::reconstitute(record)`, `From<&Sprint> for SprintRecord`. Stop `Sprint` deriving `Deserialize`. Pure unit tests.
- **B — 02-persistence.md** `refactor(persistence): route Sprint json+sqlite through SprintRecord/reconstitute`. Route JSON serde and the SQLite `row_to_sprint` mapper through `SprintRecord` + `reconstitute`/decompose. Round-trip tests on both backends.
- **C — 03-dto.md** `feat(service): Sprint v1 wire DTOs + conversions (create/update/replace/response)`. Create the `sprints` DTO module in `kanban-service::api::v1` FROM SCRATCH (no sprint DTOs exist yet): `CreateSprintRequest`/`UpdateSprintRequest`/`ReplaceSprintRequest`/`SprintResponse` + conversions. Exhaustive destructuring (compile-lock). Boundary tests per arm.
- **D — 04-service.md** `feat(service): wire all consumers to the Sprint factory + FK/client-id`. Create flow funnels through `Sprint::create` with service-seeded id + minted sprint_number/name_index; FK (board_id) + client-id uniqueness validation at the service tier; idempotent PUT-create; wire CLI/TUI/MCP/server to the factory + DTO edge; MCP drops its bespoke `requests/sprint.rs` `CreateSprintRequest`. Integration tests per consumer.

## Sprint entity field set (researched — `crates/kanban-domain/src/sprint.rs:16-31`)
`id: Uuid`, `board_id: Uuid`, `sprint_number: u32`, `name_index: Option<usize>`, `prefix: Option<String>` (serde alias `prefix_override`), `card_prefix: Option<String>`, `status: SprintStatus`, `start_date: Option<DateTime<Utc>>`, `end_date: Option<DateTime<Utc>>`, `created_at: DateTime<Utc>`, `updated_at: DateTime<Utc>`.

`SprintStatus` enum (`sprint.rs:8-14`): `Planning | Active | Completed | Cancelled`.

## Field-acceptance matrix (the through-line)
| Field | create (NewSprint) | reconstitute (SprintRecord) | CreateSprintRequest | SprintResponse |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | injected param | verbatim | optional client id | yes |
| `board_id` | yes (FK, validated at service) | verbatim | yes | yes |
| `sprint_number` | MINTED from Board counters | verbatim | NO | yes |
| `name_index` | MINTED (name pool / auto-consume) | verbatim | NO (client sends `name`, not index) | hidden (expose resolved `name` instead) |
| `prefix` | yes (explicit_prefix) | verbatim | yes | yes |
| `card_prefix` | defaults `None` | verbatim | yes (optional) | yes |
| `status` | MINTED `Planning` | verbatim | NO | yes |
| `start_date`/`end_date` | MINTED `None` | verbatim | NO (set via activate) | yes |
| `created_at`/`updated_at` | MINTED from `now` | verbatim | NO | yes |

## Sprint-number / name minting — how it fits the inject-id pattern (DECIDED)
This is the Sprint-specific quirk. Unlike Card (one `card_number` from `Board.card_counter`), Sprint mints TWO server-managed values from the Board: `sprint_number` (from `Board.sprint_counters` keyed by effective prefix) and `name_index` (from `Board.sprint_names` / `sprint_name_used_count`).

Current allocation (researched, `crates/kanban-domain/src/commands/sprint_commands.rs:280-310`, `CreateSprint::execute`):
1. Resolve effective prefix: `explicit_prefix` > `board.sprint_prefix` > `default_sprint_prefix`.
2. `board.ensure_sprint_counter_initialized(&effective_prefix, &sprints_snapshot)` (`board.rs:335`).
3. `sprint_number = board.get_next_sprint_number(&effective_prefix)` (`board.rs:295-301`) — entry-or-1, increment.
4. `name_index`: explicit name -> `board.add_sprint_name_at_used_index(name)` (`board.rs:260-269`); else if `auto_consume_name` -> `board.consume_sprint_name()` (`board.rs:249-258`); else `None`.
5. `Sprint::new(board_id, sprint_number, name_index, Some(effective_prefix))` then `sprint.id = self.id`.

**Target pattern** (mirrors `card_number` seeding): the service `create_sprint` flow, which already owns the Board (mutable) and the store, performs steps 1–4 to MINT `sprint_number` + `name_index`, then passes them INTO the factory as part of `NewSprint` (they are minted-but-injected content, exactly like the service injects `id`/`now`). `Sprint::create(spec, id, now)` stays I/O-free and counter-free: it receives `sprint_number` and `name_index` as already-allocated values inside `NewSprint`, applies the `status=Planning` / dates-`None` defaults, and enforces invariants. The Board mutation (`upsert_board`) remains a service-tier side effect ordered before `upsert_sprint`, as today.

## Sprint lifecycle (researched)
State model `Planning -> Active -> {Completed | Cancelled}` via `activate`/`complete`/`cancel` (`sprint.rs:98-114`) and command structs `ActivateSprint`/`CompleteSprint`/`CancelSprint` (`sprint_commands.rs:329-399`). Carry-over of cards lives in the service: `carry_over_sprint_cards_impl` (`crates/kanban-service/src/context/sprints.rs:8-42`) requires source `Completed`/`Cancelled` and target `Planning`. **reconstitute MUST restore `status`/`start_date`/`end_date` verbatim**; create always starts `Planning` with dates `None`. Lifecycle transition commands are OUT OF SCOPE for the factory work (they mutate an existing sprint, not construct one) — they are untouched.

## Acceptance criteria (epic-level)
- [ ] All four child cards (A-D) merged in order.
- [ ] `cargo test --workspace` green; `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo fmt --check` clean.
- [ ] `Sprint` no longer derives `Deserialize`; the ONLY paths to a `Sprint` are `create` / `reconstitute`.
- [ ] CI `..`-rest / `Default::default()` guard passes over the Sprint factory + conversion modules.
- [ ] MCP no longer defines its own `CreateSprintRequest`.

## Dependencies / sequencing
Strict A -> B -> C -> D. The shared Foundation card (Patch type, `conv` helpers, `api::v1` scaffolding — already present per the Board template at `crates/kanban-service/src/api/v1/`) precedes all. Board entity is the reference template throughout.

## TDD
This epic is an overview. Every child slice (A domain-core / B persistence / C dto / D service) follows Red → Green → Refactor: failing tests written and presented for review before implementation, then minimal implementation, then refactor. The executable TDD steps + named tests live on the child cards.

## Background

KAN-538's `chocolateyinstall.ps1` relies on `Install-ChocolateyZipPackage` to unzip the Windows release archive into `$toolsDir`. Chocolatey then auto-shims every `.exe` it finds there. The behavior on a partial archive (e.g. archive layout drift where `kanban-mcp.exe` is missing) is silent: `choco install kanban` succeeds, `kanban --version` works, `kanban-mcp` resolves to "command not found" with no error linking it to the package.

The user-visible failure mode is "I installed kanban via choco and it half-works." Cause is far from effect; debugging requires the user to know that this package was supposed to ship two binaries.

This card adds a defensive presence check so the install fails loudly if either binary is missing.

## Two options for where the check lives

### Option A — In `chocolateyinstall.ps1` itself (runtime check on every install)

After the `Install-ChocolateyZipPackage` call:

```powershell
foreach ($exe in 'kanban.exe', 'kanban-mcp.exe') {
  $path = Join-Path $toolsDir $exe
  if (-not (Test-Path $path)) {
    $found = (Get-ChildItem $toolsDir -Filter *.exe | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Name) -join ', '
    throw "kanban Chocolatey package is missing $exe. Found in `$toolsDir: [$found]. Report at https://github.com/fulsomenko/kanban/issues."
  }
}
```

**Pros**: catches drift on every install (including end-user installs).
**Cons**: lives in `packaging/chocolatey/tools/chocolateyinstall.ps1`; every choco user runs this code. Tiny perf cost (negligible).

### Option B — In KAN-541's smoke install step (CI-only)

In the `Smoke install from local nupkg` step in `.github/workflows/release.yml`, after the install + `--version` calls:

```powershell
foreach ($exe in 'kanban.exe', 'kanban-mcp.exe') {
  $found = Get-Command $exe -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
  if (-not $found) {
    throw "$exe shim not found on PATH after choco install"
  }
}
```

**Pros**: catches drift before the bad package reaches users; doesn't bloat the install script every consumer runs.
**Cons**: only catches issues we cause in CI; a hypothetical "Chocolatey strips a file during moderation" wouldn't be caught.

### Recommendation

**Both**, but if you only have time for one, pick Option A. The CI smoke install already calls `kanban-mcp --version`, which implicitly checks the shim exists — Option B is largely redundant. Option A catches the failure case where the install script itself is wrong, on any consumer's machine, with a clear message pointing at the project.

## Scope

- Edit `packaging/chocolatey/tools/chocolateyinstall.ps1` to add the Option A check.
- Optional: also tighten KAN-541's smoke step with Option B (small belt-and-suspenders).
- Test locally if you have a Windows environment (or accept that the next real release will validate it).

## Acceptance

- [ ] `chocolateyinstall.ps1` contains a presence assertion for both binaries.
- [ ] The error message points at the project's GitHub issues URL.
- [ ] On the next real release, the smoke install passes (proof the check isn't over-eager).
- [ ] Manual test (optional): pack a deliberately broken package locally and confirm the install fails loud with the expected message.

## Out of scope

- Adding more substantive integration tests for the install behavior (run `kanban` against a test board, etc.) — out of scope; the Chocolatey package's job is to deliver the binaries, not test them.
- Validating archive layout in `build-windows` (KAN-539) — already partially covered by the `--version` smoke calls there.

## Related

- **KAN-537** — parent (Chocolatey umbrella).
- **KAN-538** — sibling, source of the install script being patched.
- **KAN-541** — sibling, where Option B would live.
