## Where, Why, How

**Where.** `crates/kanban-domain/src/export/` — four public functions return raw `io::Result` / `Result<_, io::Error>` instead of the workspace's standard `KanbanResult<T>`.

**Why.** CONTRIBUTING.md mandates: *"All public APIs return `KanbanResult<T>`."* The exporter and importer slipped through. Callers that compose export/import with other domain operations cannot use `?` cleanly today — they have to map at every boundary. The shape is also misleading: import failures aren't always `io::Error` (JSON deserialization is not I/O), but the signature pretends they are.

**How.** Convert the four functions to return `KanbanResult<T>`. Map `io::Error` and `serde_json::Error` into existing `KanbanError` variants. No behaviour change at runtime — only the type at the boundary.

---

## Offenders

| File:line | Current signature |
|---|---|
| `crates/kanban-domain/src/export/exporter.rs:76` | `pub fn export_to_json(export: &AllBoardsExport) -> Result<String, io::Error>` |
| `crates/kanban-domain/src/export/exporter.rs:81` | `pub fn export_to_file(export: &AllBoardsExport, filename: &str) -> io::Result<()>` |
| `crates/kanban-domain/src/export/importer.rs:41` | `pub fn import_from_json(json: &str) -> Result<AllBoardsExport, io::Error>` |
| `crates/kanban-domain/src/export/importer.rs:127` | `pub fn import_from_file(filename: &str) -> io::Result<AllBoardsExport>` |

`import_from_json` is the most misleading — it returns `io::Error` for what is in fact a `serde_json::Error`. Today this is constructed via `io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::InvalidData, e)`, smuggling a JSON error through an I/O error type.

---

## Proposed solution

### Target signatures

```rust
pub fn export_to_json(export: &AllBoardsExport) -> KanbanResult<String>;
pub fn export_to_file(export: &AllBoardsExport, filename: &str) -> KanbanResult<()>;
pub fn import_from_json(json: &str) -> KanbanResult<AllBoardsExport>;
pub fn import_from_file(filename: &str) -> KanbanResult<AllBoardsExport>;
```

### Error mapping

- `io::Error` → `KanbanError::Io` (or whichever variant matches; check `crates/kanban-domain/src/error.rs` for the canonical variant — likely an `Io(#[from] io::Error)` already exists)
- `serde_json::Error` → `KanbanError::Serialization` (or matching variant)

### Body changes

Replace `?` chains with the new error variants. Example for `import_from_json`:

```rust
pub fn import_from_json(json: &str) -> KanbanResult<AllBoardsExport> {
    serde_json::from_str(json).map_err(KanbanError::from)
}
```

(Assumes `From<serde_json::Error> for KanbanError` exists. If not, add it — one-line `#[from]` annotation in `error.rs`.)

### Call-site updates

Search for callers: `rg "export_to_json|export_to_file|import_from_json|import_from_file" crates/` — likely under 10 sites. Each call's error-handling becomes simpler (no manual mapping).

---

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All four functions return `KanbanResult<T>`
- [ ] No `use std::io;` imports remain in `exporter.rs` / `importer.rs` unless still needed for non-signature reasons
- [ ] All call sites compile without manual error mapping
- [ ] Existing tests in `crates/kanban-domain/src/export/` still pass
- [ ] `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` clean

## Why now

Mechanical, low-risk, brings the codebase into compliance with its own stated convention. ~30 min.
cards.title: refactor(domain): replace bare io::Result with KanbanResult in export/import

cards.description:
Cross-cutting Foundation for the board-removal epic (see root spec KAN-821, DECIDED D9).

## F1 — Bounded shared archival abstraction

Card-archive and board-archive share one lifecycle: **archive** (move an entity out of its live collection into a discrete archived collection with an `archived_at` envelope), **restore** (move back, lossless), **permanent-delete** (drop from the archived collection), **scoped list**. Define this ONCE so cards (SE-B) and boards (SE-C) reuse it instead of duplicating mechanism.

### Scope
- Shared archived-metadata envelope + an archive-lifecycle trait (`archive` / `restore` / `permanent_delete` / `list_archived`) generic over the entity, so the in-memory store, JSON, and SQLite implement one generic pattern rather than per-entity copies, and the archive/restore command mechanics are written once.
- Entity-specific payload stays specialized (do NOT over-abstract): card restore-context (`board_id`, `original_column_id`, `original_position`) and board owned-sets (columns / live cards / archived cards / sprints / edges) are not forced into one shape. The abstraction covers lifecycle + storage envelope, not payload.

### Sequencing & validation
- **Cards are the first implementer (SE-B); boards the second (SE-C).** Define a first cut here; the SE-C spike (Phase 6) validates it on the second implementer, which is where a wrong abstraction reveals itself. Collapse/refine if it doesn't fit — a little duplication beats the wrong abstraction (Phase 7 quality gate).
- Depended on by SE-B and SE-C. Additive; TDD.

### Children (leaf cards, authored in Phase 3)
- F1a Domain: archived-metadata envelope + archive-lifecycle trait + generic store/command helpers + tests.

cards.description:
## Where, Why, How

**Where.** `crates/kanban-cli/Cargo.toml:30` declares `kanban-persistence` as a direct dependency.

**Why.** Per the dependency-flow diagram in CONTRIBUTING.md, `kanban-cli` depends only on `kanban-tui` and `kanban-service`. Persistence is supposed to be an implementation detail behind the service layer. The CLI knowing about `StoreRegistry`, `StoreFactory`, etc. directly means:

- The CLI can construct stores bypassing the service's lifecycle (which manages metadata, conflict detection, etc.)
- Any persistence-layer refactor cascades through the CLI surface
- The dependency-inversion principle is violated: a high-level layer (CLI) depends on a mid-level abstraction (persistence) instead of on the service abstraction that's supposed to wrap it

**How.** Audit every `use kanban_persistence::` in `kanban-cli`. For each, either (a) the type belongs in `kanban-service` and should be re-exported there, or (b) the CLI is doing something that should live in service. Move accordingly. Then drop the Cargo.toml dependency.

---

## Investigation needed (do this first)

```bash
rg "kanban_persistence" crates/kanban-cli/src/
```

Expected categories of references:
1. **`StoreRegistry` / `StoreFactory`** — CLI's `CliApp` constructs these to register backends. The `register_backend` builder method takes `Box<dyn StoreFactory>` directly. *(See `crates/kanban-cli/src/app.rs:236`.)*
2. **Snapshot helpers** — `PersistenceMetadata`, `StoreSnapshot`, `snapshot_to_json_bytes` used in `create_empty_storage_file` (`app.rs:118-133`).
3. **Errors** — `PersistenceError` referenced anywhere in CLI handlers.

---

## Proposed solution

### Option A — Re-export everything CLI needs from `kanban-service`

Pros: zero refactor of CLI logic; just changes import paths. The CLI keeps owning store registration as a builder API.
Cons: `kanban-service` becomes a passthrough for a chunk of `kanban-persistence`, blurring its purpose.

### Option B — Move `CliApp::register_backend` and registry construction into `kanban-service`

Pros: cleaner separation; the service owns store lifecycle end-to-end.
Cons: invasive — third-party crates that today extend `CliApp` (see the doctest at `app.rs:206-235`) would need their integration point moved.

**Recommendation: Option A first** as a minimal change that drops the dep edge. Option B can follow if the API ergonomics warrant it.

### Concrete steps for Option A

1. In `kanban-service/src/lib.rs`, add re-exports:
   ```rust
   pub use kanban_persistence::{StoreFactory, StoreRegistry, PersistenceStore,
       PersistenceMetadata, StoreSnapshot, snapshot_to_json_bytes};
   ```
2. In `kanban-cli`, replace every `use kanban_persistence::X` with `use kanban_service::X`.
3. Drop `kanban-persistence` from `kanban-cli/Cargo.toml`.
4. Update the rustdoc example in `crates/kanban-cli/src/app.rs:206-235` to import from `kanban_service` instead of `kanban_persistence`.

### Related layer leak (sibling card)

The same problem exists for `kanban-tui` (Cargo.toml declares `kanban-persistence`, and `FileWatcher` / `ChangeDetector` / `PersistenceMetadata` are imported directly). Tracked separately because it requires actual code restructuring, not just import-path changes.

---

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `kanban-cli/Cargo.toml` does not list `kanban-persistence` as a dependency
- [ ] No `use kanban_persistence::` remains in `crates/kanban-cli/src/`
- [ ] CLI doctest in `app.rs` compiles with the new import paths
- [ ] `cargo build --workspace` clean
- [ ] `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` clean
- [ ] Integration tests in `crates/kanban-cli/tests/` still pass

## Why now

Small, mechanical, restores the dependency-inversion property the workspace claims to follow. Reading any CLI handler today and wondering "wait, does this go through service?" becomes a non-question.

cards.description:
## Context / why
- Root epic **KAN-821**, sub-epic **KAN-823 (SE-B: archived-cards first-class retrofit)**. Implements the first half of **DECIDED D2**: give `ArchivedCard` its own `board_id` so board scoping is a direct field lookup instead of loading every column and post-filtering, and make the column reference an explicit *historical* `original_column_id` (already named that, but currently the only board linkage) rather than a live coupling. Builds on **F1a** (KAN-825) — `ArchivedCard` already implements `ArchivedEntity` after F1a.
- Board-archive (SE-C) and the discrete-store retrofit (B2) both depend on `ArchivedCard` carrying its own `board_id`; today it does not, which is the root of the parasitic design (D2 evidence).

## Current state (researched)
- `crates/kanban-domain/src/archived_card.rs:10-17`:
  ```rust
  pub struct ArchivedCard {
      #[serde(with = "crate::card_factory::card_serde")]
      pub card: Card,
      pub archived_at: DateTime<Utc>,
      pub original_column_id: ColumnId,
      pub original_position: i32,
  }
  ```
  Constructor `ArchivedCard::new(card, original_column_id, original_position)` at `archived_card.rs:20-27`. `ArchivedCardSummary` (`:54-60`) mirrors the same fields; `From<&ArchivedCard>` at `:62-70`.
- **`Card` has no `board_id`** — fields are `id, column_id, title, ...` (`crates/kanban-domain/src/card.rs:59-74`). Board is only reachable via the card's column: `Column { id, board_id, .. }` (`crates/kanban-domain/src/column.rs:11-13`, `board_id` at `:13`).
- Archive capture site: `ArchiveCards::execute` (`crates/kanban-domain/src/commands/card/lifecycle.rs:294-319`), which at `:306-308` reads `original_column_id = card.column_id` / `original_position = card.position` and calls `crate::ArchivedCard::new(card, original_column_id, original_position)` at `:308`. It has `context` (a `CommandContext`) in scope; `context.store` is `&dyn DataStore` with a fallible `get_column(id) -> KanbanResult<Option<Column>>`.
- **Board capture must be BEST-EFFORT (spike-found).** Do NOT use `context.get_column(id)?` — that resolver **propagates `NotFound`** and breaks existing tests that archive a card whose `column_id` is fake/dangling (they expect archive to succeed). Use `context.store.get_column(card.column_id)?.map(|c| c.board_id).unwrap_or_else(Uuid::nil)` — a missing column yields `Uuid::nil()`, matching D2's "may dangle" (the correct backfill is a persistence-migration concern, D7).
- **`ArchivedCard::new` has 24 call sites total (spike-verified), not ~8** — most are `#[cfg(test)]`. Within `kanban-domain` (all updated in THIS card): `in_memory_store/archived_cards.rs` (`:78,:93,:96,:111,:114,:129,:146,:168`), `in_memory_store/state.rs:77`, `snapshot.rs:391`, `commands/cascade_commands.rs:367,368`, `commands/card/tests/restore.rs:15,39,66,109`, `commands/sprint_commands.rs:683,862,967`, `commands/board_commands.rs:697,755` (+ two `ArchivedCard { .. }`-in-`archived_cards: vec![...]` struct/`::new` sites at `:735,:765`), and the production site `commands/card/lifecycle.rs:308`. **Cross-crate sites are a REQUIRED B4/coordination checklist** (fixed in their owning crates, NOT here — they only compile once B1's signature lands):
  - [ ] `crates/kanban-persistence-sqlite/src/sqlite_store/tests/entities.rs:26,:60` (2× `ArchivedCard::new`)
  - [ ] `crates/kanban-persistence-sqlite/tests/data_store.rs:289` (1× `ArchivedCard::new`)
  - [ ] `crates/kanban-persistence/src/test_helpers/helpers.rs:91` (1× `ArchivedCard { .. }` **struct literal** — needs the new `board_id` field, not a `::new` arg)
  - [ ] `crates/kanban-persistence-json/src/json_file_store.rs:1438`, `crates/kanban-service/tests/delete_board_cascade.rs:114`, `crates/kanban-tui/src/app/model.rs:143,:166`, `crates/kanban-tui/tests/model_tests.rs:118,119,140,150,151,173,174,192` (each `ArchivedCard::new` — coordinated compile fixes in the SE-B persistence/surface cards).

## Target
Additive field + a constructor that captures board explicitly:

```rust
// archived_card.rs
pub struct ArchivedCard {
    #[serde(with = "crate::card_factory::card_serde")]
    pub card: Card,
    pub archived_at: DateTime<Utc>,
    #[serde(default)]                 // back-compat: pre-V8 files have no board_id
    pub board_id: BoardId,            // NEW (D2)
    /// Historical column at archive time — NOT a live FK. May dangle if the
    /// column is later deleted; that is intentional under the first-class model.
    pub original_column_id: ColumnId,
    pub original_position: i32,
}

impl ArchivedCard {
    pub fn new(
        card: Card,
        board_id: BoardId,
        original_column_id: ColumnId,
        original_position: i32,
    ) -> Self { /* archived_at = Utc::now() */ }
}
```

`ArchivedCardSummary` gains `pub board_id: BoardId` and its `From<&ArchivedCard>` copies it.

Archive capture resolves the board from the card's column:

```rust
// lifecycle.rs ArchiveCards::execute — BEST-EFFORT board capture (tolerates a dangling column)
let board_id = context
    .store
    .get_column(card.column_id)?
    .map(|c| c.board_id)
    .unwrap_or_else(Uuid::nil);                     // NEW: nil if the column is gone (D2 "may dangle")
let original_column_id = card.column_id;
let original_position = card.position;
let archived = crate::ArchivedCard::new(card, board_id, original_column_id, original_position);
```

## Step-by-step (TDD: Red → Green → Refactor)
1. **Red** — failing tests first:
   - `test_archived_card_retains_board_id` (in `archived_card.rs`) — `ArchivedCard::new(card, board_id, col_id, 0).board_id == board_id`.
   - `test_archive_captures_board_from_column` (in `commands/card/lifecycle.rs` tests, using `TestContext`) — seed board+column+card, run `ArchiveCards::execute`, fetch via `store.get_archived_card(id)`, assert its `board_id` equals the seeded board id (proving capture walks card→column→board, not a defaulted zero-UUID).
   - `test_archived_card_summary_carries_board_id` (in `archived_card.rs`) — `ArchivedCardSummary::from(&ac).board_id == ac.board_id`.
   - `test_archived_card_board_id_defaults_when_absent_in_json` (in `snapshot.rs`) — deserialize an archived-card JSON lacking `board_id`; assert it loads with `board_id == Uuid::nil()` (serde(default)), proving old files still parse.
   - `test_archive_with_dangling_column_captures_nil_board_id` (in `commands/card/lifecycle.rs` tests) — archive a card whose `column_id` resolves to no column; assert archive SUCCEEDS (no `NotFound` propagated) and the stored `board_id == Uuid::nil()` — guards the best-effort capture.
2. **Green** — add the field with `#[serde(default)]`, update `ArchivedCard::new` signature, `ArchivedCardSummary` + its `From`, and the production call site in `ArchiveCards::execute` (best-effort `get_column` — see Target). Fix **all 22 in-crate `ArchivedCard::new` call sites** enumerated in Current state (in-memory store tests, `state.rs`, snapshot test, cascade/sprint/board command tests, `card/tests/restore.rs`) to pass a `board_id`. Cross-crate sites compile-break until their owning cards land (the B4/coordination checklist above).
3. **Refactor** — introduce a local `board_id` binding in `execute` (keep the fn < 50 lines); confirm no duplicate column fetch; keep `archived_card.rs` < 300 lines.

## Tests
- `test_archived_card_retains_board_id` — inline `archived_card.rs`; field round-trips through the constructor.
- `test_archive_captures_board_from_column` — inline `commands/card/lifecycle.rs`; the capture path derives `board_id` from the live column (the load-bearing behavior).
- `test_archived_card_summary_carries_board_id` — inline `archived_card.rs`; summary projection includes the new field.
- `test_archived_card_board_id_defaults_when_absent_in_json` — inline `snapshot.rs`; `#[serde(default)]` back-compat (proves the additive change does not break existing snapshots; the real V8 migration that backfills a *correct* board_id is a persistence card in D7).
- Layer: all `kanban-domain` inline unit tests (pure logic; the capture test uses the existing in-memory `TestContext`).

## Code examples
Before → after of the capture site (`lifecycle.rs:306-308`):

```rust
// BEFORE
let original_column_id = card.column_id;
let original_position = card.position;
let archived = crate::ArchivedCard::new(card, original_column_id, original_position);

// AFTER (best-effort: NotFound does NOT abort archive — matches D2 "may dangle")
let board_id = context.store.get_column(card.column_id)?
    .map(|c| c.board_id).unwrap_or_else(Uuid::nil);
let original_column_id = card.column_id;
let original_position = card.position;
let archived = crate::ArchivedCard::new(card, board_id, original_column_id, original_position);
```

Constructor before → after (`archived_card.rs:20`):

```rust
// BEFORE
pub fn new(card: Card, original_column_id: ColumnId, original_position: i32) -> Self
// AFTER
pub fn new(card: Card, board_id: BoardId, original_column_id: ColumnId, original_position: i32) -> Self
```

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `cargo test -p kanban-domain` green (incl. the updated `ArchivedCard::new` call sites).
- [ ] `cargo clippy -p kanban-domain -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo fmt` clean.
- [ ] `ArchivedCard.board_id` and `ArchivedCardSummary.board_id` exist; `#[serde(default)]` on the field.
- [ ] `ArchiveCards::execute` populates `board_id` from the card's column **best-effort** (asserted by `test_archive_captures_board_from_column`) and still archives with `Uuid::nil()` when the column is gone (asserted by `test_archive_with_dangling_column_captures_nil_board_id`) — no `NotFound` propagated.
- [ ] **Key invariant**: an archived card records the board it belonged to independently of any live column, and old JSON snapshots still deserialize (default nil until B-persistence backfills).

## Dependencies / sequencing
- **After F1a (KAN-825).** Precedes **B2** (B2 relies on `board_id` to implement board-scoped queries).
- **Additive to the domain type** (new field is `#[serde(default)]`; new constructor arg is the only breaking-at-call-site change, all fixed within this crate) — `kanban-domain` compiles green on its own after this card.
- Downstream crates that build `ArchivedCard` directly (service/sqlite construction sites) are touched by the persistence retrofit cards (D7), not here; within `kanban-domain` the only production call site is the archive command, updated in this card. If any cross-crate call site references `ArchivedCard::new` positionally, note it as a coordinated compile fix on those persistence cards.

## Entity-specific quirks
- `board_id` is a `BoardId` (= `Uuid`, `board.rs:9`); `#[serde(default)]` defaults it to `Uuid::nil()` for pre-V8 files. The *correct* backfill (nil → real board via `original_column_id`→column→board) is the JSON V7→V8 / SQLite 2→3 migration's job (D7), not this domain slice — this card only makes the field exist and be captured for *new* archives.
- Adding a field changes `PartialEq`: two archived cards that were equal pre-change stay equal only if their `board_id` matches. All in-crate equality assertions construct via `new`, so they stay consistent.
- Do NOT turn `original_column_id` into any kind of live/validated FK — D2 explicitly makes it historical; column deletion may legitimately leave it dangling (the guard that currently forbids that is relaxed in B2).

## Execution-validated (full spike)
GREEN (commit 1fdf28c7; workspace build PASS). Confirmed against the real implementation:
- **`ArchivedCard::new` has 24 call sites total** (spike-verified, not ~8) — most are `#[cfg(test)]`. All in-`kanban-domain` sites were fixed in this card; cross-crate sites compile-break until their owning cards land.
- **THREE of those sites are SQLite PRODUCTION struct literals** that build `ArchivedCard` from DB rows — `sqlite_store/data_store.rs:293`, `data_store.rs:372`, `sqlite_store/lists.rs:84`. B1 fills them with `board_id: Uuid::nil()` placeholders (SQLite has no `board_id` column until B4). **B4 wires these three to the real `board_id` column** (added to B4's scope + this card's cross-crate checklist). This is the one omission the draft missed — call it out so the placeholders are not forgotten.
- **Best-effort board capture confirmed:** `context.store.get_column(card.column_id)?.map(|c| c.board_id).unwrap_or_else(Uuid::nil)` is correct — using the fallible resolver (`context.get_column(id)?`) would propagate `NotFound` and break tests that archive a card with a dangling column.

## UPDATE (after F1a #363) — ArchivedCard now owns `metadata: ArchiveMetadata`
F1a replaced `ArchivedCard`'s flat `archived_at` with `metadata: ArchiveMetadata` (`#[serde(flatten)]`, no migration). So this card's `board_id` is added as a SIBLING field on `ArchivedCard` (alongside `metadata`, `original_column_id`, `original_position`) — the restore-context/scoping stays specialized, NOT inside the metadata envelope. Any `ac.archived_at` reads are now `ac.metadata.archived_at` (F1a already updated the in-memory + SQLite sites). `board_id` is additive with `#[serde(default)]`; the persistence migrations (B3/B4) still own the on-disk `board_id` backfill.
cards.title: refactor(domain): first-class ArchivedCard with board_id [B1]

cards.description:
The CLI already speaks JSON on the way out (every response is `{\"success\": ..., \"data\": ...}`). Make it symmetric on the way in: every mutating subcommand should also accept a JSON payload instead of a long list of flags. That makes scripting against the CLI from any language painless, kills shell-quoting issues for free-form fields like descriptions, and reuses the schemas the MCP layer already defines.

## Why

- Shell quoting for multi-line descriptions, embedded quotes, or JSON snippets is brittle.
- Tooling that integrates with kanban (CI scripts, bots, AI tools) can build a struct in their native language, serialize, pipe.
- The MCP layer already has typed request structs (`CreateCardRequest`, `UpdateCardRequest`, etc.) with schemars derivations. Reusing them eliminates two parallel schema definitions.
- Output is already JSON; symmetric I/O makes the CLI a true pipe-friendly tool.

## Suggested shape

Add a single `--json <SOURCE>` flag to each mutating subcommand. `SOURCE` resolves in this order:
- `-` reads stdin
- `@path/to/file.json` reads the file
- anything else is parsed inline as the JSON payload

When `--json` is present, all other flags for that subcommand are forbidden (clap `conflicts_with_all`). When absent, current flag-based behaviour is unchanged.

Example:
```
echo '{\"board\":\"KAN\",\"column\":\"TODO\",\"title\":\"Wired\",\"sprint_id\":\"alpha\"}' \\
  | kanban kanban.json card create --json -
```

## Open design questions
- Should we reuse the MCP request structs verbatim (`CreateCardRequest`, etc.), or define CLI-specific equivalents? Reuse is cheaper but couples the two surfaces; that coupling is probably fine because both layers resolve names the same way.
- Batch support: should `--json` also accept a JSON array to run N operations in one invocation? Probably yes for create/update; the existing batch endpoints can absorb it.
- Schema discovery: should we add `kanban <cmd> --print-schema` that emits the JSON Schema for the payload? Useful for downstream tooling but expands scope; could be a follow-up.

## Suggested first slice
1. `card create --json` only — establishes the pattern, reuses `CreateCardRequest` from `kanban-mcp`.
2. Then `card update`, `card move`, `card archive`.
3. Then sprint/board/column equivalents.
4. Batch arrays and `--print-schema` as follow-ups.

## Files (first slice)
- `crates/kanban-cli/src/cli.rs` — add `--json` arg + the SOURCE parser
- `crates/kanban-cli/src/handlers/card.rs` — branch on `--json`, deserialize, hand off to the existing create path
- Possibly extract the MCP request structs into `kanban-service` or a shared crate so the CLI can depend on them without dragging in the MCP server.

## Out of scope
- Read commands keeping flag-only input (filters via flags are already terse).
- Replacing the existing flag API.
cards.title: CLI accepts JSON payloads as input

cards.description:
## Context / why
Slice **D** (split, part 2 of 2) of the Sprint entity factory epic (`00-epic.md`, **KAN-786**), under root **KAN-769**. The sibling child (`core.md`) funnels the service create path through `Sprint::create` and adds the FK/client-id/conflict tier. This child widens the create operation signature and repoints every consumer (CLI / TUI / MCP / server) at the factory-backed create + the shared `api::v1::sprints` DTO edge, and drops MCP's bespoke sprint request DTOs. Final slice of the Sprint epic; mirrors Board slice D.

Depends on `core.md` (the service create funnel + signature widening it relies on), which in turn depends on slices A/B/C + Foundation.

## Current state (researched)
### Consumers
- CLI: `crates/kanban-cli/src/handlers/sprint.rs:18` -> `ctx.create_sprint(board_uuid, prefix, name)`.
- TUI: `crates/kanban-tui/src/tui_context.rs:332-338`, `handlers/sprint_handlers.rs:168`, plus test call sites (`popup_handlers.rs:657`, `detail_view_handlers.rs:1231`).
- MCP: `crates/kanban-mcp/src/tools/sprint.rs:21-27` (`tool_create_sprint`) consumes the bespoke `CreateSprintRequest` (`crates/kanban-mcp/src/requests/sprint.rs:4-12`).
- Server: HTTP backend / handlers will consume `api::v1::sprints` DTOs (slice C). The server does NOT depend on persistence (per KAN-769 dep flow).
- `operations::create_sprint(board_id, prefix, name)` trait sig: `crates/kanban-domain/src/operations.rs:115-120`.

## Target
### 1. Widen the create operation signature
- Update `create_sprint_impl`/`operations::create_sprint` to accept the optional client `id` and `card_prefix` — extend to `create_sprint(board_id, id: Option<Uuid>, prefix, name, card_prefix)` or take a `NewSprint`-parts struct. The service mints `id = req.id.unwrap_or_else(Uuid::new_v4)` before building the command. Propagate through CLI/TUI/MCP.

### 2. Consumers -> factory + DTO edge
- **MCP**: delete `crates/kanban-mcp/src/requests/sprint.rs` `CreateSprintRequest` (and `UpdateSprintRequest` if it can use the shared DTO); import `kanban_service::api::v1::sprints::CreateSprintRequest`. Map MCP's `board: String` (UUID-or-name) resolution to `board_id` before constructing the request, then call the factory-backed create.
- **CLI/TUI**: build the same create input; project results through `SprintResponse` at the JSON-output edge (CLI) / consume the domain `Sprint` in-process (TUI), per Option A.
- **Server**: idempotent PUT-create + POST create using `api::v1::sprints` DTOs and `SprintResponse` projection. `PUT /v1/sprints/:id` with a body: if the id does not exist, create with that exact id (client-supplied id path); if it exists, replace client-editable fields (`ReplaceSprintRequest` -> `SprintUpdate`). The conflict/idempotency guarantee these handlers rely on comes from `core.md` (mapped to 409 at the API edge).

## Step-by-step (TDD red -> green -> refactor)
1. **Red**: write the per-consumer tests below. Present to user.
2. **Green (consumers)**: thread optional `id`/`card_prefix` through `create_sprint_impl`/`operations::create_sprint`; repoint MCP to the shared DTO; update CLI/TUI call sites.
3. **Green (server)**: idempotent PUT-create + POST create using `api::v1::sprints` DTOs and `SprintResponse` projection.
4. **Refactor**: collapse duplicate input-building; confirm MCP no longer references its own `CreateSprintRequest`; run the `..`/`Default::default()` CI guard over touched modules.

## Tests
### MCP (`crates/kanban-mcp/tests/`)
- `test_mcp_create_sprint_uses_shared_dto_and_factory` — `tool_create_sprint` against a real `KanbanContext` creates a Planning sprint with minted number; asserts MCP no longer references its own `CreateSprintRequest`.
### CLI (`crates/kanban-cli/tests/`, `assert_cmd`)
- `test_cli_sprint_create_mints_number_and_outputs_response` — `sprint create` against a real binary returns a sprint with number 1.
### TUI (`crates/kanban-tui/tests/`)
- `test_tui_create_sprint_funnels_through_factory` — the TUI create handler produces a Planning sprint via the service factory path.

## Acceptance criteria — per-consumer checklist
- [ ] `create_sprint_impl`/`operations::create_sprint` signature widened to carry optional client `id` + `card_prefix` (or `NewSprint`-parts struct); service mints `id = req.id.unwrap_or_else(Uuid::new_v4)`.
- [ ] **CLI** (`handlers/sprint.rs:18`) creates through the widened signature; result projected through `SprintResponse` at the JSON-output edge.
- [ ] **TUI** (`tui_context.rs:332-338`, `handlers/sprint_handlers.rs:168`, test sites `popup_handlers.rs:657`, `detail_view_handlers.rs:1231`) creates through the factory path; consumes the domain `Sprint` in-process (Option A). `auto_consume_name` TUI behaviour preserved.
- [ ] **MCP** (`tools/sprint.rs:21-27`) imports `kanban_service::api::v1::sprints::CreateSprintRequest`; resolves `board: String` (UUID-or-name) to `board_id`; bespoke `crates/kanban-mcp/src/requests/sprint.rs` create DTO deleted.
- [ ] **Server** handler does POST create + idempotent PUT-create using `api::v1::sprints` DTOs (`ReplaceSprintRequest` -> `SprintUpdate`) and `SprintResponse` projection; conflict -> 409.
- [ ] `cargo test --workspace` green; `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo fmt --check` clean.

## Dependencies / sequencing
Depends on **core** (`core.md` — the service create funnel + FK/client-id/conflict tier + widened signature). This is the last slice of the Sprint epic.

## Entity-specific quirks
- **Option A** projection: CLI projects results through `SprintResponse` at the JSON-output edge; TUI consumes the domain `Sprint` in-process. The server uses `api::v1::sprints` DTOs + `SprintResponse` projection and does NOT depend on persistence (per KAN-769 dep flow).
- `auto_consume_name` (`sprint_commands.rs:276,296`) is a TUI-only behaviour (consume next pooled name when none supplied). CLI/MCP pass false today (`sprint_commands.rs:275-276` doc) — the widened input must carry the `auto_consume_name`/name-source flag so the service knows whether to `consume_sprint_name()` vs leave `name_index=None`.
- MCP's `board` field is a `String` (UUID-or-name); resolve it to a `board_id` before constructing the shared `CreateSprintRequest`.
- Idempotent PUT-create at the server depends on the service-tier collision check delivered in `core.md`: a re-PUT of an existing id is a conflict (409); a novel id creates with that exact id.
cards.title: feat(service): point CLI/TUI/MCP/server at the Sprint factory + DTO edge

cards.description:
## Where, Why, How

**Where.** `kanban-tui` constructs `FileWatcher` directly and consumes `PersistenceMetadata` from the persistence layer, bypassing the service:

- `crates/kanban-tui/Cargo.toml:16` — declares `kanban-persistence` as a direct dependency
- `crates/kanban-tui/src/app/mod.rs:1979` — `kanban_persistence::FileWatcher::new()` instantiated in `App::run()`
- `crates/kanban-tui/src/app/mod.rs:395,1977` — `use kanban_persistence::ChangeDetector`
- `crates/kanban-tui/src/ui/error_log.rs:4` — imports `kanban_persistence::PersistenceMetadata` for diagnostics display
- `crates/kanban-tui/src/tui_context.rs:137` — delegates `KanbanContext::persistence_metadata()` whose return type is `kanban_persistence::PersistenceMetadata`
- `crates/kanban-service/src/context.rs:137` — re-exports the infrastructure type instead of wrapping it
- `crates/kanban-tui/src/state/snapshot.rs:48` — `snapshot_to_json_bytes` / `snapshot_from_json_bytes` imported in tests

**Why.** Per the CONTRIBUTING.md dependency diagram, TUI → SERVICE → PERSISTENCE. Today TUI reaches around SERVICE in three places: instantiating the file watcher, consuming raw persistence metadata types, and (in tests) calling serialization helpers directly. Any refactor in the watch/metadata APIs ripples straight into TUI rendering code. Architecturally these are infrastructure concerns the service is supposed to own.

This card overlaps with — but is broader than — KAN-241 (*"Fix TUI layer violation: direct PersistenceError usage"*). Once this lands, KAN-241's surface should be empty.

**How.** Move file-watcher ownership into `KanbanContext`. Define a TUI-facing `DataSourceMetadata` type in `kanban-service` that wraps `PersistenceMetadata` without re-exporting it. Drop the `kanban-persistence` dependency from `kanban-tui/Cargo.toml`.

---

## Proposed solution

### Step 1 — Service owns the file watcher

Move `FileWatcher::new()` construction out of `App::run()` into `KanbanContext`. The context already knows the storage location and the `PersistenceStore`. Expose a method:

```rust
// crates/kanban-service/src/context.rs
impl KanbanContext {
    /// Returns a stream of change events emitted by external writers
    /// to the underlying store. None if the store doesn't support
    /// change detection (in-memory backends, etc.).
    pub fn watch_changes(&self) -> Option<ChangeReceiver> { ... }
}
```

`ChangeReceiver` is a thin newtype around whatever channel `FileWatcher` produces — the type the TUI consumes, not `FileWatcher` itself.

### Step 2 — Wrap `PersistenceMetadata`

Define in `kanban-service`:

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct DataSourceMetadata {
    pub writer_id: Uuid,
    pub saved_at: DateTime<Utc>,
    pub version: String,
    // ... whatever fields the TUI actually consumes
}

impl From<kanban_persistence::PersistenceMetadata> for DataSourceMetadata {
    fn from(m: kanban_persistence::PersistenceMetadata) -> Self { /* */ }
}
```

Change `KanbanContext::persistence_metadata()` to return `DataSourceMetadata`. The TUI's `ui/error_log.rs:4` imports this instead.

### Step 3 — Test-only serialization helpers

`state/snapshot.rs:48` uses `snapshot_to_json_bytes` in tests. Either (a) re-export from `kanban-service::testing` behind a `cfg(test)` feature, or (b) move the test that needs it down into `kanban-persistence` where the helper lives. Option (a) is less invasive.

### Step 4 — Drop the Cargo.toml dependency

Once no `use kanban_persistence::` remains in `crates/kanban-tui/src/`, remove the dependency from `crates/kanban-tui/Cargo.toml:16`. The build verifies the absence of leaks.

---

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `kanban-tui/Cargo.toml` does not list `kanban-persistence` as a dependency
- [ ] No `use kanban_persistence::` in `crates/kanban-tui/src/`
- [ ] `KanbanContext::watch_changes()` (or similar) owns file-watcher construction
- [ ] `KanbanContext::persistence_metadata()` returns a service-layer type, not `kanban_persistence::PersistenceMetadata`
- [ ] KAN-241 is satisfied (no `kanban_persistence::PersistenceError` in TUI)
- [ ] All TUI tests pass (file-watch integration tests parameterise on the new API)
- [ ] `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` clean

## Closes / overlaps

- **KAN-241** — *"Fix TUI layer violation: direct PersistenceError usage"* — subsumed by step 2/4.

## Why now

This is the only remaining layer leak in the workspace. Once closed, the dependency diagram in CONTRIBUTING.md is enforced by the build, not by convention. Medium effort — the watcher and metadata indirection are isolated changes that won't cascade.
cards.title: refactor(tui): hide FileWatcher and PersistenceMetadata behind kanban-service

cards.description:
Design question raised reviewing the KAN-769 factory PR (#353): how should the READ / presentation side of the system be layered? Currently every external surface reuses the v1 HTTP wire Response DTOs; this card decides whether that should become a pluggable projection over the domain model instead.

## The concern
The v1 `*Response` DTOs (BoardResponse, ColumnResponse, CardResponse, SprintResponse) were designed as the HTTP wire contract. We then pointed MCP (and the CLI `--json` output) at the SAME DTOs. But:
- The HTTP API those DTOs exist for does NOT exist yet (deferred to the server epic, KAN-708). So we coupled MCP/CLI presentation to a contract whose primary consumer is not built.
- Presentation is hardcoded to JSON (`serde_json::to_string_pretty` in kanban-mcp/src/helpers/serialization.rs).
- There is no field selection / verbosity control, which an LLM-facing surface (MCP) especially benefits from (token cost).
- The construction (write) side is well-layered (factory, Option A: in-process consumers use the domain entity, DTO only at the wire edge); the read side is comparatively under-designed.

## The proposal to evaluate
Make the read side a PROJECTION LAYER over the domain model, chosen per surface, rather than every surface reusing the HTTP v1 Response DTO:
- Domain model is the single source of truth; each surface (MCP, CLI, future HTTP) selects a projection/presenter.
- Switchable: format (JSON now, others later) and FIELD SELECTION (return a subset / control verbosity).
- Decoupled: MCP/CLI are not hostage to the HTTP v1 response shape; HTTP can evolve (v2) without changing MCP output, and vice versa.

## Decision to make
Option A (status quo, now consistent): every surface reuses the v1 `*Response` DTO. Pros: one shared shape across HTTP+MCP+CLI, counter-hiding for free, simplest. Cons: couples MCP/CLI to an HTTP contract (currently vapor), JSON-only, no field selection.
Option B (pluggable presenter): a projection abstraction over the domain model; surfaces pick fields/format. Pros: decoupled, field selection, format flexibility, MCP/CLI not anchored to HTTP. Cons: more machinery; must justify the abstraction; risks divergent shapes across surfaces.

Honest caveats:
- MCP is JSON-ish by protocol (tool results are text/JSON/image content blocks), so "swap JSON for another format" is more relevant to a generic output layer than to MCP itself. The durable win of B is FIELD SELECTION + decoupling from the HTTP DTO, less so raw format-switching.
- A single shared response shape (A) genuinely buys cross-surface consistency; B must earn its abstraction.

## Current state (already done in #353)
- MCP read presentation was made CONSISTENT (commit 8a022082): all read/mutation tools project through the v1 Response DTOs, so no tool leaks internal counters. This is the clean Option-A baseline. NOTE: it was previously HALF-migrated (create/get via DTO; list serialized the raw domain `Board`, leaking `card_counter`); that inconsistency + a leak is now fixed.
- The MCP server's `instructions` string ("delegates to the kanban CLI") was stale/false and is corrected; MCP holds a `KanbanContext` in-process (it does NOT shell out to the CLI). If a CLI-delegation transport was ever intended, that is a separate architectural choice to revisit.

## Scope / blast radius if Option B is chosen
- Affects all four entities' read paths across MCP and the CLI `--json` output edge (and the future HTTP server).
- Would introduce a projection/presenter abstraction (likely a trait or a field-mask mechanism over the domain model) and retire the per-surface reuse of the v1 Response DTO for in-tool surfaces, keeping the Response DTO specifically for the HTTP wire when that lands.

## Recommendation
Not a blocker for #353 (the construction side is sound; the read side is now at least consistent). Decide A vs B before the HTTP API is built (KAN-708), so MCP/CLI are not permanently anchored to the HTTP shape by default. Given the HTTP API is deferred, there is a real case for B (or at least: keep the Response DTO as the HTTP projection only, and give MCP/CLI their own thin projections of the domain model).

## DECIDED (2026-06-28) — Option A for now; B deferred to KAN-708
Resolved on closing out the KAN-769 factory epic. DECISION: Option A — every in-tool surface (MCP, CLI --json) reuses the v1 `*Response` DTOs, the consistent baseline shipped in #353 (MCP reads projected, no counter leaks). Rationale: one shared shape across surfaces, counter-hiding for free, simplest; the durable wins of B (field selection + decoupling from the HTTP contract) are not needed until the HTTP API actually exists.
DEFERRED, not dropped: Option B (pluggable presenter over the domain model with field selection) is the right thing to RE-EVALUATE when the HTTP API lands (KAN-708) — specifically: keep the v1 Response DTO as the HTTP wire projection only, and give MCP/CLI their own thin domain projections IF a divergence or token-cost/field-selection need materialises. Reopen or spawn a child of KAN-708 at that point. Closing this card now records the present decision; it does not foreclose B.
cards.title: design: read/presentation layer — pluggable projection over the domain model vs reusing v1 Response DTOs
feat(persistence-json): discrete archived_cards + V7->V8 migration [B3]

cards.description:
The changeset that shipped with PR #311 (`.changeset/kan-556-add-optional-sprint-assignment-to-card-creation.md`) was written for the original feature scope. After the in-review polish round (commits `5e8dc8b8` through `b2b7d0c2`), one user-visible behaviour change is missing from the release note.

## What's missing

`55f44b28` `fix(tui): bulk-assign dialog opens with no committed selection`. Previously, opening the bulk-assign-many-cards-to-sprint dialog and pressing Enter without first touching the picker unassigned every selected card. The fix opens that dialog with no committed selection, so a bare Enter is a no-op; users must press Space to commit a row before Enter applies.

That's a behavioural change to a workflow some users may rely on muscle memory for. It belongs in the changeset under a sentence like:

> The bulk-assign-to-sprint dialog (when multiple cards are selected) no longer mass-unassigns on a bare Enter. Press Space first to commit either a sprint or the "(None)" row, then Enter to apply.

## What's not missing (intentionally)

The other five follow-up commits are internal hardening: timestamp determinism on a domain helper, a debug_assert, dead code removal, a Selection::Unset edge case for filter-hidden sprints (currently dormant in production), and the stale-board defense (covers an interaction state that doesn't arise via keybindings today). None of those change observable behaviour for the existing user-facing flows, so they don't belong in a release note.

## How to action

Depends on how this repo consumes changesets:
- **If unreleased**: amend `.changeset/kan-556-add-optional-sprint-assignment-to-card-creation.md` directly in a tiny PR. Append the bulk-assign paragraph to the existing TUI section.
- **If already consumed by a release**: add a new changeset entry under the appropriate bump level (likely `patch` since it's a fix to a feature in the same release).

Check `git log -- .changeset/kan-556-*` and the latest release notes to decide which path applies.

## Files
- `.changeset/kan-556-add-optional-sprint-assignment-to-card-creation.md` (amend) or a new `.changeset/*.md` file (append).
cards.title: Backfill KAN-556 changeset with bulk-assign behaviour change

cards.description:
## Where, Why, How

**Where.** `crates/kanban-tui/src/handlers/detail_view_handlers.rs:627-945` — `handle_sprint_detail_key` is a **318-line single function** dispatching keyboard input across the sprint detail view.

**Why.** CONTRIBUTING.md target: functions < 50 lines. This one is 6.4× over. Symptoms today:

1. Reading is painful — the function is a giant `match key { ... }` with multi-screen arms.
2. Every new sprint-detail keybinding lands inside this function, so it grows unboundedly.
3. Branches share local state (selection cursor, filter state) by being co-located in the same scope. That coupling is what kept extraction from happening sooner — but it also forces every reader to track all 318 lines of state at once.

Closely related: the whole file is **1595 lines** (KAN-223 already flagged the file but not this specific function). This function alone accounts for 20% of the file.

**How.** Decompose by sub-action. Each match arm or small cluster of arms becomes its own pure handler method. Shared local state lifts to fields on `App` (where most of it already lives) or to a small `SprintDetailKeyContext` struct.

---

## Proposed solution

### Step 1 — Categorise the match arms

Read the function once and group its arms by intent. Typical categories you'll find:

- Cursor movement (j/k/g/G in the card list)
- Panel switching (Tab, h/l between completed/uncompleted)
- Card-level actions (Enter to open, e to edit, x to archive)
- Sprint-level actions (commit/complete/cancel)
- Sort / filter toggles
- Escape and quit

Each category becomes one method.

### Step 2 — Extract each category

Example extraction shape:

```rust
// Before — in handle_sprint_detail_key, lines ~700-740:
KeyCode::Char('j') | KeyCode::Down => {
    // 12 lines of cursor advance logic
}
KeyCode::Char('k') | KeyCode::Up => {
    // 12 lines of cursor retreat logic
}

// After:
KeyCode::Char('j') | KeyCode::Down => self.sprint_detail_cursor_down(),
KeyCode::Char('k') | KeyCode::Up   => self.sprint_detail_cursor_up(),
```

Each extracted method is < 30 lines and unit-testable on its own.

### Step 3 — Shared state

Where multiple arms read/write the same locals (e.g. "panel" and "selected index"), promote them to `App` fields or to a single `SprintDetailState` struct (if not already present). The function reduces to a dispatch table.

### Step 4 — Target shape

After decomposition, `handle_sprint_detail_key` should be a flat ~30-line match that dispatches to `self.<sub_handler>()` methods. Reading it answers "what keys are bound" in one screen; reading any sub-handler answers "what does this key do" in one screen.

### Step 5 — Tests

The integration tests at `crates/kanban-tui/tests/` that exercise sprint detail keys should pass unchanged. Add focused unit tests for each new method — the existing test file `detail_view_handlers.rs:1255-1432` already has the test shape established.

---

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `handle_sprint_detail_key` ≤ 60 lines (dispatch table)
- [ ] Each extracted sub-handler ≤ 50 lines
- [ ] No regression in existing sprint-detail integration tests
- [ ] At least one unit test per new sub-handler
- [ ] `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` clean

## Related

- **KAN-223** — Codebase Quality Audit umbrella; lists `detail_view_handlers.rs` size as Priority 1 area. This card cracks the worst single function inside it; a sibling card splits the file by entity (card/board/sprint detail).
- Sibling card: *"Split detail_view_handlers.rs by entity"* — should land after this one so the sprint-detail piece moves over already decomposed.

## Why now

`handle_sprint_detail_key` is the single largest function in the workspace and the biggest merge-conflict magnet in the TUI handler tree. Every new sprint feature passes through it. Decomposing it removes a velocity tax that compounds with each subsequent sprint-related card.
cards.title: refactor(tui): decompose handle_sprint_detail_key (318-line function)

cards.description:
## Context / why
- Root epic: **KAN-821**. Owning sub-epic: **KAN-823 (SE-B — archived-cards first-class retrofit)**.
- Implements the SQLite half of DECIDED **D2** and the storage pivot **D10 (FK extension-table, SUPERSEDES the earlier B4 "move archived rows into a separate full-data table" plan)** plus **D7** (schema `2→3` migration + round-trip test + backup).
- **D10 payoff (validated by Spike A):** the existing `archived_cards` table (`schema.sql:122`, `card_id` PK/FK → `cards(id)`, `archived_at`, `original_column_id`, `original_position`) IS **already an extension table** (1:0..1 on `cards`, holding only archival columns). So the retrofit is a **fix-in-place**, NOT a data move:
  - **KEEP the card row in `cards`.** Do NOT move rows into a new full-data table.
  - **Do NOT rebuild `sprint_logs`.** Because the card never leaves `cards`, `sprint_logs.card_id → cards(id) ON DELETE CASCADE` (`schema.sql:116`) stays valid — **the `sprint_logs` FK trap that dominated the old B4 is GONE.** State this explicitly: the entire crown-jewel migration risk (moving rows out of `cards`, deferring FKs, table-swapping `sprint_logs`, 24-site `ArchivedCard::new` churn) evaporates under D10.
- What remains is small and surgical: add `board_id` to the extension table (+ backfill), break the column-delete cascade so it cannot orphan an archived card, and modernize the live-card visibility filter from `NOT IN` to a PK-indexed `NOT EXISTS`.

## Current state (researched)
- `SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION: u32 = 2` at `crates/kanban-persistence-sqlite/src/sqlite_store/mod.rs:27`. Future-version refusal uses it at `:91`/`:94`. Fresh DBs stamp it via `init.rs:26` and normalize via `init.rs:139` (`UPDATE metadata SET schema_version = ? WHERE id = 1 AND schema_version < ?`).
- Schema: `crates/kanban-persistence-sqlite/src/schema.sql`.
  - `:119` comment "Cards table (holds both active and archived cards)"; `cards` at `:120`, `column_id` FK `REFERENCES columns(id) ON DELETE CASCADE` (`:100`-style, at `:99`/`:100` region — for `cards` it is the `FOREIGN KEY (column_id) REFERENCES columns(id) ON DELETE CASCADE` line).
  - `:121` comment "Archived cards metadata (card data lives in cards table)"; `archived_cards` table at `:122` is **metadata-only** (`card_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY`, `archived_at TEXT NOT NULL`, `original_column_id TEXT NOT NULL`, `original_position INTEGER NOT NULL`) with `FOREIGN KEY (card_id) REFERENCES cards(id) ON DELETE CASCADE` (`:127`). **This is the extension table we extend in place.**
  - `sprint_logs` (`:107`) FKs `card_id REFERENCES cards(id) ON DELETE CASCADE` (`:116`) — **stays untouched under D10** (the card stays in `cards`).
  - **The orphan hazard is the `cards → columns` cascade**, not the extension FK: deleting a column cascade-deletes the archived card's row in `cards` (`cards.column_id REFERENCES columns(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`), which cascade-deletes its `archived_cards` extension row. That chain is what B2 relaxes in the domain and this card must physically break in SQLite.
- **Live-card visibility filter** — `id NOT IN (SELECT card_id FROM archived_cards)` appears at exactly **7 sites** (verified):
  1. `entities/card.rs:129` (`fetch_cards_with_filter`)
  2. `data_store.rs:131` (`get_card`)
  3. `data_store.rs:174` (`count_cards_in_column`)
  4. `data_store.rs:197` (`count_cards_in_column_excluding`)
  5. `data_store.rs:217` (`delete_card`)
  6. `data_store.rs:236` (`delete_cards_by_columns`)
  7. `data_store.rs:257` (`clear_sprint_from_cards`)
  Plus the inverse semi-join `id IN (SELECT card_id FROM archived_cards)` at `data_store.rs:390` (`clear_sprint_from_archived_cards`) — kept, but rephrase to the `EXISTS` form for symmetry.
- Archived-card write duplicates into `cards`: `crates/kanban-persistence-sqlite/src/sqlite_store/entities/archived_card.rs:11` `Self::write_card_with_conn(conn, &ac.card)` then inserts the extension metadata row. **Under D10 this dual write is CORRECT and stays** (card row in `cards`, archival columns in `archived_cards`) — it just gains `board_id` + the column-decoupling step.
- Archived-card reads JOIN `cards`: `lists.rs:57` `list_archived_cards_async`, `data_store.rs:270` `get_archived_card`, `data_store.rs:330` `list_archived_cards_by_columns`. **Under D10 these JOINs are CORRECT and stay** (the card data genuinely lives in `cards`).
- Snapshot apply: `crates/kanban-persistence-sqlite/src/sqlite_store/snapshot.rs:24` — unchanged in shape (card row + extension row).
- `ArchivedCard` gains `board_id` in **B1**. `BoardId = Uuid` (`crates/kanban-domain/src/board.rs:9`).
- On-open migration hook: `init.rs:68` `SqliteStore::migrate(pool)` — ALTER-add-column-if-missing pattern (`:91-117`), legacy drops (`:74`, `:155`), version normalize (`:139`). The new 2→3 step goes here and **must run BEFORE `sqlx::raw_sql(SCHEMA)`** (`mod.rs:107`) — see quirks (SCHEMA declares the new `board_id` index and would fail on the old-shape table). Model it on the existing legacy-drop guard `drop_legacy_command_log_if_present`.
- Version test expectations to bump: `SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION` (`mod.rs:27`), `schema.sql:10` default, `lib.rs:43` inline mirror, and the fresh-db version tests under `src/sqlite_store/tests/init.rs`.

## Target
The extension table gains `board_id` (+ index); it stays a 1:0..1 extension of `cards`, NOT a full-data copy:
```sql
-- Archived cards: extension table over `cards` (card data stays in `cards`).
-- Adds board_id so board scoping is a direct WHERE, not a column walk (D2/D10).
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS archived_cards (
    card_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    board_id TEXT NOT NULL,              -- NEW (D10): direct board scope; backfilled on migrate
    archived_at TEXT NOT NULL,
    original_column_id TEXT NOT NULL,    -- historical column at archive time
    original_position INTEGER NOT NULL,
    FOREIGN KEY (card_id) REFERENCES cards(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_archived_cards_board_id ON archived_cards(board_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_archived_cards_archived_at ON archived_cards(archived_at);
```
**Cascade-decoupling (chosen mechanism — state it plainly):** relax the `cards.column_id` foreign key from `ON DELETE CASCADE` to `ON DELETE SET NULL` and make `cards.column_id` nullable, so deleting a column no longer cascade-deletes a card row that was archived from it (its historical column is preserved in `archived_cards.original_column_id`). This is the SQLite realization of "on archive, null the card's live `column_id`" — the FK action nulls it automatically on column-delete, and the live-card guard (retained in B2) guarantees the only rows a column-delete can reach are archived-card rows. SQLite cannot `ALTER ... DROP CONSTRAINT`, so the 2→3 migration **table-swaps `cards`** (create `cards_new` with the relaxed FK, copy, drop, rename) inside the same tx. Fresh DBs get the relaxed FK straight from SCHEMA.
Live-card visibility filter, modernized to a PK-indexed anti-join (KEPT, not removed — archived cards still live in `cards`):
```sql
-- fetch_cards_with_filter (entities/card.rs:129) and the 6 data_store.rs sites:
SELECT ... FROM cards
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM archived_cards a WHERE a.card_id = cards.id) {where_clause}
ORDER BY position ASC, created_at ASC
```
`archived_cards.card_id` is the PRIMARY KEY, so `NOT EXISTS` is an indexed point-probe per row — cheaper and clearer than `NOT IN` at any scale.

## Step-by-step (TDD: Red → Green → Refactor)
1. **Red — failing tests first (present for review):**
   - `src/sqlite_store/tests/init.rs`: bump the fresh-db version test to expect `SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION == 3`; update the inline schema-version default mirror.
   - `src/sqlite_store/tests/migration_v2_to_v3.rs` (new) or extend `init.rs`:
     - `test_migrate_v2_db_adds_board_id_and_backfills` — build a v2-shaped DB (extension `archived_cards` WITHOUT `board_id`, one archived card present in BOTH `cards` and `archived_cards`), open the store, assert the extension table now has `board_id`, backfilled via `original_column_id`→`columns.board_id` (nil + warn when the column is gone), and the card row is STILL in `cards`.
     - `test_migrate_v2_db_preserves_archived_sprint_logs` — an archived card with `sprint_logs` still has them after migration. **Now trivially green (no row move), but assert it explicitly** as the D10 regression guard.
     - `test_migrate_is_idempotent_on_v3_db` — reopening an already-migrated DB is a no-op (no duplicate column, version stays 3).
   - `src/sqlite_store/tests/cards.rs`: `test_list_all_cards_excludes_archived_via_not_exists` — archive a card, assert `list_all_cards()` omits it and the crate no longer contains `NOT IN (SELECT card_id FROM archived_cards)` (behavioural + grep).
   - `test_delete_column_does_not_cascade_delete_archived_card` — archive a card from a column, delete that column, assert the archived card survives (row intact in `cards` + `archived_cards`, its `column_id` now NULL) — proves the cascade hazard is broken.
   - `test_archived_card_round_trip_preserves_board_id_and_all_fields` — insert an `ArchivedCard` with `board_id`, snapshot→apply→read, assert equality incl. `board_id`. **Keep this all-fields test** — the writer binds each card field individually (not drift-guarded), so a dropped bind is only caught by an all-fields assertion.
   - `test_list_archived_cards_by_board_filters_by_board_id` — two boards each with an archived card; the board-scoped query returns only its own.
2. **Green — minimal implementation:**
   - Bump `SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION` to `3` (`mod.rs:27`); `schema.sql:10` + `lib.rs:43` default to 3.
   - SCHEMA: add `board_id TEXT NOT NULL` + `idx_archived_cards_board_id` to the `archived_cards` DDL; relax `cards.column_id` to nullable + `FOREIGN KEY (column_id) REFERENCES columns(id) ON DELETE SET NULL`.
   - Add `SqliteStore::migrate_v2_to_v3_archived_cards(pool)` in `init.rs`, invoked from `migrate()` BEFORE `sqlx::raw_sql(SCHEMA)` runs (guarded/idempotent, modelled on `drop_legacy_command_log_if_present`): detect the old shape (`archived_cards` lacks `board_id` via `pragma_table_info`); `ALTER TABLE archived_cards ADD COLUMN board_id TEXT`; `UPDATE archived_cards SET board_id = (SELECT c.board_id FROM columns c WHERE c.id = archived_cards.original_column_id)` (nil + warn where the column is gone); then table-swap `cards` to the relaxed `column_id` FK (create `cards_new` ON DELETE SET NULL, copy, drop, rename) and `UPDATE cards SET column_id = NULL WHERE id IN (SELECT card_id FROM archived_cards)` so already-archived cards are decoupled. Run inside one tx with `PRAGMA defer_foreign_keys = ON` (mirroring `apply_snapshot_async`).
   - Rewrite `write_archived_card_with_conn` (`entities/archived_card.rs`) to bind `board_id` in the extension INSERT and set the card row's `column_id = NULL` (historical column preserved in `original_column_id`). **Keep** the `write_card_with_conn` call — the card row stays in `cards`.
   - Replace the 7 `NOT IN (SELECT card_id FROM archived_cards)` sites (`entities/card.rs:129`; `data_store.rs:131,174,197,217,236,257`) with `NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM archived_cards a WHERE a.card_id = cards.id)`; rephrase the inverse semi-join at `data_store.rs:390` to `EXISTS (...)`.
   - Add `list_archived_cards_by_board(board_id)` override on `SqliteStore`'s `DataStore` impl (`WHERE board_id = ?`) — consumes the trait method B2 adds with a default field-filter body.
   - Readers (`list_archived_cards_async`, `get_archived_card`, `list_archived_cards_by_columns`) keep their JOIN to `cards`; add `board_id` to the projected columns.
3. **Refactor:** extract the extension-row projection (`archived_at`, `board_id`, `original_column_id`, `original_position`) into one helper reused by the three readers; keep each file < 300 lines, each fn < 50.

## Tests
- `test_fresh_db_records_schema_version_3` — `src/sqlite_store/tests/init.rs`.
- `test_migrate_v2_db_adds_board_id_and_backfills` — `src/sqlite_store/tests/migration_v2_to_v3.rs` + tempfile (**D7 migration test**): old-shape extension table gains `board_id`, backfilled via `original_column_id`→column→board; card row stays in `cards`.
- `test_migrate_v2_db_preserves_archived_sprint_logs` — archived card's `sprint_logs` survive (trivially green under D10; asserted as the regression guard proving no row move).
- `test_migrate_is_idempotent_on_v3_db` — reopen is a no-op (no duplicate `board_id` column, version stays 3).
- `test_archived_card_round_trip_preserves_board_id_and_all_fields` — all-fields identity incl. `board_id` (guards the individually-bound writer).
- `test_list_all_cards_excludes_archived_via_not_exists` — archived card omitted from live listings; `NOT IN (...)` string gone from the crate.
- `test_delete_column_does_not_cascade_delete_archived_card` — deleting the original column leaves the archived card intact (cascade hazard broken; card `column_id` now NULL).
- `test_list_archived_cards_by_board_filters_by_board_id` — board-scoped read returns only that board's archived cards.
- Future-version guard: existing refusal test still passes with `binary_max` now 3.

## Code examples
Extension INSERT — add `board_id`, null the live `column_id` (before→after, `entities/archived_card.rs:11`):
```rust
// BEFORE
Self::write_card_with_conn(conn, &ac.card).await?;   // card row stays in `cards`
sqlx::query(
    "INSERT INTO archived_cards (card_id, archived_at, original_column_id, original_position)
     VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?) ON CONFLICT(card_id) DO UPDATE SET ...")
    .bind(ac.card.id.to_string())
    .bind(fmt_dt(&ac.archived_at))
    .bind(ac.original_column_id.to_string())
    .bind(ac.original_position)
// AFTER — card row STILL written to `cards`, but with column_id decoupled:
Self::write_card_with_conn(conn, &ac.card).await?;
sqlx::query("UPDATE cards SET column_id = NULL WHERE id = ?")   // decouple from live column
    .bind(ac.card.id.to_string()).execute(&mut *conn).await.map_err(db_err)?;
sqlx::query(
    "INSERT INTO archived_cards (card_id, board_id, archived_at, original_column_id, original_position)
     VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?) ON CONFLICT(card_id) DO UPDATE SET
        board_id=excluded.board_id, archived_at=excluded.archived_at,
        original_column_id=excluded.original_column_id, original_position=excluded.original_position")
    .bind(ac.card.id.to_string())
    .bind(ac.board_id.to_string())          // NEW
    .bind(fmt_dt(&ac.archived_at))
    .bind(ac.original_column_id.to_string())
    .bind(ac.original_position)
    .execute(&mut *conn).await.map_err(db_err)?;
```
Live-card filter (before→after, all 7 sites):
```rust
// BEFORE
"... FROM cards WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT card_id FROM archived_cards) {} ORDER BY ..."
// AFTER
"... FROM cards WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM archived_cards a WHERE a.card_id = cards.id) {} ORDER BY ..."
```
Migration sketch (`init.rs`, invoked from `migrate()` BEFORE `raw_sql(SCHEMA)`):
```rust
async fn migrate_v2_to_v3_archived_cards(pool: &Pool<Sqlite>) -> KanbanResult<()> {
    let needs: bool = sqlx::query_scalar(
        "SELECT COUNT(*) = 0 FROM pragma_table_info('archived_cards') WHERE name = 'board_id'",
    ).fetch_one(pool).await.map_err(db_err)?;
    if !needs { return Ok(()); }                       // idempotent
    // SPIKE-CORRECTED: the `cards` table-swap does `DROP TABLE cards`, which with
    // foreign_keys ON fires ON DELETE CASCADE on sprint_logs/archived_cards and WIPES
    // them. `defer_foreign_keys` defers CHECKING, not cascade ACTIONS — it does NOT help.
    // Correct approach: PRAGMA foreign_keys = OFF on a dedicated pooled connection
    // OUTSIDE the BEGIN (the pragma is a no-op inside a transaction), restore after.
    let mut conn = pool.acquire().await.map_err(db_err)?;
    sqlx::query("PRAGMA foreign_keys = OFF").execute(&mut *conn).await.map_err(db_err)?;
    let mut tx = conn.begin().await.map_err(db_err)?;
    // 1. add board_id + backfill from original_column_id -> columns.board_id (nil + warn if gone)
    // 2. table-swap `cards` to `column_id` nullable + FK ON DELETE SET NULL (create _new, copy, drop, rename)
    // 3. UPDATE cards SET column_id = NULL WHERE id IN (SELECT card_id FROM archived_cards)
    tx.commit().await.map_err(db_err)?;
    sqlx::query("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON").execute(&mut *conn).await.map_err(db_err)?;
    Ok(())
}
```

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `cargo test -p kanban-persistence-sqlite` green; `cargo clippy -p kanban-persistence-sqlite -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo fmt` clean.
- [ ] `SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION == 3`; fresh DBs stamp 3; future-version guard reports `binary_max: 3`.
- [ ] `archived_cards` remains an **extension table** (card_id PK/FK to `cards`) and gains `board_id` (+ index); the card row stays in `cards`; **`sprint_logs` is NOT rebuilt** (D10 payoff — assert its FK still references `cards`).
- [ ] The string `NOT IN (SELECT card_id FROM archived_cards)` no longer exists in the crate; the 7 sites use PK-indexed `NOT EXISTS`.
- [ ] **Migration (D7):** a pre-3 fixture DB migrates on open — `board_id` added + backfilled, cards decoupled from deleted columns, sprint logs preserved, idempotent on re-open. (**No `.backup`** — SQLite has no backup mechanism; the migration is additive-in-place. Any `.backup` line here is JSON-inherited boilerplate; ignore it.)
- [ ] Invariant: deleting a column no longer deletes/orphans archived cards archived from it (their `cards.column_id` goes NULL; the row survives).

## Dependencies / sequencing
- Depends on **B1** (`ArchivedCard.board_id`) and **B2** (in-memory board-scoped query + relaxed column-delete guard; `DataStore::list_archived_cards_by_board` default). **B1/B2 land first.** This card provides the SQLite override of `list_archived_cards_by_board` that B5 consumes.
- Independent of the JSON card **B3** (different crate, separate version constant, no shared files).
- Additive to the build: once B1/B2 are in, this compiles green on its own; B5 (surfaces) can follow.

## Entity-specific quirks
- **The `sprint_logs` FK trap is GONE under D10** — the card never leaves `cards`, so `sprint_logs.card_id → cards(id)` and all edge FKs stay valid. Do NOT rebuild `sprint_logs`; the old B4 table-swap of it is deleted work. Assert its FK is unchanged.
- **Migration ordering is load-bearing:** run `migrate_v2_to_v3_archived_cards` BEFORE `sqlx::raw_sql(SCHEMA)` at `mod.rs:107`. SCHEMA declares `idx_archived_cards_board_id`, which fails to create against the old-shape (`board_id`-less) table. Model the guard on `drop_legacy_command_log_if_present`, which likewise runs pre-SCHEMA. `PRAGMA defer_foreign_keys` defers FK *checking* but does NOT suppress `ON DELETE CASCADE`/`SET NULL` *actions* — the `cards` table-swap must apply the relaxed FK, not rely on deferral.
- **`board_id` on a historical archived card whose original column was deleted** is unrecoverable relationally; backfill `Uuid::nil()` and log a warning (matches D2's "may dangle").
- **Nullable `cards.column_id`:** the relaxed FK makes `column_id` nullable. Confirm `row_to_card` / any reader tolerates a NULL `column_id` for archived-card rows (they are read through the archived path, but the all-cards path must not panic on NULL). Live cards always have a non-null `column_id` (guarded).
- `lib.rs:43` carries an inline metadata-DDL mirror used by a test harness; keep its `schema_version` default in sync with `SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION` or that test drifts.

## Execution-validated (full spike)
GREEN (commit 880b79a0; workspace build PASS). Confirmed against the real implementation:
- **Migration-safety mechanism CORRECTED (substantive):** the `cards` table-swap's `DROP TABLE cards` with `foreign_keys` ON fires `ON DELETE CASCADE` on `sprint_logs`/`archived_cards` and **wipes them**. `PRAGMA defer_foreign_keys` defers CHECKING, NOT cascade ACTIONS — it does not help. The fix is `PRAGMA foreign_keys = OFF` on a **dedicated pooled connection OUTSIDE the BEGIN** (the pragma is a no-op inside a tx), restored after. The sketch above and the quirk note are both corrected. `init.rs` documents this inline.
- **D10 payoff held:** the `sprint_logs` FK trap is GONE — the card never leaves `cards`, so `sprint_logs.card_id → cards(id)` stays valid; **no row move, no `sprint_logs` rebuild.** `test_migrate_v2_db_preserves_archived_sprint_logs` is trivially green (asserted as the regression guard).
- **No `.backup` for SQLite** (no backup mechanism; additive-in-place). **Migration runs BEFORE `sqlx::raw_sql(SCHEMA)`** at `mod.rs:107` (load-bearing — SCHEMA's `idx_archived_cards_board_id` fails against the old-shape table).
- **B1's three SQLite `board_id: nil()` placeholders** (`data_store.rs:293/372`, `lists.rs:84`) are wired to the real `board_id` column HERE. `list_archived_cards_by_board` works E2E through SQLite after this card.
- Extra test added: `test_migrate_v2_db_backfills_nil_when_original_column_missing` (the nil+warn path). The v2-seed helper needs `.foreign_keys(false)` (sqlx defaults ON and rejects forward-ref seed inserts) — test-only.

## UPDATE (after F1a #363) — archived_at now sourced from `metadata`
`ArchivedCard` owns `metadata: ArchiveMetadata` (F1a). The SQLite `archived_cards.archived_at` COLUMN and wire shape are UNCHANGED — the writer binds `ac.metadata.archived_at` and the readers build `ArchiveMetadata::at(row_archived_at)` (F1a already updated these sites). So this card's schema 2->3 work (add `board_id`, cascade fix) is unaffected: `archived_at` stays a plain column; no extra migration for the metadata envelope. Just build on the already-metadata-sourced writer/reader.

## RE-SPIKE VALIDATED (2026-07-06) — corrections (supersede the DECIDED cascade text above)
Spiked green (commit 658de981 on spike/b4-respike): 57 lib + 21 integration, clippy/fmt clean.
1. **Cascade mechanism REPLACED.** NOT "SET NULL + nullable + null-on-archive" (self-contradictory: `card.column_id` is `NOT NULL Uuid`; nulling breaks `row_to_card` and the all-fields round-trip, and diverges from in-memory/JSON which keep the dangling original). CORRECT: **DROP the `cards.column_id → columns(id)` FK** (was `schema.sql:100`); keep `column_id TEXT NOT NULL` with value intact. Migration = table-swap `cards` (create `cards_new` without the column_id FK, copy, drop, rename) under `foreign_keys = OFF`. Live-card cleanup on column delete is already explicit via `commands/cascade_commands.rs DeleteCardsByColumns`, so the FK cascade was redundant. KEEP `archived_cards.card_id → cards ON DELETE CASCADE`.
2. **DELETE** the writer step "set card row `column_id = NULL`" (`entities/archived_card.rs`) — writer only adds the `board_id` bind; `write_card_with_conn` unchanged.
3. **DELETE** the "row_to_card tolerates NULL column_id" / "nullable column_id" quirks — no longer applicable.
4. Migration MUST run BEFORE `raw_sql(SCHEMA)` (`mod.rs:105`) — SCHEMA `CREATE INDEX idx_archived_cards_board_id` errors on the old-shape table otherwise. `PRAGMA foreign_keys = OFF` on a dedicated connection OUTSIDE `BEGIN` (defer_foreign_keys does NOT suppress DROP TABLE cascade). Add `use sqlx::Acquire;` in init.rs.
5. 7 `NOT IN (SELECT card_id FROM archived_cards)` sites → `NOT EXISTS`. `list_archived_cards_by_board` override = single `WHERE board_id = ?` joined to cards + `idx_archived_cards_board_id`.
6. Tests: round-trip-all-fields+board_id; 2→3 backfill; **backfill nil when original column missing**; **delete-column-survives (assert card.column_id retained as dangling original)**; sprint-logs preserved; idempotent; fresh-db version 3.

## Review deferred follow-ups (PR #366, not blocking)
- [ ] **board_id nullability drift:** the 2->3 migration adds `board_id` via `ALTER TABLE archived_cards ADD COLUMN board_id TEXT` (nullable), while a FRESH db gets `board_id TEXT NOT NULL` (schema.sql). Backfill fills every row and the writer always binds non-null, so no data loss — but a migrated db's schema doesn't enforce the NOT NULL the fresh schema advertises. Tightening needs an archived_cards table-swap; judged not worth it now. Revisit if schema-fidelity/round-trip-equality is ever asserted.
- [ ] **Integrity-check altitude:** live-card column integrity is enforced only in `store_manager::repair_snapshot_fks` (cross-backend migration, at the JSON-Value level). Dropping the SQLite FK removed that backstop globally; a future bulk-import / snapshot-apply path would not be covered. Consider lifting the check to the domain snapshot-apply / DataStore boundary so every mutation path inherits it (migration is the only bulk path today, so deferred).
