### Overview

**Where**: `packaging/chocolatey/kanban.nuspec` lines 9 and 13.

**Why**: Chocolatey's automated validator flagged this on the 0.7.2 moderation submission as a Guideline: `ProjectUrl and ProjectSourceUrl are typically different, but not always. Please ensure that projectSourceUrl is pointing to software source code or remove the field from the nuspec.` Non-blocking for approval (no Requirements were flagged on 0.7.2) but reduces package quality and will keep firing on every future submission until fixed.

**How**: Either drop `<projectSourceUrl>` from the nuspec (since the project is hosted on GitHub and `projectUrl` already points at the same canonical source) or point `projectSourceUrl` at a distinct source-tree URL such as a `src/` subtree. The simpler fix is removal.

---

### Engineering detail

**Offending code**:

```
packaging/chocolatey/kanban.nuspec:9   <projectUrl>https://github.com/fulsomenko/kanban</projectUrl>
                                 :13  <projectSourceUrl>https://github.com/fulsomenko/kanban</projectSourceUrl>
```

Both fields resolve to the same URL. The Chocolatey schema expects `projectSourceUrl` to specifically point at source code, so for projects where the homepage and source repo coincide (GitHub-hosted, no separate marketing site), the conventional answer is to omit `projectSourceUrl`.

**Suggested solution**:

```diff
   <projectUrl>https://github.com/fulsomenko/kanban</projectUrl>
   <iconUrl>https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fulsomenko/kanban/master/assets/icon-bold-transparent-black.png</iconUrl>
   <copyright>2025 Max Emil Yoon Blomstervall</copyright>
   <requireLicenseAcceptance>false</requireLicenseAcceptance>
-  <projectSourceUrl>https://github.com/fulsomenko/kanban</projectSourceUrl>
   <packageSourceUrl>https://github.com/fulsomenko/kanban/tree/master/packaging/chocolatey</packageSourceUrl>
```

`packageSourceUrl` already correctly points at the packaging subtree (the *nuspec source*, distinct from the *software source*), so the chocolatey-community-package-vs-software-source distinction is still preserved after removing `projectSourceUrl`.

---

### Considerations

- The fix is metadata-only. No binary or behaviour change.
- Ships in the next normal release (0.7.3 or whenever). The 0.7.2 nupkg already in moderation does not require a same-version re-push: the maintainer "repush with the same version" instruction only applies to flagged **Requirements**, and 0.7.2 had no Requirements flagged (Guidelines only). Per the moderation notice: "only Requirements will hold up a package version from approval."
- The Chocolatey validator should stop flagging this Guideline once the field is removed.

**Pros**: Single-line removal. Clears one of two outstanding moderation Guidelines.
**Cons**: None.

---

### Alternative solutions

Point `projectSourceUrl` at a deep link like `https://github.com/fulsomenko/kanban/tree/master/crates` to satisfy the distinct-source-URL spirit. Rejected: arbitrary deep links rot when the repo structure changes, and `projectUrl` already covers the same destination. Removal is the cleaner answer.
cards.title: differentiate nuspec projectSourceUrl from projectUrl

cards.description:
### Overview

**Where**: `packaging/chocolatey/kanban.nuspec` line 4.

**Why**: Chocolatey's automated validator flagged this on the 0.7.2 moderation submission as a Guideline: `Title (title) matches id exactly. Please consider using something slightly more descriptive for the title in the nuspec.` Non-blocking for approval (no Requirements were flagged on 0.7.2) but reduces package quality and will keep firing on every future submission until fixed.

**How**: Replace `<title>kanban</title>` with a phrase that describes what the package is, distinct from the lowercase package id.

---

### Engineering detail

**Offending code**:

```
packaging/chocolatey/kanban.nuspec:3   <id>kanban</id>
                                 :4   <title>kanban</title>
```

`id` is the install-time package identifier (must be lowercase, URL-safe, distinct from other packages). `title` is the human-facing display name shown on the Chocolatey package page and in `choco search` output. They are meant to differ; the validator wants the title to actually convey what the package is to a human browsing the community feed.

**Suggested solution**:

```diff
   <id>kanban</id>
-  <title>kanban</title>
+  <title>Kanban (Terminal Kanban Board + MCP)</title>
```

Alternate phrasings worth considering: `Kanban - Terminal Kanban Board`, `Kanban TUI`, `Kanban (Lazygit-inspired Kanban Board)`. Pick whichever lands most cleanly alongside the existing `<summary>` (`Fast, keyboard-driven terminal kanban board (with MCP server)`).

---

### Considerations

- The fix is metadata-only. No binary or behaviour change.
- Ships in the next normal release (0.7.3 or whenever). The 0.7.2 nupkg already in moderation does not require a same-version re-push: the maintainer "repush with the same version" instruction only applies to flagged **Requirements**, and 0.7.2 had no Requirements flagged (Guidelines only). Per the moderation notice: "only Requirements will hold up a package version from approval."
- The Chocolatey validator should stop flagging this Guideline once the title differs from the id.
- `<title>` is also surfaced in the Chocolatey GUI client and in Windows package-management telemetry, so something readable is preferable.

**Pros**: Single-line change. Clears the second of two outstanding moderation Guidelines.
**Cons**: Subjective on exact phrasing; needs a one-shot picking decision.

---

### Alternative solutions

Leave the title as `kanban`. Rejected: the validator continues to flag this on every future submission, and the package-page title is the first thing a human browsing the Chocolatey feed sees. `kanban` alone is less informative than a short descriptor.
cards.title: use descriptive nuspec title distinct from id

cards.description:
### Overview

**Where**: `crates/kanban-persistence/src/watch/file_watcher.rs` — the own-write suppression mechanism in `FileWatcher`.
**Why**: The counter-based suppression assumes a bounded number of FS events per atomic rename (`store(2)`), which is false on macOS FSEvents; the test suite fails deterministically on Darwin, blocking the nixpkgs init PR and therefore the release.
**How**: Replace the event counter with a time-window suppression (`suppress_until_ms`), so the whole FSEvents burst from an own-write is suppressed regardless of how many events fire.

---

### Engineering detail

**Datapath**: TUI saves the board → `app/mod.rs:401` / `:2063` call `watcher.suppress_next_event()` → watcher arms suppression → notify/FSEvents fires events for the watched path → handler closure (`file_watcher.rs:~121`) checks suppression and drops own-write events → external edits pass through to the change channel.

**Offending code**:
```
file_watcher.rs:6    use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};
file_watcher.rs:37   suppress_remaining: Arc<AtomicUsize>,
file_watcher.rs:64   // "Using 2 is conservative — Linux fires only 1 event per rename."
file_watcher.rs:67-68  pub fn suppress_next_event(&self) { self.suppress_remaining.store(2, ...) }
file_watcher.rs:121  let suppressed = suppress_remaining_clone.fetch_update(... checked_sub(1) ...)
```
On macOS a single atomic rename can fire 3+ matching events. Events 1-2 decrement 2→0; event 3 hits `checked_sub(0) → None`, is not suppressed, and reaches the channel. `test_own_write_decrements_suppress_counter` (file_watcher.rs:317) catches this. Reproduced bare-metal on Darwin:
`cargo test --release -p kanban-persistence --lib watch::file_watcher`.

**Suggested solution** (TDD: tests commit first, then impl):
```
- AtomicUsize -> AtomicI64; field suppress_remaining -> suppress_until_ms (init 0).
- const SUPPRESS_WINDOW_MS: i64 = 500;
- suppress_next_event(): store(now_ms + SUPPRESS_WINDOW_MS).
- handler: if now_ms < suppress_until_ms -> drop event (suppressed), else deliver.
- replace #[doc(hidden)] suppress_remaining()->usize with is_suppression_active()->bool.
- rename both closure bindings (lines 84, 96) consistently.
```
`chrono::Utc::now().timestamp_millis()` is already used across the codebase, so no new dependency.

**Blast radius**:
```
crates/kanban-tui/src/app/mod.rs:401, :2063  — call suppress_next_event() (name/signature unchanged, OK)
crates/kanban-tui/src/state/mod.rs:194       — calls suppress_remaining() (test) -> update to is_suppression_active()
file_watcher.rs tests (~300-360)             — three suppress tests rewritten to window semantics
```

---

### Considerations

- Mandatory TDD per CLAUDE.md: Red (tests) and Green (impl) are **separate commits**; present failing tests before implementing. `test(persistence): ...` then `fix(persistence): ...`.
- Keep `suppress_next_event()` name/signature stable; only the test-only API renames.
- Keep window at 500 ms (FSEvents latency under sandbox/load); do not shrink to speed up tests.
- Use `AtomicI64` millis-since-epoch (lock-free, no panics) rather than `Mutex<Instant>`.
- Do not touch the lenient `test_file_watcher_detects_*` tests.

**Pros**: Robust against unbounded FSEvents bursts; matches the "suppression window" contract already described in `app/mod.rs:398-399`.
**Cons**: A genuine external edit within 500 ms of an own-write is also suppressed (acceptable: saves are user-driven and already debounced at 500 ms).

---

### Alternative solutions

- Bump the counter to 5: still unbounded in theory, doesn't fix the assumption, wouldn't satisfy the test without relaxing it.
- `#[cfg_attr(target_os="macos", ignore)]` or Nix-side `doCheck=false`: masks a real defect from macOS users; rejected.

---

### Release / packaging follow-up

- v0.7.2 tag is already cut and cannot be unmade; after merge, cut **v0.7.3** and retarget nixpkgs PR #530712 (bump version, tarball hash, cargoHash).
- Related: see the Darwin CI card (this bug shipped silently because CI has no macOS runner).
cards.title: replace file-watcher own-write suppression counter with time window for macos fsevents

cards.description:
### Overview

**Where**: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — the test matrix.
**Why**: CI runs only `ubuntu-latest` and `windows-latest`, so no test has ever run on macOS; a deterministic Darwin-only file-watcher bug (FSEvents) shipped silently in every release and was only caught when nixpkgs built on macOS. Without a macOS runner this class of bug stays invisible until a downstream packager hits it.
**How**: Add a macOS runner (`macos-latest`, Apple Silicon) to the CI job matrix so `cargo test --workspace` runs on Darwin on every PR.

---

### Engineering detail

**Current state**: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` matrix = { ubuntu-latest, windows-latest }. No Darwin coverage.

**Suggested solution**:
```
- Add macos-latest to the test job's runner matrix (GitHub-hosted, arm64).
- Run the full suite: cargo test --workspace (fmt + clippy can stay Linux-only or also run).
- Ensure FSEvents-dependent tests in kanban-persistence run there
  (watch::file_watcher), since that is the path that was silently broken.
```

**Considerations**:
- GitHub-hosted macOS runners cost more minutes than Linux; scope to `cargo test --workspace` (skip duplicating fmt/clippy if minutes are a concern).
- Some watcher tests are timing-sensitive (FSEvents latency); the time-window suppression fix (card KAN-679) should land first or alongside, or macOS CI will be red on arrival.
- Confirm the toolchain/Nix setup used in CI is available on macOS runners, or use rustup directly on the macOS leg.

**Pros**: Catches platform-specific (FSEvents, path, line-ending) regressions before release instead of at the packaging stage.
**Cons**: Higher CI minute cost and a slower overall CI wall-clock.

---

### Dependencies

- Pairs with **KAN-679** (file-watcher FSEvents fix). Land the fix first so the new macOS leg is green when introduced.
cards.title: add macos (darwin) ci runner to catch platform-specific test failures

cards.description:
### Overview

**Where**: `crates/kanban-persistence/src/watch/file_watcher.rs` (entire file in scope, ~430 lines), with one external test-API caller at `crates/kanban-tui/src/state/mod.rs:185-198`.

**Why**: The counter-based "own-write" suppression in `FileWatcher` fails deterministically on macOS / Darwin (FSEvents), which is blocking the nixpkgs init PR for kanban (https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/pull/530712) and consequently the next release. The test `test_own_write_decrements_suppress_counter` at `file_watcher.rs:317` correctly catches the bug: a single atomic rename on macOS fires 3+ matching FSEvents (Create + Modify + Rename, sometimes coalesced, sometimes not, plus extra delivery under sandbox/load), but `suppress_next_event` only arms a counter of 2.

This has shipped silently in every release to date because `.github/workflows/ci.yml` only has `ubuntu-latest` and `windows-latest` runners — no macOS CI. nixpkgs is the first time the test suite has ever run on Darwin. (Worth a follow-up ticket to add a macOS CI runner.)

**How**: Replace the counter with a time-window mechanism. Lock-free `AtomicI64` storing `suppress_until_ms` (millis-since-epoch). The handler suppresses any matching event while `now() < suppress_until_ms`. A 500ms window is generous enough for FSEvents bursts under sandbox/load and short enough that external edits within that window of an own-save are a non-issue in practice (saves are user-driven and already debounced at 500ms).

---

### Engineering detail

**Offending code** (`crates/kanban-persistence/src/watch/file_watcher.rs:67-70`):

```rust
pub fn suppress_next_event(&self) {
    self.suppress_remaining.store(2, Ordering::SeqCst);
}
```

The comment at `:60-66` says: *"Using 2 is conservative — Linux fires only 1 event per rename."* Wrong on FSEvents. The handler at `:120-131` decrements once per matching event; events 1 and 2 decrement to 0; event 3 hits `checked_sub(0) -> None` and is delivered.

**Reproduction (bare macOS, outside Nix sandbox)**:

```bash
cargo test --release -p kanban-persistence --lib watch::file_watcher
```

→ `test_own_write_decrements_suppress_counter ... FAILED` every run. Same failure as the Nix build of nixpkgs PR #530712.

**Why time-window, not "counter = 5"**: FSEvents doesn't bound how many events fire per write — it's a coalescing, latency-tunable stream. Any fixed counter is a guess. A window catches the entire burst regardless of count. The comment at `crates/kanban-tui/src/app/mod.rs:398-399` already calls the contract a "suppression window" — the author was thinking window all along, just implemented it as a counter.

**API compatibility**:
- `suppress_next_event()` — public, two callers at `crates/kanban-tui/src/app/mod.rs:401` and `:2063`. Name and signature stay the same; semantics unchanged ("arm suppression for the upcoming own-write").
- `suppress_remaining() -> usize` — `#[doc(hidden)]`, test-only. One external caller at `crates/kanban-tui/src/state/mod.rs:194`. **Rename to `is_suppression_active() -> bool`**; update the one caller.

**Suggested solution** (Green step):

```rust
const SUPPRESS_WINDOW_MS: i64 = 500;

// field
suppress_until_ms: Arc<AtomicI64>,

pub fn suppress_next_event(&self) {
    let until = chrono::Utc::now().timestamp_millis() + SUPPRESS_WINDOW_MS;
    self.suppress_until_ms.store(until, Ordering::SeqCst);
    tracing::debug!("File watcher suppress window armed for {} ms", SUPPRESS_WINDOW_MS);
}

#[doc(hidden)]
pub fn is_suppression_active(&self) -> bool {
    chrono::Utc::now().timestamp_millis() < self.suppress_until_ms.load(Ordering::SeqCst)
}

// handler (~:120-131) replaces the fetch_update block:
let now = chrono::Utc::now().timestamp_millis();
let until = suppress_until_ms_clone.load(Ordering::SeqCst);
if now < until {
    tracing::debug!(
        "Own-write event suppressed (within window): kind={:?}, path={}",
        event.kind, watch_path.display()
    );
    return;
}
```

Rename the cloned bindings at `:84` and `:96` (`suppress_remaining` → `suppress_until_ms`) consistently. Update the doc block at `:60-66` to describe a window, not a counter.

**TDD test rewrites** (Red step, in `mod tests` starting at `:209`):

| Replace | With |
|---|---|
| `test_suppress_next_event_sets_counter` (`:303`) | `test_suppress_next_event_opens_window` — assert `!is_suppression_active()` before, `is_suppression_active()` immediately after, `!is_suppression_active()` after `sleep(SUPPRESS_WINDOW + 100ms)`. |
| `test_own_write_decrements_suppress_counter` (`:317`) | `test_own_write_within_window_is_suppressed` — same flow, drop the counter assertion at `:340-343`. Only assert `rx.try_recv().is_err()` after the 150ms sleep. |
| `test_external_write_delivered_after_counter_exhausted` (`:358`) | `test_external_write_after_window_is_delivered` — extend `sleep` between own-write and external write to `SUPPRESS_WINDOW + 200ms`. |

Plus `crates/kanban-tui/src/state/mod.rs:185-198`: keep the test name `test_queue_flush_does_not_open_suppress_window`, change assertion to `assert!(!watcher.is_suppression_active(), "queue_flush must not open the suppress window");`.

---

### Considerations

- **Mandatory TDD** per `CLAUDE.md` Red → Green → Refactor. Present failing tests to the user before implementing. Tests and impl in separate commits.
- **Commit convention**: `<type>(<crate>): <description>`, scope drops `kanban-` prefix. So `test(persistence): switch file-watcher suppression to time window` then `fix(persistence): replace own-write suppression counter with time window`.
- **Atomic choice**: `AtomicI64` not `Mutex<Instant>` — lock-free, no panics, no allocation. `chrono::Utc::now().timestamp_millis()` is already used throughout the codebase (e.g. card sprint logs). `i64` millis-since-epoch covers >290M years.
- **Don't shrink the window to 250ms** to speed tests up. 500ms is the right value for FSEvents latency under sandbox/load. Eat the ~700ms test-suite cost.
- **Production impact today**: not data-corrupting — a leaked own-event causes a redundant self-reload. The test enforces the stronger invariant. Fix improves robustness; isn't fixing a corruption bug.
- **The lenient tests** at `:216` (`test_file_watcher_detects_direct_writes`) and `:257` (`test_file_watcher_detects_atomic_writes`) use `if let Ok(Ok(event)) = result` and silently pass if no event arrives. They're already lenient on macOS, leave them alone.
- **Test return-type convention**: existing watcher tests use `#[tokio::test]` with panic-style asserts because they're integration-y. Keep the existing pattern, don't restructure to `-> KanbanResult<()>`.
- **Verify on Darwin** (the user's local env is `darwin 25.5.0`, aarch64). CI alone is not sufficient because there is no macOS runner.
- **Post-merge release**: cut v0.7.3 via the existing release workflow. v0.7.2 tag is already cut and can't be unmade. After release, bump nixpkgs PR #530712 to `version = "0.7.3"` with new tarball `hash` and new `cargoHash`.

**Pros**: Lock-free, deterministic across platforms, no new dependency. Survives whatever event coalescing FSEvents decides to do today or tomorrow.
**Cons**: External writes within 500ms of an own-save are suppressed (acceptable: saves are user-driven, debounced at 500ms already, and an external edit racing a save is itself an edge case where the user is about to lose work either way).

---

### Alternative solutions

1. **Bump the counter to 5 (or 10)**: cheapest possible patch. Rejected: FSEvents has no documented upper bound on coalesced events per write. Any number is a guess that'll fail again under different sandbox/IO load.

2. **Use a `Mutex<Instant>`** instead of `AtomicI64`: equivalent semantics. Rejected: introduces lock contention on the hot path (event handler) and risk of poisoning, with no benefit over the atomic.

3. **Disable the test on macOS with `#[cfg(not(target_os = \"macos\"))]`**: makes CI green without fixing the bug. Rejected: the bug is real and nixpkgs is hitting it. Disabling the test hides the failure on Darwin without addressing it.

4. **Match-by-modification-time on the file**: compare event timestamp to last own-write mtime. Rejected: needs a syscall per event for `stat`, and FS mtime resolution varies (some FSes are second-granular). Pure-memory atomic comparison is cheaper and more reliable.
cards.title: fix file watcher own-write suppression on macos fsevents

**After KAN-689 + KAN-697 + KAN-742:**
  KAN-702  feat(service): StoreManager URL detection, http feature flag
  KAN-703  test(server): TestServer in-process harness

**After KAN-697 + KAN-701 + KAN-710:**
  KAN-700  feat(http-backend): KanbanBackend lifecycle methods

**After KAN-702:**
  KAN-705  feat(cli): URL locators in CLI and MCP

**After server read routes (parallel):**
  KAN-726  feat(http-backend): board + column DataStore reads   [needs KAN-716 + KAN-718]
  KAN-727  feat(http-backend): card DataStore reads             [needs KAN-720]
  KAN-734  feat(http-backend): archived card, sprint, graph reads  [needs KAN-724]

**After KAN-703 (parallel, additional deps noted):**
  KAN-738  test: undo/redo                                      [also: KAN-695]
  KAN-739  test: cascades and audit log                         [also: KAN-699]
  KAN-737  test: dependency graph                               [also: KAN-722 + KAN-723]
  KAN-735  test: board/column/card ops                          [also: KAN-721 + KAN-722 + KAN-726 + KAN-727]
  KAN-736  test: sprint lifecycle                               [also: KAN-725 + KAN-734]

---

### Problem and stakeholders

Today every user of this tool must run it on the same machine as the data file. A team sharing a board must either keep the file on a shared network drive (which breaks SQLite and causes JSON write conflicts) or pass the file around manually. There is no way for two people to have the board open at the same time without risking data loss.

This work makes the tool usable by teams: a single server holds the board, multiple clients (TUI, CLI, MCP) connect to it over HTTP, and every client sees changes from other clients in real time without polling.

Concrete scenarios this unlocks:
- A team lead and a developer both have the TUI open; one moves a card, the other sees it within seconds
- An MCP-connected AI assistant creates cards from a different machine than the one running the TUI
- A CI job closes cards via the CLI while a human is editing descriptions in the TUI

---

### Architecture: five crates, two phases

**Phase 0 — observability foundation (must precede Phase 2)**

Distributed systems require identity and traceability in the wire types from day one. Adding them later means versioning the API or making them optional, which undermines auditability.

- `ClientId(Uuid)` newtype in `kanban-core` — typed identity for every connected client
- `CommandEnvelope { command, correlation_id: Uuid, issued_by: ClientId, timestamp }` in `kanban-domain` — wraps every command from its origin through to the audit log
- Extended `ChangeEventFrame { writer_instance_id, detected_at, correlation_id, issued_by }` — WebSocket push frames carry full provenance
- Structured tracing spans on `KanbanContext::execute/undo/redo` emitting `correlation_id` and `issued_by`
- `HealthStatus` trait + `GET /health` endpoint — liveness signal for the server
- `MetricsCollector` trait + `GET /metrics` Prometheus endpoint — command rates, latency histograms, active connections

**Phase 1 — seam loosening (pure refactor, no behaviour change)**

The TUI is currently hardcoded to construct a `FileWatcher` on startup. An HTTP backend needs a `WebSocketChangeDetector` in the same slot. Three small changes loosen the seam without touching any existing behaviour:
- Add `suppress_next_write()` default no-op to `ChangeDetector` trait
- Change `SaveCoordinator` to hold `Arc<dyn ChangeDetector>` instead of `Arc<FileWatcher>`
- Add `change_detector() -> Option<Arc<dyn ChangeDetector>>` to `KanbanBackend`; `JsonDataStore` constructs and owns its `FileWatcher` internally and returns it here; TUI startup uses whatever the backend provides

**Phase 2 — kanban-api crate (wire contract)**

A new library crate `kanban-api` with no dependency above `kanban-domain`. Contains only:
- Request input types (where client-send shape differs from domain type: Create*/Update* requests)
- `ApiError { code, message }` — HTTP error envelope
- `ChangeEventFrame` — WebSocket push frame shape
- URL versioning: `/v1/`

Responses use domain types from `kanban-domain` directly (they already derive Serialize/Deserialize and are the stable boundary). Sprint names are free-form strings in the API; the server translates to/from `name_index` internally.

**Phase 3 — kanban-server crate (HTTP server)**

Axum binary. `AppState { ctx: Arc<RwLock<KanbanContext>>, instance_id: Uuid, event_tx: broadcast::Sender<ChangeEventFrame> }`. RwLock, not Mutex: read-only GET handlers acquire `.read()` for concurrency; write handlers acquire `.write()`. All routes use a shared `AppError(KanbanError)` implementing `IntoResponse` with a canonical status-code mapping. On every successful mutation, broadcast a `ChangeEventFrame` via `event_tx`. Routes: full CRUD for boards, columns, cards, sprints; POST `/v1/commands` for batch execution; GET `/v1/ws` for WebSocket change stream.

**Phase 4 — kanban-http-backend crate (HTTP client backend)**

Library crate implementing `KanbanBackend + DataStore + CommandStore` over HTTP. `HttpBackend` holds a `reqwest::Client`, `base_url`, and `instance_id`. Key decisions: `DataStore` and `CommandStore` are synchronous traits; use `tokio::task::block_in_place` for HTTP calls from sync context. `with_transaction()` returns `Err(Unsupported)` — the server provides atomicity per `POST /v1/commands` batch, not client-side. `WebSocketChangeDetector` connects to `/v1/ws`, filters own-instance frames, broadcasts `ChangeEvent` to local subscribers.

**Phase 5 — integration tests**

The existing `kanban-service` integration test suite (~100 tests across 27 files) is parameterized to run against `HttpBackend` via an in-process `TestServer` harness. Tests that check filesystem-specific behaviour are annotated `#[ignore]`. `CommandStore::load_commands` returns `Err(Unsupported)` on HTTP (append-only; reads are a future route).

---

### Datapath

```
Current (local):
  TUI / CLI / MCP
    -> KanbanContext
    -> Arc<dyn KanbanBackend>  (JsonDataStore | SqliteBackend)
    -> PersistenceStore        (file / WAL I/O)

Proposed (HTTP client):
  TUI / CLI / MCP
    -> KanbanContext           (unchanged)
    -> Arc<dyn KanbanBackend>  (unchanged interface)
    -> HttpBackend             (new, kanban-http-backend)
       -> reqwest::Client
          -> kanban-server     (new binary, kanban-server)
             -> KanbanContext  (server-side, same domain)
             -> JsonDataStore | SqliteBackend
```

No changes to `KanbanContext`, TUI command dispatch, CLI/MCP entry points, or any existing tests against local backends.

---

### Resolved design decisions

| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
|----------|--------|-----------|
| AppState locking | `Arc<RwLock<KanbanContext>>` | GETs acquire `.read()` concurrently; Mutex would serialise all traffic |
| `with_transaction` on HTTP | `Err(Unsupported)` | Default snapshot+restore downloads entire board twice; server atomicity per batch is sufficient |
| Response wire format | Domain types directly (`Board`, `Card`, etc.) | Already Serialize/Deserialize; stable boundary; no translation layer needed |
| kanban-api → kanban-domain | Direct dependency allowed | kanban-domain has no upstream workspace deps; no cycle |
| Sprint name in API | Free-form string | Server translates to/from `name_index`; clients never see the internal index |
| FileWatcher ownership | JsonDataStore constructs and owns it | Keeps backend self-contained; removes FileWatcher construction from App startup |
| HttpBackend `CommandStore` reads | `Err(Unsupported)` | HTTP backend is append-only; `load_commands` / `load_all_commands` are a future route |

---

### Intentionally out of scope

- **Authentication**: URL can encode a bearer token or `--server-token` flag; scoped to a follow-up card once the core transport works
- **Graph relation routes** (`blocks`, `spawns`, `relates`): KanbanContext methods exist; routes deferred to a follow-up
- **Export/import routes**: Deferred
- **Per-board locking**: `Arc<RwLock<KanbanContext>>` is a global write lock; acceptable at team scale; per-board locks are a future optimisation

cards.description:
> VERIFY FIX: AppState.ctx is `Arc<tokio::sync::RwLock<KanbanContext>>` (NOT Mutex) — the epic's resolved-decisions table mandates RwLock so GETs acquire `.read()` concurrently; writes `.write()`. Also: DROP the http-feature-flag language — kanban-server is a separate binary with no feature gate, and there is no `http` feature (KAN-702 decision).

Scaffold the axum transport for `kanban-server`: a `Router`, shared `AppState`, the `/health` endpoint, and a TCP listener that `main` binds. This is the binding all route cards (KAN-716/717/718/719/…) attach to — until it exists there is no HTTP surface, only the typed handler seams.

## Context / why
Epic: **KAN-684** (add http collaborative backend: kanban-server crate + HttpBackend). The factory (KAN-742/792/794/796/798 rerun) already delivered the **typed create seams** and the **v1 wire DTOs** in `kanban-service`. What is still missing is the transport: there is no `Router`, no `AppState`, no listener. This card adds exactly that, with no per-entity routes (those are KAN-716+). Test harness is **KAN-703** and depends on this card.

## Current state (worktree: develop + factory)
- `crates/kanban-server/src/main.rs:1` — `fn main() {}` (empty stub).
- `crates/kanban-server/src/lib.rs:1` — declares only `pub mod handlers { boards; cards; columns; sprints; }`. No `app`/`state`/`error`/`routes` modules yet.
- `crates/kanban-server/Cargo.toml` — already a workspace member (`Cargo.toml:13`) with deps wired: `axum 0.8`, `tokio (full)`, `tower`, `tower-http`, `uuid`, `serde`, `serde_json`, `tracing`, `tracing-subscriber`, `prometheus`, and `kanban-core`/`kanban-domain`/`kanban-service`. Dev-deps: `reqwest`, `tempfile`, `kanban-persistence-json`. No new deps needed.
- Handler seams exist and are tested but unbound: `handlers::boards::create_or_replace_board(ctx, req) -> Result<(BoardResponse, bool), ApiError>` (`handlers/boards.rs:20`); `handlers::columns::{create_column, create_or_replace_column}` (`handlers/columns.rs:20,39`).
- Service constructor: `KanbanContext::open_deferred(backend: Arc<dyn KanbanBackend>, config: AppConfig) -> Self` (`kanban-service/src/context/core.rs:14`) — zero-I/O, sync. `save()`/`reload()` are `async` (`context/persistence.rs:47,56`).
- `kanban_core::ClientId` exists (`kanban-core/src/client_id.rs:7`) with `::new()`/`::nil()`. `ChangeEventFrame` exists (`kanban-service/src/api/v1/events.rs`, re-exported `kanban_service::api::ChangeEventFrame`). **No broadcast channel is wired anywhere yet** (grep: only the type exists).

## Target

### Module layout (new files under `crates/kanban-server/src/`)
- `state.rs` — `AppState`.
- `app.rs` — `pub fn router(state: AppState) -> axum::Router` and the `/health` handler.
- `error.rs` — `AppError` (KAN-743; may land in this card or its own — see Dependencies).
- update `lib.rs` to add `pub mod state; pub mod app; pub mod error;` (keep `handlers`).

### AppState (`state.rs`)
```rust
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct AppState {
    pub ctx: Arc<Mutex<KanbanContext>>,           // see note on Mutex vs RwLock
    pub instance_id: Uuid,                          // minted once at startup
    pub event_tx: tokio::sync::broadcast::Sender<ChangeEventFrame>,
}
```
- `ctx` is `Arc<tokio::sync::Mutex<KanbanContext>>`. NOTE: the original card text said `Arc<RwLock<…>>` with read routes taking `.read()`. That is **not viable as written**: `KanbanContext`'s reads go through `KanbanOperations` (`&self`) but `save()` is `async` and writes take `&mut self`; mixing an `async` write path under a sync `RwLock` write guard held across an `.await` is a deadlock/`Send` hazard. Use `tokio::sync::Mutex<KanbanContext>` (async-aware, one lock kind for both read and write handlers) and document the choice. The parent epic only needs *a* shared, lock-guarded context; the read/write-concurrency optimization is explicitly out of scope for the scaffold.
- `instance_id`: `Uuid::new_v4()` minted once in `main`, stable for process lifetime; surfaced by `/health` and stamped onto future `ChangeEventFrame`s.
- `event_tx`: `broadcast::channel::<ChangeEventFrame>(capacity).0`. This field is created here so write routes (KAN-717/719) and the SSE endpoint (later epic card) have a sender to clone. **No route broadcasts in this card** — the channel is plumbed but unused until the write cards. `#[derive(Clone)]` is required because axum clones `AppState` per request; `Arc`, `Uuid`, and `broadcast::Sender` are all `Clone`.

### Router (`app.rs`)
```rust
pub fn router(state: AppState) -> Router {
    Router::new()
        .route("/health", get(health))
        .with_state(state)
}
```
- Optionally layer `tower_http::trace::TraceLayer::new_for_http()` (dep already present). Entity routes are added by later cards via `.merge(...)`/`.nest(...)` — keep `router()` the single composition point so KAN-716+ extend it rather than building their own `Router`.

### /health handler
- `async fn health(State(state): State<AppState>) -> Json<serde_json::Value>` returning `200 OK` with body `{ "status": "ok", "instance_id": "<uuid>" }` (use `state.instance_id.to_string()`). Define a small typed `HealthResponse { status: &'static str, instance_id: Uuid }` (Serialize) rather than an ad-hoc `json!` if you prefer a stable shape; either satisfies KAN-703's `test_health_endpoint_returns_ok`.

### Listener + main (`main.rs`)
```rust
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()> { // or hand-rolled Result/eprintln; avoid adding anyhow if not desired
    tracing_subscriber::fmt::init();
    let backend = /* build KanbanBackend from a path/registry */;
    let ctx = KanbanContext::open_deferred(backend, AppConfig::default());
    let (event_tx, _) = tokio::sync::broadcast::channel(256);
    let state = AppState { ctx: Arc::new(Mutex::new(ctx)), instance_id: Uuid::new_v4(), event_tx };
    let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").await?; // configurable addr later
    tracing::info!(addr = %listener.local_addr()?, "kanban-server listening");
    axum::serve(listener, app::router(state)).await?;
    Ok(())
}
```
- Bind address / backend selection can be a constant for now (a config/CLI card is separate). The point is a runnable binary that serves `/health`. The `_` receiver on the channel keeps the sender alive with zero initial subscribers (fine — `send` to no subscribers is a no-op).

### HTTP feature flag
- The original card mentions "Add HTTP feature flag to root Cargo.toml for conditional compilation of http-backend." That concerns the **http_backend module inside `kanban-service`** (per the project decision that backends are service modules, not crates), not `kanban-server` itself. `kanban-server` is an always-built workspace member. If a feature gate is still wanted for the service-side `HttpBackend`, track it on the relevant http_backend card, not here — note this on the card to avoid scope creep.

## Step-by-step TDD (Red → Green → Refactor)
1. **Red**: in `crates/kanban-server/tests/health.rs`, write `test_health_route_returns_ok_with_instance_id` that builds an `AppState` over an in-memory/tempfile `KanbanContext`, calls `app::router(state)`, and drives it with `tower::ServiceExt::oneshot` (`Request::get("/health")`); assert `StatusCode::OK` and that the JSON body has `status == "ok"` and `instance_id` parses as a `Uuid`. Add `test_router_unknown_path_returns_404`. (KAN-703 adds the real network harness; this card can prove the router with `oneshot` and no socket.)
2. **Green**: add `state.rs`, `app.rs`, the `health` handler, and `lib.rs` module decls until the test compiles and passes.
3. **Green**: flesh out `main.rs` to bind a listener and `axum::serve`; a `cargo run -p kanban-server` smoke check confirms it listens.
4. **Refactor**: extract `HealthResponse`, ensure `router()` is the single composition seam, document the Mutex-not-RwLock decision in a doc comment on `AppState`.

## Tests (named)
- `test_health_route_returns_ok_with_instance_id` — oneshot GET /health → 200, body shape.
- `test_health_instance_id_is_stable_across_requests` — two oneshots on the same `AppState` return the same `instance_id`.
- `test_router_unknown_path_returns_404`.
- (KAN-703 owns the network-level `test_health_endpoint_returns_ok` via `TestServer`.)

## Acceptance criteria
- `app::router(AppState)` exists and is the single Router composition point.
- `AppState { ctx: Arc<Mutex<KanbanContext>>, instance_id: Uuid, event_tx: broadcast::Sender<ChangeEventFrame> }`, `#[derive(Clone)]`.
- `GET /health` → 200 `{ "status": "ok", "instance_id": <uuid> }`.
- `main` binds a `TcpListener` and runs `axum::serve`; `cargo run -p kanban-server` listens.
- Mutex-vs-RwLock deviation from the old text is documented on `AppState`.
- All new tests green; `cargo test -p kanban-server` passes.

## Dependencies
- **Blocks** every route card: KAN-716, 717, 718, 719 (and the rest of the v1 surface) attach to `router()`/`AppState`.
- **Blocks** KAN-703 (test harness wraps this `AppState` + `router`).
- **KAN-743** (`AppError` IntoResponse) must land in this card or immediately after it, before any route card — handler results are `Result<_, ApiError>` and need the axum wrapper. Recommend folding KAN-743 into this scaffold.
- Uses factory output: `kanban_service::api::ChangeEventFrame`, `KanbanContext::open_deferred`, `kanban_core::ClientId`.

cards.description:
## Context / why

Part of KAN-684. This is the **primary write path** for `HttpBackend`: rather than fan out across per-entity REST routes, all client mutations flow through one batch endpoint that maps directly onto `KanbanContext::execute(Vec<Command>)` — the same transactional, undo-capturing, audit-logging path the TUI/CLI use locally. The individual REST routes (KAN-716..725) are convenience wrappers for humans and tooling; this is the machine path. It backs "feat(http-backend): implement CommandStore for HttpBackend".

## Current state

No `commands` handler or router. The transactional execute path is fully built:
- `KanbanContext::execute(&mut self, commands: Vec<Command>) -> KanbanResult<()>` — `crates/kanban-service/src/context/undo.rs:17`. Runs all commands inside one `backend.with_transaction` (all-or-nothing), captures per-command inverses for undo, and appends one `CommandBatch` to the audit log (`undo.rs:31`). On any command error the transaction rolls back and `execute` returns `Err` — exactly the `with_transaction` semantics this card needs.
- `Command` is `kanban_domain::commands::Command` (`crates/kanban-domain/src/commands/mod.rs:23`), already `Serialize`/`Deserialize` across all variants (Board/Column/Card/Sprint/…).
- `CommandBatch` (`crates/kanban-domain/src/command_batch.rs:10`) is the audit/wire wrapper `{ commands, correlation_id, issued_by, timestamp, app_type, app_version, session_id }`, with `wrap(commands, ClientId)` and `From<Vec<Command>>` constructors. `execute` builds its own batch internally from the supplied `Vec<Command>` (`undo.rs:30`), so the endpoint can accept either a bare `Vec<Command>` or a full `CommandBatch` and pass `batch.commands` through.

`AppState { ctx: Arc<RwLock<KanbanContext>>, instance_id, event_tx }` and `ChangeEventFrame::now(...)` (`api/v1/events.rs:45`) come from KAN-689.

## Target

Route (top-level, not board-nested — a batch may span boards):
```
POST /v1/commands   <- CommandBatch (or Vec<Command>)   -> 200 { "executed": <usize> }
```

Accept a JSON `CommandBatch` (preferred — it carries `correlation_id`/`issued_by` provenance from the client, KAN-729/751) and fall back to a bare array. Define the response:
```rust
#[derive(Serialize)]
struct BatchResult { executed: usize }
```

Handler signature:
```rust
async fn execute_commands(
    State(state): State<AppState>,
    Json(batch): Json<CommandBatch>,
) -> Result<Json<BatchResult>, AppError>
```

Flow:
1. `let mut ctx = state.ctx.write().await;` (batch is a write — exclusive lock).
2. `let n = batch.commands.len();`
3. `ctx.execute(batch.commands)?;` — `with_transaction` gives per-batch atomicity: the entire `Vec<Command>` commits or the whole thing rolls back. On any command error, `execute` returns `Err`, the `?` propagates to `AppError` (no partial commit, **no broadcast**).
4. On success, broadcast once: `let _ = state.event_tx.send(ChangeEventFrame::now(state.instance_id, batch.correlation_id, batch.issued_by));` — one frame per batch (not per command), carrying the batch's provenance so SSE subscribers (KAN-696) and own-write filtering (KAN-749) work.
5. `Ok(Json(BatchResult { executed: n }))`.

DTO in: `CommandBatch` (domain wire type). Service called: `KanbanContext::execute`. DTO out: `BatchResult { executed }`. Note: `with_transaction` atomicity is the server's responsibility per batch — the `HttpBackend` client returns `Unsupported` for its own `with_transaction` (KAN-684 design table) precisely because the server provides it here.

Errors via `AppError`: any `KanbanError` from a command (NotFound 404, WipLimitExceeded 409, Validation 422, dependency cycles 409, etc.) maps through `ApiError::from(&KanbanError)` (`api/v1/error_mapping.rs:8`). A malformed batch body → axum `JsonRejection` → 400/422.

## Step-by-step (TDD)

1. **Red**: `crates/kanban-server/tests/commands_endpoint.rs` — seed a board+column, POST a `CommandBatch` of `[CreateCard, CreateCard]`, assert 200 + `{"executed":2}` and both cards present via a read route. POST a batch whose 2nd command is invalid (e.g. move to a nonexistent column), assert error status **and** that the 1st command did NOT persist (rollback). Assert exactly one broadcast frame for the successful batch carrying the batch `correlation_id`.
2. **Green**: add `execute_commands` + `BatchResult`; register `POST /v1/commands`.
3. **Refactor**: reuse the shared `broadcast` helper; keep the handler thin.

## Tests (axum integration, `crates/kanban-server/tests/commands_endpoint.rs`)

- `test_post_commands_executes_batch_returns_executed_count`
- `test_post_commands_is_atomic_partial_failure_rolls_back_whole_batch`
- `test_post_commands_broadcasts_one_frame_per_batch_with_correlation_id`
- `test_post_commands_invalid_command_maps_to_error_status`
- `test_post_commands_malformed_body_returns_4xx`

## Acceptance

- A valid batch executes via `KanbanContext::execute` and returns `{ executed: N }`.
- A batch with any failing command rolls back entirely (no partial writes) and does not broadcast.
- Exactly one `ChangeEventFrame` per successful batch, carrying the batch's `correlation_id`/`issued_by`.
- `cargo test -p kanban-server` green.

## Dependencies

- KAN-689 (router + `AppState.event_tx`/`instance_id`), KAN-743 (`AppError`), KAN-729 (`CommandBatch` provenance fields — delivered).
- Unblocks the `HttpBackend` `CommandStore` impl (KAN-699) and KAN-738 (undo/redo over HTTP).

cards.description:
## Context / why

Part of KAN-684. Real-time collaboration: when one client mutates the board, every other connected client must see it within seconds without polling. Sprint-19 decision: the change-event transport is **SSE, not WebSocket** (simpler to implement and proxy; unidirectional server→client is sufficient). This supersedes the archived WebSocket endpoint and `WebSocketChangeDetector` (KAN-701). The client (`HttpBackend::subscribe_changes`, KAN-749) filters frames whose `writer_instance_id` matches its own `instance_id`, so a client never reacts to its own writes — replacing the `suppress_next_event()` counter used by `FileWatcher`.

## Current state

No events handler or router. The pieces are in place:
- `AppState.event_tx: broadcast::Sender<ChangeEventFrame>` (KAN-689) is the fan-out channel. Every write route (KAN-721/722/723/725) and the batch endpoint (KAN-695) already `event_tx.send(ChangeEventFrame::now(...))` on success — that is the **change-detection source** for this stream (server-side broadcast on successful mutation, not filesystem watching). The local `ChangeDetector`/`FileWatcher` plumbing (KAN-710, `crates/kanban-persistence/src/traits.rs:125`, `watch/file_watcher.rs`) stays for the *local* JSON backend and is not used by the server stream.
- `ChangeEventFrame` (`crates/kanban-service/src/api/v1/events.rs:19`) is `#[non_exhaustive]` and carries all four provenance fields:
  ```rust
  pub struct ChangeEventFrame {
      pub writer_instance_id: Uuid,
      pub detected_at: DateTime<Utc>,
      pub correlation_id: Uuid,
      pub issued_by: ClientId,   // kanban_core::ClientId
  }
  ```
  It is `Serialize`/`Deserialize` (snake_case) and `Clone` — safe to JSON-encode per `data:` event. The server crate already depends on `axum` with the `ws` feature and `tokio` (`crates/kanban-server/Cargo.toml:18`); SSE needs only `axum::response::sse` (in the base `axum` crate, no extra dep).

## Target

Route (board-scoped, matching the original card; a single global stream is also acceptable since frames carry full provenance, but keep the board path for symmetry and future per-board filtering):
```
GET /v1/boards/:board_id/events   -- text/event-stream (Server-Sent Events)
```
(The card body shows `/api/v1/boards/:id/events`; the rest of the server mounts under `/v1`, so use `/v1/boards/:board_id/events` for consistency unless KAN-689's root mounts an `/api` prefix.)

Handler signature:
```rust
async fn events(
    State(state): State<AppState>,
    Path(board_id): Path<Uuid>,
) -> Sse<impl Stream<Item = Result<Event, Infallible>>>
```

Flow:
1. On connection, subscribe: `let rx = state.event_tx.subscribe();`
2. Wrap the `broadcast::Receiver<ChangeEventFrame>` in a stream — `tokio_stream::wrappers::BroadcastStream::new(rx)` — and map each `Ok(frame)` to `Event::default().json_data(&frame)` (serializes the frame as the SSE `data:` payload). Drop `Lagged` errors (slow consumer) rather than terminating the stream.
3. Return `axum::response::Sse::new(stream).keep_alive(KeepAlive::new().interval(Duration::from_secs(15)))` so the connection survives idle periods and proxies.

Client filtering (KAN-749, downstream) discards frames where `frame.writer_instance_id == client.instance_id`; the server emits every frame to every subscriber and does no per-client filtering. On disconnect the `Receiver` is dropped and the broadcast channel reclaims the slot automatically.

DTO in: none (path only). Source: `AppState.event_tx` broadcast channel (populated by all write routes + KAN-695). DTO out: a stream of `ChangeEventFrame` JSON `data:` events. This is the only read route that holds a long-lived connection; it does not lock `ctx`.

Add `tokio-stream` (with `sync` feature for `BroadcastStream`) to `crates/kanban-server/Cargo.toml`.

## Step-by-step (TDD)

1. **Red**: `crates/kanban-server/tests/events_sse.rs` — start the server on a `TcpListener`, open `GET /v1/boards/:id/events` with `reqwest` (streaming body), then trigger a mutation via a write route / `POST /v1/commands` and assert the SSE stream yields one `data:` line that deserializes to a `ChangeEventFrame` whose `writer_instance_id == server.instance_id`. A second concurrent subscriber must also receive the frame (broadcast fan-out).
2. **Green**: add the `events` handler, the `BroadcastStream` mapping, and `KeepAlive`; register the route; add `tokio-stream` dep.
3. **Refactor**: extract the `frame → Event` mapping into a small testable fn; unit-test that it produces the expected `data:` JSON.

## Tests (axum integration, `crates/kanban-server/tests/events_sse.rs`)

- `test_sse_stream_emits_frame_on_mutation`
- `test_sse_frame_carries_writer_instance_id`
- `test_sse_two_subscribers_both_receive_frame`
- `test_sse_keep_alive_holds_connection_open` (assert the response is `text/event-stream` and stays open with no immediate EOF)
- unit: `test_change_event_frame_maps_to_sse_data_json`

## Acceptance

- A successful mutation anywhere on the server emits exactly one SSE `data:` frame to every connected subscriber.
- Each frame deserializes to `ChangeEventFrame` with all four provenance fields populated (`writer_instance_id == server.instance_id`, plus `correlation_id`/`issued_by` from the originating batch).
- `Content-Type: text/event-stream`; keep-alive comments hold idle connections open; disconnect drops the subscriber cleanly.
- `cargo test -p kanban-server` green.

## Dependencies

- KAN-689/KAN-750 (server scaffold; provides `AppState.event_tx` and `instance_id`).
- KAN-731 (extended `ChangeEventFrame` provenance — delivered).
- Change detection source is the server-side broadcast on successful mutation (every write route + KAN-695), i.e. KAN-710's local `ChangeDetector` is **not** the server stream's source.
- Unblocks KAN-749 (`KanbanContext::connect` + `HttpBackend` SSE subscription with own-instance filtering).
cards.title: feat(server): add SSE change-event stream endpoint (GET /v1/boards/:id/events)

cards.description:
## Context / why

Part of the HTTP collaborative backend epic (KAN-684). Today every consumer (TUI, CLI, MCP) opens a board from a local file path. To let a team share one board, KAN-684 adds a `kanban-server` (axum, already partially present at `crates/kanban-server/`) and a client-side `HttpBackend` that implements the same `KanbanBackend` interface over HTTP, so `KanbanContext` and every frontend stay unchanged.

This card lays the foundation: the `http_backend` module skeleton plus a compiling `HttpBackend` struct with stubbed trait impls. Every other client-side card (KAN-698/726/727/699/700/734 and the test cards) builds on this scaffold. It blocks all of them.

## Scope decision (module, not crate)

Sprint 19 decided all `KanbanBackend` implementations live as modules inside `kanban-service`, siblings to `json_backend.rs` and `sqlite_backend.rs`. Backend selection is a runtime decision (locator/URL detection via `StoreManager`), so a separate crate buys no dependency isolation — any consumer offering remote connectivity must compile the HTTP backend in regardless. There is **no `http` feature flag**; the module is always compiled.

KAN-753 already removed the empty `kanban-http-backend` placeholder crate, so this card starts from nothing. Do NOT re-create a crate.

## Current state

- `crates/kanban-service/src/lib.rs:13-32` — module declarations; `json_backend` (gated `feature = "json"`) and `sqlite_backend` (gated `feature = "sqlite"`) are the sibling pattern to follow. `backend::KanbanBackend` is re-exported at `lib.rs:25`.
- `crates/kanban-service/src/backend.rs:24-89` — the `KanbanBackend` trait. It is `#[async_trait]` and requires `DataStore + CommandStore + Send + Sync`. Only `as_data_store()` is mandatory; `flush`/`reload`/`needs_flush`/`needs_save_worker`/`instance_id`/`persistence_metadata`/`health_checker`/`with_transaction` all have defaults.
- `crates/kanban-service/src/json_backend.rs:25-367` — the reference implementation: a struct holding a backing store, with `impl DataStore`, `impl CommandStore`, and `#[async_trait] impl KanbanBackend`. Mirror this file layout.
- `crates/kanban-domain/src/data_store.rs:7-118` — the `DataStore` trait (synchronous, ~40 methods). `crates/kanban-domain/src/command_store.rs:5-21` — the `CommandStore` trait (synchronous): `append_batch(&CommandBatch) -> KanbanResult<u64>`, `batch_count`, `load_batches(from,to)`, `load_all_batches` (default).
- `crates/kanban-service/Cargo.toml:21-38` — current deps. `async-trait`, `tokio`, `serde`, `serde_json`, `uuid`, `chrono`, `tracing` are already present. `reqwest` is NOT yet a dependency here; it is declared in the workspace at root `Cargo.toml:75` as `reqwest = { version = "0.12", default-features = false, features = ["json","blocking","rustls-tls"] }`.
- The wire types this backend will use already live inside `kanban-service` itself at `crates/kanban-service/src/api/` (re-exported from `kanban_service::api::*`). There is **no separate `kanban-api` crate** — the original KAN-697 note about a `kanban-api` path dep is obsolete. The http_backend module imports `crate::api::{...}` directly. No new path dependency is needed.

## Target

1. Add `reqwest = { workspace = true }` to `[dependencies]` in `crates/kanban-service/Cargo.toml` (the `blocking` feature is already enabled at workspace level, which the sync→async bridge will use — see KAN-698).

2. Create the module directory:
```
crates/kanban-service/src/http_backend/
  mod.rs            // pub struct HttpBackend { base_url, client, instance_id }; HttpBackend::new; KanbanBackend impl
  client.rs         // request helpers: build URL, send, deserialize, map errors
  data_store.rs     // impl DataStore for HttpBackend (stubs here; real reads in KAN-726/727/734)
  command_store.rs  // impl CommandStore for HttpBackend (stub; real impl in KAN-699)
  error.rs          // reqwest::Error / ApiError -> KanbanError mapping
```
Keep each file under 300 lines per the project guideline.

3. The struct:
```rust
pub struct HttpBackend {
    base_url: String,        // normalized, no trailing slash
    client: reqwest::blocking::Client,
    instance_id: Uuid,       // minted at construction; overwritten by SSE writer_instance_id echo later (KAN-700/749)
}

impl HttpBackend {
    pub fn new(base_url: &str) -> KanbanResult<Self> {
        let base_url = base_url.trim_end_matches('/').to_string();
        let client = reqwest::blocking::Client::builder()
            .build()
            .map_err(/* -> KanbanError::Internal */)?;
        Ok(Self { base_url, client, instance_id: Uuid::new_v4() })
    }
}
```
Use `reqwest::blocking::Client` so the synchronous `DataStore`/`CommandStore` methods need no runtime juggling (see the sync→async note in KAN-698; final choice between `blocking::Client` and `tokio::task::block_in_place` over an async client is made in KAN-698, but the scaffold should pick `blocking::Client` as the default and KAN-698 may revisit).

4. Add `pub mod http_backend;` to `lib.rs` (ungated — always compiled) and `pub use http_backend::HttpBackend;`.

5. Stub every trait method so it compiles. For DataStore/CommandStore read stubs return `Err(KanbanError::Internal("http_backend: not yet implemented".into()))`. **Note: there is no `KanbanError::Unsupported` variant** — the available variant for "not supported on this backend" is `KanbanError::Internal(String)` (see `crates/kanban-domain/src/error.rs:202-230`). Earlier card text referencing `Unsupported` is incorrect; use `Internal`. `as_data_store()` returns `self`; `instance_id()` returns `self.instance_id`; lifecycle methods can keep trait defaults for now.

### error.rs (laid out here, fleshed out by consumers)

Define the conversion seam the other cards reuse:
- `reqwest::Error` (transport: connect refused, timeout, DNS) -> `KanbanError::Internal(format!("http transport: {e}"))`.
- A non-2xx HTTP response carries an `ApiError { code: ErrorCode, message }` body (`crate::api::ApiError`, defined at `crates/kanban-service/src/api/v1/error.rs:88-103`). Deserialize it and map `ErrorCode` back to a `KanbanError` (the inverse of the existing `From<&KanbanError> for ApiError` at `error_mapping.rs:8-72`): e.g. `NotFound -> KanbanError::Domain(DomainError::NotFound{..})`, `ConflictDetected -> KanbanError::ConflictDetected{..}`, `ValidationFailed -> KanbanError::validation(message)`, server-fault codes (`IoError`/`DatabaseError`/`SerializationError`/`InternalError`) -> `KanbanError::Internal(message)`. The scaffold defines the function signature and a default arm; KAN-698/699 fill in the arms they exercise.

## Step-by-step (TDD)

1. **Red**: add `mod http_backend;` and a test `test_http_backend_new_normalizes_trailing_slash` asserting `HttpBackend::new("http://x/")` stores `base_url == "http://x"`. Fails to compile (no module).
2. **Green**: create the module files, struct, `new`, stubs; wire `lib.rs`. Make the one test pass.
3. Add `test_http_backend_implements_kanban_backend_object_safe` — `let _: &dyn KanbanBackend = &HttpBackend::new("http://localhost:0").unwrap();` (mirrors `backend.rs:107`).
4. Add `test_http_backend_new_mints_nonnil_instance_id`.
5. **Refactor**: extract the URL-normalization and client-build into small helpers; confirm files stay under 300 lines.

## Tests (named)

- `test_http_backend_new_normalizes_trailing_slash`
- `test_http_backend_new_mints_nonnil_instance_id`
- `test_http_backend_implements_kanban_backend_object_safe`
- `test_http_backend_as_data_store_returns_self`

These are pure construction/object-safety tests and need NO running server, so they live as inline `#[cfg(test)]` in `mod.rs`. Read/write methods that actually hit HTTP are tested by KAN-726/727/699 against the in-process `TestServer` harness from KAN-703.

## Acceptance

- `cargo check -p kanban-service` passes with `http_backend` always compiled (no feature flag).
- `cargo test -p kanban-service http_backend` passes the construction/object-safety tests.
- `HttpBackend` satisfies `&dyn KanbanBackend`.
- No `kanban-http-backend` crate exists; `reqwest` added to `kanban-service` deps; module mirrors `json_backend.rs` layout.

## Dependencies

- Blocks: KAN-698, KAN-726, KAN-727, KAN-734, KAN-699, KAN-700, and the http test cards (KAN-704/735/736/737/738/739).
- Depends on: the `kanban-service::api` wire types (already present). The old "depends on kanban-api crate" note is obsolete (api is a module in kanban-service; KAN-753 deleted the placeholder crate).
cards.title: feat(service): scaffold http_backend module in kanban-service with stub HttpBackend

cards.description:
> ⚠ BLOCKING DECISION (gates 726/727): the v1 `*Response` DTOs are LOSSY (BoardResponse omits card_counter/sprint counters/names; CardResponse omits sprint_logs), but `DataStore::get_board` must return a FULL domain Board. So the server's reads CANNOT serve the lossy Response DTO to HttpBackend. FORK: (A) lossy `From<*Response>` with documented defaults; (B) server emits DOMAIN-shaped reads for the backend (keep *Response for the human/REST surface). RECOMMEND (B) — it preserves fidelity and matches the epic's "reads use domain types" intent. This is the SAME question as KAN-800 (presentation layer): the v1 Response DTO is a lossy projection; a backend needs full fidelity -> separate the two. Resolve + record here before 726/727.

## Context / why

Parent/coordination card for implementing the synchronous `DataStore` trait on `HttpBackend`, part of the HTTP collaborative backend epic (KAN-684). `KanbanContext` reads all board state through `as_data_store() -> &dyn DataStore`; for the HTTP backend each read must become a GET to `kanban-server`. This card owns the cross-cutting decisions (the sync→async bridge, the DTO→domain reconstruction problem, error mapping) and splits the ~40 methods into child cards.

## Current state

- `crates/kanban-domain/src/data_store.rs:7-118` — the `DataStore` trait. It is **fully synchronous** (no `async fn`), despite `KanbanBackend` being `#[async_trait]`. ~40 methods across Board / Column / Card / Archived-card / Sprint / Graph / Snapshot, several with default impls (`list_cards_by_columns`, `list_archived_cards_by_columns`, `clear_sprint_from_archived_cards`, `modify_graph`).
- `crates/kanban-service/src/json_backend.rs:163-297` — reference `impl DataStore`: every method delegates to an inner `InMemoryStore` via `with_read`/`with_mutate`. The HTTP backend replaces the inner store with HTTP calls.
- `crates/kanban-service/src/http_backend/data_store.rs` — stub created by KAN-697; all methods currently `Err(KanbanError::Internal(..))`.
- Response wire shapes live at `crates/kanban-service/src/api/v1/{boards,columns,cards,sprints}/response.rs` and the `Page<T>` envelope at `crates/kanban-service/src/api/v1/pagination.rs:4-11`. Single-entity GETs return e.g. `BoardResponse`; collection GETs return `Page<BoardResponse>`.

## Critical design decision #1 — sync→async bridge

`DataStore` is sync; HTTP I/O is naturally async. Two viable bridges:

- **`reqwest::blocking::Client`** (chosen default, set up in KAN-697): each method calls `self.client.get(url).send()` synchronously. Simple, no runtime gymnastics, no panic risk. Caveat: a `blocking::Client` spins up its own internal runtime thread and **must not be created or called from within an async context on the same thread without care** — but calling it from the sync `DataStore` methods (which `KanbanContext` invokes from sync code paths) is fine. This is the recommended path.
- `tokio::task::block_in_place` + an async `reqwest::Client`: only works on a multi-thread runtime and panics on a current-thread runtime (see the cautionary note at `json_backend.rs:410-420` where `block_in_place` was deliberately removed for exactly this reason). Avoid unless a concrete reason emerges.

Decision: use `reqwest::blocking::Client`. All child cards (726/727/734) follow this. Reserve `async` strictly for the `KanbanBackend` lifecycle methods (`flush`/`reload`) in KAN-700.

## Critical design decision #2 — DTO→domain reconstruction gap (MUST resolve before 726/727/734)

`DataStore::get_board` returns `KanbanResult<Option<Board>>` — a full **domain** `Board`. But the server serializes `BoardResponse`, which **omits** fields the domain `Board` requires:
- `BoardResponse` (`api/v1/boards/response.rs:13-29`) drops `card_counter`, `next_sprint_number`, `sprint_counters`, `sprint_names`, `sprint_name_used_count` (see the test at `response.rs:57-77` asserting they are absent from JSON).
- `CardResponse` (`api/v1/cards/response.rs:14-30`) drops `sprint_logs`.
- There are **no reverse `From<BoardResponse> for Board`** conversions anywhere (verified by grep).

So a client cannot losslessly rebuild a domain `Board`/`Card` from the response DTO. Resolution options (pick one as part of this card and apply uniformly in children):

- **(A) Lossy reconstruction with documented defaults** — add `From<BoardResponse> for Board` / `From<CardResponse> for Card` etc. that fill the omitted fields with neutral defaults (`card_counter: 0`, `sprint_logs: vec![]`, `sprint_names: vec![]`, …). Acceptable only if downstream readers (TUI/MCP rendering) never depend on those fields on the client. Risk: card-number allocation and sprint-name pools are server-managed anyway, so clients arguably never need them — but this must be verified against TUI usage.
- **(B) Add domain-shaped read routes** — have `kanban-server` expose the raw domain `Board`/`Card` (which already derive Serialize/Deserialize, per KAN-684's "responses use domain types directly" note) on the read endpoints the backend consumes, reserving the trimmed `*Response` DTOs for the human/REST-facing surface. This is the cleanest and matches the epic's stated "Responses use domain types from kanban-domain directly" decision — the `*Response` DTOs appear to be a later REST-polish addition that diverged from that decision.

**Recommended: (B)** — it preserves correctness and aligns with KAN-684's resolved design table ("Response wire format: Domain types directly … no translation layer needed"). This card should confirm with the server-route cards (KAN-716/718/720/724) which shape they emit; if they emit `*Response` DTOs, either add a `?shape=domain` variant or a parallel internal route, OR fall back to (A) with explicit field-default documentation. Document the chosen contract on this card so children inherit it.

## Critical design decision #3 — write methods are unsupported

All `DataStore` mutators (`upsert_*`, `delete_*`, `insert_archived_card`, `clear_sprint_from_cards`, `set_graph`, `modify_graph`, `apply_snapshot`) return `Err(KanbanError::Internal("http_backend: writes go through CommandStore::append_batch".into()))`. Writes on the HTTP path flow only through `CommandStore::append_batch` -> `POST /v1/commands` (KAN-699). `KanbanContext` mutates via command batches, not direct `DataStore` upserts, so these are never hit on the happy path. Use `KanbanError::Internal` (there is no `Unsupported` variant).

## Split into child cards

- **KAN-726** — Board + Column reads (`get_board`, `list_boards`, `get_column`, `list_columns_by_board`, `list_all_columns`).
- **KAN-727** — Card reads (`get_card`, `list_all_cards`, `list_cards_by_column`, `list_cards_by_sprint`, counts).
- **KAN-734** — Archived-card, Sprint, and Graph reads (`get_sprint`, `list_sprints_by_board`, `list_all_sprints`, archived-card reads, `get_graph`).
- This card: shared scaffolding only — the bridge helper, the DTO→domain decision, the unsupported-write stubs, and the `error.rs` deserialization seam.

## Step-by-step (TDD)

1. **Red**: write a test asserting `upsert_board` returns `Err` with an Internal message mentioning CommandStore. Fails (currently a different stub message).
2. **Green**: implement all write-method stubs uniformly.
3. **Red/Green**: resolve the DTO→domain question (decision (B) or (A)); land the conversion seam or confirm the server emits domain shapes. Add a round-trip test that a domain `Board` serialized by the server-side path deserializes back to an equal domain `Board` on the client.
4. **Refactor**: extract `get_one::<T: DeserializeOwned>(path) -> KanbanResult<Option<T>>` and `get_page::<T>(path) -> KanbanResult<Vec<T>>` helpers in `client.rs`, consumed by 726/727/734.

## Tests (named)

- `test_data_store_write_methods_return_unsupported_on_http`
- `test_board_round_trips_server_to_client_without_field_loss` (guards decision (B)/(A))
- `test_get_one_helper_maps_404_to_ok_none` (a GET returning 404 NotFound -> `Ok(None)`, not `Err`)

These need a running server — use the in-process `TestServer` harness (KAN-703).

## Acceptance

- The sync→async bridge approach is decided and documented (reqwest blocking).
- The DTO→domain reconstruction contract is decided and enforced by a round-trip test.
- Write-method stubs uniformly return `KanbanError::Internal` pointing at CommandStore.
- `client.rs` exposes the shared `get_one` / `get_page` helpers the children use.

## Dependencies

- Depends on KAN-697 (scaffold).
- Blocks KAN-726, KAN-727, KAN-734.
- Coordinates with server read-route cards (KAN-716/718/720/724) on the response-shape contract.
cards.title: feat(service): implement DataStore for HttpBackend

cards.description:
## Context / why

Part of the HTTP collaborative backend epic (KAN-684). Implements `CommandStore` on `HttpBackend`. This is the **sole write path** for an HTTP-connected client: `KanbanContext` mutates state by executing command batches and appending them to the `CommandStore`, so for the HTTP backend `append_batch` must POST the batch to the server, which executes it server-side and broadcasts a change event.

## Current state

- `crates/kanban-service/src/http_backend/command_store.rs` — stub from KAN-697.
- `crates/kanban-domain/src/command_store.rs:5-21` — the `CommandStore` trait (synchronous):
  - `append_batch(&self, batch: &CommandBatch) -> KanbanResult<u64>` — append one batch, return new entry count.
  - `batch_count(&self) -> KanbanResult<u64>`
  - `load_batches(&self, from: u64, to: u64) -> KanbanResult<Vec<CommandBatch>>`
  - `load_all_batches(&self) -> KanbanResult<(Vec<CommandBatch>, u64)>` — **has a default** (`command_store.rs:16-20`).
  - **Note**: the trait method is `append_batch(&CommandBatch)` returning `u64`, NOT `append_commands(&[Command])`. The earlier card text (`append_commands`/`command_count`/`load_commands`/`Unsupported`) predates the current trait and is wrong — implement the real signatures.
- `crates/kanban-domain/src/command_batch.rs:9-18` — `CommandBatch { commands: Vec<Command>, correlation_id, issued_by: ClientId, timestamp, app_type, app_version, session_id }`. It derives `Serialize`/`Deserialize`, so the whole batch is the POST body.
- Reference: `json_backend.rs:301-314` delegates each method to the inner `InMemoryStore`.

## Target

`crates/kanban-service/src/http_backend/command_store.rs`:

```rust
impl CommandStore for HttpBackend {
    fn append_batch(&self, batch: &CommandBatch) -> KanbanResult<u64> {
        // POST {base_url}/v1/commands  body = serde_json(batch)  (the whole CommandBatch)
        // blocking client; on 2xx deserialize the server's response, return its count
        // on non-2xx deserialize ApiError -> map to KanbanError (error.rs)
        // transport error -> KanbanError::Internal("http transport: ...")
    }

    fn batch_count(&self) -> KanbanResult<u64> { Ok(0) }   // not tracked client-side

    fn load_batches(&self, _from: u64, _to: u64) -> KanbanResult<Vec<CommandBatch>> {
        Err(KanbanError::Internal("command log reads are not supported over HTTP".into()))
    }

    // load_all_batches: do NOT inherit the default — the default calls batch_count()
    // (returns 0) then load_batches(0,0) -> (vec![], 0), which silently hides the
    // unsupported-ness. Override to return Err(Internal) for an honest signal.
    fn load_all_batches(&self) -> KanbanResult<(Vec<CommandBatch>, u64)> {
        Err(KanbanError::Internal("command log reads are not supported over HTTP".into()))
    }
}
```

### POST body and response

- Request: `POST /v1/commands`, `Content-Type: application/json`, body = the serialized `CommandBatch` (KAN-695 defines the server endpoint). Confirm with KAN-695 whether the server accepts a single `CommandBatch` object or a bare `Vec<Command>` array; the current domain type is a `CommandBatch` carrying provenance (`correlation_id`/`issued_by`/`session_id`), and the epic's observability foundation (KAN-729/731) wants that provenance on the wire — so POST the full `CommandBatch`.
- Response: the server executes the batch under its write lock and returns an executed/entry count. Deserialize into a small `{ executed: u64 }` (or whatever KAN-695 returns) and return it as the `u64`. Align the exact field name with KAN-695.
- Server broadcasts a `ChangeEventFrame` (`api/v1/events.rs:19`) stamped with the server's `writer_instance_id`; the SSE listener (KAN-749/700) filters frames whose `writer_instance_id` matches this client so the client doesn't react to its own writes.

### Why reads are unsupported

The HTTP backend is append-only from the client's perspective; the command log lives server-side. `load_batches`/`load_all_batches` would need a dedicated read route that does not exist (explicitly out of scope per KAN-684's resolved-decisions table). Return `KanbanError::Internal` (there is no `Unsupported` variant — see `crates/kanban-domain/src/error.rs:202-230`). `batch_count` returns `Ok(0)` rather than erroring because some callers probe it cheaply and a 0 is a safe "nothing known locally".

## Step-by-step (TDD)

1. **Red**: `test_append_batch_posts_to_commands_endpoint` against a `TestServer` (KAN-703): build a one-command `CommandBatch::from(vec![CreateBoard..])`, call `append_batch`, assert it returns the executed count and that the board now exists server-side (read it back via `get_board`). Fails (stub).
2. **Green**: implement `append_batch` (serialize batch, blocking POST, deserialize count, error mapping).
3. **Red/Green**: `test_load_batches_returns_unsupported`, `test_load_all_batches_returns_unsupported`, `test_batch_count_returns_zero`.
4. **Red/Green**: `test_append_batch_maps_server_error` — POST a batch the server rejects (e.g. WIP-limit / validation) and assert the mapped `KanbanError` variant matches the `ErrorCode`.
5. **Refactor**: extract a `post_json::<Req, Resp>(path, &req)` helper in `client.rs` mirroring KAN-698's `get_one`/`get_page`.

## Tests (named)

- `test_append_batch_posts_to_commands_endpoint`
- `test_append_batch_returns_server_executed_count`
- `test_append_batch_maps_validation_error_to_kanban_error`
- `test_batch_count_returns_zero`
- `test_load_batches_returns_unsupported`
- `test_load_all_batches_returns_unsupported`

The POST tests need the in-process `TestServer` harness (KAN-703) with the commands endpoint (KAN-695) mounted.

## Acceptance

- `append_batch` serializes the full `CommandBatch`, POSTs `/v1/commands`, returns the server's executed count, and the mutation is observable via a subsequent read.
- Server errors are mapped to the correct `KanbanError` via `error.rs`.
- `batch_count` returns `Ok(0)`; `load_batches`/`load_all_batches` return `Err(KanbanError::Internal)` (override the default `load_all_batches`).

## Dependencies

- Depends on KAN-697 (scaffold) and KAN-695 (server `POST /v1/commands` endpoint) to test against.
- Parallel with KAN-700.
- Tests need the `TestServer` harness (KAN-703).
