cards.description:
# Kanban HTTP API v1 — Full CRUD Specification

> Epic: KAN-684 (collaborative HTTP backend). Scaffolds: KAN-712 (api error/event types),
> KAN-713 (board/column request types). This document is the authoritative spec for the
> complete v1 request/response DTO surface across every entity.

---

## 0. Purpose & how to read this

This spec defines the **wire contract** for the kanban HTTP backend: every request body, every
response body, every endpoint, for every entity, mapped field-by-field to the domain model in
`kanban-domain`. It is exhaustive on purpose — an implementer should be able to build the entire DTO
layer from this document without re-deriving anything from the domain.

The DTOs live as a private, version-gated module inside `kanban-service` (`kanban_service::api::v1`,
re-exported flat from `kanban_service::api`), matching the existing layout from KAN-712/713.

---

## 1. Foundational decisions (locked)

These were settled during design review and apply to **every** type below.

### 1.1 Why a dedicated DTO layer (not domain types on the wire)
The domain update/entity structs' serde is **already a persistence contract** — `BoardUpdate`,
`ColumnUpdate`, `CardUpdate`, `SprintUpdate` are embedded in `Command` variants that are persisted
as JSON to the command log (`commands_json`, `sqlite_store.rs:578`, KAN-191). The wire format
therefore **cannot** reuse or annotate the domain serde (e.g. `#[serde(skip_deserializing)]` for
HTTP would corrupt command replay/undo). The DTO layer is a real boundary, not redundant
duplication. Request DTOs are dedicated, hand-curated types.

### 1.2 Verb → DTO mapping (REST, single-object bodies)
| Verb | Purpose | DTO family | Body shape |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POST` | create | `Create<Entity>Request` | entity-shaped, server fields excluded |
| `GET` | read | `<Entity>Response` / `<Entity>SummaryResponse` | entity-shaped read projection |
| `PUT` | full replace | `Replace<Entity>Request` | **straight** full entity-shaped body |
| `PATCH` | partial update | `Update<Entity>Request` | three-state (`FieldUpdate`) partial |
| `DELETE` | delete | — | no body |
| `POST .../<action>` | actions (move, activate, …) | `<Action>Request` | small action-specific body |

**Batch is deferred.** v1 bodies are plain single objects. Batch is additive later (a bulk
sub-route or an array-accepting variant) with no breaking change; the domain already has the
plural-primitive / singular-delegates pattern to back it (`archive_card` → `archive_cards(vec![id])`).

### 1.3 Server-managed field exclusion
Request DTOs **must exclude** server-managed fields (ids, timestamps, counters, derived state). The
exclusion decision is enforced at conversion time (see 1.5), not just by omission.

### 1.4 Enum wire casing — RESOLVED (D1, **revised**): decoupled snake_case mirrors
The wire is **decoupled from the domain enums**. Each domain enum used on the wire has a mirror in
`api/v1/enums.rs` (`SortFieldDto`, `SortOrderDto`, `TaskListViewDto`, and future `CardStatusDto`,
`CardPriorityDto`, `SprintStatusDto`, `SeverityDto`, `RelatesKindDto`) that serializes
`#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]` ("in_progress", "created_at", "grouped_by_column") and converts
to/from the domain enum via **exhaustive two-way `From`** impls. This keeps the public JSON casing
independent of the domain's serde (which is also the persistence format) and turns a domain variant
rename into a compile error rather than a silent wire change.
> Earlier D1 reused the domain enums directly (PascalCase); reversed at the user's request to fully
> decouple the API from the domain.

`ErrorCode` remains `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE` — a deliberate exception for machine-readable error codes.

### 1.5 The drift guard (mandatory convention)
Every request DTO gets a conversion to its domain counterpart — `impl TryFrom<Update<E>Request> for
<E>Update` (fallible where validation can fail; `From` where it cannot). It **must** be written as an
**exhaustive destructure + exhaustive construct with no `..Default::default()`**, so that a new
domain field becomes a compile error forcing a deliberate exposed/excluded decision. This conversion
is mandatory code (the handler can't function without it), so the guard has no per-type bootstrap
problem. Excluded server-managed fields appear as explicit lines (e.g. `active_sprint_id:
FieldUpdate::NoChange`) with a comment.

### 1.6 PATCH wire shape — RESOLVED (D2): JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7386)
PATCH bodies follow **JSON Merge Patch** semantics — the clean, standard REST convention:
- **field absent** → no change
- **field `null`** → clear (set to `None`)
- **field present with value** → set

This maps one-to-one onto the domain's three-state `FieldUpdate<T>` (`NoChange` / `Clear` / `Set`),
but the **wire form is plain** — no externally-tagged `{"Set":v}`/`"Clear"`. The PATCH DTOs therefore
do **not** reuse the domain `FieldUpdate` serde; they use a wire wrapper with custom serde
(the `Option<Option<T>>` "double-option" pattern: outer absent = no change, `Some(None)` = clear,
`Some(Some(v))` = set), converting to domain `FieldUpdate` in the `TryFrom`. RFC 7386's only caveat
(null cannot also be a legitimate value) does not apply — our nullable fields use null to mean unset.
> This **supersedes** the externally-tagged FieldUpdate wire shape currently in KAN-713's
> `UpdateBoardRequest`/`UpdateColumnRequest`; those must migrate to the merge-patch wire form.

### 1.7 Module layout
One file per entity under `crates/kanban-service/src/api/v1/`, each holding that entity's request +
response DTOs + conversions + tests, to stay under the 300-line guideline:
`boards.rs`, `columns.rs`, `cards.rs`, `sprints.rs`, `dependencies.rs`, plus existing `error.rs`,
`events.rs`. Shared read projections may live in `responses.rs` if files grow. An entity file is
promoted to a directory module (`<entity>/mod.rs` + `requests.rs`/`actions.rs`/`response.rs`) once it
crosses 300 lines (already done for `boards/`).

### 1.8 HTTP method semantics — RFC 9110 (cross-cutting, all entities)
Methods follow [RFC 9110](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9110); every endpoint inherits
these rules:
- **POST — create** (§9.3.3): collection POST creates a subordinate; respond **`201 Created` with a
  `Location` header** pointing to the new resource (e.g. `Location: /v1/boards/{id}`).
- **POST — action**: lifecycle/side-effecting verbs (`move`, `archive`, `restore`, `assign`,
  `activate`, `complete`, `cancel`, `carry-over`, `import`) are RPC-over-POST — the correct method
  for non-idempotent operations that aren't a field set. State transitions stay POST, **not** PUT/PATCH.
- **PUT** (§9.3.4): full replace, **idempotent** (see §1.6 / Board PUT).
- **PATCH**: merge-patch; our set/clear patches are **idempotent in effect**.
- **DELETE** (§9.3.5): removes a resource **or an association** (`DELETE /cards/:id/sprint` unassign,
  `DELETE /cards/:id/spawns/:target` edge removal are textbook association-removal). Must be
  **idempotent**: repeating a delete yields the same end state — `204` then `404` is acceptable
  (effect is identical); edge removal honors `?tolerate_missing=` so removing a missing edge succeeds.
  **DELETE requests carry no body** — options go in query params (RFC 9110: DELETE content "has no
  defined semantics").
- **GET** (§9.2.1): safe — reads only, no side effects (incl. `branch-name`/`git-checkout`).

> **`reorder` decision (open):** `POST /columns/:id/reorder` is redundant with `PATCH /columns/:id
> {position}`. Keep the named action for explicitness, or drop it for PATCH — to decide before the
> column slice is considered final. Recorded under Deferred follow-ups (§10).

---

## 2. Error model & HTTP status mapping

Response envelope (KAN-712, exists): `ApiError { code: ErrorCode, message: String }`,
`code` serialized `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE`.

Mapping from domain errors → `ErrorCode` → HTTP status:

| Domain error | ErrorCode | HTTP | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DomainError::NotFound` | `NOT_FOUND` | 404 | |
| `DomainError::NotFoundByName` | `NOT_FOUND_BY_NAME` | 404 | message carries available alternatives |
| `DomainError::Ambiguous` | `AMBIGUOUS` | 409 | message carries the matches |
| `DomainError::BatchResolutionFailed` | `BATCH_RESOLUTION_FAILED` *(new — D3)* | 400 | per-input typed failure causes in message |
| `DomainError::Validation` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` | 422 | |
| `DomainError::Dependency(CycleDetected)` | `CYCLE_DETECTED` *(new — D3)* | 409 | |
| `DomainError::Dependency(SelfReference)` | `SELF_REFERENCE` *(new — D3)* | 422 | |
| `DomainError::Dependency(EdgeNotFound)` | `EDGE_NOT_FOUND` *(new — D3)* | 404 | |
| `DomainError::Dependency(DuplicateEdge)` | `DUPLICATE_EDGE` *(new — D3)* | 409 | |
| `DomainError::WipLimitExceeded` | `WIP_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` | 409 | |
| `DomainError::SprintBoardMismatch` | `SPRINT_BOARD_MISMATCH` | 422 | |
| `KanbanError::ConflictDetected` | `CONFLICT_DETECTED` | 409 | optimistic-concurrency / external write |
| `KanbanError::UnsupportedFutureVersion` | `UNSUPPORTED_VERSION` | 409 | |
| `KanbanError::Io` | `IO_ERROR` | 500 | |
| `KanbanError::Serialization` | `SERIALIZATION_ERROR` | 500 | |
| `KanbanError::Database` | `DATABASE_ERROR` | 500 | |
| `KanbanError::Internal` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` | 500 | |

The error→status mapping lives in one place in the server (an `impl From<&KanbanError> for
(StatusCode, ApiError)` or equivalent), written as an exhaustive match so new domain errors force a
mapping decision.

**`ErrorCode` additions required (D3):** extend the KAN-712 enum (it is `#[non_exhaustive]`, so this
is non-breaking) with `BATCH_RESOLUTION_FAILED`, `CYCLE_DETECTED`, `SELF_REFERENCE`, `EDGE_NOT_FOUND`,
`DUPLICATE_EDGE`, and drop the now-unused coarse `DEPENDENCY_ERROR` (or keep as a fallback).

### 2.1 Pagination & list envelope (cross-cutting)
All collection `GET`s (boards, columns, cards, sprints, archived cards) return the existing paginated
envelope (as already emitted by the CLI/service):
```json
{ "items": [ ... ], "total": 123, "page": 1, "page_size": 50, "total_pages": 3 }
```
Query params: `?page=<1-based>&page_size=<n>` (sensible default page_size, hard max to cap payloads),
composed with each entity's filter params (e.g. cards also take `board_id`, `status`, `search`, …).
Single-resource `GET`s return the bare `*Response` object, not the envelope.

## 8. Decisions — RESOLVED

- **D1 — Enum wire casing (revised):** **decoupled snake_case mirrors** in `api/v1/enums.rs` with
  exhaustive two-way `From` conversions — the wire is independent of the domain enums. (Reverses the
  earlier "reuse domain enums" call.) `ErrorCode` stays `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE`. See §1.4.
- **D2 — PATCH wire shape:** **JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7386)** — absent = no change, `null` = clear,
  value = set. Wire DTOs use the double-option pattern, not domain `FieldUpdate` serde. Supersedes the
  externally-tagged shape in KAN-713's update DTOs. See §1.6.
- **D3 — Error granularity:** **Yes.** Add `BATCH_RESOLUTION_FAILED`; split `DEPENDENCY_ERROR` into
  `CYCLE_DETECTED` / `SELF_REFERENCE` / `EDGE_NOT_FOUND` / `DUPLICATE_EDGE`. See §2 / §2.1.
- **D4 — Board response curation:** **Hide internal allocation state by default.** "Internal
  counters/pools" are the server-side bookkeeping the board keeps to mint identifiers, not
  user-facing data:
  - `card_counter` — next card number (mints `KAN-757`, …).
  - `next_sprint_number`, `sprint_counters: HashMap<prefix,u32>` — next sprint number(s) per prefix.
  - `sprint_names: Vec<String>`, `sprint_name_used_count` — the pool of pre-named sprints and how many
    are consumed.

  These are implementation detail; `BoardResponse` omits them by default (optionally surfaced via
  `?include=internal` for admin/debug). **Pagination is separate and IS supported** — all list
  endpoints use the envelope in §2.1; it does not depend on exposing these counters.
- **D5 — Card sprint membership = action-only (not PATCH).** *The difference:* `PATCH /cards/:id`
  with a `sprint_id` would only flip the scalar field, **bypassing the side effects** that
  `assign_card_to_sprint`/`unassign_card_from_sprint` perform — appending/closing the `sprint_logs`
  audit entry and the sprint↔board validation (`SprintBoardMismatch`). Routing membership through the
  dedicated actions (`POST`/`DELETE /v1/cards/:id/sprint`) guarantees the log + validation run.
  Therefore `sprint_id` is **excluded from `UpdateCardRequest`** and accepted only at create
  (`CreateCardRequest`, mirroring `CreateCardOptions.sprint_id`) and via the actions.
- **D6 — Links response = richer objects.** *Context:* the dependency graph (§7). A card has
  parents/children (`spawns`), blockers/blocked (`blocks`, carrying `Severity`), and related cards
  (`relates`, carrying `RelatesKind`). `GET /v1/cards/:id/links` returns each edge as an object
  including its metadata and the target card's identity, so the UI renders severity/kind without a
  second round-trip:
  ```json
  {
    "parents":  [ { "card_id": "…", "card_number": 12 } ],
    "children": [ … ],
    "blockers": [ { "card_id": "…", "severity": "High" } ],
    "blocked":  [ … ],
    "related":  [ { "card_id": "…", "kind": "Duplicates" } ]
  }
  ```
- **D7 — PUT replace = full replace, respecting foreign keys.** PUT replaces all **client-editable**
  fields wholesale, **including mutable relational FKs** (e.g. a card's `column_id`), but the server
  **validates every FK** (target board/column/sprint must exist; cross-board moves rejected with
  `SprintBoardMismatch`/`Validation`) and never touches server-managed/derived fields (ids,
  timestamps, counters, `sprint_logs`, `completed_at`). Referential integrity is enforced in the
  `TryFrom`/handler, not assumed.

## 9. Conventions checklist (per DTO, enforced)

- [ ] Dedicated wire type (never reuse domain serde for requests).
- [ ] `#[serde(default)]` on every optional / `FieldUpdate` field so partial bodies deserialize.
- [ ] Server-managed fields excluded from request DTOs.
- [ ] `TryFrom<Request> for <DomainUpdate/Args>` written **exhaustively, no `..Default::default()`**
      (the drift guard); excluded fields explicit + commented.
- [ ] Validation (negatives, enum bounds, cross-field) lives in the `TryFrom` (the validation
      boundary), surfaced as `DomainError::Validation` → 422.
- [ ] serde round-trip test (full + minimal payloads + `FieldUpdate` defaults).
- [ ] Response projections (`*Response`/`*SummaryResponse`) mirror domain read shapes.
- [ ] Error→status mapping extended (exhaustive match) if a new error path is introduced.

4. **Card**: create/replace/patch + actions (move/archive/restore/assign) + responses + list filter.
5. **Sprint**: create/replace/patch + lifecycle actions + responses.
6. **Dependencies**: edge add/remove + subcard + rich links response (D6).
7. **Cross-cutting**: shared `responses.rs` / per-entity directory promotion as files exceed 300.
8. **Server** (`kanban-server`): routing, handlers wired to `KanbanContext` (run the
   `into_parts` create-then-update orchestration), `StatusCode::from_u16(code.http_status())`, SSE.

Each step: TDD (serde round-trips + conversion exhaustiveness), `test`/`feat` commits split per
convention, one changeset per PR.

### Deferred follow-ups (consciously postponed)

  excluded from PATCH/PUT, and unlike columns there is no `reorder` endpoint). Add
  `POST /v1/boards/:id/reorder` (mirroring `ReorderColumnRequest`) in a later slice.

  /columns/:id {position}`; decide keep-named-action vs drop-for-PATCH before the column slice is final.

#### v1 polish / tech-debt (low-value; fix opportunistically when the server slice touches this code)

      an api-owned "create plan" type so no domain type appears on the public wire-type surface.
- [ ] Consolidate the "is this code internal" knowledge: `error_mapping.rs` message policy + `error.rs`
      `http_status()` both classify it — extract `ErrorCode::is_internal()` or derive from status class.
- [ ] `ErrorCode::DependencyError` is now unreachable from the mapping (the four granular codes
      replaced it); remove it or mark it an intentional fallback.
- [ ] `api/mod.rs` doc comment overclaims versioning ("allows the versioning strategy to evolve") —
      HTTP versioning is URL-based (`/v1/`), not the Rust module path; soften or make path-based.

## Appendix B — Sources consulted

### External (REST / PATCH design — basis for D2)
- **RFC 7386: JSON Merge Patch** — https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7386
  (the adopted PATCH convention: absent = no change, `null` = clear, value = set; and its caveat that
  `null` cannot also be a legitimate value — which does not apply to our model).
- **REST: Partial updates with PATCH** — Michael Scharhag —
  https://www.mscharhag.com/api-design/rest-partial-updates-patch

  https://zuplo.com/learning-center/what-is-json-merge-patch
- **Building a Safe Partial-Update API: JSON Patch, Merge Patch, and the Null Problem** —
  https://blog.ipuau.com/en/posts/20260320-building-a-safe-partial-update-api-json-patch-merge-patch-and-the-null-problem.html
- **JSON Patch vs Merge Patch for Partial Updates (Spring Boot)** —
  https://medium.com/@AlexanderObregon/working-with-json-patch-vs-merge-patch-for-partial-updates-in-spring-boot-apis-57377bfe4e5a

### Internal (current implementation — basis for every field/operation mapping)

layer in `crates/kanban-service/src/api/v1/`; exact files and line ranges are cited inline throughout

(`commands/*.rs`); pagination (§2.1) from the live CLI/service list envelope.

cards.description:
Guarantee that a retried POST /v1/commands does not double-apply and -- critically -- does not double-log the audit trail.

PROBLEM: HTTP is at-least-once. A lost ack makes a safe client re-POST the same batch. Entity state is naturally idempotent (client-supplied UUIDs, absolute-state mutations, max-style counter bump at card_commands.rs:225), so re-applying state is harmless. But append_batch is NOT idempotent -- it adds a row every call. A retry therefore double-logs the audit trail even though state stays correct.

SOLUTION (dedup the request at the server, BEFORE execute()):
- Client sends an idempotency key = the batch correlation_id, reused verbatim on retry (not regenerated).
- Server keeps a bounded, evictable key store (in-memory LRU, or a small table with TTL). This is the server request layer's own mechanism; it is NOT the audit log.
- Key HIT  -> skip execute() entirely; return the original result. State untouched, log untouched. No double anything.
- Key MISS -> run execute() once (one transaction: state mutation + single append_batch), then record the key.

EXPLICITLY NOT: correlation_id UNIQUE in the audit log. That mutates state then fails the log insert on the constraint, rolls back the whole tx, and returns an error instead of a clean already-done replay. It couples command-application correctness to log storage and makes the log load-bearing. The audit log stays dumb -- it appends exactly what it is handed and never participates in dedup.

SCOPE: only meaningful once the HTTP server + POST /v1/commands exist; the local TUI/CLI/MCP path has no retries (one action = one execute = one log entry). Do not build until then. Depends on KAN-689 (server scaffold) and KAN-695 (POST /v1/commands endpoint).
cards.title: feat(server): request-level idempotency for POST /v1/commands (no double-logging on retry)

## Motivation
When kanban-http-backend was scaffolded (KAN-742), tokio-tungstenite was added as a dependency in anticipation of WebSocket-based push notifications from kanban-server. During sprint 19 planning, the transport decision was revised: the server will use SSE (Server-Sent Events) for push, not WebSocket. SSE is unidirectional (server to client), sufficient for kanban change notifications, simpler to implement, and works through any HTTP proxy without special handling.

tokio-tungstenite is now unused and untargeted by any planned card. KAN-701 (WebSocketChangeDetector) was the only card that would have consumed it -- that card has been superseded by KAN-749, which covers SSE-based push via subscribe_changes() on KanbanBackend.

## Change
Remove tokio-tungstenite from crates/kanban-http-backend/Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock.

## Offender
crates/kanban-http-backend/Cargo.toml:
```toml
[dependencies]
tokio-tungstenite = { workspace = true }  # unused -- remove
```

## Acceptance criteria
- tokio-tungstenite removed from kanban-http-backend/Cargo.toml
- Cargo.lock updated
- cargo check --package kanban-http-backend passes clean
- No other crate in the workspace references tokio-tungstenite for http-backend purposes

## Related
- KAN-701 (superseded WebSocketChangeDetector card)
- KAN-749 (SSE-based push via subscribe_changes -- the replacement)
- KAN-748 (HttpBackend implementation -- will use reqwest SSE streaming, not tungstenite)

cards.description:
# RE-SCOPED (2026-06-30) to the JSON conflict flow (see KAN-803 finding). The pure Snapshot x Snapshot diff is backend-agnostic; its CONSUMER is now the JSON whole-snapshot conflict dialog (JSON caches an in-memory snapshot and saves wholesale, so mine=cached snapshot, theirs=on-disk file genuinely diverge). No longer tied to SQLite/KAN-806.

---
Context: KAN-803 / informed conflict dialog. The detection side (KAN-806) is coarse — the version CAS only knows "the store moved." To make the conflict window LEGIBLE and ACTIONABLE, we need to compute WHAT actually differs between the user's in-memory state and the now-current on-disk state. This card is the pure, testable diff; the TUI rendering is its sibling.

Current state:
- On a stale save, SqliteStore::save returns PersistenceError::ConflictDetected (KAN-806). It carries no detail about what conflicts.
- Snapshot (kanban-domain) holds boards/columns/cards/sprints/archived_cards/graph as flat collections. Two Snapshots are fully comparable.

Target: a pure function in kanban-domain:
  pub struct FieldConflict { pub entity_kind: EntityKind, pub entity_id: Uuid, pub entity_label: String, pub field: String, pub mine: String, pub theirs: String }
  pub fn diff_snapshots(mine: &Snapshot, theirs: &Snapshot) -> Vec<FieldConflict>
- 2-WAY diff (mine vs theirs), NOT 3-way. Sufficient for "show what differs, let the user choose"; 3-way/overlap-awareness is Phase B (merge) and out of scope.
- entity_label is HUMAN-LEGIBLE: card -> "#<card_number> <title>", board -> name, column -> name, sprint -> resolved name. NEVER a bare UUID.
- Report per differing FIELD (e.g. card.status, board.name), plus added/removed entities (entity present on one side only -> a Created/Deleted FieldConflict).
- Stable ordering (by entity_kind then label) so the rendered list is deterministic.

Step-by-step (TDD):
1. Red: test_diff_same_snapshots_is_empty; test_diff_changed_card_field_reports_field_mine_theirs; test_diff_added_entity_reports_created; test_diff_removed_entity_reports_deleted; test_entity_label_is_human_legible_not_uuid.
2. Green: implement diff_snapshots (iterate each collection, match by id, compare fields).
3. Refactor.

Acceptance: empty diff for identical snapshots; every differing field surfaced with legible label + mine/theirs; added/removed entities reported; deterministic order; clippy -D warnings + fmt green; pure (no I/O).
Dependencies: none (pure). Consumed by the TUI card. Conceptually follows KAN-806.
cards.title: feat(domain): snapshot field-level diff for conflict reporting

cards.description:
Context: KAN-803. REFRAMED 2026-06-30 from "per-row OCC" after a 5-agent research pass (empirical branch conc-research, commit f785f56c). The dominant SQLite same-entity lost-update is an artifact of the WHOLE-ROW write shape, NOT a concurrency-control gap — and it's fixable cheaply by writing only the changed columns. This is also just cleaner persistence (write what changed, not the whole row), valuable even with zero concurrency. Per-row OCC is DEFERRED (see Residual).

Current state:
- UpdateCard::execute (crates/kanban-domain/src/commands/card/lifecycle.rs:17-27): get_card -> card.update(self.updates, now) -> context.store.upsert_card(card). The store exposes ONLY whole-row upsert_card (data_store.rs:209); write_card_with_conn (entities/card.rs:32) is `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET <every column>=excluded.<col>`. So editing ONE field rewrites the WHOLE row from a possibly-stale in-memory base.
- Consequence (empirically confirmed, conc-research): two concurrent edits to the SAME card on DIFFERENT fields clobber each other (whole-row last-writer-wins). A field-targeted UPDATE makes both survive.
- CardUpdate already carries per-field intent (FieldUpdate::Set/Clear/NoChange), so a targeted writer is derivable from it.

Target: make entity UPDATES field-targeted (CREATE stays whole-row).
- Add a targeted update path on the store: build `UPDATE cards SET <only the changed cols>, updated_at=? WHERE id=?` from the XUpdate's set of touched fields (or a XUpdate-aware store method). Same for Board/Column/Sprint updates.
- Change the domain update commands (UpdateCard / UpdateBoard / UpdateColumn / UpdateSprint) to emit only touched columns instead of upsert_card(whole entity).
- Keep whole-row upsert for CREATE (new row). Only the UPDATE path goes field-targeted.
- JSON backend: per-field mutation already happens in-memory; the whole-file save is unaffected. So this is primarily a SQLite write-path + domain-command change.

Benefit: concurrent different-field edits to the same entity MERGE for free (the common same-entity case); writes are smaller and intention-revealing. A concurrency-independent persistence improvement.

RESIDUAL (deferred, probably not worth it): same-FIELD true conflict (two writers set the SAME field) stays last-writer-wins. Only a per-row version + CAS (OCC) catches it. NOTED as a future option, NOT in scope here — rare for a single-user tool, and true multi-writer is the server's job (KAN-684, already underway: Arc<RwLock<KanbanContext>> = one writer, no lost updates).

Scope: touches the store/DataStore trait (a targeted-update method), the per-entity UPDATE SQL, and the per-entity domain update commands. LIKELY DECOMPOSE into per-entity slices (Card as the template, then Board/Column/Sprint) — smaller than the dropped OCC epic.
Acceptance: concurrent different-field edits to one entity both survive; create unaffected; same-field stays LWW (documented); TDD per slice; clippy -D warnings + fmt green.
Dependencies: none. Independent of the JSON dialog cards (811/812).
cards.title: feat(persistence): field-targeted entity updates (write only changed columns)

cards.description:
# WHY THIS MATTERS: TRUST, not annoyance (2026-06-30)
Today the JSON conflict dialog asks reload-or-overwrite BLIND — the user cannot know what they will lose, so they either lose work or lose confidence in the tool. And JSON OVER-detects (conflicts even on unrelated changes), so the common case is "nothing of yours is at risk" yet the user cannot tell. The field-level diff makes the choice informed ("you will revert Card #42 status Done -> In Progress") and the empty-diff case ("nothing of yours differs — safe to reload") removes the false alarms that erode trust. This is a correctness-of-trust fix, NOT polish.

---
# RE-SCOPED (2026-06-30) to JSON (see KAN-803 finding). This enriches the EXISTING JSON conflict dialogs (ConflictResolution / ExternalChangeDetected), which fire when JsonFileStore::save detects the file changed since load. mine = JsonDataStore cached snapshot; theirs = on-disk file. Render the diff_snapshots() field-level list; keep whole-snapshot Reload/Overwrite (now informed); empty-diff suppresses the dialog. OVERWRITE re-saves after adopting the on-disk FileMetadata as the new last-known (JSON path), not a version. Depends on KAN-811 ONLY (NOT the dropped SQLite cards 806/809).

---
Context: KAN-803 / informed conflict dialog. Make the conflict window show WHAT conflicts and let the user act on it. Consumes the diff from the sibling diff card; depends on the SQLite dialog wiring (KAN-809).

Current state:
- TUI conflict UX exists: render_conflict_resolution_popup (Overwrite / Take-theirs / Retry) and render_external_change_detected_popup (Reload / Keep) in conflict_popup.rs; handlers dialog_handlers.rs:458-499; conflict opens on save returning KanbanError::ConflictDetected (lifecycle.rs:186) or a poller event while dirty.
- Today the dialog is a generic "the file changed" message with NO detail about what changed.

Target: when a conflict fires, enrich the dialog with the field-level diff.
- On ConflictDetected (or external-change-while-dirty), the TUI loads the now-current on-disk Snapshot and runs diff_snapshots(in_memory, on_disk) (the sibling card) at the PRESENTATION tier. Persistence error stays simple (layering: persistence stays dumb; the diff + render live in the TUI).
- Render a LEGIBLE, scrollable list: "<entity_label> · <field>: you=<mine>, file=<theirs>" (e.g. Card #42 "Fix login" · status: you=Done, file=In Progress). Truncate/scroll when long.
- Actions stay WHOLE-SNAPSHOT and unambiguous, now informed by the diff: Reload (take the file, discard mine) / Overwrite (force mine over the file). Per-field resolution is Phase B (merge), out of scope.
- OVERWRITE-BEATS-CAS: "Overwrite" adopts the current on-disk version as the CAS baseline (the value just loaded for the diff) then saves, so the forced write lands. Leans on KAN-806 version tracking.
- BONUS (cheap "don't go loud unless real"): if diff_snapshots returns EMPTY (their write didn't actually differ from my state), suppress the dialog and silently reconcile (adopt their version as baseline).

Step-by-step (TDD): characterization tests modelled on conflict_popup_tests.rs / conflict_detection_tests.rs:
1. Red: test_conflict_dialog_lists_changed_fields_legibly; test_empty_diff_suppresses_dialog; test_overwrite_adopts_current_version_then_saves_succeeds; test_reload_discards_local_and_takes_file.
2. Green: wire load+diff at conflict time, render the list, implement overwrite-beats-CAS + empty-diff suppression.
3. Refactor.

Acceptance: conflict window shows the differing fields with legible labels + mine/theirs; Reload and Overwrite both work and are unambiguous; empty diff never pops; clippy/fmt green.
Dependencies: the diff card (logic), KAN-806 (version baseline for overwrite), KAN-809 (SQLite dialog wiring).
cards.title: feat(tui): field-level conflict detail in the resolution dialog (legible, actionable)

cards.description:
## Background

Distribute `kanban` via the **Windows Package Manager (winget)**, Microsoft's
first-party, in-box package manager shipped with Windows 10/11. winget is the
sibling Windows registry to Chocolatey (KAN-537): Chocolatey covers the
community-tooling crowd, winget covers everyone who has Windows out of the box
and runs `winget install`. Together they give Windows users a first-class
install path instead of hand-downloading a release zip.

This card is the umbrella for all winget work, scoped narrowly to one registry.
It is the parallel sibling to **KAN-537 (Chocolatey)** and supersedes the winget
section of **KAN-452**. Mirror KAN-537's structural style where applicable.

## Deliverable shape

```powershell
winget install fulsomenko.kanban
# or pin a version
winget install fulsomenko.kanban --version 0.7.2
```

End state:

- A `fulsomenko.kanban` package exists in the **microsoft/winget-pkgs**
  community repository.
- Each upstream release (driven by `release.yml`) auto-opens a PR to
  winget-pkgs with the new version's manifests. Microsoft's automated
  validation + maintainer review merges it (typically hours-to-days; the
  first-ever submission of a brand-new package is the slow one).
- The winget package downloads the **existing** official Windows release
  archive from GitHub at install time and verifies it against an embedded
  SHA256. winget unpacks the zip and registers both binaries as portable
  command aliases.

## Key difference from Chocolatey: manifests live upstream

Unlike Chocolatey (where we `choco push` a `.nupkg` to community.chocolatey.org),
winget manifests are **YAML files that live in `microsoft/winget-pkgs`**, under
a partitioned path:

```
manifests/f/fulsomenko/kanban/<version>/
  fulsomenko.kanban.yaml                 # version manifest
  fulsomenko.kanban.installer.yaml       # installer manifest
  fulsomenko.kanban.locale.en-US.yaml    # default-locale manifest
```

We cannot host the canonical manifest in our own repo. The in-repo
`packaging/winget/` directory is a **dev/staging template** (with `$version$` /
`$sha256$` placeholders) used for local validation and as the source the CI
generator fills in. The real submission is a **pull request to a fork of
microsoft/winget-pkgs**, opened automatically by the
`vedantmgoyal9/winget-releaser` GitHub Action on each release.

Reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/package-manager/package/

## Installer model: zip + nested portable, BOTH binaries

The existing `build-windows` job in `release.yml` already produces and uploads
`kanban-v$VERSION-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip` (+ `SHA256SUMS`) on every release
(`release.yml:243-307`). That zip contains **two** executables: `kanban.exe`
and `kanban-mcp.exe` (plus `LICENSE.md`, `README.md`). So:

- **No Windows-archive prerequisite** for winget — it reuses the asset
  Chocolatey already relies on. (This is why winget is lighter than KAN-537,
  which had to add the archive job as a prereq.)
- The installer manifest uses `InstallerType: zip` with
  `NestedInstallerType: portable`, and declares **both** nested files so winget
  registers both command aliases:

```yaml
NestedInstallerType: portable
NestedInstallerFiles:
  - RelativeFilePath: kanban.exe
    PortableCommandAlias: kanban
  - RelativeFilePath: kanban-mcp.exe
    PortableCommandAlias: kanban-mcp
```

NOTE: the draft in KAN-452 only aliased `kanban.exe` — that is a bug; we ship
two binaries and Chocolatey installs both, so winget must too.

## Identifier and metadata (DECIDED)

- **PackageIdentifier:** `fulsomenko.kanban` (Publisher.Package; matches the
  GitHub org and the KAN-452 draft). Rationale: stable, matches `owners` in the
  Chocolatey nuspec; the publisher folder `manifests/f/fulsomenko/` is created
  on first submission and reused forever.
- **License:** `Apache-2.0` (SPDX), matching the AUR PKGBUILD and the repo
  `LICENSE.md`. (NB: the choco nuspec uses a `licenseUrl`; winget wants the SPDX
  identifier in `License` plus a `LicenseUrl`.)
- **ManifestVersion:** pin to the schema the chosen `winget-releaser` version
  emits (currently the 1.x line, e.g. `1.6.0`); let the action own the exact
  value rather than hand-pinning and drifting.
- **Automation tool (DECIDED):** `vedantmgoyal9/winget-releaser` GitHub Action,
  not raw `wingetcreate`. It handles manifest generation, the winget-pkgs fork
  sync, PR creation, and the PAT dance. `wingetcreate` stays the documented
  manual fallback in the recovery runbook.

## Subtask breakdown (each is its own child card)

1. **packaging/winget/ skeleton** — author the three manifest templates
   (version + installer + defaultLocale) for zip/portable-nested with both
   binaries; document local `winget validate` + Windows Sandbox smoke test.
2. **Fork winget-pkgs + WINGET_TOKEN secret** — fork `microsoft/winget-pkgs`
   under `fulsomenko/`, mint a classic PAT with `public_repo` scope, add it as
   the `WINGET_TOKEN` repo secret.
3. **release.yml: winget publish job** — add a `winget-releaser`-driven job,
   gated on `has_changesets`, that opens the upstream PR on each release.
   Depends on (1) and (2).
4. **Initial submission + verify** — one-time first PR of the current version to
   microsoft/winget-pkgs (the slow, brand-new-package review), then verify
   `winget install fulsomenko.kanban` from a clean Windows box / Sandbox.
5. **Docs + RECOVERY runbook** — `packaging/winget/README.md`, a
   `packaging/winget/RECOVERY.md` runbook for PR-failure modes, a row in the
   top-level `packaging/README.md` table, and the winget install line in the
   project README + CONTRIBUTING maintainer playbook.

Suggested execution order: (1) and (2) in parallel (no inter-dependency). (3)
depends on both. (4) depends on (1) producing valid manifests; the *automated*
path of (4) depends on (3), but the first submission can be done manually with
`wingetcreate` if we want winget live before the CI job lands. (5) can be
drafted alongside (1) and finalized once (4) produces a real, installable
package.

## Maintenance burden expectations

- **Per-release work:** zero in the steady state. `winget-releaser` regenerates
  manifests (version + SHA256 from the GitHub release asset) and opens the PR
  automatically; Microsoft's bot validates and a maintainer merges.
- **Review lag:** the first-ever submission of a new package is the slow one
  (manual maintainer attention, can take days). Subsequent version-bump PRs are
  usually validated and merged within hours when the manifest is well-formed and
  the installer URL/SHA resolve.
- **Fork drift:** the `fulsomenko/winget-pkgs` fork must stay roughly current
  with upstream `master`; `winget-releaser` rebases, but a very stale fork can
  cause PR conflicts. Covered in the recovery runbook.
- **CVE / security:** ship a new release with the fix; the next
  `winget-releaser` run carries it upstream like any other version.

## Out of scope (separate cards if/when)

- **arm64 / x86 winget installers** — we only build x86_64 Windows today; add
  architectures here once the build matrix produces them.
- **MSIX / signed installer** — we ship an unsigned portable zip; code signing
  and an MSIX path are a separate effort (also removes SmartScreen warnings).
- **Bundling shell completions / man pages** into the winget package — initial
  release ships only the two binaries + LICENSE.
- **Migrating to a winget DSC / configuration** surface.
- **Polling for PR merge in CI** — the initial submission verification is
  manual; file a follow-up if friction grows.

## Related

- **KAN-537** — Chocolatey umbrella; the structural template for this card.
  Mirror its child-card breakdown, gating idioms, and recovery-runbook style.
- **KAN-452** — superseded for the winget portion; this card is the new home.
- **KAN-539 / build-windows job** — produces the Windows zip asset winget
  reuses; do not duplicate it.
- **KAN-541** — Chocolatey publish step; reuse its `has_changesets` gating and
  the `Read Windows ZIP digest from GitHub Release` asset-readiness pattern if a
  SHA is needed before the release asset is fully uploaded.

cards.description:
## Context / why

Child of the winget umbrella (see parent epic). This card authors the in-repo
**dev/staging manifest templates** that the winget CI job (sibling card) fills
in and submits to `microsoft/winget-pkgs`. Structural analogue of KAN-538
(`packaging/chocolatey/` skeleton). winget manifests cannot canonically live in
our repo — these are templates with placeholders, used for local validation and
as the source the generator consumes.

Reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/package-manager/package/manifest

## Current state (researched)

- `packaging/` exists with `aur/` and `chocolatey/` siblings; the top-level
  `packaging/README.md` table lists AUR + Chocolatey. No `winget/` yet.
- The Windows release asset already exists:
  `kanban-v$VERSION-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip`, built and uploaded by the
  `build-windows` job (`.github/workflows/release.yml:243-307`). It contains
  `kanban.exe`, `kanban-mcp.exe`, `LICENSE.md`, `README.md`.
- Chocolatey installs **both** binaries
  (`packaging/chocolatey/tools/chocolateyinstall.ps1` unzips the whole archive);
  winget must match that and alias both.
- License is `Apache-2.0` (`packaging/aur/PKGBUILD:8`, repo `LICENSE.md`).

## Target

Create `packaging/winget/` with the three multi-file manifest templates under
the partitioned path winget-pkgs expects:

```
packaging/winget/manifests/f/fulsomenko/kanban/
  fulsomenko.kanban.yaml                 # version manifest
  fulsomenko.kanban.installer.yaml       # installer manifest
  fulsomenko.kanban.locale.en-US.yaml    # default-locale manifest
```

### Version manifest — `fulsomenko.kanban.yaml`

```yaml
PackageIdentifier: fulsomenko.kanban
PackageVersion: $version$
DefaultLocale: en-US
ManifestType: version
ManifestVersion: 1.6.0
```

### Default-locale manifest — `fulsomenko.kanban.locale.en-US.yaml`

```yaml
PackageIdentifier: fulsomenko.kanban
PackageVersion: $version$
PackageLocale: en-US
Publisher: fulsomenko
PublisherUrl: https://github.com/fulsomenko
PublisherSupportUrl: https://github.com/fulsomenko/kanban/issues
Author: Max Emil Yoon Blomstervall
PackageName: kanban
PackageUrl: https://github.com/fulsomenko/kanban
License: Apache-2.0
LicenseUrl: https://github.com/fulsomenko/kanban/blob/master/LICENSE.md
Copyright: 2025 Max Emil Yoon Blomstervall
ShortDescription: Fast, keyboard-driven terminal kanban board (with MCP server)
Description: |-
  A terminal-based kanban / project management tool written in Rust, inspired by
  lazygit's interface design. Provides a fast, keyboard-driven UI for tracking
  tasks across boards, columns, and sprints. Stores data in a portable JSON or
  SQLite file. Ships two binaries: `kanban` (the TUI / CLI) and `kanban-mcp`
  (a Model Context Protocol server for LLM integrations).
Moniker: kanban
Tags:
  - kanban
  - tui
  - terminal
  - productivity
  - rust
  - mcp
ReleaseNotesUrl: https://github.com/fulsomenko/kanban/releases/tag/v$version$
ManifestType: defaultLocale
ManifestVersion: 1.6.0
```

### Installer manifest — `fulsomenko.kanban.installer.yaml`

```yaml
PackageIdentifier: fulsomenko.kanban
PackageVersion: $version$
InstallerType: zip
NestedInstallerType: portable
NestedInstallerFiles:
  - RelativeFilePath: kanban-v$version$-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc\kanban.exe
    PortableCommandAlias: kanban
  - RelativeFilePath: kanban-v$version$-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc\kanban-mcp.exe
    PortableCommandAlias: kanban-mcp
Installers:
  - Architecture: x64
    InstallerUrl: https://github.com/fulsomenko/kanban/releases/download/v$version$/kanban-v$version$-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip
    InstallerSha256: $sha256$
ManifestType: installer
ManifestVersion: 1.6.0
```

**Critical: verify `RelativeFilePath` against the actual zip layout.**
`Compress-Archive -Path "stage/$name/*"` (`release.yml:289`) zips the *contents*
of the staged folder, so the exes are likely at the archive root
(`kanban.exe`), NOT under a `kanban-v.../` subfolder. Confirm by inspecting a
real release asset and set `RelativeFilePath` accordingly (root: `kanban.exe`).
Getting this wrong makes winget fail to find the nested binaries at install
time. This is the single highest-risk field in the card — validate it against a
downloaded asset before submitting.

## Step-by-step (TDD-adapted for a manifest/packaging card)

1. **Red (validation as the test):** download a real published release asset,
   extract it, and record the exact internal paths of `kanban.exe` /
   `kanban-mcp.exe`. Write the three manifests with a concrete version + real
   SHA256 substituted (not placeholders) into a scratch copy.
2. **Green:** run `winget validate --manifest <scratch dir>` until it passes
   with no errors. Then run the Windows Sandbox manifest test (see below) and
   confirm both `kanban --version` and `kanban-mcp --version` work after a
   `winget install --manifest`.
3. **Refactor:** restore the `$version$` / `$sha256$` placeholders in the
   committed templates; ensure they exactly match the substitution tokens the
   CI job (sibling card) will replace. Keep each file < 100 chars/line per the
   winget style guidance.

## Local validation / smoke test (document in the card output, mirror choco README)

```powershell
# Schema + reachability validation (placeholders must be substituted first):
winget validate --manifest packaging\winget\manifests\f\fulsomenko\kanban

# Full install test in Windows Sandbox (winget-pkgs provides the harness):
#   https://github.com/microsoft/winget-pkgs/blob/master/doc/tools/SandboxTest.md
.\Tools\SandboxTest.ps1 packaging\winget\manifests\f\fulsomenko\kanban
winget install --manifest packaging\winget\manifests\f\fulsomenko\kanban
kanban --version
kanban-mcp --version
```

## Tests

- `test_winget_manifests_validate_clean` — `winget validate` exits 0 on the
  substituted manifests (manual gate; record the output in the PR).
- `test_winget_install_registers_both_aliases` — after
  `winget install --manifest`, both `kanban` and `kanban-mcp` resolve on PATH in
  a clean Sandbox.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `packaging/winget/manifests/f/fulsomenko/kanban/` contains the three
      manifest templates above.
- [ ] `RelativeFilePath` matches the real zip layout (verified against a
      downloaded asset).
- [ ] Both `kanban` and `kanban-mcp` are declared as portable command aliases.
- [ ] Substituted manifests pass `winget validate` with zero errors.
- [ ] Sandbox install registers both aliases; `--version` works for both.
- [ ] Placeholder tokens (`$version$`, `$sha256$`) match the CI job's
      substitution contract (coordinate with the release.yml winget-job card).
- [ ] Files committed with placeholders, NOT substituted values.

## Dependencies / sequencing

- No code dependency; parallel with the fork+token card.
- Coordinate the placeholder-token contract with the `release.yml` winget-job
  card (sibling) so substitution matches.
- The `License: Apache-2.0` SPDX id and `LicenseUrl` must agree with the repo
  LICENSE.md.

## Quirks

- winget keys are PascalCase and must not be duplicated.
- `ManifestVersion` should match what the chosen `winget-releaser` version
  emits; if it differs from `1.6.0`, align all three files to that value.
- winget rejects manifests whose `InstallerSha256` does not match the byte
  content at `InstallerUrl` — the SHA must be the zip's SHA256, the same value
  `SHA256SUMS` already records in the release.

cards.description:
## Stakeholders

- **Windows users who prefer winget** — `winget` ships in-box on Windows 10 1709+ and Windows 11. It is the default discovery surface for a large class of Windows developers who never touch Chocolatey. Today they can only get kanban via the Chocolatey package or by hand-unzipping the GitHub Release archive.
- **Release manager (Max)** — owns one more distribution channel that must stay in lockstep with the version that crates.io / AUR / Homebrew / Chocolatey ship. The channel should publish automatically from the same release pipeline, not as a manual side-task.
- **Anyone evaluating kanban's "install everywhere" story** — winget is the conspicuous gap in an otherwise complete matrix (crates.io, AUR, Homebrew, Chocolatey, raw GitHub ZIP).

## Where

- `.github/workflows/release.yml:243-307` — `build-windows` job already builds and uploads the exact artifact winget will consume: `kanban-v$VERSION-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip` (containing `kanban.exe`, `kanban-mcp.exe`, `LICENSE.md`, `README.md` at the archive root) plus `SHA256SUMS`, attached to the v$VERSION GitHub Release.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml:309-445` — `publish-chocolatey` job is the structural template to mirror: it `needs: [release, build-windows]`, polls the GitHub Release for the ZIP asset and reads its `digest` (the same SHA256 winget needs), is `continue-on-error: true` (moderation is async), and has a pre-check that makes re-runs idempotent.
- `packaging/chocolatey/` — the structural sibling for a new `packaging/winget/` directory (templated manifests + README + smoke-test notes).
- `packaging/README.md:7-10` — the packager index table; add a `winget` / Windows row.
- No existing winget setup: `grep -ri winget` across the repo returns nothing, and `packaging/winget/` does not exist. This is greenfield.

## Why

winget consumes a manifest, not a binary, and that manifest lives in a **separate public repo** (`microsoft/winget-pkgs`) rather than in this repo. Publishing is a PR into that repo that then goes through automated validation + human/bot moderation. So unlike Chocolatey (push a `.nupkg` to a feed) the deliverable here is:

1. A set of YAML manifest files describing the package, pointing at the already-published GitHub Release ZIP.
2. A PR submitting those manifests to `microsoft/winget-pkgs` for **every** new version.

The kanban Windows ZIP is a portable archive (two `.exe`s, no installer), which maps cleanly to winget's `InstallerType: zip` + `NestedInstallerType: portable` shape — winget extracts the zip and registers `kanban` / `kanban-mcp` as portable command aliases on the user's PATH. No MSI/installer authoring is required, which keeps this small.

The right automation is Microsoft's first-party `wingetcreate` tool: given the new version and the ZIP URL it downloads the archive, computes the SHA256, rewrites the version + installer manifests from the previous version's manifest, validates against the schema, and opens the PR — all headless with a GitHub PAT. That makes the per-release cost one CI step, mirroring `publish-chocolatey`.

## Package facts (grounded)

- **PackageIdentifier**: `Fulsomenko.Kanban` (winget `Publisher.Package` convention; publisher folder `Fulsomenko` matches the GitHub org `fulsomenko`).
- **Manifest path in winget-pkgs**: `manifests/f/Fulsomenko/Kanban/<version>/` with three files:
  - `Fulsomenko.Kanban.yaml` (ManifestType: version)
  - `Fulsomenko.Kanban.installer.yaml` (ManifestType: installer)
  - `Fulsomenko.Kanban.locale.en-US.yaml` (ManifestType: defaultLocale)
- **License**: `Apache-2.0` (confirmed from `LICENSE.md`), LicenseUrl `https://github.com/fulsomenko/kanban/blob/master/LICENSE.md`.
- **Installer URL pattern**: `https://github.com/fulsomenko/kanban/releases/download/v$VERSION/kanban-v$VERSION-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip`.
- **SHA256 source**: identical to what `publish-chocolatey` already reads — the GitHub Release asset `digest` (`release.yml:322-353`), or recomputed by `wingetcreate` from the downloaded URL.
- **Nested binaries** (zip root, per `release.yml:269-289`): `kanban.exe` → alias `kanban`; `kanban-mcp.exe` → alias `kanban-mcp`.
- **Schema**: `ManifestVersion: 1.12.0` (current at time of writing; let `wingetcreate` pin the schema it validates against rather than hard-coding a stale version).

## How

Three phases: author the seed manifests, get the first version accepted manually, then automate every subsequent release.

### Phase 1 — author the seed manifests (committed under `packaging/winget/`)

Keep a source-of-truth copy of the manifests in this repo (the way `packaging/chocolatey/` keeps the nuspec), even though the canonical published copy lives in `microsoft/winget-pkgs`. Use `$version$` / `$sha256$` placeholders so CI can substitute, exactly like `chocolateyinstall.ps1`.

`packaging/winget/Fulsomenko.Kanban.installer.yaml`:
```yaml
PackageIdentifier: Fulsomenko.Kanban
PackageVersion: $version$
InstallerType: zip
NestedInstallerType: portable
NestedInstallerFiles:
  - RelativeFilePath: kanban.exe
    PortableCommandAlias: kanban
  - RelativeFilePath: kanban-mcp.exe
    PortableCommandAlias: kanban-mcp
Installers:
  - Architecture: x64
    InstallerUrl: https://github.com/fulsomenko/kanban/releases/download/v$version$/kanban-v$version$-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip
    InstallerSha256: $sha256$
ManifestType: installer
ManifestVersion: 1.12.0
```

`packaging/winget/Fulsomenko.Kanban.locale.en-US.yaml`:
```yaml
PackageIdentifier: Fulsomenko.Kanban
PackageVersion: $version$
PackageLocale: en-US
Publisher: fulsomenko
PublisherUrl: https://github.com/fulsomenko
PackageName: kanban
PackageUrl: https://github.com/fulsomenko/kanban
License: Apache-2.0
LicenseUrl: https://github.com/fulsomenko/kanban/blob/master/LICENSE.md
Copyright: Copyright 2025 Max Emil Yoon Blomstervall
ShortDescription: Fast, keyboard-driven terminal kanban board (with MCP server)
Description: >-
  A terminal-based kanban / project management tool written in Rust, inspired by
  lazygit. Installs the `kanban` TUI/CLI and the `kanban-mcp` Model Context
  Protocol server for LLM integrations. Stores data in a portable JSON or SQLite file.
Moniker: kanban
Tags:
  - kanban
  - tui
  - terminal
  - productivity
  - rust
  - mcp
  - cli
ManifestType: defaultLocale
ManifestVersion: 1.12.0
```

`packaging/winget/Fulsomenko.Kanban.yaml`:
```yaml
PackageIdentifier: Fulsomenko.Kanban
PackageVersion: $version$
DefaultLocale: en-US
ManifestType: version
ManifestVersion: 1.12.0
```

### Phase 2 — get the first version (0.7.2) accepted manually

The first submission validates the identity, publisher folder, and manifest shape; later automation just bumps versions.

1. On a Windows machine (or Windows CI runner), install the tool: `winget install wingetcreate`.
2. Render the placeholders for the current released version (0.7.2) and its ZIP SHA256 (from `gh release view v0.7.2 --json assets`).
3. Validate locally: `winget validate --manifest <dir>` and, sandboxed, `winget install --manifest <dir>` to confirm both aliases resolve.
4. Submit the PR to `microsoft/winget-pkgs` (via `wingetcreate submit <dir> --token <PAT>` or `wingetcreate new` interactively).
5. Respond to the winget validation bot until the PR merges. Record any reviewer-requested field changes back into the `packaging/winget/` templates so CI inherits them.

### Phase 3 — automate per-release submission (new `publish-winget` job)

Add a job to `release.yml` mirroring `publish-chocolatey`:
```yaml
publish-winget:
  name: Publish to winget
  needs: [release, build-windows]
  if: needs.release.outputs.has_changesets == 'true'
  runs-on: windows-latest
  continue-on-error: true   # winget PR validation + moderation is async, like Chocolatey
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      with:
        ref: v${{ needs.release.outputs.new }}
    - name: Submit manifest update to winget-pkgs
      shell: pwsh
      env:
        VERSION: ${{ needs.release.outputs.new }}
        WINGET_PAT: ${{ secrets.WINGET_PAT }}
      run: |
        $zip = "https://github.com/fulsomenko/kanban/releases/download/v$env:VERSION/kanban-v$env:VERSION-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip"
        # wingetcreate downloads the URL, computes the SHA256, clones the prior
        # manifest, bumps the version, validates, and opens the winget-pkgs PR.
        wingetcreate update Fulsomenko.Kanban `
          --version $env:VERSION `
          --urls "$zip" `
          --submit `
          --token $env:WINGET_PAT
```
Notes:
- New secret `WINGET_PAT`: a GitHub PAT with `public_repo` scope (used to fork `microsoft/winget-pkgs` and open the PR). Document its lineage the way the deploy-key rotation is documented for Homebrew.
- `wingetcreate update` only works once Phase 2 has landed at least one accepted version (it diffs from the prior manifest). Order matters: the job is a no-op-failure until the first manual submission exists.
- `continue-on-error: true` so a winget validation hiccup never blocks the rest of the release, consistent with `publish-chocolatey`.

### Phase 4 — docs

- Add a `packaging/winget/README.md` (per-package release flow + local `winget validate` smoke-test), mirroring `packaging/chocolatey/README.md`.
- Add a `winget` / Windows row to `packaging/README.md`.
- Add the winget `winget install Fulsomenko.Kanban` line to the project README's install section.

## Tests / verification

This is packaging + CI; the "tests" are validation and smoke installs, mirroring how `publish-chocolatey` is verified (it has no unit tests, it has a `Smoke install from local nupkg` step).

- `test_winget_manifest_validates` (manual/CI): `winget validate --manifest packaging/winget` (after placeholder substitution) exits 0 against schema 1.12.0.
- `test_winget_install_registers_both_aliases` (manual, sandbox): `winget install --manifest <dir>` then `kanban --version` and `kanban-mcp --version` both succeed — proving the `NestedInstallerFiles` RelativeFilePaths match the actual zip layout (`kanban.exe`, `kanban-mcp.exe` at root).
- CI gate: the `publish-winget` job's `wingetcreate update` step performs schema validation before it submits; a malformed manifest fails the step.
- Optionally add a lightweight repo-side YAML lint of `packaging/winget/*.yaml` to PR CI so template drift is caught before release time (cf. KAN-669 adding Windows/choco jobs to PR CI).

## Acceptance criteria

- `packaging/winget/` holds the three placeholder manifest files (version, installer, defaultLocale) with `$version$` / `$sha256$` substitution points.
- `Fulsomenko.Kanban` exists in `microsoft/winget-pkgs` for at least the current release; `winget install Fulsomenko.Kanban` installs both `kanban` and `kanban-mcp` and they run.
- `release.yml` has a `publish-winget` job (`needs: [release, build-windows]`, `continue-on-error: true`) that submits a winget-pkgs PR on every changeset-bearing release using `wingetcreate` + the `WINGET_PAT` secret.
- `WINGET_PAT` secret created and documented.
- `winget validate` passes on the rendered manifests; both portable aliases resolve in a sandbox install.
- `packaging/README.md` and `packaging/winget/README.md` document the channel; project README install section lists the winget command.

## Dependencies / sequencing

- Hard dependency on the `build-windows` job's ZIP + SHA256 (already shipping, `release.yml:243-307`). No code change to that job is needed; winget reads the same asset Chocolatey does.
- Phase 3 automation cannot run until Phase 2's first manual submission is accepted (`wingetcreate update` diffs from an existing manifest).
- Independent of the Homebrew/Chocolatey cards; it is the same "finish the Windows distribution story" theme as KAN-a0a7db14 (now archived) but a distinct, additive channel.

## Risks

- **winget-pkgs PR moderation latency / bot rejections.** First submission can bounce on publisher-folder casing, manifest-version, or description-length rules. Mitigation: `wingetcreate`/`winget validate` locally first; fold reviewer feedback into the `packaging/winget/` templates.
- **`NestedInstallerFiles` path mismatch.** If the ZIP layout ever changes (e.g. a future job nests the exes under a subfolder), the RelativeFilePath breaks and installs fail silently-ish. Mitigation: the sandbox install test pins this; keep the manifest co-located with the build job so a layout change is an obvious co-edit. Note the current zip has the exes at **root** because `Compress-Archive -Path "stage/$name/*"` archives contents, not the wrapping folder (`release.yml:285-289`).
- **PAT scope / expiry.** `WINGET_PAT` expiring silently makes the job fail (soft, due to `continue-on-error`), so a release could ship without updating winget unnoticed. Mitigation: document the credential lineage; consider a visible-failure surfacing step like `publish-chocolatey`'s `Surface chocolatey failure`.
- **One PR per version rule.** winget allows only one open PR per package version; a re-run after a partial failure can collide. Mitigation: `wingetcreate` is generally idempotent per version, but document the manual recovery (close/supersede the stale PR) in `packaging/winget/README.md`, mirroring `packaging/chocolatey/RECOVERY.md`.

## Out of scope

- arm64 / x86 Windows builds — the pipeline only produces `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`. A second architecture is a separate card (it would add an `Installers:` entry).
- MSI / installer authoring — the portable-zip path is sufficient and simplest.
- Auto-merging winget PRs or self-hosting a manifest mirror.
- Migrating Chocolatey off — winget is additive, both channels coexist.

## Sizing

~3pt. The manifest authoring is small and well-specified; the real cost is the first-submission round-trip with the winget-pkgs validation bot (async, a few days of latency) and wiring + testing the `publish-winget` CI job against the existing Windows artifact.

## References

- Microsoft: [Submit packages to winget](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/package-manager/package/) and [Create your package manifest](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/package-manager/package/manifest) (schema 1.12.0).
- `microsoft/winget-pkgs` (submission target) and `microsoft/winget-create` (`wingetcreate`).
- `.github/workflows/release.yml:243-307` (build-windows, the artifact source) and `:309-445` (publish-chocolatey, the job template to mirror).
- `packaging/chocolatey/` (structural sibling) and `packaging/chocolatey/RECOVERY.md` (recovery-doc pattern).
- KAN-a0a7db14 (archived) — "Ship 0.7.1 distribution", the broader Windows-distribution context this completes.
