cards.description:
# feat: board removal + reversible board archive, with first-class archived collections

Root epic. Closes #359 (no TUI way to remove a project) and, in the same coherent effort, fixes the "archived things are second-class" design miss project-wide and adds reversible, lossless board archiving.

## Goal

Give users a way to **remove a board from the TUI**, and a way to **archive a board reversibly** (like cards can be archived), while promoting **archived collections to first-class, discrete peer collections** at every level so restoration is lossless and the persistence model stops being parasitic.

## Why now

- #359: the only way to delete a board today is the CLI `kanban board delete`. The service-layer cascade (`kanban-service/src/cascade.rs:10` `delete_board`) is implemented, tested, atomic and fully undoable; only the TUI wiring is missing.
- The existing archived-cards design is parasitic on live cards (see DECIDED D2 evidence). Building board-archive on top of that model would replicate the miss at a larger scale. We fix the model first, then build board-archive on the corrected foundation.

## Core model (target)

**Principle: `archived_X` is a first-class, discrete peer collection to `X` at every level.**

Live collections: `boards`, `columns`, `cards`, `archived_cards`, `sprints`, dependency edges — where `archived_cards` is genuinely discrete (NOT duplicated inside `cards`), and each `ArchivedCard` carries its own `board_id`.

Archived boards are a **discrete collection listed next to `boards`** (distinguished by an `archived_at` marker on the board; in JSON serialized as an `archived_boards` array of the same `Board` type). A board is a **scoping root**: an archived board simply is not in the live board set, so its entire subtree (columns, live cards, archived cards, sprints, edges) is **naturally unreachable from live queries and stays exactly in place, in its own existing first-class normalized tables, untouched**. Restore clears the marker — nothing is torn apart and reconstructed, so restoration respects all state losslessly (sprint assignments, edge active/archived flags, counters, completion column, active sprint). This is the archived-marker design (D3), which supersedes the earlier relational-mirror plan.

```
LIVE (archived_at IS NULL):             ARCHIVED (archived_at IS NOT NULL):
  boards  ─────────────────────────────  same table / same Board type, marker set;
                                          in JSON, partitioned into an archived_boards array
  columns / cards / archived_cards /      UNCHANGED, in place. A board's subtree stays in the
  sprints / edges                         existing first-class tables; excluded from live views
  archived_cards is its own discrete      because its root board is not in the live board set.
  first-class table (has board_id)        Only a few GLOBAL/unscoped queries join board.archived_at.
```

## DECIDED

### D1 — Scope: one epic, three coordinated deliverables
- **(I) TUI permanent board delete** (closes #359) on the existing tested `cascade::delete_board`, with tiered confirmation (empty board = light one-step confirm; non-empty = confirm showing what will be destroyed).
- **(II) Archived-cards first-class retrofit**: promote `ArchivedCard` to a discrete first-class collection with `board_id`, own storage, no duplication in the `cards` table, no `NOT IN` subquery, direct board-scoped queries, no FK cascade orphaning hazard.
- **(III) Reversible board archive (archived-marker, subtree-in-place)**: a board's `archived_at` marker makes it a discrete archived collection while its subtree stays in place in the existing first-class tables; lossless restore by clearing the marker; permanent delete of an archived board via the existing cascade.
- **Rationale**: (II) is the corrected foundation (III) builds on; shipping (III) on the old model would scale the design miss. (I) is independent and ships first for immediate value.

### D2 — First-class principle supersedes the parasitic wrapper design
Supersedes the current `ArchivedCard { card, archived_at, original_column_id, original_position }` wrapper that is parasitic on live cards.
Evidence of the miss (to be removed by the retrofit):
- SQLite writes the archived card into `cards` AND `archived_cards` (`kanban-persistence-sqlite/src/sqlite_store/entities/archived_card.rs:11`); schema comment admits it (`schema.sql:84` "holds both active and archived cards").
- Every live-card query filters `WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT card_id FROM archived_cards)` (`entities/card.rs:126`).
- No `board_id` on `ArchivedCard` (`kanban-domain/src/archived_card.rs:10`); board scoping loads all columns and post-filters (`kanban-domain/src/operations.rs:61`).
- Column deletion would orphan archived cards; only a validation guard prevents it (`commands/column_commands.rs:175`); FK `archived_cards.card_id -> cards(id) ON DELETE CASCADE` (`schema.sql:127`).
- `card.column_id` goes stale in the archived state (`commands/card/lifecycle.rs:308`).
Target: `ArchivedCard` gains `board_id`; column reference becomes an explicit historical `original_column_id` (not a live cascading FK); archived cards get their own complete storage; live-card queries no longer filter against the archive.

### D3 — Board archive storage = archived-marker, subtree-in-place (SUPERSEDES the relational mirror)
**Supersedes** the earlier "relational `archived_board_*` mirror tables" decision. Reason: the mirror re-declares every live entity's columns, so every future schema change to board/column/card/sprint/edge must be applied twice — a recurring maintenance burden and silent-drift risk (SE-C research found it needed ~10 mirror tables). Normalization was never the cost; *duplication* was. The archived-marker design keeps normalization with **one source of truth per entity**:
- The board carries an `archived_at: Option<DateTime>` (+ an archived-ordering field). Archived boards are the discrete collection `archived_at IS NOT NULL`; live boards are `archived_at IS NULL`. In JSON, serialized as a separate `archived_boards` array of the same `Board` type (no new type, no mirror).
- The board's **columns, live cards, archived cards, sprints, and edges stay in their existing first-class tables, untouched.** No `archived_board_*` tables. SQLite change is a single `ALTER TABLE boards ADD COLUMN archived_at` (+ ordering), not ~10 tables.
- **Card/board asymmetry (the principle):** separate the archived collection where co-location forces a *per-row* filter — a **card** is a leaf sharing a live column, so archived cards need their own discrete table (D2, still true). Use an **in-place archived marker** where the entity is a *scoping root* whose descendants are naturally excluded — a **board** is a root, so its subtree needs no mirror and no per-row filter.
- **Bounded cost (honest):** a handful of *global/unscoped* queries (snapshot save, any cross-board "list all cards", cross-board MCP list) must join `board.archived_at` to decide inclusion. One-time audit of a few call sites, not a per-schema-change burden.

### D4 — Lossless restore + undo
Archive = set the board's `archived_at` marker (and record archived ordering). Restore = clear it. Because the subtree is **never moved or reconstructed**, restoration is losslessly perfect by construction — live cards stay live, archived cards stay archived (metadata intact), edges keep their active/archived state, sprints/counters/completion column/active sprint are exactly as they were. Archive, restore, and permanent-delete (permanent delete = the existing `cascade::delete_board` on the archived board) are undoable via the command model. Undo of archive/restore is a trivial marker toggle.

### D5 — Command/undo integration
New `BoardCommand::ArchiveBoard` / `RestoreBoard` (`commands/board_commands.rs:11`) that set / clear the board's `archived_at` marker (and archived ordering). Symmetric inverse (ArchiveBoard⇄RestoreBoard) exploiting `capture_inverse` running before `execute` (`kanban-service/src/context/undo.rs:25`) — no `ImportEntities` payload needed for archive/restore because nothing is moved (a marker toggle). Permanent delete reuses the existing `cascade::delete_board` (already `ImportEntities`-based undo). Batches append to `command_log` as today.

### D6 — DataStore trait extension without breaking the build
New trait methods (board archive: `archive_board`/`restore_board`/`list_archived_boards` toggling/reading the marker; retrofitted board-scoped archived-card methods) are added to the `DataStore` trait (`kanban-domain/src/data_store.rs`). Where a functional default exists (e.g. `list_archived_cards_by_board` filtering the new `board_id` field), use it so every backend stays green. Where none is possible, use a default body returning a new `KanbanError::unsupported` (introduced by F1a — no such error exists today) so the domain slice compiles green and each backend overrides additively. Keeps every slice green at its boundary.

### D7 — Proper migrations (mandated, tested, with backups)
- **JSON**: version constant lives at `kanban-persistence-json/src/json_file_store.rs:312` (`version: 7`) and `kanban-persistence/src/traits.rs:180` (`FormatVersion::MAX = V7`). Two sequential additive bumps: **V7→V8** normalizes archived cards (discrete bucket, add `board_id`, ensure no duplication in `cards`); **V8→V9** adds the `archived_boards` array (same `Board` type, marker set) and the `Board.archived_at` field. Each writes a `.v{N}.backup` (per `migration/backup.rs:17`), older readers default missing fields via `#[serde(default)]` (`kanban-domain/src/snapshot.rs`).
- **SQLite**: `SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION` at `kanban-persistence-sqlite/src/sqlite_store/mod.rs:27` (currently 2). Two sequential bumps: **2→3** creates discrete archived-cards storage and migrates existing archived rows OUT of `cards` (backfilling `board_id` via `original_column_id`→column→board), dropping the `NOT IN` dependency and the cascade hazard; **3→4** is a single `ALTER TABLE boards ADD COLUMN archived_at` (+ archived-ordering column) — no mirror tables (D3). On-open, idempotent, guarded migration steps in `sqlite_store/init.rs:68`.
- Every migration card's acceptance includes a **round-trip test**: old-format fixture → migrate → load → save → reload → assert data-preserving; and a backup-written assertion.

### D8 — TUI UX
- **Keybinding scheme mirrors cards (VALIDATED in the SE-A PR #362):** the primary removal action is the lowercase key on both panels — `d` = delete a board / archive a card (focus-aware). `D` is RESERVED on the boards panel for the archived-boards view (mirroring the cards panel where `D` = toggle archived view); it is a no-op until archival lands. So SE-C wires `d` = archive board, `D` = toggle archived-boards view, and inside that view `r` = restore, `x` = permanent-delete — exactly the card scheme. (SE-A ships board *delete* on `d` as the interim; the archive slice re-homes it per the card model.) New `DialogMode::DeleteBoardConfirm` (`app/mode.rs:19`) mirrors the column-delete flow; `q`/`n`/`Esc` cancel the confirm dialogs (the quit guard excludes them).
- New `AppMode::ArchivedBoardsView` mirroring `ArchivedCardsView` (`app/mode.rs:41`) to list, restore, and permanently delete archived boards. Board archive/restore/permanent-delete are **synchronous** — no board-level animation (the `Archiving`/`Restoring`/`Deleting` animations are keyed by `card_id`), same as column/board delete.
- **Board multi-select is DEFERRED to SE-C (DECIDED — mirror card bulk).** SE-A ships single-board delete only. The archived-cards view already has bulk `v` (select) / `r` (restore-selected) / `x` (delete-selected); the archived-boards view must match. SE-C therefore: generalizes `MultiSelectState` (`app/multi_select.rs`, currently `selected_cards` only) to boards, adds `v` + selection rendering on the boards panel and the archived-boards view, and adds **batch service ops** `delete_boards`/`archive_boards`/`restore_boards` with **atomic undo** (one command batch, like `archive_cards` — NOT a loop of single ops, which would give per-board undo entries). Rationale: boards are few (single-delete covers #359), and the selection generalization + batch ops are work the archive slice does anyway.

### D9 — Bounded shared archival abstraction (reduce card/board duplication)
Card-archive and board-archive share the same lifecycle: **archive** (move entity out of its live collection into a discrete archived collection with an `archived_at` envelope), **restore** (move back, lossless), **permanent-delete** (drop from the archived collection), **scoped list**. Introduce ONE bounded abstraction that captures this shared mechanism and is implemented by both:
- A shared archived-metadata envelope + an `Archivable`/archive-lifecycle trait covering `archive`/`restore`/`permanent_delete`/`list_archived` over a generic entity, so the in-memory store, JSON, and SQLite implement one generic pattern instead of duplicating per entity, and the archive/restore command mechanics are written once.
- **Entity-specific stays specialized** (do not over-abstract, per Phase 7 quality gate): a card's restore context (`board_id`, `original_column_id`, `original_position`) and a board's owned discrete sets (columns / live cards / archived cards / sprints / edges) are NOT forced into a single shape. The abstraction covers the *lifecycle and storage envelope*, not the payload.
- **Cards are the first implementer (SE-B), boards the second (SE-C).** The abstraction is defined in the Foundation card, validated by the SE-C spike (Phase 6) — the second implementer is where a wrong abstraction reveals itself. Collapse/refine if it does not fit; a little duplication beats the wrong abstraction.
- **VALIDATED (both spikes) — COLLAPSE `ArchiveCollection`.** Spike A (cards, first implementer) and Spike B (boards, second) both found `ArchiveCollection` implemented by no backend and near-dead: stores keep hand-rolled per-entity `DataStore` methods. Keep only the genuinely-cross-cutting pieces — `KanbanError::unsupported` and a thin `ArchiveMetadata`/`ArchivedEntity` (used at exactly one HashMap-key site) — and DROP `ArchiveCollection`. F1a shrinks accordingly (see Execution learnings).

## Open decisions (leans)
- Global/unscoped query audit (D3 bounded cost): enumerate every query that reads entities across boards without a live-board scope (snapshot save/serialize, `list_all_cards`, cross-board MCP/CLI lists) and decide inclusion vs exclusion of archived-board descendants. Settle during the SE-C spike; record the concrete call-site list on C3/C5.
- Whether empty boards are archivable at all or only deletable. Lean: allow archiving empty boards too (uniform UX), trivially cheap.
- Whether archived boards keep their own ordering (`archived_position`) or sort by `archived_at`. Lean: `archived_at` desc for the view; keep an `archived_position` only if reordering the archived list is wanted.

### D10 — Archival persistence = FK extension-table pattern (SUPERSEDES B4 full-data move + C1/C5 board marker column)
Uniform for cards and boards: archival state is a `*_archival` extension table (1:0..1, FK to the entity, holding ONLY archival columns), entities stay in their home tables. This is the normalized design with the LOWEST maintenance — it does not duplicate the entity schema (the smell that killed both the board mirror **and** B4's separate full-data `archived_cards` table). Persistence-layer only: the **domain keeps its simple shape** (an `ArchivedCard` with `board_id`; a `Board.archived_at` marker — the model Spike B proved lossless byte-for-byte).
- **Cards:** the existing `archived_cards` table IS already an extension table (`card_id` PK/FK, `archived_at`, `original_column_id`, `original_position`). Retrofit = **fix-in-place**: add `board_id` (+ backfill), break the column-delete cascade so it cannot orphan, keep the card row in `cards`. **Consequences validated by Spike A:** no row-move, no `sprint_logs` rebuild, no `sprint_logs` FK trap (the card never leaves `cards`, so its logs/edges stay valid) — the entire crown-jewel risk of the old B4 evaporates. Live-card queries keep a cheap PK-indexed anti-join (`WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM archived_cards a WHERE a.card_id = cards.id)`); at kanban scale this is a non-issue and is the price of not duplicating the schema.
- **Boards:** domain keeps `Board.archived_at`; SQLite persists it via a `board_archival(board_id PK/FK, archived_at, archived_position)` extension table (not a `boards` column) for consistency and to avoid a sparse nullable column. Archive = insert extension row; restore = delete it; the subtree stays live (so the C3b global-query audit is unchanged).

### D11 — Layering: service is the single impl; v1 DTO layer needs archived representation
- **Single implementation, thin consumers.** All archive/restore/list/permanent-delete logic lives in the **service layer** (`KanbanContext`, C3a/B5); CLI (C7), TUI (C6), and MCP (C8) are thin consumers that call those methods — no logic duplicated per surface (confirmed: every surface already routes through `KanbanContext`).
- **v1 DTO surface (`crates/kanban-service/src/api/v1/`) needs archived representation.** The DTO layer (KAN-769/KAN-713) projects domain types via `From<&Domain>` with **exhaustive destructuring** (a CI-guarded compile-time drift lock — no `..`/`Default`). Consequences:
  - **Green-boundary (cross-crate) rule:** adding `Board.archived_at` (C1) FORCES a `BoardResponse` update in the SAME slice, or `kanban-service` fails to compile. Same class as F1a's `error_mapping.rs:19` break. **Both spikes built crate-scoped and missed this — verify with `cargo build -p kanban-service` when a domain type a DTO projects gains a field.** Folded into C1 (BoardResponse) and F1a (error_mapping).
  - **New response DTOs (additive):** there is NO `ArchivedCardResponse`/`ArchivedBoardResponse` today (archived cards are currently serialized as the domain `ArchivedCardSummary` directly by CLI/MCP). Add `ArchivedCardResponse` (carrying `board_id`) in **B6** and `ArchivedBoardResponse` in **C9**, each with an exhaustive `From<&_>` projection, and route the CLI/MCP list-archived surfaces through them for consistency with the v1 direction. TUI stays in domain types (no serialization boundary).

## Execution learnings (VALIDATED — Phase 6 spikes A & B, both green)
Two isolated worktree spikes drove the hardest slice chains TDD-to-green (Spike A: F1a→B1→B2→B4 cards; Spike B: F1a→C1→C2 boards). Headline: the **archived-marker / lossless-restore design and the first-class card retrofit both HELD** (Spike B proved archive→restore is byte-identical; Spike A removed the `NOT IN` subquery and migrated rows cleanly). Corrections folded into the cards:
- **Storage pivot (D10)** — Spike A showed the move-to-full-table is high-risk (sprint_logs FK trap, 24 `ArchivedCard::new` sites, non-drift-guarded writer). The extension-table pivot deletes that risk. **B4 and C5 rewritten.**
- **F1a is NOT purely additive** — adding `DomainError::Unsupported` breaks the exhaustive match at `crates/kanban-service/src/api/v1/error_mapping.rs:19` (added by KAN-769 after the card). F1a acceptance must include that arm; it is additive to `kanban-domain` only.
- **`ArchivedCard::new` has 24 call sites**, not ~8, incl. cross-crate (`kanban-persistence-sqlite/tests/{entities,data_store}.rs`, `kanban-persistence/src/test_helpers/helpers.rs`). B1 must enumerate them; cross-crate repair coordinates with B4.
- **B1 board capture must be best-effort** — `context.get_column(id)?` propagates `NotFound` and breaks existing "archive a card whose column_id is fake" tests. Use `store.get_column(id)?.map(|c| c.board_id).unwrap_or_else(Uuid::nil)` (matches D2 "may dangle").
- **B2 trait placement** — `list_archived_cards_by_board` is consumed in `operations.rs::list_archived_cards_sorted`, which is on `KanbanOperations` (no in-domain impl). Repoint by inline `board_id` field filter AND set `CardListFilter.board_id = None` (else `filter_and_sort_cards` re-drops the dangling-column card via `allowed_column_ids`). Move the "tolerate deleted column" assertion to a store-level test.
- **C2 real correctness bug** — `ImportEntities::execute` dedups board ids via `list_boards()`, now live-only, so an import colliding with an ARCHIVED board's id slips through. Add a marker-agnostic listing (`list_boards()` + `list_archived_boards()`) for dedup.
- **`Snapshot { .. }` struct literals** also ripple (not just `from_data`) — found `export/importer.rs:247`; expect more in service/sqlite. C1/C4/C5/service cards need the checklist item.
- **Test friction** — proving `DataStore` trait defaults needs a ~34-method stub double; add a shared `#[cfg(test)]` stub/mockall so each trait-extension card doesn't re-pay it. The SQLite writer binds fields individually (not drift-guarded) → an all-fields round-trip test is the practical guard.
- **Migration ordering (SQLite)** — the on-open schema migration must run BEFORE `sqlx::raw_sql(SCHEMA)` (SCHEMA declares an index on the new column and fails on the old-shape table). `defer_foreign_keys` does NOT stop `ON DELETE CASCADE` actions.

## FULL-SPIKE EXECUTION — the entire epic implemented green (all 19 + 2 slices)
The whole tree was executed for real on isolated branches (`spike/board-archive-full` = 17 commits, `spike/board-archive-sea` = 2), TDD, with a **`cargo build --workspace --tests`** gate between batches. Final result: **the complete feature compiles and tests green across all 10 crates** (domain marker + commands, JSON V9 + SQLite schema-4 persistence, service ops + global-query audit + v1 DTOs, and CLI/MCP/TUI surfaces). This is a validation branch — no code lands on develop; the cards are the deliverable, now corrected to match what actually compiled. Key corrections folded into the cards:
- **B4 migration safety:** relaxing `cards.column_id` to `ON DELETE SET NULL` needs a `cards` table-swap; do it with `PRAGMA foreign_keys = OFF` on a dedicated connection OUTSIDE the tx (`defer_foreign_keys` does NOT stop cascade actions — it would wipe archived rows + sprint_logs). The `sprint_logs` FK trap is otherwise GONE (card row never leaves `cards`).
- **`BoardResponse` is NOT compile-locked:** it uses field access, not exhaustive destructure, so `Board.archived_at` does not break `kanban-service` (correcting D11). The DTO field is added for consistency, not by force. (The lock IS real for `CardResponse`/`ArchivedCardResponse` — exhaustive destructure — confirmed.)
- **Backend invariant:** any backend whose `list_boards` is live-only MUST implement `list_archived_boards` — else `ImportEntities` dedup bricks core `create_board` on the hand-written JSON/SQLite backends. Both now forward to the real archived query.
- **Build gate must be `--workspace --tests`:** plain `--workspace` skips test targets and hid ~18 `Snapshot{}` + `Board{}` `#[cfg(test)]` literal ripples and a latent cross-crate compile break for two batches.
- **C3b audit is bounded and cheap:** 1 helper (`list_live_cards`) + ~7 EXCLUDE repoints, all in `kanban-service`; repointing the single `list_all_cards_impl` trait-impl makes domain-tier consumers live-scoped transitively (CLI/MCP need no change). Correction: `export_board_impl` (`sprints.rs:244`) is INCLUDE (fidelity), not EXCLUDE. Fidelity guards (snapshot + import see archived) pass.
- **Naming/shape:** service method is `permanently_delete_archived_board`; `list_archived_boards -> Vec<ArchivedBoardSummary>` (fields `{board_id,name,description,archived_at,position}`, no `ArchivedBoard` type); board archive ops are INHERENT on `KanbanContext`, not `KanbanOperations`.
- **B2 stale cross-crate test:** removing the DeleteColumn archived-cards guard (intended, D2) breaks `kanban-tui/tests/data_integrity_tests.rs:116 test_delete_column_with_archived_cards_fails` — B2 must update it to `_succeeds` (deleting a column with archived cards is now safe via `SET NULL`).
- **C6/SE-A coordination:** both add arms to the same exhaustive TUI match sites (AppMode/DialogMode/KeybindingAction) — real single-branch execution lands A1 first, then C6 adds its arms (the spike ran them on separate branches).
- **Deferred follow-up:** `export_board_impl` filters `list_boards()` (live-only), so exporting an ARCHIVED board yields an empty `boards` vec (restore-before-export, or read raw store). Recorded on C3a.

## Out of scope
- Changing the dependency-edge model semantics beyond adding board-scoped archive fidelity.
- Cross-board card moves; multi-select board operations.
- Any UI beyond the boards panel + archived-boards view.

## Tree (see spawns children)
- SE-A TUI permanent board delete (#359) — ships first, independent (no archive dependency).
- F1 Foundation: bounded shared archival abstraction (D9) — depended on by SE-B and SE-C.
- SE-B Archived-cards first-class retrofit — corrected foundation; first implementer of F1.
- SE-C Reversible board archive (archived-marker) — builds on F1 + SE-B; second implementer of F1.

Template area for the spike (Phase 6): the SE-B SQLite retrofit + migration slice (B4 — move archived cards out of `cards`, kill the `NOT IN` subquery, mind the `sprint_logs` cascade-FK trap) and the SE-C archive-command slice (C2 — the marker toggle, which also validates the F1 abstraction on its second implementer). B4 is now the riskiest migration (the mirror is gone). C5 collapsed to a single `ALTER TABLE` and is no longer a spike target.

## Build order (verified Phase 4 — acyclic, green at every boundary)
`A1 → A2` (SE-A, independent, closes #359) · `F1a` (foundation: abstraction + `KanbanError::unsupported` + `error_mapping.rs` arm) · `B1 → B2` (domain: `board_id`, board-scoped queries) · `B3, B4` (parallel; JSON V7→V8, SQLite 2→3 extension table) · `B5` (service+surface wiring) · `B6` (v1 `ArchivedCardResponse` DTO) · `C1 → C2` (domain: `archived_at` marker + `BoardResponse` DTO + commands) · `C4, C5` (parallel; JSON V8→V9, SQLite 3→4 `board_archival` table) · `C3a` (service wiring) · `C3b` (global-query audit; after B5 + C5, spike-confirmed) · `C6, C7, C8` (parallel; TUI/CLI/MCP surfaces) · `C9` (v1 `ArchivedBoardResponse` DTO; with C7/C8).
Version-bump ordering is load-bearing: B3 before C4 (JSON), B4 before C5 (SQLite). DataStore trait additions stay green via functional defaults or the `unsupported` default (D6).

## Structure & grooming
- 24 cards: root `KAN-821`; sub-epics SE-A `822`, SE-B `823`, SE-C `824`, F1 `825`; leaves `826..842` + DTO cards **B6**/**C9** (D11 fold-in). C3 was split (Phase 4 scope fix) into C3a `836` (wiring) + C3b `842` (audit).
- Points (leaves, 1–5): SE-A=4, F1=3, SE-B=18 (incl. B6=2), SE-C=24 (incl. C9=2) → **49 total**. Epics/sub-epics unpointed (roll-up only).
- Sprint: all 22 assigned to the **board-archive-epic** sprint (`ae79ba83`).


## UPDATE — ArchiveMetadata promoted to an owned field (F1a #363)
Refines D9. `ArchiveMetadata` is now a genuinely OWNED field on the archived RECORD (`ArchivedCard.metadata`), not a projection — `#[serde(flatten)]` keeps the wire shape byte-identical so there is no migration. It is the seam a future `archived_by`/reason lands in once, for every entity that carries a discrete archived record.
- **Boards are unaffected — the marker was NOT dropped (only the column was).** Clarifying to avoid confusion: the board archive marker stays a bare `Board.archived_at` DOMAIN field (D10: "domain keeps its simple shape"), persisted via the `board_archival` extension table (D10/C5) — the persistence COLUMN was dropped for the table, the domain marker was kept. Boards do NOT adopt the `ArchiveMetadata` envelope: a board is archived by an in-place marker and its archival columns (`archived_at`, `archived_position`) live in the extension row. So `ArchiveMetadata` is a card-record concept only; C1-C5 are unchanged. (Record-with-envelope for cards vs marker-plus-extension-table for boards — consistent with D3/D10.)

## Execution learnings — VALIDATED (re-spike, 2026-07-06)
Re-spiked B3/B4/B5 in isolated worktrees off the post-review B2 tip (all three reached green + clippy -D warnings + fmt). Two DECIDED corrections and one cross-cutting sequencing rule:

### SUPERSEDES D10 SQLite cascade mechanism
D10 originally said: relax `cards.column_id` to `ON DELETE SET NULL`, make it nullable, and NULL the live `column_id` on archive. **That is wrong and self-contradictory** (validated in the B4 spike):
- `CardRecord.column_id` is a non-optional `Uuid`; nulling it breaks `row_to_card` (`try_get::<String>("column_id")` on NULL) and the all-fields round-trip identity test.
- It diverges from in-memory + JSON, which KEEP `card.column_id` as the dangling original after the column is deleted.
**Corrected mechanism:** DROP the `cards.column_id → columns(id)` FK entirely (keep `column_id TEXT NOT NULL`, value intact). Live-card cleanup on column delete is already explicit via the command tier (`DeleteCardsByColumns`), so the FK cascade was redundant and only harmful to archived cards. Simpler: no nullable change, no null-on-archive writer step, no NULL-tolerant reader. `archived_cards.card_id → cards ON DELETE CASCADE` is KEPT.

### Cross-cutting: board-scoped WRITES require board_id populated in EVERY backend
Board scoping by the `board_id` field is only safe for reads AND cascades once every backend populates it (B3 JSON backfill + B4 SQLite column). A cascade that misses a record leaks it PERMANENTLY (edge tables have no FK). Until B4 lands, SQLite reads board_id as nil, so a pure board-scoped board-delete cascade silently leaks on SQLite. **Safe bridge (validated in B5 spike): union gather = `list_archived_cards_by_board(board_id)` ∪ `list_archived_cards_by_columns(column_ids)`, deduped by card id** — the by-board arm catches dangling-column records (in-memory/JSON), the by-columns arm keeps pre-B4 SQLite correct. Collapse to pure board-scoped once B4 is everywhere.

Per-card corrections folded into KAN-831 (B3), KAN-832 (B4), KAN-833 (B5). Green spike branches: spike/b3-respike, spike/b4-respike, spike/b5-respike.

cards.description:
## Context / why

Child of the winget umbrella (see parent epic). The winget publish job
(sibling card) opens a PR to `microsoft/winget-pkgs` via the
`vedantmgoyal9/winget-releaser` Action. That Action pushes a branch to a
**fork** of winget-pkgs owned by us and opens the PR from there, authenticating
with a Personal Access Token. This card provisions both. Pure ops, no code in
this repo. Structural analogue of KAN-540 (Chocolatey account + CHOCO_API_KEY).

## Current state

- Existing release secrets in use (`release.yml`): `DEPLOY_KEY`,
  `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, `AUR_SSH_KEY`, `HOMEBREW_TAP_DEPLOY_KEY`,
  `CHOCO_API_KEY`. No `WINGET_TOKEN` yet.
- No `fulsomenko/winget-pkgs` fork exists yet (verify on GitHub).

## Target

1. **Fork** `microsoft/winget-pkgs` to `fulsomenko/winget-pkgs`
   (GitHub UI → Fork). The fork only needs the default branch; keep it.
2. **Mint a PAT** for the Action to push the manifest branch and open the PR:
   - `winget-releaser` requires a **classic** PAT with the `public_repo`
     scope (it pushes to the public fork and opens a cross-repo PR). A
     fine-grained token with Contents:write + Pull requests:write on the fork
     also works on recent action versions — confirm against the action's
     current README and prefer the narrowest that works.
   - Create under the account that owns the fork (Max).
3. **Add the repo secret** `WINGET_TOKEN` in
   *Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions* on `fulsomenko/kanban`.
4. **Keep the fork reasonably current** with upstream `master` (the action
   rebases, but a wildly stale fork causes PR conflicts). Document a one-line
   "sync fork" note in the recovery runbook (sibling docs card).

## Step-by-step

1. Fork `microsoft/winget-pkgs` → `fulsomenko/winget-pkgs`.
2. Read the chosen `winget-releaser` version's README for the exact required
   token type/scope (it has changed across major versions). Pin the action to a
   specific commit/tag in the CI card to avoid scope drift.
3. Create the PAT with the minimum scope that the pinned action version accepts.
4. Add `WINGET_TOKEN` secret.
5. Record the PAT's expiry and rotation owner in the maintainer playbook (sibling
   docs card) — classic `public_repo` PATs can be set to expire.

## Tests / verification

- `test_winget_token_secret_present` — the `winget` publish job (sibling) reads
  `${{ secrets.WINGET_TOKEN }}` without an "empty secret" failure on its first
  real run.
- Verification gate: a manual `winget-releaser` dry run (or the first real
  release) successfully pushes a branch to `fulsomenko/winget-pkgs` and opens a
  PR upstream — proving both the fork and the token scope are correct.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `fulsomenko/winget-pkgs` fork exists.
- [ ] PAT minted with the minimum scope the pinned action version requires.
- [ ] `WINGET_TOKEN` secret added to `fulsomenko/kanban`.
- [ ] Token type/scope/expiry + rotation owner recorded in the maintainer
      playbook (sibling docs card).

## Dependencies / sequencing

- Parallel with the skeleton card; no inter-dependency.
- Blocks the `release.yml` winget-job card (that job cannot authenticate without
  the fork + token).

## Quirks

- This is an out-of-band, human-only task (GitHub UI + secret entry); there is
  no code artifact in this repo beyond the secret reference that lands in the CI
  card.
- Do NOT commit the PAT anywhere; it lives only as a repo Actions secret.
cards.title: Fork microsoft/winget-pkgs + provision WINGET_TOKEN secret

cards.description:
## Context / why

Child of the winget umbrella (see parent epic). Adds the CI step that, on each
upstream release, opens a PR to `microsoft/winget-pkgs` with the new version's
manifests. Structural analogue of KAN-541 (Chocolatey publish step). Steady-state
per-release work after this lands: zero.

## Current state (researched)

- `.github/workflows/release.yml` already has, after the main `release` job:
  - `build-windows` (`:243-307`) — builds + uploads
    `kanban-v$VERSION-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip` and `SHA256SUMS` to the GitHub
    Release. **winget reuses this asset; do not rebuild it.**
  - `publish-chocolatey` (`:309-462`) — `needs: [release, build-windows]`,
    `if: needs.release.outputs.has_changesets == 'true'`, `continue-on-error: true`.
    It demonstrates the asset-readiness wait pattern (`Read Windows ZIP digest
    from GitHub Release`, `:322-353`) that polls until the release asset is
    `uploaded` before reading its digest.
- The `release` job exposes outputs `new` (version) and `has_changesets`
  (`:21-23`), already consumed by downstream jobs for gating.

## Target

Add a `publish-winget` job to `release.yml`, modeled on `publish-chocolatey`:

```yaml
  publish-winget:
    name: Submit to winget
    needs: [release, build-windows]
    if: needs.release.outputs.has_changesets == 'true'
    runs-on: windows-latest
    continue-on-error: true          # match choco: never block the rest of the release
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Wait for release asset to be ready
        # Reuse the choco poll pattern (release.yml:322-353): poll
        # `gh release view v$VERSION --json assets` until the zip asset's
        # state == 'uploaded'. winget-releaser reads the asset by URL, so the
        # asset must exist and be fully uploaded before the action runs.
        shell: pwsh
        env:
          VERSION: ${{ needs.release.outputs.new }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: |
          # ... (lift the loop from publish-chocolatey's `Read ... digest` step)

      - name: Submit PR to winget-pkgs
        uses: vedantmgoyal9/winget-releaser@<pin-to-tag-or-sha>
        with:
          identifier: fulsomenko.kanban
          version: ${{ needs.release.outputs.new }}
          installers-regex: 'x86_64-pc-windows-msvc\.zip$'
          token: ${{ secrets.WINGET_TOKEN }}
          # fork-user defaults to the token owner (fulsomenko); set explicitly
          # if the token owner differs from the fork owner.
```

`winget-releaser` does the rest: it fetches the matched release asset, computes
its SHA256, generates the version/installer/defaultLocale manifests (carrying
forward locale metadata from the previous version's manifests in winget-pkgs),
pushes a branch to `fulsomenko/winget-pkgs`, and opens the upstream PR.

### Important interactions

- **Manifest metadata source:** `winget-releaser` regenerates installer + SHA
  each release but inherits locale metadata (description, tags, URLs) from the
  *previously merged* version in winget-pkgs. So the locale fields authored in
  the skeleton card (and accepted in the initial submission) are what propagate
  forward — the in-repo `packaging/winget/` templates are not consumed by this
  action directly; they exist for local validation and the manual fallback.
  Note this clearly so no one assumes the action reads `packaging/winget/`.
- **Pin the action** to a tag or commit SHA (the repo already pins
  `KSXGitHub/github-actions-deploy-aur` to a SHA, `release.yml:175`). Match that
  hygiene.
- **`continue-on-error: true`** mirrors choco: a winget failure must not fail
  the crates.io / GitHub Release / AUR / Homebrew / Chocolatey path.
- **Failure surfacing:** add a `Surface winget failure` step
  (`if: failure()`, `continue-on-error: true`) writing a `::warning::` + a
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` block pointing at `packaging/winget/RECOVERY.md`,
  exactly like `Surface chocolatey failure` (`release.yml:441-462`).

## Step-by-step (TDD-adapted)

1. **Red:** add the job behind the `has_changesets` gate; add a deliberate
   probe (a no-op `winget-releaser` dry run or a `--dry-run`-style flag if the
   action supports it) on a throwaway branch and confirm it *would* open a PR
   against the fork. Confirm the `Surface winget failure` step fires when the
   token is intentionally blanked (mirrors KAN-673's deliberate-failure test for
   the choco surfacing step).
2. **Green:** wire the real action with `WINGET_TOKEN`; on the next real release
   it opens the upstream PR.
3. **Refactor:** factor the asset-readiness wait if it is now duplicated across
   `publish-chocolatey` and `publish-winget` (KAN-755 already tracks extracting
   duplicated publish steps into a reusable workflow — link it; do not
   pre-factor here if it complicates review).

## Tests

- `test_publish_winget_gated_on_changesets` — job is skipped when
  `has_changesets == 'false'` (assert via a no-changeset PR-merge dry run).
- `test_publish_winget_does_not_block_release` — `continue-on-error: true`
  verified by forcing the winget step to fail and confirming the overall release
  conclusion is unaffected.
- `test_surface_winget_failure_writes_runbook_link` — deliberate-failure probe
  (blank token) produces the warning + step-summary pointing at RECOVERY.md.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `publish-winget` job added, `needs: [release, build-windows]`, gated on
      `has_changesets`, `continue-on-error: true`.
- [ ] Waits for the release zip asset to be `uploaded` before invoking the
      action (reuse the choco poll).
- [ ] `vedantmgoyal9/winget-releaser` pinned to a tag/SHA, configured with
      `identifier`, `version`, `installers-regex`, `token`.
- [ ] `Surface winget failure` step points at `packaging/winget/RECOVERY.md`.
- [ ] A real (or dry-run) execution opens a PR to `microsoft/winget-pkgs` from
      the `fulsomenko/winget-pkgs` fork.
- [ ] `cargo`/workflow YAML lints clean; no change to the existing choco/AUR/brew
      steps.

## Dependencies / sequencing

- Depends on **W2 (fork + WINGET_TOKEN)** — cannot authenticate without it.
- Depends on **W1 (skeleton)** for the identifier + manifest shape the first
  merged version establishes (the action then carries metadata forward).
- Relates to **KAN-755** (extract duplicated publish steps into a reusable
  workflow) — the asset-readiness wait is the shared piece.

## Quirks

- The action opens the PR but cannot merge it — a Microsoft maintainer (or bot)
  merges upstream. The job "succeeding" means "PR opened", not "package live".
- `installers-regex` must match exactly one asset; the `SHA256SUMS` file must NOT
  match the regex or the action errors on ambiguity.
cards.title: release.yml: winget publish job (winget-releaser PR on release)

cards.description:
## Context / why

Child of the winget umbrella (see parent epic). The **first-ever** submission of
a brand-new package to `microsoft/winget-pkgs` is a distinct, one-time event:
it creates the `manifests/f/fulsomenko/` publisher folder and the
`fulsomenko.kanban` package, and it gets slower, manual maintainer review than
subsequent version bumps. This card owns that one-time submission and the
end-to-end verification that `winget install fulsomenko.kanban` actually works.

Once this lands, the CI job (sibling W3) handles every future version
automatically. No analogue was needed for Chocolatey (choco's first push goes
through the same `choco push` path as every later one); winget's first PR is
special, so it gets its own card.

## Current state

- No `fulsomenko.kanban` package exists in winget-pkgs yet (verify:
  `winget show fulsomenko.kanban` returns "No package found").
- Skeleton manifests (W1) and the fork+token (W2) are prerequisites.

## Target

A merged PR in `microsoft/winget-pkgs` creating
`manifests/f/fulsomenko/kanban/<version>/` with the three manifests, and a
clean-machine verification that install works and registers both aliases.

## Two viable paths for the first submission

1. **Manual via `wingetcreate` (recommended for the first one):**
   ```powershell
   winget install wingetcreate
   wingetcreate new https://github.com/fulsomenko/kanban/releases/download/v$VERSION/kanban-v$VERSION-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip
   # fill prompts to match the W1 templates (identifier fulsomenko.kanban,
   # zip + nested portable, both aliases), then submit the PR.
   wingetcreate submit --token <PAT> <generated-manifest-dir>
   ```
   Doing the first one manually de-risks it: you see validation feedback
   directly and can iterate before the CI job exists.

2. **Via the CI job (W3):** cut a release after W3 lands and let
   `winget-releaser` open the PR. Works, but couples the first (slow) review to
   a real release and gives less interactive feedback.

Recommendation: do the first submission manually with `wingetcreate` (path 1),
then let W3 own all subsequent versions. This also validates the manifest shape
independently of the CI wiring.

## Step-by-step

1. Ensure W1 manifests pass `winget validate` with a real version + SHA256.
2. Generate/submit the first PR (`wingetcreate` path above), targeting the
   current released version (e.g. `v0.7.2` or whatever is current at execution).
3. Respond to Microsoft's automated validation (manifest schema, installer
   reachability, SHA match, SmartScreen/Defender scan of the zip) and any
   maintainer comments until merged.
4. After merge, wait for the manifest to propagate to the winget source index
   (minutes-to-hours), then verify on a clean Windows box / Sandbox:
   ```powershell
   winget source update
   winget show fulsomenko.kanban
   winget install fulsomenko.kanban
   kanban --version
   kanban-mcp --version
   winget uninstall fulsomenko.kanban   # confirm clean uninstall too
   ```

## Tests / verification gates

- `test_winget_show_finds_package` — `winget show fulsomenko.kanban` returns the
  package after merge + source update.
- `test_winget_install_both_binaries_on_path` — after install, both `kanban` and
  `kanban-mcp` resolve and report a version on a clean machine.
- `test_winget_uninstall_clean` — `winget uninstall` removes both aliases.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] First PR merged into `microsoft/winget-pkgs` creating
      `manifests/f/fulsomenko/kanban/<version>/`.
- [ ] `winget install fulsomenko.kanban` works from a clean Windows install /
      Sandbox.
- [ ] Both `kanban` and `kanban-mcp` are on PATH and report versions.
- [ ] `winget uninstall fulsomenko.kanban` is clean.
- [ ] Any validation feedback fed back into the W1 templates so the CI-generated
      manifests (W3) match what was accepted.

## Dependencies / sequencing

- Depends on **W1** (manifests) and **W2** (fork + token).
- The *manual* first submission does NOT require **W3**; doing it before W3 lets
  winget go live sooner and validates the manifest shape independently.
- Feeds corrections back into **W1** (and therefore W3, since winget-releaser
  carries the merged metadata forward).

## Quirks

- First-package review is human and can take days; subsequent bumps are fast.
- Microsoft scans the installer with Defender/SmartScreen; an unsigned portable
  zip is accepted but a false-positive AV hit can stall the PR — note this in
  the recovery runbook (W5).
- Only one PR per package version is allowed; if the first PR is rejected for a
  malformed manifest, fix and re-push to the same PR rather than opening a
  second for the same version.
cards.title: Initial winget-pkgs submission + verify winget install fulsomenko.kanban

cards.description:
## Context / why

Child of the winget umbrella (see parent epic). Documents the winget package for
both users (install path) and maintainers (release flow, recovery). Structural
analogue of KAN-542 (Chocolatey docs) + `packaging/chocolatey/RECOVERY.md`.
Mirror the existing choco docs' shape and tone.

## Current state (researched)

- `packaging/README.md` has a table listing AUR + Chocolatey with links to each
  subdir README; winget is missing.
- `packaging/chocolatey/README.md` documents the CI release flow + local
  smoke-test; `packaging/chocolatey/RECOVERY.md` is a failure-mode runbook the
  workflow's failure step links to.
- `packaging/aur/README.md` follows the same shape.
- Project `README.md` install section lists install paths (per KAN-683 it gained
  Chocolatey instructions); winget line to be added.
- `docs/release-recovery.md` is the umbrella recovery doc the packaging READMEs
  reference.

## Target

1. **`packaging/winget/README.md`** — mirror the choco README:
   - What lives here (dev/staging manifest templates; canonical home is
     `microsoft/winget-pkgs`).
   - How releases publish: the `publish-winget` job runs
     `vedantmgoyal9/winget-releaser`, which regenerates manifests from the
     GitHub release asset and opens a PR upstream; metadata is carried forward
     from the previously merged version.
   - Local validation + Windows Sandbox smoke test (the `winget validate` /
     `SandboxTest.ps1` block from W1).
   - Manual fallback with `wingetcreate` (for re-publishing a tag or the first
     submission).
   - Pointer to `RECOVERY.md` for publish failures.

2. **`packaging/winget/RECOVERY.md`** — failure-mode runbook for the
   `publish-winget` job, in the same diagnosis-flowchart style as
   `packaging/chocolatey/RECOVERY.md`. Cover:
   - **PR opened but workflow reported failure** — the PR is upstream; do
     nothing, watch the winget-pkgs PR. (Like choco scenario 1.)
   - **Manifest validation failed** (schema, `RelativeFilePath` wrong, SHA
     mismatch, installer URL 404) — fix the W1 templates / the action config;
     push to the same PR (one PR per version). Do NOT open a second PR for the
     same version.
   - **AV / SmartScreen false positive** on the unsigned zip stalls the PR —
     how to request a re-scan / comment on the PR.
   - **Token rejected (401/403)** — rotate `WINGET_TOKEN`; re-run.
   - **Fork stale / PR conflicts** — sync `fulsomenko/winget-pkgs` with upstream
     `master`, re-run.
   - **First-package review is slow** — expected; not a failure. Watch the PR.
   - Anti-patterns (don't open duplicate PRs for the same version; keep this
     runbook's link in sync with the workflow's failure-surfacing step, mirroring
     the choco runbook's self-reference note).

3. **`packaging/README.md` table** — add a winget row:
   `| winget | Windows | [winget/](winget/README.md) |`.

4. **Project `README.md`** — add the winget install line alongside Chocolatey,
   e.g. `winget install fulsomenko.kanban`.

5. **`CONTRIBUTING.md`** (or the maintainer playbook section) — winget entry:
   file layout under `packaging/winget/`, where the publish step lives in
   `release.yml`, the `WINGET_TOKEN` secret + its rotation owner/expiry (from
   W2), and the fork-sync note.

## Step-by-step (TDD-adapted for docs)

1. **Red:** draft the READMEs/runbook referencing the real file paths and the
   real job name; have the parent confirm they match the landed W1/W3 reality
   (no invented step names).
2. **Green:** land the docs; verify every internal link resolves
   (`packaging/README.md` → `winget/README.md` → `RECOVERY.md`;
   workflow failure step → `RECOVERY.md`).
3. **Refactor:** dedupe with `docs/release-recovery.md` — link to it rather than
   restating the umbrella recovery flow.

## Tests / verification

- `test_packaging_readme_lists_winget` — the top-level table row exists and the
  link resolves.
- `test_winget_recovery_link_matches_workflow` — the path in the
  `Surface winget failure` step (W3) equals `packaging/winget/RECOVERY.md`
  (guard against drift, mirroring the choco runbook's stated invariant).
- Manual: all relative links in the new docs resolve on GitHub.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `packaging/winget/README.md` documents the release flow + local validation
      + `wingetcreate` fallback.
- [ ] `packaging/winget/RECOVERY.md` covers the failure modes above in the choco
      runbook's flowchart style.
- [ ] `packaging/README.md` table has a winget row.
- [ ] Project README shows `winget install fulsomenko.kanban`.
- [ ] CONTRIBUTING maintainer playbook covers winget (layout, CI location,
      `WINGET_TOKEN`, fork-sync).
- [ ] The RECOVERY.md path matches the W3 failure-surfacing step exactly.
- [ ] All internal links resolve.

## Dependencies / sequencing

- Can be drafted alongside W1; finalize once **W3** (real job name + failure
  step) and **W4** (a real, installable package to point users at) have landed,
  so the docs describe reality, not intent.

## Quirks

- Keep the recovery runbook and the workflow's failure-link in lockstep — the
  choco runbook calls out that drift between the two is worse than no runbook.
- Do not claim `winget install` works until W4 has actually verified it.

cards.description:
Sub-epic of the board-removal epic (see root spec KAN-821).

## SE-C — Reversible encapsulated board archive (builds on SE-B)

`archived_boards` as a **first-class discrete peer collection** to `boards` (root spec DECIDED D3/D4). Archiving captures the board's **entire aggregate in full**, keeping the board's live cards and archived cards as **two discrete sets**, so restore is lossless (live→live, archived→archived, edges with active/archived flag, sprints, counters, completion column, active sprint). Permanent-delete drops the archived aggregate. Depends on SE-B's corrected archived-card model.

### Storage (relational mirror, discrete sets — D3)
`archived_boards`, `archived_board_columns`, `archived_board_cards` (live-at-archive), `archived_board_archived_cards` (archived-at-archive, w/ metadata), `archived_board_sprints`, `archived_board_edges` (spawns/blocks/relates, active/archived preserved).

### Children (leaf cards)
- C1 Domain: first-class `ArchivedBoard` aggregate type (board + columns + discrete cards set + discrete archived_cards set + sprints + edges + `archived_at` + position) + summary + tests.
- C2 Domain commands + store: `BoardCommand::ArchiveBoard`/`RestoreBoard`, `DataStore` methods (default `Unsupported` per D6), in-memory discrete storage, inverse via extended `ImportEntities` + tests. **[TEMPLATE core — spike target]**
- C3 Service: `archive_board`/`restore_board`/`list_archived_boards`/`delete_archived_board` (permanent) + cascade-collect + undo + integration tests.
- C4 Persistence JSON: `archived_boards` bucket, **V8→V9 migration** + backup + round-trip tests.
- C5 Persistence SQLite: `archived_board_*` mirror tables, **schema_version 3→4 migration**, writers/readers/snapshot-apply wiring + round-trip tests. **[RISKY replicated — spike target]**
- C6 TUI: `AppMode::ArchivedBoardsView` + archive key `A` + restore + permanent-delete + unify with delete UX + tests.
- C7 CLI: board archive/restore/list-archived/delete-archived + tests.
- C8 MCP: tool_archive_board/restore_board/list_archived_boards/delete_archived_board + tests.## SE-C VERIFICATION + C3b RE-SPIKE (2026-07-09) — validated learnings
- **C3b was incomplete (cards-only); corrected + re-spiked green.** Archived-board COLUMNS (by name) and SPRINTS (by number) also leaked; both close transitively by repointing `list_all_columns_impl`/`list_all_sprints_impl` to live helpers (NO `search/` change). Helpers + a cached archived-board-id set live in C3a.
- **The TUI display leak is snapshot-fed -> owned by C6a**, not inherited from C3b (`core.rs` accessors have no production/TUI consumers).
- **C6 split** into C6a (single-board archived surface; keys corrected: `d`=delete shipped, `D`=archived view reserved by SE-A, `a`=archive) + C6b (KAN-847, multi-select) + C3c (KAN-846, batch board ops).
- **KAN-845 must precede C5** (schema 3->4 is an irreversible version bump; the generic pre-migration backup covers it for free once landed). C5 "SQLite has no backup mechanism" claim is false.
- **Acceptance gates elevated to `cargo build --workspace --tests`** across the tree (crate-scoped hid 3 cross-crate breaks in SE-B).
- Accuracy drift fixed: `ArchivedCardSummary` is GONE (C1/C7/C8 referenced it); board ops are INHERENT on `KanbanContext` not `KanbanOperations`; C9 nil-handling is correct as-is (own id never nil).

cards.description:
Follow-up to KAN-848 (deterministic ordering, GitHub #358). KAN-848 fixed the in-memory/domain store and the JSON backend inherits it (JSON reads delegate to an InMemoryStore cache). The SQLite backend does NOT: `SqliteBackend::list_*` delegate straight to `SqliteStore`'s live SQL (`crates/kanban-service/src/sqlite_backend.rs:45` -> `self.db.list_boards()`), bypassing the fixed in-memory store. Its `ORDER BY position` clauses lack a total-order tiebreak, so equal-position rows come back in SQLite's unspecified order.

## Severity note
Unlike the HashMap path, SQLite tie order is *unspecified* but not *randomized per process*; in practice it follows rowid/insertion order, so it is usually stable across launches of a given file (it can shift after VACUUM, an index change, or a query-plan change). This is a latent parity/correctness gap, not the acute per-launch reshuffle #358 reported. Fix it for guaranteed determinism and parity with the domain fix.

## Current state (real refs)
- `crates/kanban-persistence-sqlite/src/sqlite_store/lists.rs:16` — `list_boards_async`: `... FROM boards ORDER BY position ASC` (no tiebreak)
- `crates/kanban-persistence-sqlite/src/sqlite_store/lists.rs:37` — `list_all_columns_async`: `... FROM columns ORDER BY position` (no tiebreak)
- `crates/kanban-persistence-sqlite/src/sqlite_store/data_store.rs:83` — `list_columns_by_board`: `... FROM columns WHERE board_id = ? ORDER BY position` (no tiebreak)
- `crates/kanban-persistence-sqlite/src/sqlite_store/entities/card.rs:130` — `fetch_cards_with_filter` (backs list_all_cards / list_cards_by_column / list_cards_by_columns / list_cards_by_sprint): `... ORDER BY position ASC, created_at ASC` (partial: missing `id`)
- Fine as-is: sprints `ORDER BY sprint_number` (board-unique); archived cards `ORDER BY ac.archived_at`.

## Target
Match the domain policy `(position, created_at, id)` for a total order:
- boards: `ORDER BY position ASC, created_at ASC, id ASC`
- columns (both queries): `ORDER BY position ASC, created_at ASC, id ASC`
- cards (`fetch_cards_with_filter`): `ORDER BY position ASC, created_at ASC, id ASC`

Prefer a single shared ordering-clause constant so the SQL side has one owner of the tiebreak (mirrors the `sort_by_position` helper on the domain side), e.g.:
```rust
// in sqlite_store (module-level)
const CARD_ORDER: &str = "ORDER BY position ASC, created_at ASC, id ASC";
const POSITION_ORDER: &str = "ORDER BY position ASC, created_at ASC, id ASC";
```
Note `id`/`created_at` are stored as TEXT; confirm ASC string comparison gives the intended order (UUID text + RFC3339/ISO timestamps both sort lexicographically consistent with value order). If stored differently, cast/normalize in the clause.

## Step-by-step (TDD)
1. Red: add tempfile round-trip tests that insert >=2 boards / columns / cards with equal `position` and distinct `created_at` (and a pair with equal position AND created_at, distinct `id`), then assert `list_*` returns them ordered by created_at then id. Insert in reverse to defeat incidental rowid ordering.
2. Green: add the tiebreak to the four query sites (via the shared constant).
3. Refactor: dedupe the ORDER BY string through the constant; keep sprint/archived queries unchanged.

## Tests (named)
- `test_list_boards_orders_equal_position_by_created_at_then_id`
- `test_list_all_columns_orders_equal_position_by_created_at_then_id`

cards.description:
# Backend-specific rollback: replace the `with_transaction` snapshot with inverse-replay

Parent / design card. Decides how a failed command BATCH is rolled back, and the per-backend strategy. Children KAN-355 (in-memory) and KAN-700 (HTTP) implement the two faces.

## Context
User undo/redo is already command-reversal (inverse-based, no snapshots). The ONE place still snapshotting is the intra-batch error rollback in `KanbanBackend::with_transaction`, which restores a FULL state snapshot if a command fails partway through a batch. But `KanbanContext::execute` ALREADY captures the per-command inverses (for the undo stack) in the very same call — so the snapshot is redundant work. It is O(N) in board size (KAN-355) and impossible/wrong for a remote backend (KAN-700).

## Current state (path:line)
- `crates/kanban-service/src/backend.rs:75` — `with_transaction` default:
  `let before = self.snapshot()?; match f() { Ok(())=>Ok(()), Err(e)=>{ self.apply_snapshot(before)?; Err(e) } }`. No backend overrides it (InMemoryStore, JSON, SQLite all use this default).
- `crates/kanban-service/src/context/undo.rs:17` — `execute()` wraps its work in `with_transaction` AND, inside the closure, does `per_cmd_inverses.push(cmd.capture_inverse(store)?); cmd.execute(&ctx)?;` per command, then `append_batch(&batch)`, then pushes `UndoEntry { forward, inverse }`. `undo()`/`redo()` also wrap in `with_transaction`. So the inverses required to roll back are already in hand a few lines above the snapshot.

## Decision
Replace snapshot-based batch rollback with INVERSE-REPLAY, and reduce `with_transaction` to a thin per-backend hook (default: run the closure directly, no snapshot):
- Logical atomicity = apply commands one by one capturing each inverse; on any failure (a command, or the command-log append), replay the inverses of the successfully-applied PREFIX in reverse. The failing command's inverse is NOT replayed (it did not apply).
- in-memory / file: rollback via inverse-replay; drop the O(N) snapshot. -> KAN-355.
- HTTP: `with_transaction` runs the closure directly; the `POST /v1/commands` batch is the server-side atomic unit, nothing local to snapshot. -> KAN-700.
- SQLite: MAY additionally wrap the batch in a native DB transaction (BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK) for crash durability — a separate concern from logical rollback; optional/future.

## Command contract (document + test)
Inverse-replay of the applied prefix is correct only if commands FAIL BEFORE THEY MUTATE (validate, then apply). A command that mutates then errors leaves partial state its inverse cannot cleanly reverse. The factory create path already validates (FK, uniqueness) before mutating; audit the command set, document this as a command-authoring contract, and add a guard test.

## Path to resolution
1. Add a shared atomic-apply helper at the service tier: `fn apply_atomic(store: &dyn DataStore, cmds: &[Command]) -> KanbanResult<Vec<Vec<Command>>>` — applies each command (capturing its inverse first), on failure replays the applied-prefix inverses in reverse and returns the error; returns the inverses on success (for the undo stack).
2. Rewire `execute()`: `apply_atomic` for the forward batch, then `append_batch` (roll back via the returned inverses if append fails); build `UndoEntry` from the returned inverses. Apply the same helper to `undo()`/`redo()`.
3. Change `with_transaction` default to run `f()` directly (no snapshot); keep it as an OPTIONAL native-transaction hook (SQLite may override). Remove the `snapshot()`/`apply_snapshot` rollback path from it (keep `snapshot()` if still used elsewhere, e.g. export).
4. KAN-355 = in-memory/file implementation + perf validation. KAN-700 = HTTP direct-call override.

## Tests / acceptance
- A 3-command batch whose 2nd command fails rolls back the 1st via its inverse, state == before, with NO `snapshot()` call on the in-memory path (assert via a spy/counter + state).
- A batch whose `append_batch` fails rolls back all applied commands.
- All existing `undo_redo` + `inverse_commands` suites stay green — run against JSON + SQLite, not just InMemory (KAN-478).
- `with_transaction` no longer snapshots; per-backend overrides as above.

## Children
spawns -> KAN-355 (in-memory inverse-replay + drop snapshot), KAN-700 (HTTP direct-call `with_transaction`).

cards.description:
## Goal (REGROUNDED 2026-06-30 after investigation)
Local multi-writer correctness when TUI + CLI + MCP write the same store concurrently. The original framing — "give SQLite whole-snapshot conflict detection like JSON" — was DISPROVEN by an empirical investigation (see Finding). The two backends have OPPOSITE problems; this epic now targets the two small, real gaps that investigation surfaced.

## Finding (VALIDATED empirically — conc-probe, 5 tests on real backends, one shared db)
SQLite, as the live app uses it, does NOT have a whole-snapshot clobber problem:
- The SqliteBackend is per-operation WRITE-THROUGH (each upsert/delete commits immediately) with LIVE reads (no cached in-memory snapshot); flush() = stamp_writer + checkpoint (writes no data); reload() is a no-op.
- It NEVER calls PersistenceStore::save (the whole-snapshot DELETE-all path). That destructive path is only the JSON/conversion path, never the live SQLite flow.
- Consequence: concurrent edits to DIFFERENT rows MERGE for free at the row level. No whole-snapshot wipe.
- REAL residual gap: upsert_card (entities/card.rs:32) is a WHOLE-ROW upsert. Two writers editing the SAME entity concurrently (e.g. a long-lived TUI card edit while CLI/MCP changes that same card) → whole-row last-writer-wins → the later save silently reverts ALL of the other writer's changes to that row, even different fields. (The earlier probe missed this — its "different field" test used two different cards.)

JSON, by contrast, caches the whole snapshot and saves it WHOLESALE, so it already conflict-detects at the whole-file level — it OVER-detects (any concurrent change trips it, even non-overlapping) and already has the TUI ConflictResolution/ExternalChangeDetected dialogs.

So: SQLite UNDER-detects (per-entity lost update, no guard) ; JSON OVER-detects (whole-file, already guarded, coarse).

## DECIDED — new scope
- DROP the whole-snapshot SQLite conflict-detection work (old Phase A: KAN-804, 806-810) — wrong premise, wrong granularity, and KAN-806 guarded PersistenceStore::save which the SQLite app never calls. Archived. (KAN-806 was built green on a branch; superseded — the version-integer learning is recorded but the whole-snapshot CAS is not the right mechanism.)
- DROP the merge-model Phase B (KAN-805) — SQLite write-through ALREADY provides per-row merge for different entities; the command-log-append merge epic is moot for SQLite, and overturning the audit-only log (KAN-474) for JSON is not warranted now.
- ADD: SQLite per-row optimistic concurrency — the genuine residual. Row-level CAS on a per-row version/updated_at in upsert_*: write only if the row is unchanged since this handle read it, else surface a conflict. Catches the same-entity lost update (TUI-edit vs CLI/MCP). Small, targeted, per-method — NOT a snapshot epic.
- KEEP for JSON: the informed conflict dialog (KAN-811 pure diff + KAN-812 dialog), re-targeted at the JSON whole-snapshot conflict (where the in-memory cached snapshot genuinely diverges from the on-disk file) so JSON's existing-but-coarse conflict becomes legible + actionable.

## Out of scope / notes
- JSON over-detection (conflicts on non-overlapping changes) — could be refined later but not now.
- JSON check->write TOCTOU (json_file_store.rs:285-322) — known limitation, future flock follow-up.
- The investigation's throwaway probe tests are on branch conc-probe (commit 2d3eaf5f) as evidence.

## New tree
- KAN-803 (this) -> KAN-811 (pure snapshot diff, for the JSON conflict dialog) ; KAN-812 (JSON conflict dialog enrichment) ; NEW (SQLite per-row optimistic concurrency).

## UPDATE (2026-06-30) — KAN-819 reframed after research
A 5-agent research pass refined the SQLite fix: the dominant same-entity lost-update is the WHOLE-ROW write shape, not a concurrency-control gap. KAN-819 is reframed from "per-row OCC" to "field-targeted entity updates" (write only changed columns) — eliminates the common different-field clobber, is cleaner persistence, and is valuable with zero concurrency. Per-row OCC is DEFERRED (only catches same-FIELD true conflict; probably not worth it for a single-user tool). True multi-writer is the SERVER (KAN-684, already underway: one-writer Arc<RwLock<KanbanContext>>). Supersedes the "ADD: SQLite per-row optimistic concurrency" line above.
